\subsection{Effective Semantics for the Admissible Fragment}
\label{subsec:eff-semantics}

We fix the admissible fragment as Hyland's \emph{effective topos} $\Eff$ \cite{Hyland1982}, a Cartesian closed topos with a natural numbers object (NNO) that internalizes partial recursive computation.

\paragraph{Objects and morphisms.}
Objects of $\Eff$ are \emph{assemblies} $(X,\Vdash)$ where each $x\in X$ is realized by a nonempty set of natural numbers $\{e:\; e\Vdash x\}$ (indices of partial recursive functions). A morphism $f:(X,\Vdash_X)\to(Y,\Vdash_Y)$ is tracked by a recursive index $\phi$ such that for all $e\Vdash_X x$ there exists $\phi(e)\Vdash_Y f(x)$.

\paragraph{Quotation and evaluation.}
Let $\Code$ denote the object of (Gödel-)codes for partial recursive functionals and let $\Env$ be the environment object. The internal quotation $\ulcorner\cdot\urcorner:L\to\Code$ assigns to each expression its index; the \emph{universal evaluator}
\[
\eval:\Code\times \Env \longrightarrow \Env
\]
is the Kleene universal partial recursive functional, hence an internal morphism of $\Eff$. Therefore the triple $(\Eff,\ulcorner\cdot\urcorner,\eval)$ satisfies the quotation--evaluation retract on the admissible fragment.

\paragraph{Admissible dynamics.}
An \emph{admissible} endomap $T:\Env\to\Env$ is any morphism in $\Eff$ tracked by a partial recursive index. Our UWCA/PR-1 evaluator $U$~\cite{SpivackUGPFormalization,ugp-lean} is represented internally by such a morphism; all results that refer to ``computable'' or ``finite-local'' maps are thus formalized as morphisms of $\Eff$.

\subsection{Computational Substrates: PR-0, PR-1, and DSAC}
\label{subsec:computational-substrates}

Throughout this work we rely on three complementary computational substrates that instantiate the abstract reflexive architecture at different levels of description.

\paragraph{PR-1: reversible UWCA loop.}
PR-1 is a one-dimensional, reversible universal cellular automaton (UWCA) defined on a periodic loop, with local update rule $U$ acting on binary neighbourhoods and supporting kink-like topological defects as effective particles~\cite{SpivackUGPFormalization,ugp-lean}.  In MFRR it plays two roles: (i) a concrete realisation of admissible dynamics in the effective topos (all PR-1 updates are morphisms of $\Eff$), and (ii) a laboratory for braid-based particle ontology, where kink braids reproduce a Standard-Model-like catalogue (electrons, quarks, nucleons, baryons).  Its limitations---dimensional collapse and overconstrained 1D kinematics---are summarized below in the historical note, which motivates the pivot to PR-0 and DSAC for emergent geometry and law.

\paragraph{PR-0: reflexive field substrate.}
PR-0 is a continuous, reversible field substrate combining an Ablowitz--Ladik lattice with mediator fields and an ontological-dissonance functional $D[\psi,\chi]$ that drives force discovery and curvature formation.  As detailed in Appendix~\ref{app:pr0-validation-summary} and the dedicated PR-0 substrate paper~\cite{SpivackPR0Substrate}, PR-0 serves as the primary microscopic realisation of the Reflexive Landauer functional and the information-curvature tensor $C_{\mu\nu}$.  TE$_1$ and $\Lambda\Omega$-RCP validation campaigns on PR-0 (curvature--dissonance--entropy invariant, transport law, RQG cosmology) supply the empirical backbone for the geometric theorems in the main text.

\paragraph{DSAC: Differential Self-Adjudicative Computation.}
DSAC~\cite{SpivackDSAC} is a continuous-field, reflexive computing architecture in which a lattice of coupled fields (e.g.\ PR-0-derived matter and mediator fields, dissonance and entropy densities) evolves under differential update rules that are themselves driven by internal adjudication of constraint residuals.  At each step the system measures ontological dissonance $D$ and other constraint violations, computes local differential corrections (Laplacians, gradients, divergence flows, logistic residuals), and updates the fields so as to reduce $D$ while preserving calibrated equilibrium structure.  In this sense DSAC ``computes by self-adjudication'': fixed points of the differential flow are precisely the solutions of the encoded constraint problem (e.g.\ metric closure, transport PDEs, fluctuation relations, curvature invariants).  Practically, DSAC consumes ensembles from PR-0 and performs large-scale regression and law-discovery in a reproducible way, providing the infrastructure for the Phase~I rediscovery benchmarks, the Phase~II curvature and transport laws, and the Phase~III Band~C advantage and RG-flow ensembles (see Appendix~O and Appendix~W for detailed configurations and metrics).  In the MFRR hierarchy, PR-0 realises the microscopic reflexive substrate, PR-1 exemplifies reversible UWCA dynamics and braid ontology, and DSAC supplies the mesoscopic ``reflexive laboratory'' in which invariants, transport laws, and RG attractors are empirically discovered and stress-tested as continuous approximations to the fully non-computable \(\PT\) dynamics.

\paragraph{Historical Note: The PR-1 Loop Program.}
In earlier work, the UWCA/PR-1 evaluator was instantiated as a 1D periodic loop with kink-based particles and a rich detection stack (Sessions~11--18).\footnote{For a full record see the SESSION\_11–18 master summaries and code in the PR-1 loop repository.}  That program achieved a detailed Standard-Model-like particle catalogue (electrons, quarks, nucleons, baryons) with zone-based braid extraction, validated detectors (COM stability, OTOC chaos, spectral-dimension estimators), and striking hierarchical dimensional signatures at the kink and particle levels.  However, systematic large-scale tests revealed that the entire mask family under study (masks~17,130 with $g_0\neq g_1$) exhibits dimensional \emph{collapse} rather than emergence: the spectral dimension $d_s$ flows downward toward a universal $\approx 2.14$ attractor, contrary to the $d_s$-increasing pattern required for emergent QM/GR.  Subsequent topology and kinematics experiments (collide--stream mechanisms, 2D torus, sphere, Möbius, and chiral drift) established a stronger verdict: on a 1D periodic loop the cyclic ordering of kinks is a topological invariant, and with the conserved winding, twist, and dipole-like quantities this overconstrains motion so that only collective shifts are possible.  PR-1 thus remains in MFRR as a reversible UWCA model and a laboratory for braid-based particle ontology, but the TE$_1$ program ultimately pivoted to PR-0 and DSAC as the primary substrates for emergent kinematics, dimensional flow, and reflexive law.

\subsection{The Reflexive Substrate and SDS Architecture}
\label{subsec:alpha-sds}

For completeness with the companion works (RR, TFTT), we summarize the non-hierarchical substrate on which Reflexive Systems are internalized.

\begin{definition}[Reflexive Substrate \(\alpha\)]
Let \(L\) denote the language-creation functor assigning to a formal system its minimal complete meta-language. The \emph{reflexive substrate} \(\alpha\) is the (maximal) fixed point of \(L\) satisfying
\[
\alpha \;=\; L(\alpha).
\]
Formally, \(\alpha\) is the self-defining ground on which description and meta-description coincide. Within non-well-founded settings (AFA) and categorical fixed-point semantics (Lawvere), such objects are well-formed.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Self-Defining System (SDS)]
An \emph{SDS} is a dynamical system internal to \(\alpha\) whose states and laws are co-instantiated; in the present paper, it is realized as a Reflexive System \(\mathfrak{R}\) internal to the topos \(\mathbf{E}\) with AFA and quotation/evaluation (\cref{asm:regularity}). Thus, our \(\mathbf{E}\) and its admissible fragment \(\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{adm}}\) serve as the internalization of \(\alpha\).
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}
The central closure results of this paper (PSC, \(\PT\), URP) are therefore implemented \emph{inside} \(\alpha\): the \(\PT\) operator is the lawful, non-algorithmic adjudicator available in the reflexive substrate; PSC is the internal availability of a complete, simultaneous self-model; and URP (\cref{sec:URP}) is the global identity condition of the SDS.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Choice Points as Ontological Primitives}
\label{subsec:ontology-choice-points}

\begin{definition}[Choice Points as Ontological Objects]
\label{def:CP-ontological}
A \emph{Choice Point} (\(\mathcal{C}\!P\)) is an internal object of the reflexive topos \(\mathbf{E}\) representing a locus of lawful indeterminacy---a point in the system's state space at which multiple admissible, equally coherent continuations coexist.
Formally, given a dissonance functional \(D:\Man\to\RR_{\ge0}\), a Choice Point is a pair
\[
(\theta^\star,\mathcal{B})
\]
where \(\theta^\star\in\Man\) is a degenerate critical point of \(D\) and \(\mathcal{B}=\{\gamma_i\}_{i\in I}\subset\Gamma_{\mathrm{adm}}\) is the finite set of admissible successor branches such that
\[
\nabla D(\theta^\star)=0,\qquad
\det(\nabla_i\nabla_j D(\theta^\star))=0,
\]
and all branches in \(\mathcal{B}\) satisfy the tie condition
\(D(\gamma_i(t))=D(\gamma_j(t))+o(t)\).
\end{definition}

\paragraph{Ontological role.}
Choice Points are primitive \emph{events} of Reflexive Reality:
\begin{itemize}
  \item They instantiate the system's inherent incompleteness---the loci where law, computation, and geometry meet.
  \item They are not externally imposed perturbations but internal morphisms of the topos \(\mathbf{E}\): each \(\mathcal{C}\!P\) is an object admitting admissible morphisms (branches) into the environment object \(\mathrm{Env}\).
  \item They are the necessary substrate for the \emph{Transputation Operator} \(\PT\), which provides lawful adjudication among the admissible branches.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Hierarchy within the ontology.}
\begin{align*}
&\text{Reflexive Substrate }(\alpha)
\;\longrightarrow\;
\text{Self-Defining System }(\mathfrak{R})
\;\longrightarrow\;
\text{Choice Points }(\mathcal{C}\!P) \\
&\qquad\qquad\qquad
\;\longrightarrow\;
\text{Transputation }(\PT)
\;\longrightarrow\;
\text{Perfect Self-Containment }(\PSC).
\end{align*}
Thus, CPs occupy the ontological stratum between the existence of the system and the operation of its law.

\paragraph{Interpretation.}
Each Choice Point represents an \emph{internal micro-crisis of coherence}:
the moment where Reflexive Reality must decide, from within itself, which branch preserves MDL minimality and coherence.  
They are the universal ``atoms'' of reflexive causation.

\begin{example}[Toy Choice-Point: Two-Dimensional Degenerate Potential]
\label{ex:toy-CP}
Consider the dissonance functional $D(x,y)=x^4+y^4-2x^2y^2$ on the domain $[-1,1]^2$.
This potential exhibits degeneracy along the curves $x=\pm y$, where $D$ has saddle points.
A Choice Point arises at the origin $(0,0)$ where four branches are approximately equivalent:
$\gamma_1=(+\epsilon,+\epsilon)$, $\gamma_2=(-\epsilon,-\epsilon)$, $\gamma_3=(+\epsilon,-\epsilon)$, $\gamma_4=(-\epsilon,+\epsilon)$ for small $\epsilon>0$.

Applying the Transputation operator $\PT$ with MDL complexity penalty $C(x,y)=x^2+y^2$, the combined functional is
\[
L(x,y) = D(x,y) + \lambda C(x,y) = x^4+y^4-2x^2y^2 + \lambda(x^2+y^2).
\]
For $\lambda>0$, the global minima occur at $(\pm 1,0)$ and $(0,\pm 1)$ with $L_{\min}=\lambda$.
The Transputation operator selects one of these four branches via code-order tie-breaking, actualizing (say) $(\pm 1,0)$ and leaving the other three counterfactual.

The energetic cost (Reflexive Landauer) is
\[
\Delta E_{\PT} = k_B T \log 4 + \lambda_\Psi \int_{\mathcal{U}} (\alpha_1\Psi^2 + \alpha_2\|\nabla\Psi\|^2)\,dV,
\]
where the first term accounts for the four-fold degeneracy ($n=4$) and the second term accounts for the coherence field configuration around the CP. For laboratory parameters ($T=300\,$K, $\lambda_\Psi\alpha_1\sim 10^{-6}\,{\rm J·m^{-3}}$, $\mathcal{U}\sim 10^{-15}\,{\rm m}^3$), one estimates $\Delta E_{\PT}\approx 10^{-20}\,$J, measurable via high-precision calorimetry in coherence-rich substrates.
\end{example}

\subsection{Reflexive Systems and Internal Semantics}
\label{subsec:reflexive-systems}
\begin{definition}[Reflexive System]
\label{def:ReflexiveSystem}
A \emph{Reflexive System} is a tuple
\[
\mathfrak{R}=\big(\mathbf{E},\,L,\,\ulcorner\cdot\urcorner,\,\mathrm{eval},\,\mathrm{Env},\,\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{adm}}\big)
\]
such that:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \(\mathbf{E}\) is a Cartesian closed topos with internal language \(L\).
  \item \(\ulcorner\cdot\urcorner\) assigns to each internal expression \(e\in L\) a code \(\ulcorner e\urcorner\in \mathrm{Code}\subset \mathbf{E}\).
  \item \(\mathrm{eval}:\mathrm{Code}\times \mathrm{Env}\to \mathrm{Env}\) interprets admissible codes as endomaps of \(\mathrm{Env}\), i.e.\ for admissible \(c\), there exists \(f_c:\mathrm{Env}\to \mathrm{Env}\) with \(\mathrm{eval}(c,s)=f_c(s)\).
  \item The admissible fragment \(\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{adm}}\) is closed under the constructions needed to internalize the universal evaluator \(U:\mathrm{Code}\times \mathrm{Env}\to \mathrm{Env}\).
\end{enumerate}
We say \(\mathfrak{R}\) is \emph{self-executing} if there exists a (law) code \(c_T=\ulcorner T\urcorner\) such that \(T(s)=\mathrm{eval}(c_T,s)\) for all \(s\in \mathrm{Env}\).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Perfect Self-Containment (\(\PSC\))]
\label{def:PSC}
A state \(S\in \mathrm{Env}\) achieves \emph{Perfect Self-Containment} if there exists an internal \emph{self-model} \(M_S\in \mathrm{Env}\) and an isomorphism \(\phi:M_S\overset{\sim}{\to}\iota(S)\) (for the canonical inclusion \(\iota:\mathrm{Env}\hookrightarrow \mathbf{E}\)) such that the following hold simultaneously (and, in particular, every \(\PSC\) system must internally represent and lawfully resolve its admissible Choice Points, \cref{subsec:ontology-choice-points}):
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Completeness:} \(M_S\) encodes the entire current information state of \(S\) (no external descriptors are required).
  \item \textbf{Consistency:} \(M_S\) is logically consistent in the internal logic of \(\mathbf{E}\) (no paradoxical self-ascription).
  \item \textbf{Non-Lossiness (Isomorphism):} \(\phi\) is an isomorphism of internal structures: no information essential to \(S\) is lost in \(M_S\).
  \item \textbf{Simultaneity/Internality:} \(M_S\) is an internal component of \(S\) and is concurrently accessible at the time of ascription (not merely a historical record).
\end{enumerate}
If a system admits such \(M_S\) for all allowable states \(S\), we say the system is \(\PSC\) (strong \(\PSC\)). If only an admissible endomorphism fragment admits \(\PSC\), we say it is \emph{weak \(\PSC\)}.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Choice Points --- Operational Specification]
\label{def:CP}
We provide here the operational/technical specification of Choice Points, whose ontological status as primitive events was established in \cref{subsec:ontology-choice-points}.

Let \(D:\Man\to \RR_{\ge 0}\) be a dissonance functional (equivalently, minus a coherence functional). A \emph{Choice Point} is a pair \((\theta^\star,\mathcal{B})\) with \(\theta^\star\in \Man\) a critical point of \(D\) and \(\mathcal{B}\) a nontrivial set of admissible outgoing macro-branches \(\{\gamma_i\}\) from \(\theta^\star\) such that:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \emph{Degeneracy:} the Hessian of \(D\) at \(\theta^\star\) has at least one zero (flat) direction corresponding to equally coherent successor branches;
  \item \emph{Admissibility:} each \(\gamma_i\) is generated by an admissible internal evaluator in \(\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{adm}}\);
  \item \emph{Locality:} there exists a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\theta^\star\) in \(\Man\) where branches initially do not separate by value of \(D\) (tie condition), i.e.\ \(D(\gamma_i(t))=D(\gamma_j(t)) + o(t)\).
\end{enumerate}
A \emph{lawful adjudication} at a CP is an internal selection of a single branch \(\gamma_k\) determined by a coherence principle (e.g.\ MDL minimization under constraints).
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Choice Points and the Primordial Loop]
In the companion ontology (RR), Choice Points are the operational loci where the universe's reflexive ground (the ``Primordial Loop'') becomes manifest: locally, as degenerate criticalities of the dissonance functional \(D\); globally, as the necessity of a lawful, non-hierarchical adjudicator (\(\PT\)). The present formalism realizes this by tying CPs to degeneracies on \((\Man,\Fisher)\) and resolving them via \(\PT\) in the admissible fragment, thereby unifying the ontological and geometric views.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Inevitability and Resolution of Choice Points}
\label{subsec:inevitability-choice-points}

\paragraph{Motivation.}
Having defined \emph{Choice Points} (\cref{def:CP}) as degeneracies of the dissonance functional \(D\), we now show that such points are not exceptional but \emph{inevitable}.  They arise wherever the universe's logical, computational, or geometric structures reach a local indeterminacy of coherence.  This section explains (i) why Choice Points must exist in any consistent computable cosmos, (ii) why Standard Computation (SC) cannot resolve them, and (iii) how Reflexive Reality provides the lawful resolution via the \emph{Transputation Operator}~\(\PT\).

\subsubsection{Why Choice Points Are Inevitable}

\paragraph{Logical necessity.}
Gödel's incompleteness and Lawvere's fixed-point theorem jointly ensure that any expressive formal system contains undecidable propositions---internal statements that admit multiple equally consistent continuations.  In the physical semantics of Reflexive Reality, such undecidable states correspond to degenerate critical points of \(D\): the system's internal self-description reaches a tie among equally coherent branches.  Formally, for a CP \((\theta^\star,\mathcal{B})\),
\[
\nabla D(\theta^\star)=0,\qquad 
\det(\nabla_i\nabla_j D(\theta^\star))=0,
\]
so that first-order dynamics vanish and second-order curvature fails to select a unique trajectory.  Logical undecidability thus manifests geometrically as degeneracy of coherence.

\paragraph{Computational necessity.}
Within any Turing-complete substrate (UWCA, reversible circuit, or local Hamiltonian simulator), the halting and Kolmogorov undecidability barriers guarantee states whose future evolution cannot be determined finitely by the evaluator~\(U\).  At such states, multiple admissible successor branches \(\gamma_i\) exist that are locally indistinguishable yet globally inequivalent in coherence.  Hence, computational expressiveness itself ensures the appearance of CPs: wherever the evaluator's predictive radius terminates, adjudication becomes non-computable.

\paragraph{Geometric necessity.}
On the Fisher information manifold \((\Man,\Fisher)\), the same inevitability arises from curvature.  The \emph{Choice–Curvature Correspondence} (\cref{thm:ChoiceCurv}) shows that CP density tracks the positive part of the Ricci curvature, \(\rho_{\mathrm{CP}}\propto(\mathrm{Ric}_F)^+\).  Flat or sign-changing curvature corresponds to degenerate coherence directions; positive curvature marks convergence loci requiring adjudication.  Thus geometry itself enforces that lawful dynamics must periodically encounter non-unique continuation points---the geometric avatar of Gödel–Turing incompleteness.

\paragraph{Tri-convergence.}
Logical, computational, and geometric inevitabilities converge: any universe rich enough to compute and describe itself must confront internal degeneracies.  These are the structural loci where Reflexive Closure demands a lawful, internal act of choice.

\subsubsection{Why Standard Computation Cannot Resolve Them}

\paragraph{Algorithmic limitation.}
Any SC process \(M\in\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{adm}}\) is finitely local and algorithmically decidable.  Emulating \(\PT\) would require \(M\) to compute
\[
\arg\min_{\gamma_i\in\mathcal{B}}\big[D(\gamma_i)+\lambda\,C(\gamma_i)\big],
\]
where \(C(\gamma_i)\) is a code-length (Kolmogorov complexity) penalty.  Because \(K(\cdot)\) is uncomputable, no Turing machine can perform this minimization exactly.  Hence, SC can enumerate branches but not select the MDL-optimal one.

\paragraph{Locality limitation.}
Finite-radius update rules see only local neighborhoods.  Yet \(D\) depends on global correlations and long-range recurrence.  At a CP, branches are locally identical to all orders visible within any finite \(r\); only global coherence distinguishes them.  Therefore no local SC rule can resolve a CP lawfully.

\paragraph{Diagonal limitation.}
Assume an SC emulator \(M\) exists that perfectly reproduces \(\PT\).  Feeding \(M\) its own description as input---\((\ulcorner M\urcorner,\ulcorner M\urcorner)\)---produces the paradoxical self-application ``choose the branch not chosen by yourself,'' reproducing the Gödel–Turing diagonal contradiction.  Thus emulation of \(\PT\) by any SC evaluator is impossible.  Choice Points mark the precise boundary between computability and reflexive law.

\paragraph{Reversibility and the Absence of Intrinsic Choice Points.}
A fully reversible cellular automaton---such as PR-1 with Margolus tiling---cannot generate genuine Choice Points.  
By construction, a reversible automaton defines a bijective global evolution map $U:S_t\!\mapsto\!S_{t+1}$ with a unique inverse $U^{-1}$; every configuration possesses exactly one admissible successor and one admissible predecessor.  
Hence the local Jacobian determinant of the update rule is everywhere nonzero (discrete analogue $\det\nabla U=\pm1$), precluding any degeneracy of admissible continuations.  
The state-transition graph of such a system decomposes into disjoint cyclic orbits with no branching or merging, and therefore no loci of lawful indeterminacy.  
Irreversible automata, by contrast, implement many-to-one local maps that destroy information; multiple distinct neighborhoods evolve to the same successor configuration, giving rise to non-invertible transitions and the possibility of degenerate forward continuations.  
Only in this irreversible regime---or equivalently under an explicit non-computable adjudicator such as the Transputation operator~$\PT$---can true Choice Points arise, since only non-injective dynamics permit multiple lawful futures competing under the coherence functional.  
Reversibility thus forbids the \emph{execution} of Choice Points at the global level: PR-1 realizes the reversible substrate $U$ of the Reflexive law but cannot, by itself, instantiate $\PT$.  
Irreversible field substrates such as PR-0, which minimize the dissonance functional $D$ by gradient descent, naturally generate and resolve executed Choice Points, providing the empirical realization of transputational adjudication.
The formal distinction between latent and executed CPs, and its implications for PR-1's structure, are developed rigorously in Remark~\ref{rem:latentCP}.

\paragraph{PR-0 Field Substrate and Implementation.}
In the validation program we instantiate PR-0 as a complex matter field $\psi$ and real mediator field $\chi$ on a periodic lattice, evolved by a coupled Ablowitz--Ladik plus mediator dynamics that realizes the reversible map $U_{\mathrm{PR\text{-}0}}$ and an internal ontological-dissonance functional $D[\psi,\chi]$.  The functional $D$ is built from local curvature, localization, kinetic, and temporal-coherence terms and is minimized subject to the microscopic equations of motion; different constraint manifolds of $D$ select effective strong, electromagnetic, weak, and gravitational force laws, as developed in the dedicated PR-0 substrate manuscript~\cite{SpivackPR0Substrate}.  The corresponding implementation is provided by the \texttt{pr0\_system} package, which supplies the lattice and field containers, Ablowitz--Ladik integrator, adaptive damping, and a bootstrap layer that searches the space of damping and potential parameters for low-$D$ configurations.\footnote{See the PR-0 code documentation in the \texttt{pr0\_system/} directory for the module layout (\texttt{core}, \texttt{evolution}, \texttt{bootstrap}, \texttt{forces}, \texttt{integration}, \texttt{analysis}) and example scripts.}
TE$_1$.B uses this substrate to validate the reflexive fluctuation equalities and quantify the identification $D\!\equiv\!-\Phi$ (empirical correlation $r\approx-0.91$), while TE$_1$.U builds the Weak Transputational Universality pipeline on top of the same \texttt{pr0\_system} implementation.  In $\Delta$-Machine experiments PR-0 also serves as the field-state backend for DSAC, providing a concrete realization of an irreversible transputational substrate whose macroscopic behavior is governed by $D$-minimization rather than a fixed symbolic rule.

\paragraph{Weak Transputational Universality of PR-0.}
Beyond merely generating Choice Points, the PR-0 field substrate can emulate universal discrete dynamics on compact windows via a guard-banded encode--evolve--decode pipeline.  In particular, TE$_1$.U establishes that PR-0 can realize Rule~110 exactly on finite rings, proving \emph{Weak Transputational Universality} (WTU) for the substrate.

\begin{theorem}[Weak Transputational Universality Theorem (PR-0)]
\label{thm:pr0-wtu}
Let $X_t\in\{0,1\}^N$ be a Rule~110 configuration at macrostep $t$ and define the encoding and decoding maps
\[
\iota(X_t)_i =
\begin{cases}
\mu - \Delta & X_t(i)=0,\\
\mu + \Delta & X_t(i)=1,
\end{cases}
\qquad
\pi(U_t)_i = \mathbf{1}\{\mathrm{median}_3(U_t(i)) > \mu\},
\]
with guard-banded parameters $\mu=0.5$, $\Delta=0.45$ and periodic boundaries on a PR-0 ring.  Implement each macrostep as four PR-0 micro-phases:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=*]
\item \textbf{Sample (S):} optional neighbor mixing with rate $\eta$ (WTU configuration uses $\eta=0$);
\item \textbf{Compute (C):} decode bits $x_j=\pi(U_t)_j$ and apply the exact Rule~110 truth table to obtain $\tilde f(x_{i-1},x_i,x_{i+1})$;
\item \textbf{Inhibit (I):} soft damping toward $\mu$, $U^{(I)}=(1-\gamma)U^{(S)}+\gamma\mu$ (WTU configuration uses $\gamma=0$);
\item \textbf{Commit (K):} write back the new guard-banded state
\[
U_{t+1} = (1-\lambda)\,U^{(I)} + \lambda\big(\mu + (2\tilde f-1)\Delta\big),
\]
with $\lambda=1$.
\end{enumerate}
If $U_0=\iota(X_0)$, then for all $0\le t\le T$ the decoded trajectory satisfies
\[
\pi(U_t)=X_t,
\]
so PR-0 reproduces the Rule~110 space--time diagram exactly on the chosen window.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The guard-banded encoding ensures that, in the pass configuration ($\eta=\gamma=0$, $\lambda=1$), the field values remain confined to $\{\mu-\Delta,\mu+\Delta\}$ after each commit.  The compute phase applies the exact Rule~110 truth table to the decoded bits, and the commit phase writes back the corresponding guard-banded amplitudes.  Since the CA rule depends only on three-bit neighborhoods and the same map is applied uniformly, the invariant $\pi(U_t)=X_t$ is preserved by induction on $t$.  The TE$_1$.U numerical implementation (using the WTU benchmark configuration \texttt{configs/soft\_rule110.yaml}) yields $\varepsilon_{L^2}=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{TV}}=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Hamming}}=0$ on a $256\times256$ window, confirming exact agreement within floating-point precision.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Interpretation of WTU]
The Weak Transputational Universality Theorem shows that PR-0 is \emph{functionally universal} for discrete decision problems that can be expressed as cellular automata on finite windows: any such dynamics can be realized by a physically instantiated encode--evolve--decode loop on the PR-0 field substrate.  In the broader MFRR architecture this means that, even though $\PT$ is not Turing-emulable in general, the universe possesses an internal substrate whose lawful dynamics can reproduce all algorithmically describable discrete decision structures that arise inside it.  WTU is therefore the minimal universality property required for reflexive systems to support general decision-making, error correction, and self-organization on their internal computational substrates.
\end{remark}

\paragraph{WTU Benchmark Metrics.}
The TE$_1$.U benchmark suite further validates the WTU metric pipeline on three surrogate systems using \texttt{analysis/wtu\_encode.py} with configurations \texttt{configs/wtu\_rule110.yaml}, \texttt{configs/wtu\_logistic.yaml}, and \texttt{configs/wtu\_ric.yaml}.  The baseline epsilon metrics and corresponding JSON summaries are:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
\item \textbf{Rule~110 surrogate:} $\varepsilon_{L^2}\approx 0.289$, $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{TV}}\approx 0.143$;
\item \textbf{Logistic surrogate:} $\varepsilon_{L^2}\approx 7.9\times10^{-3}$, spectral coherence $\approx 0.997$;
\item \textbf{RIC surrogate (TE$_1$.F):} $\varepsilon_{L^2}\approx 5.4\times10^{-3}$, AUC shift $\Delta\mathrm{AUC}\approx2.4\times10^{-3}$, calibration error $\approx 8.9\times10^{-3}$.
\end{itemize}
The PR-0 ``soft'' Rule~110 runner (\path{analysis/soft_rule110_runner.py} with \path{configs/soft_rule110.yaml}) achieves $\varepsilon_{L^2}=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{TV}}=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Hamming}}=0$, establishing Weak Transputational Universality on compact windows.  A separate TE$_1$.U Track~B attempt to embed Rule~110 directly into generic PR-0 soliton dynamics yields large residuals ($\varepsilon_{L^2}\sim 6.9\times10^2$), indicating that full PR-0 strong universality requires a dedicated encoding of the CA rule or a shared observable projection.  For strong transputational advantage on TPU-class workloads, see the TE$_2$.U TPU-C baseline (Theorem~\ref{thm:te2u_advantage}).

\subsubsection{How Reflexive Reality Resolves Them}

\paragraph{The Transputation Operator.}
Reflexive Reality introduces a lawful but non-SC operator
\[
\PT:\mathcal{C}\!P_{\mathrm{adm}}\to\Gamma_{\mathrm{adm}},\qquad
\PT(\theta^\star,\mathcal{B})
=\arg\min_{\gamma_i\in\mathcal{B}}\!\big[D(\gamma_i)+\lambda\,C(\gamma_i)\big],
\]
which performs \emph{global coherence adjudication}.  Internally, this arg-min is guaranteed by finite internal choice (Lemma~\ref{lem:coherence-order}) and realized as a natural transformation in the topos semantics (\cref{app:proof-PT-PSC}).  \(\PT\) is lawful, unique up to code-order tie-breaking, and exists even though it is not Turing-computable.

\paragraph{Energetic signature.}
Each adjudication incurs a measurable energetic cost:
\[
\Delta E_{\PT} \ge k_B T\log n
+\lambda_\Psi\!\int\!(\alpha_1\Psi^2+\alpha_2\|\nabla\Psi\|^2)dV,
\]
the \emph{Reflexive Landauer inequality} (\cref{thm:RefLandauer-rigorous}).  The first term expresses logical irreversibility; the second encodes geometric coherence maintenance.  Transputation thus bridges information, energy, and geometry.\footnote{In laboratory and cosmological calibrations the coherence coefficients $(\lambda_\Psi,\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$ are extremely large in conventional units (e.g.\ an effective prefactor $\alpha_0\sim 10^{58}\,{\rm m}^2$ for cosmological coherence shells), reflecting the fact that even tiny fractional changes in global coherence correspond to macroscopic energetic rebalancings.  Throughout this work we keep the bound in symbolic form and treat concrete magnitudes via the calibration routes described in the cosmology and DSAC sections, so that back-of-the-envelope estimates remain consistent with the underlying normalization.}

\paragraph{Geometric interpretation.}
On \((\Man,\Fisher)\), each \(\PT\)-act restores curvature minimality by selecting the path that maximizes global coherence.  Locally, \(\PT\) adds a nonlocal correction to the MDL gradient flow, steering the system through flat saddles toward renewed coherence.  In differential form,
\[
\delta\theta_{\PT} = -\,\Fisher^{-1}\!\nabla D_{\mathrm{global}}.
\]

\paragraph{Categorical semantics.}
Within the topos \(\mathbf{E}\), the existence of \(\PT\) follows from internal finite choice and AFA coinduction: a lawful adjudicator exists, is unique, and maintains consistency.  Thus Reflexive Reality closes the circle: what logic and computation cannot decide, category theory guarantees to exist as an internal morphism.

\subsection{Phase II.A: Curvature--Dissonance--Entropy Invariant}
\label{subsec:phase-II-curvature-invariant}

Following the Phase~I validation that established DSAC as a reflexive symbolic regressor capable of recovering known laws to machine precision, we now demonstrate its ability to discover \emph{new} invariants from live field dynamics.  The first Phase~II experiment targets a relation between the metric-residual curvature, local ontological dissonance, and entropy density within the DSAC lattice.

\subsubsection{Experimental Configuration}

We instrumented the metric-closure scenario (\path{scenarios/discovery_phase2/curvature_invariant.yaml}) to track three key observables at each lattice site $x$:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Curvature proxy} $\mathcal{R}(x)$: derived from the metric-closure residual
  \[
    \mathcal{R}(x) \equiv \chi(x) - 0.25\bigl(\psi_r(x)^2 + \psi_i(x)^2\bigr) - 0.15\,\chi(x)^3 + 0.1\,\dot{\chi}(x),
  \]
  spatially smoothed (Gaussian radius 2) and temporally averaged over a 200-sample exponential window to suppress lattice noise.
  \item \textbf{Local dissonance} $D(x) = \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{local}}(x)$: per-site ontological dissonance computed from the field gradients and constraint residuals.
  \item \textbf{Entropy density} $E(x) = S(x)$: local information/entropy measure derived from field magnitude and phase coherence.
\end{itemize}

The discovery pipeline employed a dimensionless feature basis including ratios ($\mathcal{R}/D$, $\mathcal{R}/|E|$, $\mathcal{R}/\sqrt{D^2+E^2}$), polynomial terms ($D$, $E$, $D^2$, $E^2$, $DE$), and logarithmic combinations ($\ln D$, $\ln|E|$).  No external supervision or prior regularization was applied; the optional \texttt{discovery\_prior} block remained disabled to avoid biasing the fit.  Sampling occurred after a 4000-step burn-in period at 50-step intervals, with only quasi-stationary snapshots (verification streak $\geq 80$) included in the least-squares regression.

\subsubsection{DSAC-Discovered Invariant}

An ensemble of 20 independent runs (16\,000 steps each, 9 workers per run) converged to a consistent invariant relation.  All runs achieved \texttt{discovery\_verified = 1} with residual RMS $3.34\times 10^{-3} \pm 4.6\times 10^{-5}$ and invariant variance $1.12\times 10^{-5} \pm 3.0\times 10^{-7}$.  The ensemble-averaged coefficients (with dispersion $<10\%$ of magnitude) yield the following near-zero residual condition:
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
\mathcal{R} - 0.708\,\frac{\mathcal{R}}{D} - 0.000004\,\frac{\mathcal{R}}{|E|} + 0.141\,\frac{\mathcal{R}}{\sqrt{D^2+E^2}} \\
{}+ 0.281 D + 0.205 E - 0.148 D^2 - 0.095 E^2 - 0.351 D E \\
{}+ 0.085\ln(D) + 0.0011\ln|E| - 0.059 \approx 0.
\end{split}
\label{eq:curvature-dissonance-entropy-invariant}
\end{equation}
The consistency of coefficients across all 20 seeds (see the CSV summary \path{curvature_invariant_production.csv}) indicates that DSAC uncovered a single robust invariant rather than multiple disjoint candidates.  The relation ties the metric-residual curvature to both the magnitude and mixed products of the dissonance and entropy fields, validating the holographic intuition that boundary observables ($D$, $E$) govern the effective bulk curvature term $\mathcal{R}$.

Collecting the curvature terms in \eqref{eq:curvature-dissonance-entropy-invariant} yields a factorised form
\begin{equation}
\alpha(D,E)\,\mathcal{R} + \beta(D,E) \approx 0,
\label{eq:curvature-factorized}
\end{equation}
with
\begin{align}
\alpha(D,E) &= 1 - \frac{0.708}{D} - \frac{4\times 10^{-6}}{|E|} + \frac{0.141}{\sqrt{D^2 + E^2}}, \\
\beta(D,E) &= 0.281 D + 0.205 E - 0.148 D^2 - 0.095 E^2 - 0.351 D E \nonumber\\
           &\quad + 0.085\ln D + 0.0011\ln|E| - 0.059.
\end{align}
This factorization makes explicit that $\mathcal{R}$ is constrained to lie on a two-dimensional manifold in $(D,E)$-space,
\begin{equation}
\mathcal{R}(D,E) = -\frac{\beta(D,E)}{\alpha(D,E)},
\label{eq:R-DE-full}
\end{equation}
with $\alpha(D,E) > 0.74$ across the ensemble, ensuring that the relation is well-conditioned and not dominated by near-singular ratios.

\subsubsection{Reduced Boundary-Only Surrogate}

For analytic work it is convenient to compress \eqref{eq:R-DE-full} onto a simpler basis that depends only on $D$ and $E$ without explicit curvature ratios.  To this end we introduced a dedicated refit tool (\texttt{DSAC\_tools/fit\_curvature\_invariant.py}) that ingests archived run tensors, reconstructs $(D,E,\mathcal{R})$ with the same smoothing discipline, and solves a least-squares problem over a reduced polynomial+log feature set:
\[
\{\;D,\;E,\;D^2,\;E^2,\;DE,\;\ln D,\;\ln|E|,\;1\;\}.
\]
Running this refit over the 20 production runs with 10\% lattice subsampling (maximum 200\,000 samples) yields the boundary-only surrogate
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
\mathcal{R} \approx -0.1940\,D + 0.1473\,E - 0.0569\,D^2 - 0.00787\,E^2 \\
\qquad\qquad {}- 0.0566\,D E - 0.00611\,\ln D - 2.2\times 10^{-5}\,\ln|E| + 0.00162,
\end{split}
\label{eq:R-DE-reduced}
\end{equation}
with diagnostics
\[
\mathrm{RMS}(|\mathcal{R} - \hat{\mathcal{R}}|) = 8.5\times 10^{-4}, \qquad
\frac{\sqrt{\langle (\mathcal{R} - \hat{\mathcal{R}})^2\rangle}}{\sqrt{\langle \mathcal{R}^2\rangle}} \approx 4.76\times 10^{-3},
\]
and full column rank of the feature matrix.  Thus the reduced surrogate reproduces the invariant to better than $0.5\%$ relative RMS error across the ensemble, while eliminating all curvature-ratio features and expressing $\mathcal{R}$ entirely as a boundary functional $F(D,E)$.

Linearising \eqref{eq:R-DE-reduced} around the ensemble means $\langle D\rangle$, $\langle E\rangle$ (with $\tilde D = D/\langle D\rangle$ and $\hat E = (E - \langle E\rangle)/\sigma_E$) shows that curvature is chiefly controlled by a weighted difference between relative dissonance and entropy fluctuations, with a small cross-term providing the leading nonlinearity:
\begin{equation}
\mathcal{R} \approx 0.0304 - 0.147\,\tilde D + 0.0592\,\hat E - 0.0129\,\tilde D\,\hat E + \mathcal{O}\bigl((\tilde D - 1)^2,\hat E^2\bigr).
\end{equation}

\subsubsection{Theorem and Interpretation}

\begin{theorem}[Reflexive Curvature--Dissonance--Entropy Law (numerical form)]
\label{thm:reflexive-curvature-dissonance-entropy}
Let a metric-closure DSAC run satisfy:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item a steady-state regime after a burn-in of at least 4000 steps with verification streak $\geq 80/80$;
  \item spatial smoothing of radius 2 and exponential temporal averaging over 200 samples applied uniformly to $\mathcal{R}$, $D$, and $E$;
  \item positive entropy density in the measurement window.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a functional $F(D,E)$ such that
\begin{equation}
\frac{\sqrt{\big\langle\big(\mathcal{R} - F(D,E)\big)^2\big\rangle}}{\sqrt{\langle \mathcal{R}^2 \rangle}} \;\le\; \varepsilon,
\end{equation}
with
\[
\varepsilon \lesssim 10^{-2} \quad \text{for the full DSAC invariant } F = -\beta/\alpha,
\]
and
\[
\varepsilon \lesssim 4.8\times 10^{-3} \quad \text{for the reduced polynomial+log surrogate $F(D,E)$ in \eqref{eq:R-DE-reduced}}.
\]
Here $\langle \cdot \rangle$ denotes spatial averaging over the lattice and ensemble averaging over runs.  In other words, curvature is determined by boundary dissonance and entropy up to a controlled relative error set by the DSAC smoothing discipline and solver tolerance.
\end{theorem}

Equations~\eqref{eq:curvature-dissonance-entropy-invariant}, \eqref{eq:R-DE-full}, and \eqref{eq:R-DE-reduced} together represent the first Phase~II discovery: a new MFRR invariant derived entirely from DSAC's reflexive dynamics.  The nonlinear coupling between curvature, dissonance, and entropy supports the holographic principle that boundary information (encoded in $D$ and $E$) constrains bulk geometry (encoded in $\mathcal{R}$).  In particular, the reduced boundary-only form \eqref{eq:R-DE-reduced} shows that, after appropriate smoothing, curvature behaves as a low-complexity functional of dissonance and entropy with controlled error.  This theorem provides the empirical core of the analytic derivation sketched above and supplies the Phase~II curvature invariant referenced in the computational holography and PSC discussions.

\subsection{Phase II.B: Reflexive PR-0 Transport Law}
\label{subsec:phase-II-pr0-transport}

Building on the curvature invariant of Phase~II.A, we next target the coarse-grained transport behaviour of PR-0 ensembles.  In this experiment DSAC operates in ``freeze-field'' replay mode, consuming precomputed density $\rho$, damping $\gamma$, gradients, and coarse-grained acceleration $\dot{\rho}$ tensors captured from the PR-0 runtime.  All observables are smoothed over a five-frame window, sampled every ten PR-0 steps, and centred to remove mean offsets.

\subsubsection{Feature Basis and Regression Policy}

The discovery scenario (\texttt{scenarios/discovery\_phase2/pr0\_transport.yaml}) uses a dimensionless reduced basis
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{red}} = \{&\rho',\; \nabla^2\rho,\; \gamma',\; \nabla^2\gamma,\; \|\nabla\rho\|_{\mathrm{norm}},\; \gamma_{\mathrm{norm}},\; 1\},
\end{align*}
where primes denote centred fields ($\phi' = \phi - \langle\phi\rangle$) and ``norm'' quantities divide by their RMS to ensure dimensionless coefficients.  DSAC accumulates $X^\top X$ and $X^\top y$ on the Python side and solves every ten steps with a ridge penalty $\lambda = 10^{-9}$.

\subsubsection{DSAC Discovery Result}

Across 15 long-run seeds per regime (baseline, high-drive, asymmetric; 8000 DSAC steps each) the solver converges to
\begin{equation}
\dot{\rho} = -\nabla\cdot\bigl(0.113\,\nabla\rho - 0.056\,\nabla\gamma\bigr) + S(\rho,\gamma,\nabla\rho) + \varepsilon,
\label{eq:pr0-transport-law}
\end{equation}
where the affine source term is
\begin{equation}
S = -0.113\,\rho' + 0.985\,\gamma' - 0.108\,\gamma_{\mathrm{norm}} - 0.004\,\|\nabla\rho\|_{\mathrm{norm}} + 0.076,
\label{eq:pr0-source-term}
\end{equation}
and the residual satisfies
\[
\|\varepsilon\|_{\mathrm{RMS}} \le 6.4\times 10^{-1}, \qquad \mathrm{MAPE}_{95\%} \le 1.0, \qquad \text{verification streak} \ge 8000
\]
for every seed and regime.  These coefficients agree with the reduced surrogate fit reported in the Phase~II.B results note and remain stable (variation $<10\%$) across regimes.

\subsubsection{Flux Decomposition Diagnostics}

To verify the Laplacian contribution, we reconstruct the effective flux
\[
J = 0.113\,\nabla\rho - 0.056\,\nabla\gamma
\]
using the analysis tool \texttt{DSAC\_tools/analyze\_pr0\_transport\_flux.py}.  Five evenly spaced samples per regime yield the statistics in Table~\ref{tab:pr0-flux-diagnostics}: flux RMS remains an order of magnitude below the additive source, demonstrating that the Laplacian term captures the diffusive envelope while the affine drift handles boundary forcing.  Trimmed ($95\%$) MAPE remains below unity, consistent with the ensemble aggregates.

\subsubsection{Theorem and Interpretation}

\begin{theorem}[Reflexive PR-0 Transport]
\label{thm:reflexive-pr0-transport}
Within the metric-closure replay ensembles configured by \texttt{scenarios/discovery\_phase2/pr0\_transport\_longrun.yaml}, the coarse-grained density $\rho$, damping field $\gamma$, and temporal increment $\dot{\rho}$ obey the effective transport law \eqref{eq:pr0-transport-law} with coefficients bounded by $\pm 10\%$ across baseline, high-drive, and asymmetric regimes.  The residual error satisfies $\|\varepsilon\|_{\mathrm{RMS}} \le 6.4\times 10^{-1}$ and $\mathrm{MAPE}_{95\%} \le 1.0$ in all three regimes.  Consequently the Laplacian coefficients generalise across forcings, providing a regime-agnostic effective transport law for PR-0.
\end{theorem}

The Laplacian coefficient $0.113$ matches the effective diffusivity extracted from TE$_1$ transport experiments, while the damping-gradient term parallels the mobility factor multiplying external forcing in Green--Kubo/Crooks-style relations.  The large positive response to $\gamma'$ corroborates the TE$_1$ picture that dissonance-driven drift dominates PR-0 transport.  Together with the curvature invariant of \cref{subsec:phase-II-curvature-invariant}, this law completes the Phase~II.B program: DSAC not only recovers known transport structure but discovers a stable, regime-invariant coarse-grained transport law on PR-0 ensembles.

\subsection{Phase I: DSAC Rediscovery Benchmarks}
\label{subsec:phase-I-rediscovery}

Before turning DSAC loose on new laws, Phase~I calibrated it as a reflexive symbolic regressor on problems with known ground truth.  Three rediscovery benchmarks establish that, when the target law lies in the hypothesis class, DSAC recovers it to floating-point precision across independent seeds.

\paragraph{Analytic Polynomial + Logarithm Law.}
In the ``frozen lattice'' configuration (\path{scenarios/discovery_phase1/polynomial_law.yaml}) the fields are held static on a synthetic truth surface implementing a mixed polynomial+logarithm expression $\chi=f(\psi_r,\psi_i)$.  The Phase~I ensemble (10 seeds, 6000 steps, 9 workers; CSV \path{runs/discovery_phase1/polynomial_ensemble.csv}) achieves residual RMS $(8.58\pm0.97)\times 10^{-16}$ and coefficient RMS errors $1.4\times10^{-15}$ (max $5.1\times10^{-15}$), with 60/60 verification streaks on all runs.  All linear, quadratic, cubic, mixed, log, and bias coefficients match the analytic truth within femto-scale tolerances, showing that DSAC's discovery error is limited by double-precision rounding rather than the reflexive dynamics.

\paragraph{TE\texorpdfstring{$_1$}{1} Jarzynski Rediscovery.}
The second benchmark feeds DSAC an archived TE$_1$.B reflexive statistical mechanics dataset (\path{TE_1.B_RSM/results/run_20251113_183804/jarzynski.json}) via the scenario \path{discovery_phase1/te1_jarzynski.yaml} in frozen-lattice mode.  Each lattice sample carries $(T,\sigma,\mu,\log\langle e^{-\Delta S}\rangle)$, and the feature basis includes quadratic and cross terms in $(T,\sigma,\mu)$ so that any hidden parameter dependence of the Jarzynski equality could be expressed.  Over 10 seeds $\times$ 6000 steps, DSAC recovers $\log\langle e^{-\Delta S}\rangle \approx 0$ with residual RMS $6.2\times10^{-17}$, coefficient RMS error $4.1\times10^{-14}$, and max coefficient error $6.2\times10^{-14}$, with 40/40 verification streaks for every run (\path{runs/discovery_phase1/te1_jarzynski_ensemble.csv}).  Within the explored TE$_1$ parameter range, DSAC therefore finds no spurious parametric drift: the invariant is a constant as predicted.

\paragraph{PR-0 Flux Rediscovery.}
The third benchmark applies the same architecture to PR-0 observer data in a diffusion test based on the ``soft'' Rule~110 configuration.  The scenario \path{discovery_phase1/pr0_flux.yaml} ingests the PR-0 CSV log (\path{.../results/wtu/rule110/pr0_output.csv} under \texttt{TE\_1.U}) and exposes a feature set \{\texttt{density\_delta}, \texttt{damping\_flux}, \texttt{gamma\_mean}, bias\} with truth relation
\[
\texttt{damping\_flux} + \kappa\,\texttt{density\_delta} = 0,\qquad \kappa=50.
\]
The Phase~I ensemble (10 seeds, 6000 steps, 9 workers; see \texttt{pr0\_flux\_ensemble.csv} in the run artifacts) achieves residual RMS $1.9\times10^{-13}$, coefficient RMS error $4.1\times10^{-14}$, and max coefficient error $9.4\times10^{-14}$, with 40/40 verification streaks for all runs.  DSAC precisely recovers the flux-closure coefficients, verifying that the discovery stack works on PR-0 observer outputs as cleanly as on analytic and TE$_1$ datasets and setting the stage for the Phase~II transport law of \cref{subsec:phase-II-pr0-transport}.

\paragraph{Conclusion.}
Choice Points are not exceptional; they are the unavoidable loci where self-consistency meets incompleteness. \subsection{Equivalence of Transputation and Perfect Self-Containment}
\label{subsec:pt-psc}
We now formalize the central equivalence between lawful adjudication (\(\PT\)) and \(\PSC\). Intuitively, \(\PSC\) implies that the system can, from within, represent and lawfully resolve its own degeneracies; conversely, the presence of a lawful internal adjudicator suffices to build a complete, simultaneous, non-lossy self-model.

\begin{theorem}[Equivalence \(\PT\leftrightarrow\PSC\)]
\label{thm:PTPSC}
In a Reflexive System \(\mathfrak{R}\) satisfying \cref{asm:regularity}, the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \(\mathfrak{R}\) is \(\PSC\) (strong) in the sense of \cref{def:PSC}.
  \item \(\mathfrak{R}\) implements lawful \(\PT\) for all admissible Choice Points in the sense of \cref{def:CP}: there exists an internal adjudicator that, from within \(\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{adm}}\), selects a unique successor branch consistent with the global coherence principle and the internal evaluator.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof outline]
The full proof is given in Appendix~\ref{app:proof-PT-PSC}. We sketch the key ideas here.

\textbf{Direction (\(\PSC \Rightarrow \PT\)):} Assume \(\PSC\). For any state \(S\) with self-model \(M_S\), any admissible CP \((\theta^\star,\mathcal{B})\) reachable from \(S\) is internally represented in \(M_S\). Since \(M_S\) is complete, consistent, and simultaneous, it must contain a lawful internal selector on the finite branch set \(\mathcal{B}\). Using finite internal choice and MDL-coherence ordering (Lemma~\ref{lem:coherence-order} in the appendix), we construct an internal adjudication map \(\mathcal{A}\) that minimizes \(D(\gamma)+\lambda C(\gamma)\) over \(\mathcal{B}\), breaking ties by code order. Define \(\PT \equiv \mathcal{A}\). This \(\PT\) is internal, total, and lawful; note that it need not lie in \(\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{adm}}\) (the computable fragment).

\textbf{Direction (\(\PT \Rightarrow \PSC\)):} Assume lawful \(\PT\) exists (internal but not necessarily computable). Using AFA, construct a guarded corecursive self-model \(M_S\) via the operator \(\mathcal{F}(X) = (S, \mathrm{eval}(c_T,X), \PT(\mathrm{CP}(X)))\). AFA guarantees a greatest fixed point \(M_S\) with \(\mathcal{F}(M_S)=M_S\). This \(M_S\) satisfies all four \(\PSC\) clauses: it is complete (encodes \(S\) and all lawful successors), consistent (guarded corecursion + AFA prevents regress), non-lossy (coinductive isomorphism \(\phi:M_S\to\iota(S)\)), and simultaneous/internal (fixed point in \(\mathbf{E}\)).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Uniqueness of Lawful Adjudication]
\label{cor:uniquenessPT}
Under the regularity assumptions of \cref{asm:regularity}, any two internal adjudicators \(\PT_1,\PT_2\) that respect the same coherence/MDL principle and use the same code tie-breaking order agree on all admissible CPs, hence are equal as internal morphisms in \(\mathbf{E}\). See Appendix~\ref{app:proof-PT-PSC} for the complete argument.
\end{corollary}

\begin{lemma}[Total measurable adjudicator]
\label{lem:MeasurablePT}
Let $(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{B})$ be a standard Borel state space internal to $E$ and let 
$B:\mathcal{S}\rightrightarrows\Gamma_{\mathrm{adm}}$ assign to each $s\in\mathcal{S}$ 
a nonempty, finite or compact branch set $B(s)$ with Borel graph. 
Assume the MDL-coherence functional $F:\Gamma_{\mathrm{adm}}\to\mathbb{R}$ is lower semicontinuous 
and the instrument foliation is Borel. 
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item There exists a Borel selector 
${\rm PT}:\mathcal{S}\to\Gamma_{\mathrm{adm}}$ satisfying 
${\rm PT}(s)\in\arg\min_{\gamma\in B(s)}F(\gamma)$ for all $s$ (Kuratowski–Ryll-Nardzewski).
\item If $F$ is $\alpha$-Hölder on each $B(s)$ and the correspondence is outer semicontinuous, 
then ${\rm PT}$ is locally $\alpha$-Hölder almost everywhere.
\item If each $F|_{B(s)}$ is strongly convex with uniform modulus $\mu>0$, then ${\rm PT}$ is locally Lipschitz with constant $L_{\rm PT}\le\mu^{-1}$ on each stratum.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By the Kuratowski–Ryll–Nardzewski measurable selection theorem, every 
lower semicontinuous compact-valued map with Borel graph admits a measurable selector. 
Hölder stability follows from the regularity of $F$ and continuity of minimizers.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Gauge invariance of observables under code reordering]
\label{prop:PT-gauge-invariance}
Let $\pi$ be any admissible permutation of $\mathrm{Code}$ that preserves MDL monotonicity. 
Then for any observable $\mathcal{O}$ derived from ${\rm PT}$, 
$\mathcal{O}({\rm PT}) = \mathcal{O}({\rm PT}_\pi)$. 
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Since $\pi$ acts within MDL-equivalence classes and $F$ is invariant under such reparameterizations, 
the argmin defining ${\rm PT}$ is stable, preserving observable outcomes.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
Hence PT is unique modulo admissible representation, and all physical observables are gauge-invariant under code reordering.
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Internal Provability and Reflexive Semantics]
\label{cor:internaltruth}
If \(\mathfrak{R}\) is \(\PSC\) and implements \(\PT\), then there exists an internal provability predicate \(\Box\) for admissible endomaps that is stable under admissible reindexing (a Lawvere/AFA fixed-point semantics), consistent with the evaluator \(U\), and satisfying the Hilbert--Bernays--Löb derivability conditions (Section~\ref{subsec:RR-Loeb-prov}).
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Semantic Self--Interpretation]
\label{thm:semantic_closure}
Let $\mathbf{E}$ be the reflexive topos used to model the PSC universe, equipped with:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item An internal quotation map $\ulcorner \cdot \urcorner : L \to \mathrm{Code}$ for its internal
        language $L$;
  \item An evaluation morphism $\mathrm{eval}:\mathrm{Code}\times \mathrm{Env}\to \mathrm{Env}$
        realizing admissible codes as endomaps of the environment;
  \item An effective admissible fragment (e.g.\ the effective topos $\mathbf{Eff}$) capturing
        partial recursive dynamics;
  \item An internal truth/ provability predicate $\Box$ on admissible propositions satisfying the
        usual derivability conditions in the reflexive fragment.
\end{enumerate}
Then the universe is semantically closed in the following sense:
\begin{itemize}
  \item Every admissible law, state, and PT-induced adjudication can be encoded as an internal
        object and evaluated inside $\mathbf{E}$;
  \item No external meta-language or meta-truth predicate is required to interpret any admissible
        physical statement or law.
\end{itemize}
In particular, the semantics of UGP/GTE dynamics, SRRG flows, and PT events are all internally
representable and interpretable within the same reflexive category.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The existence of quotation and evaluation internalizes the syntax and execution of laws; the
effective fragment ensures that all computable dynamics are representable as morphisms; and the
internal truth predicate, together with PSC and the PT$\leftrightarrow$PSC equivalence, guarantees
that the system can assign internal truth values and consistency checks to its own descriptions.
Lawvere-style fixed points and Löb-type provability within the reflexive topos then show that
semantics---``what the laws and states mean''---is fully internal to $\mathbf{E}$: every admissible
law, state, and adjudication has an internal representation and interpretation, and no external
meta-semantics are required to complete PSC.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Interpretation and Scope}
\label{subsec:interpretation}
The equivalence \(\PT\leftrightarrow\PSC\) positions \(\PT\) as the precise mathematical mechanism that allows a universe to be fully self-contained: from within, the system can represent itself, detect degeneracies of its predictive manifold, and lawfully resolve them in accordance with a global coherence (MDL) principle. This result:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Links Logic and Dynamics.} The logical closure problem (self-reference) is solved by a dynamical law (\(\PT\)) rather than an external meta-theory.
  \item \textbf{Consolidates TFT and RR.} TFT's adjudication operator is necessary and sufficient for RR's \(\PSC\) postulate; conversely, RR's requirement of \(\PSC\) demands a \(\PT\)-like mechanism.
  \item \textbf{Prepares Geometry and Physics.} The internal availability of \(\PT\) enables coherent evolution on \((\Man,\Fisher)\), and later sections will quantify the energetic and geometric signatures (Reflexive Landauer, Choice--Curvature, \(\Psifield\), \(\Cten\)).
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Observation as lawful information exchange.}
Throughout, ``observation'' denotes an internal, lawful transfer of information within the reflexive topos, not a psychological notion.
An observer is any subsystem that implements admissible evaluation and participates in PT-mediated selection.
All results depend only on information-geometric structure (Fisher metric, MDL), not on anthropic assumptions.

\subsection{$\Lambda\Omega$ Reflexive Equivalence and Perfect Self--Containment}
\label{subsec:lambda-omega-equivalence}

\begin{theorem}[$\Lambda\Omega$ Reflexive Equivalence]
\label{thm:LambdaOmegaEquivalence}
Let the \emph{Universal Generative Principle} (UGP/GTE)~\cite{SpivackUGPFormalization,ugp-lean} define the computable substrate 
through a sequence of canonical $\Lambda$--operations, and let the \emph{$Z$--hypercomplex recurrence}
represent the uncomputable self--closure through $\Omega$--operations of the form
\[
Z = \Lambda + j\,\Omega, \qquad (2\pi\Lambda)^2 + g(\Omega)^2 = (m\pi)^2,\quad m\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}.
\]
Then $\Lambda$ and $\Omega$ are dual projections of a single SU(2) rotation in information--space:
\[
\mathcal{U}(m) = e^{\,i\,2\pi\Lambda + j\,g(\Omega)} \in SU(2),
\]
such that the $\Lambda$--axis generates the deterministic law (computable dynamics) 
and the $\Omega$--axis enforces the reflexive closure (self--description).
Therefore the partial differential equation emerging from $\Lambda$
already satisfies its own reflexive closure under $\Omega$,
\[
\partial_t \Phi(\Lambda) = \mathcal{L}_{\Lambda}\Phi 
\;\Longleftrightarrow\;
\mathcal{R}_{\Omega}\,\Phi = 0.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{remark}[Relation to Transputation and PSC]
\label{rem:TransputationRelation}
Transputation (PT) expresses the \emph{process} by which execution and evaluation coincide;
$\Lambda\Omega$ Equivalence expresses the \emph{structure} of that process as an SU(2) closure.
This unifies prior PSC demonstrations (thermodynamic, informational, geometric) under one algebraic symmetry.
The discrete harmonics $m=1,2,3$ act as eigen--choices of a self--referential phase (micro $\Lambda$, meso $\Lambda\Omega$, macro $\Lambda\Omega\Lambda$). 
The TE$_1$.K validation confirms that the $\Lambda$ backbone already saturates the PDE (no $\Omega$--side tweak is needed numerically), establishing that the $Z_2$ synthesis is \emph{conceptual closure} (self--verification) rather than a dial for fit-tuning; the complete derivation and computational validation follow the TE$_1$.K report.

\subsection{The Self-Computation Principle and Reflexive Completeness}
\label{subsec:scp}

\begin{definition}[Self-Computation Principle (SCP)]
\label{def:scp}
A reflexive theory $S$ satisfies the
\emph{Self-Computation Principle}
if it internally contains the resources required
to derive and verify its own governing law.
The violation of this principle introduces a
\emph{self-computation penalty} $C_{\mathrm{SCP}}[S]\!>\!0$
within the SRRG cost functional $C_\Lambda[S]$
(cf.\ \cref{def:srrg}).
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Vanishing CSCP at Reflexive Closure]
\label{prop:CSCPzero}
For any system achieving both Perfect Self-Containment (PSC)
and lawful adjudication (\(\PT\)),
the self-computation penalty vanishes,
$C_{\mathrm{SCP}}[S]=0$.
Such a system represents a fixed point of the SRRG flow
(\cref{eq:srrg-flow})
and a minimal description-length realization of Reflexive Reality.
\end{proposition}

\paragraph{Interpretation.}
The SCP converts the philosophical statement
``the universe computes itself''
(\cite{SpivackSelfDefiningUniverse,SpivackRR})
into a quantitative selection rule:
only theories that perform their own verification
satisfy PSC and remain stable under SRRG evolution
(\cref{thm:srrg-monotonicity}).
This establishes a direct link between computational self-sufficiency
and physical stability.

\begin{theorem}[Existence and (Essential) Uniqueness of the PSC Self-Model]
\label{thm:PSC-unique}
Let $\Eff$ be the effective topos and suppose the \emph{guarded} endofunctor
\[
\mathcal{F}(X)\;=\;\big(S,\; \eval(\ulcorner T\urcorner,X),\; \PT(\mathrm{CP}(X))\big)
\]
on the category of $\Eff$-objects is well-defined (the guard is the $\eval$ application). Then there exists a greatest fixed point $M_S$ with $\mathcal{F}(M_S)=M_S$. Moreover, $M_S$ is unique up to isomorphism among fixed points of $\mathcal{F}$: if $\mathcal{F}(Y)=Y$ then $Y\simeq M_S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Guarded corecursion in the presence of AFA (anti-foundation) yields a final coalgebra for $\mathcal{F}$; see Aczel \cite{Aczel1988} and standard coalgebra texts. Existence follows by finality. Essential uniqueness follows from the universal property of the final coalgebra: any coalgebra morphism into the final one is unique, implying all fixed points are isomorphic to $M_S$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Limitations \& Scope}
\label{subsec:limitations}

\paragraph{Model predictions and parameter bounds.}
The predictions for gravitational-wave polarization mixing, singularity avoidance, and the coherence--radiation equivalence ($L=A$) are \emph{derived model predictions} subject to the couplings $(\lambda_\Psi,\alpha_{1,2})$ remaining within positivity bounds. These are proposed tests, not established observations. The coherence-induced curvature perturbations are $\sim 10^{-33}$ fractional mass density, well below current and near-future detectability thresholds. Any $|w_a| \lesssim 0.05$ signal should therefore be interpreted as a possible \emph{second-order} drift correlated with information-density evolution, not as a deviation from the leading-order prediction $w_a \approx 0$ confirmed by the FRW+$\Psi$ runs.
