\section{Transputation Theory and the No-Emulation Barrier}
\label{sec:transputation}

\paragraph{Section summary.}
We define the Transputation operator $\PT$ as the lawful MDL-minimizing adjudicator at Choice Points, prove it cannot be emulated by standard computation (No-Emulation theorem), and derive the Reflexive Landauer bound linking logical irreversibility to geometric coherence cost.

\subsection{Definition of the Transputation Operator}
\label{subsec:PT-operator}

\begin{definition}[Admissible and Internal Morphisms]
\label{def:admissible-internal}
Let \(E_{\mathrm{adm}}\subset E\) denote the full subcategory of morphisms computable by finite local processes within the Reflexive topos \(E\). 
A morphism \(f:X\to Y\) is \emph{admissible} if its graph is both measurable and finitely refutable under the internal logic;
\(f\) is \emph{internal} if it exists by AFA coinduction in \(E\) without necessarily being algorithmically realizable in \(E_{\mathrm{adm}}\).
The Transputation operator \(\PT\) resides in \(E\setminus E_{\mathrm{adm}}\) but induces a measurable selection 
\(\pi(\PT)\) on admissible branch sets via Kuratowski–Ryll-Nardzewski selection theory.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}
This stratification resolves the foundational tension between PT being non-computable yet physically realizable: admissible dynamics evolve under deterministic rules in \(E_{\mathrm{adm}}\), while PT acts as a higher-order internal selector that is measurable and microcausal but not algorithmically reducible.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[Transputation Operator]
\label{def:PT}
Let \(\mathfrak{R}\) be a Reflexive System satisfying \cref{thm:PTPSC}. A \emph{Transputation} operator
\[
\PT:\mathcal{C}\!P_{\mathrm{adm}}\longrightarrow \Gamma_{\mathrm{adm}}
\]
acts on the class of admissible Choice Points \(\mathcal{C}\!P_{\mathrm{adm}}\) (\cref{def:CP}) and selects a single admissible successor branch \(\gamma_k\) in the branch set \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{adm}}\) according to the global coherence functional (MDL minimization under admissibility). Formally, for a CP \((\theta^\star,\mathcal{B})\) with admissible branches \(\mathcal{B}=\{\gamma_i\}\),
\[
\PT(\theta^\star,\mathcal{B})=\arg\min_{\gamma_i\in \mathcal{B}}\, D(\gamma_i(t)) + \lambda\, C(\gamma_i),
\]
where \(D\) is the dissonance functional and \(C\) is the MDL complexity penalty. The selected \(\gamma_k\) is actualized, while all others remain counterfactual.
\end{definition}

\subsubsection*{Mathematical Definition of PT: Dynamic, Operator, and Variational Forms}

\paragraph{Dynamic (coinductive) form.}
Let \(E\) be the ambient topos with admissible fragment \(E_{\mathrm{adm}}\), \(B(x)\) the finite/compact admissible branch set at base point \(x\), and
\(L(x,\gamma) = D(\gamma) + \lambda_{\Psi}\,C(\gamma)\) the MDL coherence functional. Define the guarded endofunctor
\[
\mathcal{F}(X)(x) \equiv \operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\gamma\in B(x)} L(x,\gamma)\; \cup\; \{\,\mathrm{eval}(\ulcorner T\urcorner, X)\,\}.
\]
By AFA, \(\mathcal{F}\) admits a greatest fixed point \(X^\star\), and the \emph{Transputation operator} is the measurable selector
\[
\mathrm{PT}(x) \in \operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\gamma\in B(x)} L(x,\gamma),
\qquad
x\mapsto \mathrm{PT}(x)\in\Gamma_{\mathrm{adm}},
\]
unique a.e. under the MDL tie order. This realizes PT as a coinductively defined internal morphism (non-SC in general).

\paragraph{Operator-theoretic form.}
Let \(\mathsf{Sel}_{x}\) denote the set of admissible selectors on \(B(x)\). Equip \(\mathsf{Sel}_{x}\) with the preorder
\(\sigma\preceq \sigma'\iff L(x,\sigma(x))\le L(x,\sigma'(x))\).
Then PT is the least element w.r.t. \(\preceq\):
\[
\mathrm{PT}(x)=\inf_{\preceq}\mathsf{Sel}_{x},
\quad
\text{with tie-breaking by code order on \(\mathrm{Code}\)}.
\]
Measurability follows from Kuratowski–Ryll-Nardzewski; microcausality from finite support of \(B(x)\).

\paragraph{Variational form.}
On any region \(U\subset\) base, define the discrete action
\[
\mathcal{A}[\gamma_U] \;=\; \sum_{x\in U} \Big( D(\gamma(x)) + \lambda_{\Psi}\,C(\gamma(x)) \Big),
\]
subject to admissibility and local cone constraints. A PT-trajectory \(\gamma_U^\star\) satisfies the Euler–Lagrange selection rule
\[
\gamma_U^\star \in \operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\gamma_U\in \Pi_{x\in U} B(x)} \mathcal{A}[\gamma_U],
\]
with locality implying that \(\gamma^\star(x)\) depends only on data in the causal cone of \(x\).

\subsection{Formal Variational Definition of Transputation and SRRG}
\label{subsec:PT-SRRG-formal}

We now provide explicit, self-contained variational definitions of the Transputation operator and the Self-Referential Renormalization Group, which serve as the operational foundations for all subsequent computational and physical derivations.

\begin{definition}[Transputation Operator $\PT$ (Variational Form)]
\label{def:PT-variational}
Let $\mathcal{S}_t$ denote the complete information state of a Reflexive system at discrete step $t$. The Transputation operator acts as
\[
\PT : \mathcal{S}_t \longrightarrow \mathcal{S}_{t+1}
= \arg\!\min_{\mathcal{S}'} L(\mathcal{S}',\mathcal{S}_t)
\]
where the loss functional $L$ encodes the Reflexive Landauer cost:
\[
L(\mathcal{S}',\mathcal{S}_t)
= k_B T \log\!\frac{P(\mathcal{S}_t)}{P(\mathcal{S}')} + 
\lambda_\Psi \int_{\Man} \Big(\|\nabla\Psi\|^2 + \alpha \Psi^2\Big)\,dV.
\]
The first term quantifies the logical irreversibility (Landauer bit cost); the second term quantifies the geometric coherence energy. $\PT$ acts only at Choice Points, i.e., configurations where the system's internal model cannot predict its next admissible state without self-referential evaluation.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Self-Referential Renormalization Group (SRRG)]
\label{def:SRRG}
A map
\[
\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{SRRG}} : (\Man,\Psi,\PT) 
\longrightarrow (\Man',\Psi',\PT')
\]
that co-renormalizes both physical fields and their adjudicators such that
\[
\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{SRRG}}(\PT) = \PT' = \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{SRRG}}\!\circ\!\PT\!\circ\!\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{SRRG}}^{-1}.
\]
Fixed points $(\Man^*,\Psi^*,\PT^*)$ satisfying 
$\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{SRRG}}(\PT^*) = \PT^*$ correspond to self-consistent Reflexive universes. The SRRG flow is a gradient flow on the space of theories that maximizes reflexive viability (self-containment and MDL coherence).
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}
These variational forms make explicit the physical cost structure of adjudication and the principle that a self-consistent universe must be a fixed point of its own renormalization dynamics. The SRRG framework provides the mechanism by which the Standard Model emerges as the inevitable, unique attractor of reflexive self-consistency (see \S\ref{subsec:SM-FP}). The cosmic-scale application of SRRG flow connects directly to \textbf{Reflexive Cosmogenesis} (Thm.~\ref{thm:cosmogenesis}): the Big Bang itself can be understood as the first SRRG fixed-point transition, where the universe's initial energy budget emerges from the Landauer cost of resolving the primordial maximal degeneracy, establishing the fundamental connection between cosmic genesis and reflexive self-consistency.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Dual-Operator Dynamics and Reflexive Causality}
\label{subsec:dual-operator}
The microdynamics of the substrate admit two adjoint evolutions \(T,\,T^\dagger\) acting on state codes \(c\in\mathrm{Code}\):
\begin{align}
T &: c\mapsto f(c)\quad\text{(matter evolution)},\\
T^\dagger &: c\mapsto f^\dagger(c)\quad\text{(antimatter / conjugate evolution)}.
\end{align}
They satisfy \(\langle f^\dagger(a),b\rangle=\langle a,f(b)\rangle\) in the internal Hilbert object \(\Hil\) of the topos, establishing a dual adjunction between trajectories. Each transputational act corresponds to a pair \((T,T^\dagger)\) selecting a branch and its conjugate un-realized alternative. 

\paragraph{Reflexive light-cone bound.}
On the emergent Fisher manifold \((\Man,\Fisher)\), signals and adjudications propagate along causal cones defined by a finite maximal speed \(v_{\mathrm{LR}}\) (Lieb–Robinson bound). The reflexive bound requires
\begin{equation}
v_{\PT}\le v_{\mathrm{LR}}=c,
\end{equation}
ensuring compatibility of \(\PT\) with relativistic causality.

\paragraph{Causal bound.}
Let \(v_{\mathrm{LR}}\) be the Lieb--Robinson velocity (or \(c\) in relativistic settings). PT selection signals are constrained by the same cone: \(v_{\PT}\le v_{\mathrm{LR}}\). This holds because PT's adjudications are encoded in admissible interactions of the evaluator and respect its finite-speed locality.

\subsection{The No-Emulation and No-Cloning Barrier}
\label{subsec:noemulation}
\begin{theorem}[No-Emulation/No-Cloning for \(\PT\)]
\label{thm:NoEmulation}
Let \(\mathfrak{R}\) be a Reflexive System implementing \(\PT\). Then no Standard Computational (SC) machine \(M\) expressible as a Turing-equivalent endomorphism in \(\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{adm}}\) can emulate the total adjudication map of \(\PT\) on all admissible CPs; likewise, no local process can clone the complete input–output relation of \(\PT\) on any domain with coherence density \(\OmegaGlobal\ge\Omega_c\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Assume, for contradiction, that such an emulator \(M\) exists. Then there is a computable map \(m\) that, given a description of a CP \((\theta^\star,\mathcal{B})\), outputs the same branch index as \(\PT\). Encoding \(m\) internally yields a code \(\ulcorner m\urcorner\). Construct the diagonal input \(\delta=(\ulcorner m\urcorner,\ulcorner m\urcorner)\) and apply the evaluation \(U(\ulcorner m\urcorner,\delta)\). If \(m\) emulates \(\PT\), it must decide its own adjudication on \(\delta\), creating the paradox “select the branch not selected by yourself,” a direct analog of the Gödel–Turing diagonal contradiction. Hence such \(m\) cannot exist in the SC class. 

For the cloning claim, suppose a local reversible process \(C\) duplicates the entire relation graph of \(\PT\): \(C(\PT)=\PT\otimes\PT\). This would internalize the full self-mapping, violating the information-content inequality \(K(M_S)<K(I(S))\) from \cref{thm:PTPSC}. Above the coherence threshold \(\Omega_c\), the \(\PT\) act involves non-computable adjudication (continuous global coherence), rendering cloning impossible. Therefore, no SC or local process can emulate or clone \(\PT\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Hardware agnosticism]
\label{cor:hardware-agnostic}
The No-Emulation/No-Cloning barrier for \(\PT\) holds for any evaluator \(U\) that is Turing-equivalent and respects a finite signaling speed. In particular, \(\PT\) cannot be emulated by quantum circuits, reversible logic, or local Hamiltonian evolutions when restricted to the SC class.
\end{corollary}

\begin{remark}[PT as a Physical Oracle, not an Algorithmic One]
\label{rem:pt-physical-oracle}
The No-Emulation theorem establishes that \(\PT\) is non-computable in the Turing sense. This does \emph{not} imply that \(\PT\) requires infinite time, violates causality, or is physically mysterious. Rather, \(\PT\) is a \textbf{physical oracle}---a lawful process that nature implements directly via energy and coherence extremization, not via algorithm execution.

\paragraph{Analogy with path integrals.}
Consider the Feynman path integral in quantum field theory:
\[
\langle \phi_f | e^{-iHt/\hbar} | \phi_i \rangle \;=\; \int \mathcal{D}\phi\,e^{iS[\phi]/\hbar}.
\]
This sum over an uncountable infinity of field configurations is \emph{lawful} (given \(S[\phi]\), the amplitude is uniquely defined) but \emph{non-computable} via Turing machines. Yet nature ``evaluates'' the path integral physically in finite time via quantum evolution. We approximate it numerically via lattice QFT or perturbation theory, but the physical process does not ``compute''---it simply evolves according to the Schrödinger equation.

\paragraph{PT implementation via thermodynamics.}
Similarly, \(\PT\) is not computed but \emph{realized} through the Reflexive Landauer bound (Theorem~\ref{thm:RefLandauer-rigorous}):
\[
\Delta E_{\PT} \;\ge\; k_B T \log n \;+\; \lambda_\Psi\!\int\big(\alpha_1\Psi^2 + \alpha_2\|\nabla\Psi\|^2\big)\,dV.
\]
Among \(n\) admissible branches, \(\PT\) selects the one that minimizes \(\Delta E_{\PT}\)---a thermodynamic extremum principle analogous to Fermat's principle (light follows the path of least time) or the principle of least action (particles follow stationary-action trajectories). The selection is enforced by energy conservation and coherence maximization, not by running an algorithm.

\paragraph{Finite-time, causal operation.}
Tests V9 and V10 validate that \(\PT\) respects quantum speed limits (\(\tau_{\PT} \ge \hbar/(2\Delta E)\), 99.8\% compliance) and causal speed bounds (\(v_{\PT} \le c\), 100\% compliance). Non-computability refers to \emph{algorithmic complexity} (the halting problem for MDL optimization), not \emph{time complexity}. The universe does not ``solve'' the halting problem; it implements \(\PT\) via physical dynamics that converge in finite time.

\paragraph{Emergence from collective dynamics.}
At macroscopic scales, \(\PT\)-like behavior emerges from coupled Choice Point ensembles (E9--E26): synchronization (E9, E9b), GKSL master equations (E9c), power-law cascades (E9d), and long-range order (E26). These are all \emph{physical processes}, not algorithms.

\paragraph{Summary.}
\(\PT\) is lawful, deterministic, and causal, yet non-computable---just like path integrals, ergodic averages, or ground-state finding in quantum many-body systems. The universe does not compute itself; it transputes itself: selecting branches via energetic and coherence extremization. This is not a bug but a feature: it explains how reflexive self-reference (which requires solving undecidable problems) can occur within finite energy and time budgets.
\end{remark}

\begin{lemma}[Kolmogorov barrier for PT]
\label{lem:Kbarrier}
Let \(\PT\) select the MDL-minimal branch \(\gamma^\star=\arg\min_{\gamma\in\mathcal B}\big(D(\gamma)+\lambda C(\gamma)\big)\) where \(C(\gamma)\) is a code-length proxy for Kolmogorov complexity. If an SC machine \(M\) emulated \(\PT\) on all admissible CPs, then \(M\) would decide the ordering of Kolmogorov complexity between branch codes, contradicting the uncomputability of \(K(\cdot)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Construct CPs whose branches are programs competing by shortest description. An exact emulator of \(\PT\) would decide the shorter description uniformly, violating Rice's theorem.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[UWCA Universality vs.\ \(\PT\) Non-Computability]\label{rem:UWCAvsT}
The UWCA evaluator \(U\) (e.g., PR-1) is Turing-universal and self-hosting~\cite{SpivackUGPMath}. This universality concerns the \emph{execution} of admissible dynamics: given any \(\PT\)-selected trajectory (i.e., a sequence of already-resolved CP outcomes), the UWCA can encode and realize that trajectory without an external runner. However, this does \emph{not} imply that the adjudication map \(\PT\) itself—a global MDL/coherence extremizer over admissible branches—is SC-computable. The distinction is analogous to quantum mechanics: unitary evolution \(U(t)\) is computable and can propagate any state, but the Born rule selection at measurement is lawful yet not derived algorithmically from \(U\) alone. Here, UWCA plays the role of \(U(t)\) (carrying dynamics), while \(\PT\) plays the role of wavefunction collapse (selecting branches). Thus UWCA can \emph{host} any lawful (i.e., \(\PT\)-adjudicated) history, but cannot in general \emph{compute} \(\PT\) (Theorem~\ref{thm:NoEmulation}). The full law \((U+\PT)\) is determinate at the cosmic level—fixing a unique history—yet \(\PT\) remains effectively indeterminate to any SC subsystem, as CP resolutions are uncomputable from within standard computation.

\medskip\noindent\emph{Oracle perspective.}
Formally, the non-computability of $\PT$ is relative to the admissible class.
If one endows the evaluator with an oracle that returns the global MDL minimizer
(the ``physical oracle'' realized by the universe itself), then $\PT$ is computable relative to that oracle.
Hence the full law $(U,\PT)$ is determinate and effectively computable in the \emph{oracle-enhanced}
model while remaining supra-computational within $\Eff$.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Why Local SC Rules Cannot Guarantee Global \(D\)-Minimization]\label{rem:LocalSCvsGlobalD}
A finite-local, time-homogeneous SC update rule \(U\) maps each neighborhood of radius \(r\) to a unique next-state for the center cell. A global dissonance functional \(D\) combines \emph{nonlocal} structure (e.g., long-range correlations, temporal coherence, topological regularities). At a choice point, two successor macro-branches may be \emph{locally indistinguishable} on radius-\(r\) neighborhoods while differing dramatically in \(D\). Thus no fixed finite-local SC rule can, in general, implement the MDL \(\arg\min\) that \(\PT\) computes over \(\mathcal{B}\): the mapping \(\mathcal{B}\to\arg\min (D+\lambda C)\) is \emph{not} an SC function (Theorem~\ref{thm:NoEmulation}). This explains both why chaotic irreversible CAs (e.g., Rule 110) do not reliably reduce \(D\), and why naively ``coherence-hardening'' a local rule often leads to \emph{freezing}, not progress (Appendix~\ref{subsec:toy-validation}, E11 tests). In our empirical work, the PR-0 annealer~\cite{SpivackSDS_PR0} is an \emph{explicit surrogate} for \(\PT\); it supplies the global choice the SC evaluator cannot compute. Cellular automata are the engine; \(\PT\) is the driver.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Determinism vs.\ Computability]\label{rem:DetVsComp}
The \(\PT\) principle (MDL/coherence extremization) is \emph{lawful} and, in that sense, \emph{determinate} at the level of the full law \((U,\PT)\). What fails is \emph{SC computability} from within the evaluator \(U\): determining the globally minimal branch at a CP reduces to a Kolmogorov-minimality problem, triggering the No-Emulation theorem. This is the same structural situation as in quantum theory (unitary vs collapse): an operationally needed selection rule that is not obtained by iterating a local SC map. In our PR-0 experiments~\cite{SpivackSDS_PR0}, the role of \(\PT\) is approximated by an annealed \(D\)-optimizer that acts as a \emph{proxy} for this non-algorithmic global selection.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Energetic and Thermodynamic Bounds}
\label{subsec:energetic}
Each transputational act is irreversible: it selects one branch from \(n\) equiprobable alternatives, destroying \(\log n\) bits of logical entropy. By Landauer's principle, the minimal dissipated energy is \(k_B T\log n\). Reflexive adjudication adds an information-geometric contribution due to field gradients of the coherence field \(\Psifield\). 

\begin{theorem}[Reflexive Landauer Bound with Coherence Term]
\label{thm:RefLandauer-rigorous}
Let $\mathcal{U}\subset M_{\mathrm{ST}}$ be a bounded spacetime region with spatial slices of finite measure $V_t$ and temperature field $T(x,t)$ bounded below by $T_{\min}>0$. Let $n\ge 2$ be the adjudication degeneracy, and let $\Psi\in H^1(\mathcal{U})$ be dimensionless with $|\Psi|\le \Psi_0$ and coherence correlation length $\ell>0$ (i.e.\ $|\nabla\Psi|\lesssim \Psi_0/\ell$ a.e.). Assume $V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Psi,\omega)$ is convex in $\Psi$ and $C^1$ in $(\Psi,\omega)$. Then any transputational adjudication in $\mathcal{U}$ obeys
\[
\Delta E_{\PT}\;\ge\; k_B\,T_{\min}\,\log n
\;+\; \lambda_\Psi \!\int_{\mathcal U}\Big(\alpha_1 \Psi^2+\alpha_2\|\nabla \Psi\|^2\Big)\,dV,
\]
with $\lambda_\Psi>0$, $[\alpha_1]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, $[\alpha_2]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-1}}$.\footnote{Dimensional consistency:
$[\alpha_1]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$ and $[\alpha_2]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-1}}$,
so $\int (\alpha_1\Psi^2+\alpha_2\|\nabla\Psi\|^2)\,dV$ has units of energy (see Appendix~U).}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The $k_BT\log n$ term is the standard Landauer lower bound for logical irreversibility. The additional term arises from the energetic cost of coherence maintenance. Under the convexity hypothesis, the incremental free-energy functional
\[
\mathcal{F}[\Psi]\;=\;\int_{\mathcal U}\!\Big(\alpha_1 \Psi^2+\alpha_2\|\nabla\Psi\|^2\Big)\,dV
\]
is positive and lower semicontinuous; any admissible adjudication that changes $\Psi$ by $\delta\Psi$ must supply at least $\delta \mathcal{F}$ units of energy (by convexity and Poincar\'e-type estimates on $\nabla\Psi$). Summing the logical and geometric contributions yields the claim.

For a rigorous microphysical derivation using Crooks--Jarzynski fluctuation relations and Ginzburg--Landau theory, see Appendix~\ref{app:stat-mech-rlb}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Dimensional Consistency of Reflexive Landauer Inequality]
\label{lem:dimensional-consistency-RL}
Using natural units where $[k_B T]={\rm J}$ and $[\Psi]=1$ (dimensionless coherence amplitude), the integrand
$\lambda_\Psi (\alpha_1\Psi^2+\alpha_2\|\nabla\Psi\|^2)$ has units of energy density (J·m$^{-3}$) 
provided $[\lambda_\Psi\alpha_1]={\rm J·m^{-3}}$ and $[\lambda_\Psi\alpha_2]={\rm J·m^{-1}}$.
Hence $\int(\cdot)\,dV$ yields energy (J), confirming that $\Delta E_{\mathrm{PT}}$ 
is a physically measurable calorimetric observable.
Under the calibration $\alpha_0\sim 10^{58}\,{\rm m}^2$ (Appendix A), one obtains $\lambda_\Psi\alpha_1 \sim 10^{-6}\,{\rm J·m^{-3}}$ and $\lambda_\Psi\alpha_2 \sim 10^{-6}\,{\rm J·m^{-1}}$ as fiducial values for laboratory-scale tests.
\end{lemma}

\paragraph{Normalization and units.}
The region \(\mathcal U\subset M_{\mathrm{ST}}\) is the spacetime domain of the PT act as bounded by the causal cone. \paragraph{Calibration of \(\lambda_{\Psi}\) to measurable coherence.}
In laboratory settings we treat \(\lambda_{\Psi}\) as a phenomenological coupling that scales the coherence contribution
\(\int(\alpha_1\Psi^2+\alpha_2\|\nabla\Psi\|^2)\,dV\) by a directly measurable proxy of information-geometric order.
Two practical calibrations are:
(i) \emph{Fisher-metric route:} estimate \(\Psi\) from the Fisher information of a parametric device model, so that
\(\|\nabla\Psi\|^2\) coincides with spatial gradients of the Fisher curvature density; 
(ii) \emph{coherence–energy route:} in optical lattices, BECs, or superconducting qubit arrays, use spectroscopic linewidth narrowing,
interference fringe visibility, or entanglement-witness amplitudes to construct a normalized \(\widehat{\Psi}\in[0,1]\),
and set \(\lambda_{\Psi}=\kappa\,\widehat{I}_{\mathrm{coh}}\) with \(\widehat{I}_{\mathrm{coh}}\propto \widehat{\Psi}^2\).
This yields an operational \(\lambda_{\Psi}\) that maps increases in device coherence to a predictable calorimetric increment in \(\Delta E_{PT}\).

\begin{proposition}[Reflexive Landauer under LDB and MDL penalty]
\label{prop:RefLandauer-ldb}
Consider a finite CP with admissible branches $\{\gamma_i\}_{i=1}^n$ at temperature $T$. Suppose the adjudication kernel satisfies local detailed balance (LDB)
\[
\frac{K(i\to j)}{K(j\to i)}=\exp\!\big[-\beta(Q_{ij}+\Delta\Phi_{ij})\big]
\]
with $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ and $\Delta\Phi_{ij}=\lambda_\Psi\Delta\mathcal{E}_\Psi(\gamma_i\to\gamma_j)$ the MDL coherence penalty difference, where $\mathcal{E}_\Psi=\int(\alpha_1\Psi^2+\alpha_2\|\nabla\Psi\|^2)dV$. Then, for any admissible selection rule,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:GeneralizedLandauer}
\langle Q\rangle \;\ge\; k_BT\,\Delta H + \lambda_\Psi\,\Delta E_\Psi,
\qquad 
\Delta H = H(p_{\mathrm{prior}})-H(p_{\mathrm{post}}),
\end{equation}
where $\Delta E_\Psi = \int(\alpha_1\Delta\Psi^2+\alpha_2\Delta|\nabla\Psi|^2)dV$. 
The uniform-tie specialization yields $\Delta H\ge \log n$ when all $n$ branches have equal prior probability, giving
\[
\langle Q\rangle \;\ge\; k_BT\log n + \lambda_\Psi \int(\alpha_1\Psi^2+\alpha_2\|\nabla\Psi\|^2)\,dV.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
KL non-negativity $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\|q)\ge 0$ with LDB gives $\beta\langle Q+\Delta\Phi\rangle \ge \Delta H$ for any stochastic transition, where $\Delta H = H(p_{\mathrm{prior}})-H(p_{\mathrm{post}})$ is the Shannon entropy difference. Expand $\Delta\Phi$ using the MDL penalty definition to obtain Equation \eqref{eq:GeneralizedLandauer}. This subsumes the uniform-tie case and remains tight under nonuniform adjudication priors.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Generality]
Equation \eqref{eq:GeneralizedLandauer} is the general form valid for arbitrary prior distributions. The uniform bound $\langle Q\rangle \ge k_BT\log n$ holds when $p_{\mathrm{prior}}$ is uniform over $n$ branches; empirical calibrations with nonuniform priors should use the full $\Delta H$ expression.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}
The first term of \(\Delta E_{\PT}\) expresses logical irreversibility; the second encodes geometric/field coherence cost. This connects the microscopic act of choice to macroscopic curvature through \(dE=\alphazero\,d\OmegaGlobal\): each bit of lawful decision increases the universe's geometric complexity by \(\alphazero^{-1}k_BT\log n\). Thus, Reflexive Landauer can be read as the energetic expression of the Principle of Coherence realized by \(\PT\).
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Empirical Validation via PR-0 Field Substrate]\label{rem:PR0validation}
A separate study~\cite{SpivackSDS_PR0} implements the ontological dissonance operator \(D\) within a continuous reversible field substrate (PR-0) and empirically verifies the main predictions of the Reflexive framework. Minimizing \(D\) under simple constraints yields the emergent forms of all four fundamental interactions (confinement, electromagnetic, weak, and gravitational), and the measured correlation between \(D\) and integrated information \(\Phi\) (in the sense of Tononi's Integrated Information Theory) satisfies \(r=-0.91\) (\(r^2=0.83\), \(p<0.001\)). These results provide numerical confirmation that the energetic law \(dE=\alphazero\,d\OmegaGlobal\) and the \(D\leftrightarrow -\Phi\) equivalence predicted by Reflexive theory hold in a physical dynamical system. PR-0 thus serves as an empirical realization of Reflexive Geometry, whereas discrete cellular automata (e.g.\ PR-1, a reversible CA studied in earlier work) function only as reversible computational analogues incapable of true transputational adjudication or spontaneous coherence emergence. The continuous field-theoretic approach of PR-0, with explicit dissonance minimization dynamics, appears essential for manifesting the emergent phenomena predicted by MFRR.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of Reflexive Landauer Bound under Coarse-Graining]
\label{thm:monotonic-bound}
Let $\Delta E_{\mathrm{PT}}(\mathcal{U})$ be the Reflexive Landauer bound for a domain $\mathcal{U}$ and let $\{\mathcal{U}_i\}$ be a partition of $\mathcal{U}$ into subdomains. Then the bound satisfies monotonicity:
\[
\Delta E_{\mathrm{PT}}(\mathcal{U})\ \ge\ \sum_i \Delta E_{\mathrm{PT}}(\mathcal{U}_i),
\]
with equality if and only if the coherence field $\Psi$ factorizes across the partition (no cross-domain coherence).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
The bound $\Delta E_{\mathrm{PT}}(\mathcal{U}) = k_B T\log n + \lambda_\Psi\int_{\mathcal{U}}(\alpha_1\Psi^2+\alpha_2\|\nabla\Psi\|^2)\,dV$ includes both a logical term (independent of partition) and a coherence term. The coherence integral $\int_{\mathcal{U}}(\cdot)\,dV$ decomposes as $\sum_i\int_{\mathcal{U}_i}(\cdot)\,dV$ plus boundary terms. When $\Psi$ factorizes, the boundary terms vanish, yielding equality. When $\Psi$ has cross-domain correlations, the boundary terms contribute additional positive energy, making the total bound larger than the sum of subdomain bounds.
For the full proof including explicit forms of the boundary corrections, see Appendix~\ref{app:monotonic-bound}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
This theorem establishes that the Reflexive Landauer bound is a \emph{monotone} under coarse-graining: aggregating domains never decreases the total bound. This property ensures that the bound provides a consistent lower limit on adjudication energy at all scales, from microscopic CPs to macroscopic coherent regions.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Interpretation and Consequences}
\label{subsec:interpretation-transputation}
The \emph{No-Emulation} theorem formalizes the boundary between computation and transputation: adjudicative acts lie beyond Turing emulation yet remain lawfully constrained by coherence. The \emph{Reflexive Landauer} inequality quantifies the thermodynamic signature of adjudication, uniting logical and geometric irreversibility. 

Consequences:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Energetic link.} Each \(\PT\) act deposits an irreducible energy quantum proportional to its informational degeneracy and coherence curvature. 
  \item \textbf{Field coupling.} The gradient term \(\|\grad\Psifield\|^2\) couples adjudication to spatial coherence, preparing the emergence of \(\Cten\) in \cref{sec:geometry}.
  \item \textbf{Observation.} These energy quanta manifest as minimal dissipative signatures—potential experimental traces of transputational events in high-coherence systems.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{The Physical Meaning of Lawful Non-Computability}
\label{subsec:PT-physical-meaning}

The No-Emulation theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:NoEmulation}) establishes that \(\PT\) is \emph{lawful} (measurable, deterministic, causal) but \emph{non-computable} (not Turing-emulable). This raises a foundational question: What does it mean for a physical process to be lawful yet non-algorithmic? This framework provides a direct physical answer: \textbf{Transputation is the physical process of a system relaxing to a global minimum of a free energy functional that combines thermodynamic entropy with a field-theoretic potential representing informational coherence (or compressibility).} The coherence field $\Psi$ is the critical link that translates the abstract logic of Minimum Description Length (MDL) into concrete, energetic physics. 

The universe does not \emph{compute} the MDL-optimal state; its dynamics physically \emph{realize} it by seeking the state of minimum free energy, a process analogous to thermodynamic relaxation or the evaluation of a path integral. The non-computability of \(\PT\) is therefore the well-known non-computability of predicting the final ground state of a complex, non-linear field relaxation. This section formalizes this interpretation by showing that \(\PT\) is a physical oracle, not an algorithmic one, and that its operation is both finite-time and causal.

\paragraph{Distinction: Computable vs.\ Lawful.}
In standard physics and computer science, these terms are often conflated, but they are logically distinct:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*,nosep]
  \item \textbf{Computable}: A function \(f\) is computable if there exists a Turing machine (or equivalently, a recursive algorithm) that, given input \(x\), halts and outputs \(f(x)\) in finite time. Computability is an \emph{algorithmic} property.
  \item \textbf{Lawful}: A process is lawful if it is \emph{deterministic} (same initial conditions yield same outcomes), \emph{measurable} (outputs are well-defined elements of a measurable space), and \emph{causal} (respects spacetime light-cone structure). Lawfulness is a \emph{physical} property.
\end{itemize}
Crucially, \textbf{lawful does not imply computable}. Many physical processes are deterministic and causal but not algorithmically computable. Examples:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=*,nosep]
  \item \textbf{Path integrals in quantum field theory:} The Feynman path integral \(\int \mathcal{D}\phi\,e^{iS[\phi]/\hbar}\) sums over an uncountable infinity of field configurations. This is a lawful, deterministic prescription (given \(S[\phi]\), the amplitude is uniquely defined), but it is not computable via Turing machines. Nature ``evaluates'' the path integral physically; we approximate it numerically.
  \item \textbf{Ergodic systems:} The long-time average of an observable in an ergodic system is deterministically given by the microcanonical ensemble average, but computing this average exactly requires infinite time (in general). The physical system \emph{realizes} the average via thermalization, without ``computing'' it algorithmically.
  \item \textbf{Ground-state finding in quantum many-body systems:} Finding the exact ground state of a Hamiltonian is QMA-complete (exponentially hard for quantum computers), yet physical systems relax to their ground states in polynomial time via thermalization and quantum annealing. The process is lawful (energy minimization) but not efficiently computable.
\end{enumerate}
\(\PT\) belongs to this category: it is a \emph{selection oracle}---a lawful physical process that nature implements directly, not an algorithm that can be simulated on a Turing machine.

\paragraph{PT as a physical oracle: Energetic implementation.}
The key insight is that \(\PT\) is not \emph{computed} but \emph{realized} through physical dynamics. The Reflexive Landauer bound (Theorem~\ref{thm:RefLandauer-rigorous}) provides the implementation mechanism:
\[
\Delta E_{\PT} \;\ge\; k_B T \log n \;+\; \lambda_\Psi\!\int_{\mathcal U}\big(\alpha_1\Psi^2 + \alpha_2\|\nabla\Psi\|^2\big)\,dV.
\]
This inequality has two critical implications:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=*,nosep]
  \item \textbf{Energy minimization as selection:} Among the \(n\) admissible branches at a Choice Point, \(\PT\) selects the branch that minimizes the total energy cost \(\Delta E_{\PT}\). This is a \emph{thermodynamic extremum principle}, analogous to Fermat's principle in optics or the principle of least action in classical mechanics. The ``selection'' is not computed algorithmically; it is \emph{enforced by energy conservation}.
  \item \textbf{Coherence maximization as tie-breaking:} The \(\lambda_\Psi\!\int(\Psi^2 + \|\nabla\Psi\|^2)\,dV\) term selects the branch with highest coherence (lowest dissonance \(D\)). Physical processes---decoherence, thermalization, quantum annealing---naturally drive systems toward coherent states (maximum entropy production, minimum free energy). \(\PT\) is the limiting idealization of this tendency.
\end{enumerate}
Thus, \(\PT\) is not a mysterious ``non-algorithmic oracle''; it is the \textbf{physical realization of energy and coherence extremization} under admissibility constraints. Nature does not ``compute'' \(\PT\); it \emph{is} \(\PT\).

\paragraph{Finite-time operation and causality.}
The non-computability of \(\PT\) does not imply infinite time or acausal propagation. This is a common misconception. Two key results establish finite-time, causal operation:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*,nosep]
  \item \textbf{Quantum Speed Limit (V9):} Tests V9 validate that \(\PT\)-mediated transitions respect the Mandelstam-Tamm bound:
  \[
  \tau_{\PT} \;\ge\; \frac{\hbar}{2\,\Delta E},
  \]
  where \(\Delta E\) is the energy gap between branches. This ensures that adjudication time is finite and scales with the energy cost. Computational validation achieves $99.8\%$ compliance over $10^4$ transitions.
  \item \textbf{Causal Speed Bound (V10):} Tests V10 validate that information propagation via \(\PT\) respects the light-cone constraint:
  \[
  v_{\PT} \;\le\; c.
  \]
  All tested configurations yield $v_{\PT}/c < 1$ (mean $0.87 \pm 0.09$), confirming that \(\PT\) is local and causal despite non-computability.
\end{itemize}
Non-computability is about \emph{algorithmic complexity} (the halting problem for optimal selection), not \emph{time complexity} (how long the physical process takes). An analogy: finding the global minimum of a complex energy landscape is NP-hard algorithmically, but simulated annealing or gradient descent can find good solutions in polynomial time. \(\PT\) is the idealized limit of such physical optimization processes.

\paragraph{Emergence from collective dynamics.}
At macroscopic scales, \(\PT\)-like behavior \emph{emerges} from collective dynamics of coupled Choice Point ensembles. Tests E9--E26 validate this:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*,nosep]
  \item \textbf{E9, E9b: Synchronization:} Coupled CP ensembles spontaneously synchronize above a spectral threshold \(\|W\|_2 > \|W\|_c\), exhibiting collective selection that mimics global \(\PT\).
  \item \textbf{E9c: GKSL emergence:} Master equations with Lindblad structure emerge from internal CP dynamics, without external environments. This shows that decoherence (pointer-basis selection) is a reflexive process.
  \item \textbf{E9d: Power-law cascades:} Avalanche distributions follow power laws \(\kappa \in [1.3, 2.3]\), characteristic of self-organized criticality. This indicates that \(\PT\) operates at the edge of order and chaos, where collective selection is most efficient.
  \item \textbf{E9e: Kuramoto phases:} Continuous-phase oscillators synchronize via mean-field coupling, demonstrating that coherence-driven selection (a hallmark of \(\PT\)) arises naturally in coupled systems.
  \item \textbf{E26: Long-range order and hysteresis:} Coherence length \(\xi\) diverges near the synchronization threshold, and the system exhibits temporal memory (hysteresis loops), indicating that \(\PT\) has a ``history-dependent'' character, consistent with path-dependent MDL selection.
\end{itemize}
These results show that at the fundamental level, \(\PT\) is a primitive (coinductively defined via AFA, \S\ref{subsec:eff-semantics}), but at emergent scales, \(\PT\)-like selection arises from \emph{collective thermodynamic and coherence dynamics}. This bridges the gap between the abstract categorical definition and physical realization.

\paragraph{Comparison with other non-algorithmic physical processes.}
\(\PT\) is not the first non-computable physical process to appear in fundamental physics:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*,nosep]
  \item \textbf{Penrose Objective Reduction (OR):} Penrose's gravitational collapse of the wavefunction is non-algorithmic but lawful. However, OR lacks a concrete energetic signature or selection criterion. \(\PT\) provides both: the Reflexive Landauer bound and MDL selection.
  \item \textbf{Wheeler's Participatory Universe:} Wheeler proposed that observation is not passive but participatory, with the universe ``computing'' itself. \(\PT\) formalizes this: the universe does not compute (Turing sense) but transputes (MDL-selects via energy/coherence extremization).
  \item \textbf{'t Hooft's Cellular Automaton Interpretation of QM:} 't Hooft suggests QM may emerge from deterministic but non-computable cellular automata. \(\PT\) is similar but differs in two ways: (i) \(\PT\) is explicitly tied to information geometry (Fisher metric, coherence), not just deterministic rules; (ii) \(\PT\) is provably non-emulable (No-Emulation theorem), not merely conjectured.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Operational summary.}
To summarize the physical meaning of ``lawful non-computability'':
\begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*.,leftmargin=*]
  \item \(\PT\) is \textbf{deterministic}: Given a Choice Point state \(x\) and admissible branch set \(B(x)\), the output \(\PT(x)\) is unique a.e.\ (up to MDL tie order).
  \item \(\PT\) is \textbf{measurable}: The selector \(\PT:X\to\Gamma_{\mathrm{adm}}\) is a measurable morphism in the effective topos \(\Eff\).
  \item \(\PT\) is \textbf{causal}: Information propagation via \(\PT\) respects \(v_{\PT}\le c\) (V10), and adjudication time satisfies quantum speed limits (V9).
  \item \(\PT\) is \textbf{non-computable}: There is no Turing machine that, given \(\ulcorner x\urcorner\) and \(\ulcorner B(x)\urcorner\), outputs \(\ulcorner\PT(x)\urcorner\) (Theorem~\ref{thm:NoEmulation}). This is because MDL optimization is equivalent to the halting problem (Rice-Kolmogorov reduction).
  \item \(\PT\) is \textbf{physically realized}: Nature implements \(\PT\) via energy minimization (\(\Delta E_{\PT}\) bound) and coherence maximization (\(\lambda_\Psi\!\int\Psi^2\,dV\) term). No algorithm is executed; the selection is enforced by thermodynamics.
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{Conclusion.}
\(\PT\) is not a renaming of ignorance but a \emph{precise physical mechanism}: the universe selects branches at Choice Points by minimizing the Reflexive Landauer bound, which combines logical irreversibility (\(k_B T \log n\)) with geometric coherence cost (\(\lambda_\Psi\!\int(\Psi^2 + \|\nabla\Psi\|^2)\,dV\)). This process is lawful, causal, and finite-time, yet non-computable because exact MDL selection is undecidable. The distinction is the same as between a path integral (lawful but non-algorithmic) and a Monte Carlo approximation (computable but approximate). Nature ``evaluates'' \(\PT\) directly via energy and coherence dynamics; we can only approximate it computationally. This is not a bug of the theory but a feature: it explains why the universe can execute reflexive self-reference (which requires solving the halting problem for self-consistency) while remaining within finite energy and time budgets. The universe does not compute itself---it transputes itself.

\section{Computability Barrier for Transputation}
\label{sec:computability}

\paragraph{Section summary.}
We prove that exact $\PT$ is not $\Eff$-computable via Rice's theorem reduction, establish a Kleene diagonal argument for non-clonability, and show that approximate $\PT$ is $\Delta^0_2$ (limit computable) under uniqueness conditions.

We work in the effective topos $\Eff$ as in \S\ref{subsec:eff-semantics}. The admissible evaluator $U:\Code\times\Env\to\Env$ is the universal partial recursive functional, so ``admissible'' means ``$\Eff$--computable''.

\subsection{PT is not an $\Eff$--computable morphism}
\label{subsec:PT-not-computable}

Fix a universal prefix-free machine $\mathcal U$ and let $K(\cdot)$ denote its prefix-free Kolmogorov complexity. In the MDL formulation (constant additive invariance), the adjudication functional compares branches by
\[
\mathfrak L(\gamma)\;=\; D(\gamma)\;+\;\lambda\,C(\gamma),\qquad
C(\gamma)=K(\text{code}(\gamma)) + O(1),
\]
and $\PT$ returns $\arg\min_\gamma \mathfrak L(\gamma)$ with a fixed code tie-breaker.

\begin{lemma}[Explicit CP encoding of $K$-order]
\label{lem:cp-encode-K}
There is a uniform, $\Eff$--computable reduction that maps any pair of self-delimiting programs $(p,q)$ to an admissible choice point $\mathcal C_{p,q}$ with branches $\gamma_p,\gamma_q$ such that $D(\gamma_p)=D(\gamma_q)$ and
\[
\PT(\mathcal C_{p,q})=
\begin{cases}
\gamma_p,&\text{if }K(p)\le K(q),\\
\gamma_q,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\]
with a fixed tie-breaking order on codes.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof idea]
Use the admissible evaluator $U$ to build two branch generators that, on input of their own code, reconstruct the corresponding macro-branch by running the program and emitting a canonical description of the branch. The tie on $D$ is enforced by padding the $D$--neutral parts of both branches identically. Then $\mathfrak L(\gamma_p)-\mathfrak L(\gamma_q)=\lambda(K(p)-K(q))+O(1)$, so the MDL minimizer matches the $K$--order (up to a global additive constant absorbed by the fixed tie-breaker).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact PT is not $\Eff$--computable]
\label{thm:PT-not-eff}
Let $\PT$ denote the exact MDL adjudication functional on admissible choice points $\mathcal C=(\theta^\star,\{\gamma_0,\gamma_1\})$ with $D(\gamma_0)=D(\gamma_1)$. If $\PT$ were an $\Eff$--morphism, then the predicate
\[
\mathsf{LEQ}_K(p,q)\;:\;\;K(p)\le K(q)
\]
would be computable. Since $\mathsf{LEQ}_K$ is not computable, $\PT$ cannot be an $\Eff$--morphism.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Reduction. Given arbitrary binary strings $p,q$, construct an admissible choice point $\mathcal C_{p,q}$ with two branches $\gamma_p,\gamma_q$ such that: (i) the dissonance tie holds, $D(\gamma_p)=D(\gamma_q)$; (ii) the code map satisfies $\text{code}(\gamma_p)=p$ and $\text{code}(\gamma_q)=q$ in the sense of the fixed universal machine $\mathcal U$; (iii) the admissibility witnesses embed $p,q$ as the minimal self-delimiting programs that reconstruct the corresponding branches. Then
\[
\mathfrak L(\gamma_p)-\mathfrak L(\gamma_q)
= \lambda\big(K(p)-K(q)\big)+O(1).
\]
For any fixed tie-breaker and fixed additive constant, the sign of this difference matches the truth of $K(p)\le K(q)$ except on a finite set of pairs absorbed by the constant. Thus an $\Eff$--procedure computing $\PT(\mathcal C_{p,q})$ would decide $\mathsf{LEQ}_K(p,q)$. But $\mathsf{LEQ}_K$ is not recursive (follows from the non-recursiveness and non r.e.\ nature of $K$), a contradiction. Hence $\PT$ is not $\Eff$--computable.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Rice's theorem viewpoint]
The property ``program $r$ is the MDL-minimizer among $\{p,q\}$ for the induced branches'' is a non-trivial extensional property of partial recursive functions, hence undecidable by Rice's theorem. The reduction above makes the dependence on $K(\cdot)$ explicit.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Diagonalization via Kleene's Recursion Theorem}
\label{subsec:kleene-diagonal}

\begin{theorem}[No total emulator of PT]
\label{thm:no-total-emulator}
There is no total $\Eff$--morphism $M$ such that for every admissible choice point $\mathcal C$, $M(\ulcorner \mathcal C\urcorner)=\PT(\mathcal C)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Assume a total emulator $M$ exists. By Kleene's Recursion Theorem there is a code $e$ such that $\mathcal C_e$ (a computably defined pair of admissible branches) can access its own code and the emulator's output. Define $\mathcal C_e$ so that it selects the branch \emph{opposite} to $M(\ulcorner \mathcal C_e\urcorner)$ while keeping $D$ tied. Then $M(\ulcorner \mathcal C_e\urcorner)\neq \PT(\mathcal C_e)$ by construction, a contradiction.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Non-clonability of PT]
\label{cor:no-clone}
There is no local admissible process that replicates the full input--output graph of $\PT$ on all admissible choice points.
\end{corollary}

\subsection{Approximate Adjudication and Arithmetic Hierarchy}
\label{subsec:approx-pt}

Kolmogorov complexity $K(\cdot)$ is \emph{upper semicomputable}: there exist total computable monotone bounds $K_t(\cdot)\downarrow K(\cdot)$. Define the stage-$t$ surrogate
\[
\PT^{(t)}(\mathcal C)\;=\;\arg\min_{\gamma\in\mathcal B}\Big(D(\gamma)+\lambda\,K_t(\text{code}(\gamma))\Big),
\]
with fixed code tie-breaker.

\begin{proposition}[Limit computability under uniqueness]
\label{prop:delta02}
If the MDL minimizer is unique (i.e.\ there is a strict gap $\delta>0$ between the smallest and second smallest true MDL values), then there exists $t_0$ such that for all $t\ge t_0$, $\PT^{(t)}(\mathcal C)=\PT(\mathcal C)$. Hence, under uniqueness, $\PT$ is $\Delta^0_2$ (limit computable).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Monotone convergence $K_t\downarrow K$ implies eventual stabilization of the order whenever there is a strict margin $\delta>0$. The unique minimizer is preserved once the approximation error drops below $\delta/2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
Pathological tie cases (zero margin) may prevent stabilization. This mirrors the standard boundary phenomena in MDL model selection with non-identifiable optima.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Physical lawfulness of supra-computational adjudication]
\label{rem:lawful-uncomputable}
Non-computability here is \emph{relative} to the admissible evaluator (the $\Eff$ fragment):
it states that no Turing-equivalent internal process evaluates the global MDL extremum exactly.
Lawfulness follows from existence and continuity: the argmin of
$D+\lambda C$ over a compact admissible set exists by standard extremal principles, just as
least-action principles select physically realized trajectories without requiring a constructive
algorithm. Thus $\PT$ is lawful and determinate while remaining supra-computational relative
to $\Eff$.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Ontological Dissonance and the Principle of Coherence}
\label{subsec:dissonance}

We recall the \emph{Ontological Dissonance} functional \(D\) that operationalizes the Principle of Coherence (RR/TFTT). At a coarse level,
\[
D \;=\; w_{\mathrm{inc}}\, D_{\mathrm{inc}} \;+\; w_{\mathrm{comp}}\, D_{\mathrm{comp}}
\;+\; w_{\mathrm{temp}}\, D_{\mathrm{temp}} \;+\; w_{\mathrm{clos}}\, D_{\mathrm{clos}},
\]
with positive weights and: (i) \(D_{\mathrm{inc}}\) penalizing spatial roughness/inconsistency, (ii) \(D_{\mathrm{comp}}\) penalizing incompleteness/diffuseness, (iii) \(D_{\mathrm{temp}}\) penalizing pathological temporal instability, and (iv) \(D_{\mathrm{clos}}\) penalizing failure of recurrence/self-similarity. Choice Points are degenerate critical points of \(D\) (ties).

In the information-geometric regime (\cref{sec:geometry}), \(D\) is represented on \((\Man,\Fisher)\) and its curvature lift yields the global complexity
\[
\Omega \;=\; \int_{\Man} R_F(\theta)\sqrt{\det \Fisher(\theta)}\, d^k\theta,
\]
with local density \(\omega=R_F\sqrt{\det\Fisher}\). The coherence field \(\Psi\) is the macroscopic order parameter that lowers \(D\); its energetic footprint is the \emph{coherence energy}
\[
\mathcal{E}_\Psi \;=\; \int_{\mathcal{U}}\big(\alpha_1 \Psi^2 + \alpha_2 \|\nabla \Psi\|^2\big)\, dV,
\]
and the energetic–complexity law \(dE=\alpha_0\, d\Omega\) links geometric complexity to energy. Combining these gives the Reflexive Landauer inequality (\cref{thm:RefLandauer-rigorous}), making explicit that adjudication lowers \(D\) while incurring a physically measurable energy cost.

\section{The Insufficiency of Stochasticity: A No-Go Theorem for Random Resolution}
\label{sec:insufficiency-of-stochasticity}

A critical question arises when considering the resolution of indeterminacy at Choice Points: why is a lawful, non-computable adjudicator like Transputation (PT) necessary? Could a fundamentally stochastic universe not resolve these degeneracies through random quantum fluctuations, obviating the need for PT and the entire reflexive architecture it supports? This section answers this question definitively by proving a no-go theorem: any universe capable of producing the stable, complex, and coherent structures we observe cannot be governed by purely stochastic resolutions.

\begin{theorem}[No-Go Theorem for Stochastic Resolution]
\label{thm:no-go-stochastic}
Let a universe be described by a computable framework that satisfies the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item \textbf{Existence of Complexity:} It permits the existence of stable, complex, self-organizing structures (e.g., galaxies, stars, life).
    \item \textbf{Parsimony:} It is maximally parsimonious, containing no unexplained, externally postulated meta-laws (in accordance with the principle of Perfect Self-Containment).
\end{enumerate}
Then, the mechanism for resolving computational and physical degeneracies (Choice Points) in such a universe cannot be purely stochastic. It must be a lawful, coherence-preserving process.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The proof proceeds by contradiction, demonstrating that the assumption of a purely stochastic resolution mechanism violates the premises. Assume that all Choice Points are resolved by a random process (a "stochastic kick"). We show this leads to three independent contradictions.

The "purely stochastic" or "random" process described here can be formalized using the principles of algorithmic information theory, founded by Kolmogorov, Chaitin, and L.~A.~Levin~\cite{Levin1973}. A sequence is defined as algorithmically random if it is incompressible---that is, its shortest possible description (its Kolmogorov complexity) is equal to its own length. Such a sequence is, by definition, devoid of patterns or compressible structure. The injection of this "Levin-style randomness" is therefore equivalent to injecting maximal-entropy, high-Kolmogorov-complexity noise. As our computational validations confirm (see Appendix~\ref{app:levin-profit-validation}), this form of noise acts as a powerful "drain" that corrupts the information profit accounting necessary for self-organization. In a profound synthesis, the very metric of this randomness---compressibility, or description length---is what the Transputation operator minimizes (via MDL) to select for \emph{non-random}, coherent states, thereby using the language of randomness to lawfully create order.

\paragraph{1. Contradiction with the Existence of Complexity.}
This is not merely a theoretical argument; it is a computationally verified fact. Our own computational validation of the Information Profit Principle (Theorem \ref{thm:info-profit} and Test E35) provides a decisive, empirical refutation of the stochastic alternative. In these simulations, we demonstrated that while self-organizing structures are robust to internal, multiplicative noise, they are catastrophically corrupted by untracked, additive noise, which destroys the system's ability to perform the necessary "profit accounting" and drives the viability threshold down by nearly 50\%.

A stochastic resolution mechanism is, by its very nature, a source of perpetual, internal, additive noise. The E35 result thus serves as the \textbf{steel-man experiment for this No-Go Theorem}. It proves that a universe governed by random adjudications would be fundamentally incapable of achieving the sustained information profit required to build any complex structure. It would be a universe of universal, perpetual decoherence and decay, unable to satisfy premise (i). This is a contradiction. The existence of a single stable galaxy, star, or living cell is therefore empirical proof that the resolution of indeterminacy in our universe is lawful and coherence-preserving, not random.

\paragraph{2. Contradiction with Parsimony and the Ontological Burden of Stochasticity.}
Postulating a "stochastic" resolution violates premise (ii) by introducing an unexplained and ontologically burdensome meta-law. To see this, we must ask: where does this randomness originate? There are only two possibilities: it is either the product of a deeper, deterministic process, or it is a fundamental, irreducible feature of reality.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{If it is generated by a deeper process:} If the randomness is generated by a computable law or physical process, it is not truly random. It is pseudo-random, a product of "hidden determinism." This does not solve the problem; it merely hides the deterministic mechanism one level deeper, making the theory less parsimonious.
    \item \textbf{If it is a fundamental primitive:} The only alternative is to posit that "pure randomness" is a fundamental, ontological primitive—a brute fact of existence. This introduces an inexplicable "magic" into the cosmos: a source of acausality at the very heart of reality. It is an axiom of lawlessness used to explain the emergence of law, a profound contradiction. Furthermore, if randomness is the fundamental ground, the emergence of the apparently deterministic, lawful, and predictable macroscopic world becomes a profound mystery rather than an explanation.
\end{itemize}
From the perspective of Minimum Description Length (MDL), a universe founded on a single, deterministic, self-consistent principle (like reflexive closure) is vastly more parsimonious than a universe requiring two fundamental principles: one for determinism and another for an independent, acausal source of pure randomness. Reflexive Reality offers a more elegant and powerful solution. It does not postulate randomness. It \emph{derives} the \emph{appearance} of randomness in quantum measurements as a statistical consequence of a deeper, lawful (though non-computable) deterministic process, as proven by the PT–Born Bridge (Theorem \ref{thm:PTBorn-strong}). Therefore, the stochastic model fails the test of parsimony. It is either a disguised form of hidden determinism or it introduces an ontologically burdensome and unexplained primitive that makes the existence of a lawful universe less, not more, likely.

\paragraph{3. Contradiction with Observed Fine-Structure.}
The universe is not a generic, featureless thermal bath. It contains the highly specific, non-generic structures of the Standard Model of particle physics. A stochastic resolution model has zero explanatory power for this observed fine-structure. There is no conceivable mechanism by which random kicks would conspire to produce the precise mass of the top quark, the CKM mixing angles, or the binding energies of atomic nuclei.

The RR framework, with its principle of lawful adjudication, successfully derives these values from first principles. The computational proof that the Standard Model is the 97\%-attractor of the Self-Referential Renormalization Group (SRRG) flow (Theorem \ref{thm:SM-FP}) is dispositive evidence that the resolution of indeterminacy in our universe is lawful and directed by a deep principle of coherence. The specific, observed order of our universe is a direct signature of a lawful, not random, process.

\paragraph{Conclusion of Proof.}
Each of these three arguments independently shows that the assumption of a purely stochastic resolution mechanism is incompatible with the observed nature of our universe and the principles of parsimony. Therefore, the resolution of indeterminacy must be a lawful, coherence-preserving process. This proves the necessity of a mechanism with the formal properties of Transputation.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The Emergence of Apparent Stochasticity from Deterministic Reflexivity}

The No-Go Theorem for Stochastic Resolution proves that randomness cannot be a fundamental principle of a coherent universe. This raises a crucial question: if the underlying reality is deterministic, why does it \emph{appear} stochastic at the quantum level? Reflexive Reality provides a complete and self-consistent answer: apparent randomness is an emergent phenomenon arising from the fundamental limitations of any local observer within a global, reflexively computing system.

\paragraph{Mechanism 1: Informational Coarse-Graining and the PT--Born Bridge.}

A single transputational event is fully deterministic, but its outcome is determined by the global coherence state of the universe, minimizing the total dissonance functional. Any observer, being a proper subsystem of the universe, is necessarily local. It lacks access to the complete, global information state required to predict the outcome of the adjudication.

\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Fundamental Unpredictability:} The No-Emulation Theorem (Thm.~\ref{thm:NoEmulation}) proves that the outcome of a PT event is non-computable for any observer \emph{within} the system. For a local observer, an event that is deterministic but fundamentally unpredictable is operationally indistinguishable from a random event.
    \item \textbf{Derivation of Probability:} The PT--Born Bridge (Thm.~\ref{thm:PTBorn-strong}) completes the picture. It proves that an ensemble of such unpredictable, MDL-driven adjudication events must, statistically, conform to the Born rule probabilities.
\end{itemize}

Therefore, quantum probability is not a sign of fundamental randomness. It is the necessary statistical manifestation of a deeper, lawful, but non-computable determinism, as perceived by an informationally coarse-grained internal observer.

\paragraph{Mechanism 2: Vacuum Fluctuations as Unresolved Micro-Adjudications.}

Phenomena like quantum vacuum fluctuations, which appear as a stochastic foam of virtual particles, can be understood within RR as the macroscopic statistical signature of a dense sea of unresolved microscopic Choice Points. The UGP substrate at the Planck scale is not static; it is a dynamic computational medium.

\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Micro-CPs:} The ground state of this substrate is filled with latent, primordial Choice Points that are constantly being formed and resolved by PT.
    \item \textbf{Coarse-Grained View:} A macroscopic observer, whose instruments lack the resolution to track each individual, deterministic micro-adjudication, perceives only the aggregate statistical effect. This appears as a random, fluctuating field. It is analogous to hearing the ``white noise'' of a distant waterfall without being able to resolve the motion of individual water molecules. The underlying process is deterministic, but the coarse-grained perception is stochastic.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Mechanism 3: Computational Irreducibility and the Limit of Prediction.}

The deterministic evolution of the UGP substrate itself provides a powerful source of apparent randomness, as described by the principle of Computational Irreducibility~\cite{Wolfram2002}. For many complex computational systems, even if their underlying rules are simple and deterministic, their long-term behavior cannot be predicted by any shortcut. The only way to determine the future state is to execute the computation step-by-step.

The evolution of the reflexive substrate between Choice Points is a prime example of such a computationally irreducible process. To any observer embedded within the system, who cannot out-compute the universe itself, the detailed evolution of the substrate is fundamentally unpredictable in practice. Its behavior, while deterministic, would pass all statistical tests for randomness.

Reflexive Reality thus provides a dual-layered explanation for apparent stochasticity that is far more robust than either principle alone:
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Between Choice Points:} The evolution is deterministic but \emph{computationally irreducible}, making its detailed behavior practically unpredictable.
    \item \textbf{At Choice Points:} The evolution is deterministic but \emph{fundamentally non-computable}, making its outcome logically unpredictable to any internal observer.
\end{itemize}

This synthesis demonstrates that the apparent randomness of the quantum world is not a sign of fundamental lawlessness. It is the necessary consequence of observing a universe of profound, layered, deterministic complexity from a limited, internal perspective.

\section{Reflexive Geometry and the Coherence Field}
\label{sec:geometry}

\paragraph{Section summary.}
We construct the Fisher information manifold, prove the Choice--Curvature Correspondence linking adjudicative degeneracy to Ricci curvature, derive the coherence field $\Psi$ and its scaling law $\Psi\propto\Omega$, and obtain the information stress-energy tensor $\Cten_{\mu\nu}$ coupling to Einstein's equations.

\subsection{Assumptions and Regularity}
\label{asm:geom-regularity}
Throughout this section we assume:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \((\Man,\Fisher)\) is a smooth, connected statistical manifold of finite dimension \(k\), with Fisher information metric \(\Fisher_{ij}=\EE_\theta[\partial_i\log p_\theta\,\partial_j\log p_\theta]\).
  \item The manifold is orientable and either compact or admits a compact exhaustion ensuring integrability of curvature scalars.
  \item The dissonance functional \(D:\Man\to\RR_{\ge0}\) is \(C^2\) with nondegenerate Hessian except at finitely many degenerate critical points (Choice Points).
  \item Metric signature for emergent spacetime coupling is \(+---\); units \(c=\hbar=1\).
  \item Gradients and divergences are taken with respect to \(\Fisher\); all integrals use the measure \(\sqrt{\det\Fisher}\,d^k\theta\).
\end{enumerate}

We use \((\Omega,\omega)\) as the curvature lifts of the dissonance functional \(D\) under Fisher geometry, consistent with \cref{subsec:dissonance}.

\subsection{Geometric Complexity and Local Density}
\label{subsec:geom-complexity}
\begin{definition}[Geometric Complexity and Density]
\label{def:Omega}
The \emph{geometric complexity} of a Reflexive System is
\begin{equation}
\OmegaGlobal=\int_{\Man}\Rsc(\theta)\sqrt{\det\Fisher(\theta)}\,d^k\theta,
\end{equation}
where \(\Rsc=\Fisher^{ij}\Ric_{ij}\) is the scalar curvature of the Fisher metric.  The \emph{local complexity density} is
\(\omegalocal(\theta)=\Rsc(\theta)\sqrt{\det\Fisher(\theta)}\).  The pair \((\OmegaGlobal,\omegalocal)\) measures the total and pointwise curvature of informational space and quantifies the system’s intrinsic capacity for integrated information processing.
\end{definition}

\subsection{Choice--Curvature Correspondence}
\label{subsec:choice-curvature}

\paragraph{Reflexive Ensemble fluctuations.}
The dissonance functional \(D:\Man\to\RR\) experiences small quantum fluctuations generated by the coherence field \(\psifield\). We model these as \(D(\theta)=D_0(\theta)+\epsilon\,\eta(\theta)\), where \(\EE[\eta(\theta)]=0\) and \(\EE[\eta(\theta)\eta(\theta')]=C(\theta,\theta')\) is a smooth, rapidly decaying covariance. The \textbf{Reflexive Ensemble} is the probability measure on dissonance configurations induced by this microscopic noise:
\[
\mathcal{P}[D]\propto
\exp\left[-\frac{1}{2}
\int (D-D_0)(\theta)\,C^{-1}(\theta,\theta')(D-D_0)(\theta')\,d\theta\,d\theta'
\right].
\]
This ensemble permits rigorous application of the Kac--Rice formula for computing expected CP densities.

\begin{theorem}[Reflexive Choice--Curvature Correspondence]
\label{thm:ChoiceCurv}
Let \((\Man,\Fisher)\) be a compact \(k\)-dimensional information manifold and \(D:\Man\to\RR\) an admissible dissonance functional.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Ensemble (stochastic) regime.} For the Reflexive Ensemble defined above, the mean CP density obeys
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:ensemble-CP-density}
\EE[\rho_{\mathrm{CP}}]=\beta\,(\mathrm{Ric}_{F})^++\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^2),
\end{equation}
where \(\beta=(2\pi)^{-k/2}\sqrt{\det\Sigma_{\nabla^2D}}/\sqrt{\det C_{\nabla D}}\) is an ensemble constant and \((\mathrm{Ric}_{F})^+=\max(\mathrm{Ric}_{F},0)\) is the positive part of the Fisher Ricci scalar. \vspace{-0.05em}
\item \textbf{Deterministic (Morse) regime.} For smooth, non-random \(D\), the number of critical points satisfies the Morse--Smale bound
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:morse-CP-bound}
N_{\mathrm{CP}}\ge \kappa\int_{\Man}|\mathrm{Ric}_{F}|\sqrt{\det\Fisher}\,d^k\theta,
\end{equation}
for some constant \(\kappa>0\) depending on the chosen norm and coordinate chart.
\end{enumerate}
These relations connect topological complexity, curvature, and adjudicative structure without appealing to any ensemble average beyond controllable \(\epsilon\) corrections.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
\textbf{Part (i):} Choice Points occur where \(\nabla D(\theta)=0\) and \(\det(\nabla_i\nabla_jD)=0\). The expected density of such degeneracies in the Reflexive Ensemble is given by the Kac--Rice functional:
\[
\EE[\rho_{\mathrm{CP}}(\theta)]
= \EE\left[\delta(\nabla D(\theta))\,|\det(\nabla_i\nabla_j D(\theta))|\right].
\]
Expanding in \(\epsilon\) using standard Gaussian-field calculus and noting that the MDL potential induces a metric proportional to \(\Fisher^{-1}\), the curvature of \(D\)'s gradient flow coincides (up to normalization) with the Ricci curvature of \(\Fisher\). Counting positive degeneracy directions yields proportionality to \((\mathrm{Ric}_{F})^+\).

\textbf{Part (ii):} For deterministic smooth \(D\), classical Morse theory applies. Let \(m(\lambda)\) denote the number of non-degenerate critical points of index \(\lambda\). The Morse inequalities yield:
\[
\sum_{\lambda=0}^k (-1)^\lambda m(\lambda)
= \chi(\Man),
\]
and consequently
\[
N_{\mathrm{CP}}
= \sum_{\lambda=0}^k m(\lambda)
\ge \sum_{\lambda=0}^k |\chi_\lambda|
\ge |\chi(\Man)|.
\]
Since information curvature controls the density of degenerate Hessian directions, integrating over \(\Man\) yields the deterministic inequality \eqref{eq:morse-CP-bound}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Physical interpretation]
The two regimes complement each other:
\begin{itemize}
    \item In the \textbf{stochastic regime}, quantum fluctuations of \(\psifield\) induce an ensemble of dissonance landscapes. Regions of positive information curvature \((\mathrm{Ric}_{F})^+\) are statistical loci where lawful adjudication (\(\PT\)) is required.
    \item In the \textbf{deterministic regime}, the Morse bound provides a topological lower limit on CP count, ensuring that adjudicative structure is tied to the manifold's intrinsic topology (\(\chi(\Man)\)).
\end{itemize}
Flat regions evolve deterministically; negative curvature corresponds to divergent, chaotic manifolds lacking coherent resolution.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Connection to Mirror PSC index]
When integrated over \(\Man\), the deterministic bound \eqref{eq:morse-CP-bound} recovers the conserved PT--Quarter-Lock index \(\mathcal{I}_{\PT} = N_{\mathrm{CP}} - \chi(\Man)\) established in the topological framework (Section~\ref{sec:topology}), providing a bridge between continuous curvature dynamics and discrete braid operations.
\end{remark}

\begin{lemma}[Two-regime scaling of $\Psi$--$\Omega$ relation]
\label{lem:PsiOmega-regimes}
In the massive, quasi-static regime ($\nabla^2\Psi\approx m^2\Psi$), the coupling 
$\Omega\propto \Psi$ holds with exponent $\alpha=1$. 
In the boundary-dominated or massless regime ($m\to0$, Dirichlet/Neumann BCs), 
the integrated Green function yields $\Omega\propto\Psi^{3/2}$. 
Hence the empirical scaling exponent $\alpha$ lies in $[1,3/2]$ 
depending on curvature and boundary conditions.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
In the massive regime, the equation $(\nabla^2 - m^2)\Psi = J$ with source $J \propto \omega$ yields $\Psi \sim m^{-2}\int J dV \propto m^{-2}\Omega$ (linear scaling). In the massless regime $m \to 0$ with compact boundary, the Green function $G(x,x')$ behaves as $|x-x'|^{2-d}$ in $d$ dimensions; integrating over the source gives $\Psi(x) \sim \int G(x,x')J(x')dV' \propto \Omega^{(2-d)/d}$. For $d=3$, this yields $\alpha = 3/2$. The crossover between regimes depends on the ratio $m\ell$ where $\ell$ is the system size.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Holonomy Defect and Geometric Incompleteness}
\label{subsec:holonomy-defect}

\begin{theorem}[Holonomy defect \(\Rightarrow\) no global potential]
\label{thm:holonomy-defect}
Let \(\mathcal{M}\) be a state manifold whose balance between discrete growth and continuous closure exhibits a nonzero holonomy defect \(\delta \neq 0\). Then there is no globally defined single-valued potential \(\Phi:\mathcal{M}\to\mathbb{R}\) whose gradient generates the macrodynamics; equivalently, the state space is not globally flat. 
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textit{Sketch.} Parallel transport around a fundamental cycle accumulates a nonvanishing phase proportional to \(\delta\), implying path-dependence of the line integral and hence non-exactness of the would-be global one-form. Therefore \(\mathcal{M}\) has intrinsic curvature and no single global potential exists. \hfill\(\square\)

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Interpretation.} The obstruction \(\delta\neq 0\) is the geometric counterpart of the Gödel--Turing--Tarski barrier: it forbids a globally hierarchical, flat description. In the information-geometric formulation, the same obstruction appears as positive Ricci sectors in which Choice Points concentrate (Choice--Curvature correspondence), requiring lawful adjudication \(\PT\). This provides an independent geometric route to the necessity of internal transputation, converging with the logical and physical arguments to form a three-way proof that reflexive closure is unavoidable in any self-consistent universe.

\subsection{The Coherence Field and Scaling Law}
\label{subsec:psi-field}
\begin{definition}[Coherence Field \(\Psifield\)]
\label{def:Psi}
The macroscopic \emph{Coherence Field} is a scalar field \(\Psifield:\Man\to\RR\) representing the local density of transputational coherence, defined phenomenologically by
\begin{equation}
\Psifield(\theta)\propto \int_{\mathcal{N}(\theta)} \frac{1}{1+D(\theta')}\,\sqrt{\det\Fisher(\theta')}\,d^k\theta',
\end{equation}
where \(\mathcal{N}(\theta)\) is a neighborhood of \(\theta\) weighted by inverse dissonance.

\paragraph{Terminology and operational meaning.}
In other work~\cite{SpivackUGPMath,SpivackSDS_PR0} we have sometimes referred to \(\Psifield\) as the ``consciousness field.'' However, this is strictly an order-parameter for macroscopic informational coherence on \((\Man,\Fisher)\); it does \emph{not} imply subjective awareness or phenomenology. For clarity on this issue, in the present paper we adopt the neutral term ``coherence field,'' emphasizing that \(\Psifield\) encodes integrated self-consistency as a physical quantity without psychological connotations.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Adjudicative Manifold]
\label{def:MCP}
An \emph{Adjudicative Manifold} $M_{\mathrm{CP}}$ is a smooth manifold equipped with a coherence field $\Psifield$, Fisher information metric $g_{\mu\nu}$, and a choice-point foliation whose leaves represent admissible degeneracy manifolds for $\PT$; local neighborhoods carry a well-defined Laplace--Beltrami operator $\Delta_{M_{\mathrm{CP}}}$ coupled to $\Psifield$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Spectral Structure of Adjudicative Manifolds]
\label{thm:spectral-MCP}
Let $M_{\mathrm{CP}}$ be an Adjudicative Manifold in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:MCP},
equipped with the Fisher information metric $g_{\mu\nu}$ inherited from the underlying
statistical manifold of reflexive states. Let $\Delta_{M_{\mathrm{CP}}}$ denote the associated
Laplace--Beltrami operator, and let $m^2(\theta)$ be the effective reflexive mass term arising
from the local curvature of the coherence field $\Psifield$.

Assume that $M_{\mathrm{CP}}$ is compact (or that $\Psifield$ satisfies confining boundary
conditions ensuring ellipticity of the associated operator). Then the
self--adjoint operator
\[
L \;\equiv\; -\Delta_{M_{\mathrm{CP}}} + m^2
\]
acting on $L^2(M_{\mathrm{CP}})$ possesses the following properties:

\begin{enumerate}
\item $L$ has a purely discrete spectrum $\{\omega_n^2\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ with
$0 < \omega_1^2 \le \omega_2^2 \le \dots$ and $\omega_n^2 \to \infty$ as $n\to\infty$.

\item There exists a complete orthonormal basis $\{\psi_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$
of smooth eigenfunctions satisfying
\[
L\psi_n = \omega_n^2\psi_n ,
\qquad
\langle \psi_m,\psi_n\rangle = \delta_{mn}.
\]

\item Any admissible coherence field $\Psifield(t,\theta)$ on $M_{\mathrm{CP}}$ admits
a normal--mode decomposition
\[
\Psifield(t,\theta)
=
\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n(t)\,\psi_n(\theta),
\]
where the mode amplitudes obey the driven generalized harmonic oscillator equation
\[
\ddot{a}_n + \omega_n^2 a_n = F_n(t)
\]
for external generalized forces $F_n(t)$ induced by reflexive interactions.
\end{enumerate}

Thus the dynamics of $\Psifield$ on $M_{\mathrm{CP}}$ separate cleanly into a countable
family of natural adjudicative eigenmodes.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[\(\Psi\)--\(\Omega\) Scaling in the Massive Regime]
\label{thm:PsiOmega-massive}
Let $(\Man,\mathcal I)$ be a compact $d$-dimensional Fisher manifold with bounded geometry. Suppose $\Psi$ solves
\[
-\Delta_F \Psi + m^2 \Psi \;=\; \kappa\,\omega, \qquad
\omega(\theta)=R_F(\theta)\sqrt{\det\mathcal I(\theta)}\in L^2(\Man),
\]
with $m>0$, $\kappa>0$. Let $B_r\subset\Man$ be a geodesic ball with $m r\gg 1$ and define \(\displaystyle \overline{\Psi}(B_r)=\frac{1}{\mathrm{Vol}_F(B_r)}\int_{B_r}\Psi\,d\mu_F\) and \(\displaystyle \Omega(B_r)=\int_{B_r} R_F\,d\mu_F\). Then there exists $C=C(m,\kappa,\Man)>0$ such that
\[
\overline{\Psi}(B_r)\;=\; C\,\frac{\Omega(B_r)}{\mathrm{Vol}_F(B_r)}\;+\;o(1)
\qquad (mr\to\infty).
\]
In particular, the volume average of $\Psi$ is linear in the integrated complexity density on $B_r$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Write $\Psi=G_m\ast(\kappa\,\omega)$ where $G_m$ is the Green kernel of $(-\Delta_F+m^2)$. For $mr\gg 1$, $G_m$ is exponentially localized at scale $m^{-1}$, so averaging over $B_r$ smears $\omega$ with a nearly constant kernel, yielding \(\overline{\Psi}(B_r)\approx \kappa\,\overline{G}_m\cdot \overline{\omega}(B_r)\). Since $\overline{\omega}(B_r)=\Omega(B_r)/\mathrm{Vol}_F(B_r)$, the claim follows; the $o(1)$ term is controlled by standard elliptic estimates and bounded geometry.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Boundary/critical regimes]
When $m\to 0$ or $mr\lesssim 1$, boundary data and long-range Green function tails alter the exponent; the empirical $3/2$ law reported in Sec.~\ref{subsec:psi-field} corresponds to boundary-influenced or massless-like regimes and is stated separately as an empirical scaling.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Scaling Law under standard Fisher scaling]
\label{thm:PsiScaling-Refined}
Let \((\Man,\Fisher)\) be a \(d\)-dimensional Fisher information manifold satisfying: (i) scale dilation \(\varphi_\lambda^\ast \Fisher=\lambda^{2}\Fisher\); (ii) scalar curvature scaling \(R_F(\varphi_\lambda(\theta))=\lambda^{-2}R_F(\theta)\); (iii) bounded geometry as in \textbf{(S3)}. Let \(\Psifield\) solve the elliptic equation
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:elliptic-Psi}
-\,\Delta_F \Psifield + m^2 \Psifield = \kappa\,\omegalocal,\qquad \omegalocal\equiv R_F\sqrt{\det\Fisher}.
\end{equation}
Then on geodesic balls \(B_r\) in the quasi-static massive regime \((m r\gg 1)\),
\[
\overline{\Psifield}(B_r)=\frac{1}{\mathrm{Vol}_F(B_r)}\int_{B_r}\Psifield\,d\mu_F \;=\; C\,\Omega(B_r)\,\mathrm{Vol}_F(B_r)^{-1}+o(1)\;\propto\;\Omega(B_r),
\]
where \(\Omega(B_r)=\int_{B_r}R_F\,d\mu_F\) and \(C>0\) is a constant depending on \((m,\kappa)\). In particular, the volume-average scales linearly with the integrated complexity in this regime. In massless or boundary-dominated regimes the scaling exponent depends on boundary data and Green's function asymptotics; we report empirical exponents separately.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Work in a chart where \(\varphi_\lambda\) acts as a dilation. Scale the ball: \(B_r=\varphi_r(B_1)\).
By (S1), \(\Fisher\) scales as \(\Fisher\mapsto r^2\Fisher\) and \(R_F\mapsto r^{-1}R_F\). The Fisher volume element scales as \(d\mu_F=\sqrt{\det\Fisher}\,d^d\theta\mapsto r^d\,d\mu_F\). Hence
\[
\Omega(B_r)=\int_{B_r} R_F\,d\mu_F \;\sim\; r^{d-1}\,\Omega(B_1)
\quad\text{as } r\to\infty.
\]
Next, rescale the elliptic equation \eqref{eq:elliptic-Psi} to the unit ball using \(\varphi_r^\ast\) and define \(\widetilde{\Psifield}(\theta)=\Psifield(\varphi_r(\theta))\). Since \(-\Delta_F + m^2\) has the principal term scaling as \(r^{-2}\Delta_F\) under \(\Fisher\mapsto r^2\Fisher\), while the source scales as \(\omegalocal\mapsto r^{d-1}\,\omegalocal\), a standard parametrix/Green's function estimate (or energy method) yields
\[
\int_{B_r}\Psifield\,d\mu_F
\;\sim\; r^{d}\,\Big(\int_{B_1}\widetilde{\Psifield}\,d\mu_F\Big)
\;\sim\; r^{d}\, \Big(\text{const}\times r^{\frac{d-1}{1}}\Big)
\;=\; \text{const}\times r^{d+\,(d-1)}.
\]
Dividing by \(\mathrm{Vol}_F(B_r)\sim r^d\) gives \(\overline{\Psifield}(B_r)\sim r^{d-1}\). Using \(\Omega(B_r)\sim r^{d-1}\), we conclude
\[
\overline{\Psifield}(B_r) \;\propto\; \big(\Omega(B_r)\big)^{\,\frac{d}{d-1}}.
\]
For \(d=3\) the exponent is \(3/2\). Elliptic regularity and bounded geometry (S3) control the \(o(1)\) error.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Empirical exponent and domain of validity]
The theorem above establishes linear scaling (\(\overline{\Psi}\propto\Omega\)) in the massive quasi-static regime with standard curvature scaling. Empirical validation (E3, Appendix~\ref{app:reflexive-toy}) finds exponents ranging from \(\alpha\approx 1.5\) to \(\alpha\approx 1.0\) depending on the regime and boundary conditions. The \(3/2\) exponent observed in specific numerical tests may correspond to a boundary-dominated or massless regime with different effective scaling laws; we report these as empirical findings pending full analysis of the Green's function asymptotics in those regimes. The critical threshold \(\Omega_c\) below which no stable \(\Psifield\)-phase exists follows from percolation theory on the Fisher manifold, analogous to phase transitions in connectivity.
\end{remark}
