\subsection{Information/Complexity Stress-Energy Tensor}
\label{subsec:C-tensor}
From the covariant Lagrangian density for the coherence field \(\Psifield\) and local complexity \(\omegalocal\),
\[
\Lag_\Psi=\tfrac{1}{2}\,\nabla^\mu\Psifield\,\nabla_\mu\Psifield - \tfrac{1}{2}\mu^2\Psifield^2 - V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Psifield,\omegalocal),
\]
the canonical stress-energy tensor is
\[
\TtenPsi_{\mu\nu} = \nabla_\mu\Psifield\,\nabla_\nu\Psifield - \tfrac{1}{2}g_{\mu\nu}\big(\nabla^\alpha\Psifield\,\nabla_\alpha\Psifield-\mu^2\Psifield^2-2V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Psifield,\omegalocal)\big).
\]
In the total information sector we write \( \Cten_{\mu\nu} \equiv \TtenPsi_{\mu\nu} + \XiTen_{\mu\nu}\), where \(\XiTen_{\mu\nu}\) is introduced in Theorem~\ref{thm:InfoGravCoupling-Refined}.
Variation of the total action \(S=\int(\Rsc+2\Lambda+8\pi G(\Tten_{\mu\nu}+\Cten_{\mu\nu}))\sqrt{-g}\,d^4x\) yields modified Einstein equations \(\Gten_{\mu\nu}=8\pi G(\Tten_{\mu\nu}+\Cten_{\mu\nu})\).
The potential \(V\) encodes the energetic cost of coherence maintenance derived from the Reflexive Landauer inequality (\cref{thm:RefLandauer-rigorous}).

\subsection{Information--Gravity Coupling and Bundle Euler--Lagrange Equations}
\label{subsec:info-grav-coupling-refined}

We now formalize the coupling between the information-geometric manifold \((\Man,\Fisher)\) and physical spacetime \((M_{\text{ST}},g_{\mu\nu})\) via a rigorous variational principle on a fibered total space. This establishes the origin of the information stress-energy tensor \(\Cten\) from first principles and proves covariant energy-momentum conservation.

We adopt explicit gravitational units with \(8\pi G\) retained.

\paragraph{Setup: The Total Configuration Bundle.}
Let the spacetime manifold \(\mathcal{M}_{\text{ST}}\) (dimension 4) and the information manifold \(\Man\) (dimension \(k\)) form a total space \(\mathcal{X} = \mathcal{M}_{\text{ST}} \times \Man\) (trivial bundle for simplicity, with projection \(\pi:\mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{M}_{\text{ST}}\)).

\textbf{Coordinates:} \(x^\mu\) on the base (spacetime), \(\theta^i\) on the fiber (information manifold).

\textbf{Total metric:} We assume a block-diagonal structure:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:block-diagonal-metric}
\hat{g}_{AB} = 
\begin{pmatrix}
g_{\mu\nu}(x) & 0 \\
0 & \Fisher_{ij}(x,\theta)
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\det\hat{g} = (\det g) \cdot (\det \Fisher).
\end{equation}
Here \(g_{\mu\nu}\) is the spacetime metric (signature \(+---\)), and \(\Fisher_{ij}\) is the Fisher information metric on the fiber, which may depend on both base and fiber coordinates.

\textbf{Fields:} 
\begin{itemize}
    \item Scalar field \(\Psi(x,\theta)\) living on the total space.
    \item Local information-complexity density \(\omega(\theta) \equiv R_F[\Fisher](\theta)\sqrt{\det\Fisher(\theta)}\), where \(R_F[\Fisher]\) is the scalar curvature of the Fisher metric.
    \item Local potential \(V(\Psi,\omega)\).
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Action Functional.}
The total action integrates over the full bundle:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:bundle-action}
S[g,\Fisher,\Psi] = \frac{1}{16\pi G}\int_{\mathcal{X}} \sqrt{-g}\,\sqrt{\det \Fisher}\,
\Big( R[g] + R_F[\Fisher] \Big)\, d^4x\, d^k\theta \;+\; S_\Psi,
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
S_\Psi = -\int_{\mathcal{X}} \sqrt{-g}\,\sqrt{\det \Fisher}\,\Big( \tfrac{1}{2}\,\hat g^{AB}\nabla_A\Psi\nabla_B\Psi + V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Psi,\omega) \Big)\, d^4x\, d^k\theta,
\end{equation}
where \(R[g]\) is the spacetime Ricci scalar, \(R_F[\Fisher]\) is the Fisher manifold's scalar curvature, and \(\hat{g}^{AB}\) is the inverse of the total metric \eqref{eq:block-diagonal-metric}.

\paragraph{Variational Derivation.}

\textbf{Step 1: Variation with respect to \(g_{\mu\nu}\).}
The variation of the total action with respect to the spacetime metric yields:
\begin{equation}
\frac{\delta S}{\delta g^{\mu\nu}} = 
\int_{\Man} \sqrt{\det\Fisher}\,
\Big\{
\sqrt{-g}\,\big[ G_{\mu\nu}[g] - T^{(\Psi)}_{\mu\nu} - \XiTen_{\mu\nu} \big]
\Big\}\, d^k\theta = 0,
\end{equation}
where the matter stress-energy from the \(\Psi\)-field kinetic term is:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:T-Psi}
T^{(\Psi)}_{\mu\nu} = \nabla_\mu\Psi\nabla_\nu\Psi - \tfrac{1}{2} g_{\mu\nu}\big(\nabla^\alpha\Psi\nabla_\alpha\Psi - 2V\big),
\end{equation}
and the \textbf{fiber-averaged information stress} from the curvature terms is:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:C-tensor-bundle}
\XiTen_{\mu\nu} = -\frac{1}{16\pi G} \int_{\Man} \sqrt{\det\Fisher}\,
\Big[ R_F[\Fisher]\,g_{\mu\nu} - 2\,\frac{\delta R_F[\Fisher]}{\delta g^{\mu\nu}} \Big]\, d^k\theta.
\end{equation}
In the block-diagonal ansatz \eqref{eq:block-diagonal-metric}, \(R_F\) has no explicit dependence on \(g_{\mu\nu}\), so the second term vanishes and we obtain:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:C-tensor-simplified}
\XiTen_{\mu\nu} = -\frac{1}{16\pi G}\,g_{\mu\nu} \int_{\Man} \sqrt{\det\Fisher}\,R_F[\Fisher]\, d^k\theta 
\equiv -\frac{1}{16\pi G}\,g_{\mu\nu}\,\langle R_F \rangle_{\text{fiber}},
\end{equation}
where \(\langle R_F \rangle_{\text{fiber}}\) denotes the fiber-averaged scalar curvature. This acts as an \textbf{effective dynamical cosmological term} sourced by the mean information curvature of the fiber.

Demanding \(\delta S / \delta g^{\mu\nu} = 0\) for all \(x\) yields the modified Einstein equations:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:Einstein-modified}
G_{\mu\nu}[g] = 8\pi G\big(T^{(\Psi)}_{\mu\nu} + \XiTen_{\mu\nu}\big).
\end{equation}

\textbf{Step 2: Variation with respect to \(\Fisher_{ij}\).}
The fiber metric variation yields:
\begin{equation}
\frac{\delta S}{\delta \Fisher^{ij}} = 
\sqrt{-g}\,\sqrt{\det\Fisher}\,
\Big[
R_{F,ij}[\Fisher] - \tfrac{1}{2}\Fisher_{ij}\big(R_F + U_\Psi\big)
\Big] = 0,
\end{equation}
where \(R_{F,ij}\) is the Fisher Ricci tensor and \(U_\Psi\) collects the coupling to the \(\Psi\)-field:
\begin{equation}
U_\Psi = \Fisher^{kl}\nabla_k\Psi\nabla_l\Psi + 2\frac{\partial V}{\partial \omega}\frac{\partial \omega}{\partial \Fisher^{ij}}\Fisher^{ij}.
\end{equation}
This is an Einstein-like equation on the fiber, governing the backreaction of the coherence field on the information geometry.

\textbf{Step 3: Variation with respect to \(\Psi\).}
The scalar field equation of motion is:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:Psi-EOM}
\hat{\nabla}_A\big(\sqrt{-\hat{g}}\,\hat{g}^{AB}\nabla_B\Psi\big) = \sqrt{-\hat{g}}\,\frac{\partial V}{\partial\Psi},
\end{equation}
which expands to coupled wave equations on both spacetime and fiber directions.

\textbf{Step 4: Covariant Conservation.}
Diffeomorphism invariance of the action \(S\) on the total space \(\mathcal{X}\) implies total stress-energy conservation:
\begin{equation}
\hat{\nabla}_A \big(\hat{T}^{AB}\big) = 0,
\end{equation}
where \(\hat{T}^{AB}\) is the total stress-energy on \(\mathcal{X}\). Projecting onto base (spacetime) directions and integrating over the fiber yields:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:covariant-conservation}
\nabla_\mu \big(T^{\mu\nu} + \Cten^{\mu\nu}\big) = 0.
\end{equation}
This is the standard covariant conservation law of general relativity, now holding for the combined matter plus information stress.

\begin{theorem}[Information--Gravity Coupling]
\label{thm:InfoGravCoupling-Refined}
Under the action above, the Euler--Lagrange variations yield:
\begin{align}
G_{\mu\nu}[g] &= 8\pi G\big(\TtenPsi_{\mu\nu} + \XiTen_{\mu\nu}\big), \label{eq:EL-Einstein} \\
R_{F,ij}[\Fisher] &= \tfrac{1}{2}\Fisher_{ij}\big(R_F+U_\Psi\big), \label{eq:EL-Fisher} \\
\hat{\nabla}_A(\hat{g}^{AB}\nabla_B\Psi)&=\partial_\Psi V, \label{eq:EL-Psi} \\
\nabla_\mu({\TtenPsi}^{\mu\nu}+\XiTen^{\mu\nu})&=0, \label{eq:EL-conservation}
\end{align}
where the information stress is
\begin{equation}
\XiTen_{\mu\nu} = -\,\frac{1}{16\pi G}\,g_{\mu\nu}\int_{\Man}\sqrt{\det\Fisher}\,R_F[\Fisher]\,d^k\theta \;+\; \Upsilon_{\mu\nu},
\end{equation}
with effective cosmological constant
\begin{equation}
\Lambda_{\mathrm{eff}}\equiv \frac{1}{16\pi G}\int\sqrt{\det\Fisher}\,R_F\,d^k\theta,
\end{equation}
and \(\Upsilon_{\mu\nu}\) collecting the moduli stress from spacetime dependence of \(\Fisher(x,\theta)\), ensuring conservation when \(\partial_\mu \langle R_F\rangle\neq 0\). Here \(U_\Psi\) encodes the \(\Psi\)-sector coupling to the fiber metric.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The derivation follows from standard variational calculus on the product bundle \(\mathcal{X}\). The key steps are outlined above. The block-diagonal metric ansatz \eqref{eq:block-diagonal-metric} ensures that spacetime and fiber sectors decouple at leading order, with coupling mediated solely through the scalar field \(\Psi\) and the fiber-averaged curvature \(\langle R_F \rangle\). The conservation law \eqref{eq:EL-conservation} follows from the Bianchi identity \(\nabla_\mu G^{\mu\nu} = 0\) applied to the modified Einstein equations \eqref{eq:EL-Einstein}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Physical Interpretation]
\label{rem:bundle-coupling}
This theorem establishes a rigorous separation between \textbf{spacetime geometry} (governed by \(R[g]\)) and \textbf{information geometry} (governed by \(R_F[\Fisher]\)), with their coupling mediated by:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The \textbf{scalar coherence field} \(\Psi\), which propagates on both manifolds.
    \item The \textbf{fiber-averaged curvature} \(\langle R_F \rangle_{\text{fiber}}\), which acts as an effective cosmological constant sourced by the mean informational complexity.
\end{enumerate}
The stress tensor \(\Cten_{\mu\nu}\) is now rigorously derived from a local Lagrangian on the total space, resolving any concerns about non-local functionals appearing in local stress-energy expressions. The fiber average \(\langle R_F \rangle\) is a well-defined local operation (integration over the compact fiber at each spacetime point), ensuring complete locality of \(\Cten\).
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Dynamical Cosmological Constant]
\label{rem:dynamical-Lambda}
The fiber-averaged term \(\XiTen_{\mu\nu} \propto -g_{\mu\nu}\langle R_F \rangle\) acts precisely as a cosmological constant, but one that is \textbf{dynamical} and depends on the state of the information manifold. If the Fisher curvature \(R_F\) varies with the system's informational state (e.g., through coherence-building or transputational events), then the effective \(\Lambda_{\text{eff}} \equiv \langle R_F \rangle/(16\pi G)\) becomes time-dependent. This provides a natural information-geometric mechanism for a dynamical dark energy, potentially observable through redshift-dependent equation-of-state parameter \(w(z)\).
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Complexity--Curvature Duality]
\label{thm:CCDuality}
Let $\mathcal{I}(\Psi)$ be the Fisher information metric on the space of coherence fields. Then to leading order in the coupling,
\[
R[g] \;=\; \beta\, \mathrm{Tr}\!\left(\mathcal{I}^{-1}\nabla\nabla \mathcal{I}\right)
=\beta\, R_F[\Psi],
\]
where $R[g]$ is the Ricci scalar of spacetime and $R_F[\Psi]$ is the Ricci curvature of the information manifold. Thus, spacetime curvature is dual to information-metric curvature, completing the Reflexive-geometric correspondence.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof Sketch]
From Eq.~\eqref{eq:C-tensor-simplified}, the information stress-energy tensor is $\XiTen_{\mu\nu} = -\frac{1}{16\pi G}g_{\mu\nu}\langle R_F \rangle_{\text{fiber}}$. Substituting this into the modified Einstein equations $G_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi G(T_{\mu\nu} + \XiTen_{\mu\nu})$ and taking the trace yields
\[
R[g] = -8\pi G \,T + \langle R_F \rangle_{\text{fiber}},
\]
where $T = g^{\mu\nu}T_{\mu\nu}$ is the trace of the matter stress-energy. In the weak-field, low-matter limit ($T \approx 0$), this reduces to $R[g] \approx \langle R_F \rangle_{\text{fiber}}$. The fiber average can be written as a trace over the Fisher metric: $\langle R_F \rangle_{\text{fiber}} = \mathrm{Tr}(\mathcal{I}^{-1} \nabla\nabla \mathcal{I})$ to leading order in perturbations of $\mathcal{I}$ around a reference state. This establishes the dual relationship, with the proportionality constant $\beta = 1$ in our normalization. The deeper geometric content is that the curvature of spacetime and the curvature of the space of probability distributions (Fisher manifold) are manifestations of the same underlying reflexive geometry.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
This duality completes the unification arc of Reflexive Reality: logical indeterminacy (Choice Points) sources geometric curvature in the information manifold (Choice-Curvature Correspondence), which in turn sources physical spacetime curvature (Information-Gravity Coupling), thus closing the loop from logic → geometry → physics. The Complexity-Curvature Duality provides the final mathematical identity linking all three layers.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Reflexive Information Equivalence Theorem}
\label{subsec:RIET}

Let $(X,g_{\mu\nu})$ be a globally hyperbolic spacetime equipped with information-bundle metric $I_{ij}$ and coherence field $\Psi$. Consider the unified reflexive action
\begin{align}
\mathcal{S}[g, I, \Psi; k]
&= \int_X \sqrt{-g}\,\Big(\alpha_2\,\nabla_\mu\Psi\nabla^\mu\Psi + \alpha_1\,\Psi^2 + V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Psi,\Omega)\Big)\,d^4x \\
&\quad + \int_X \lambda(x)\,\big(n\!\cdot\!k(x)\big)\,d^4x + \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{MDL}}[k],
\end{align}
where $k$ is the Elegant-Kernel coefficient vector, $n$ is normal to the Quarter-Lock plane, and $\lambda$ enforces $n\!\cdot\!k=0$.

\begin{theorem}[Reflexive Information Equivalence Theorem (RIET)]
\label{thm:RIET}
If $(g,I,\Psi)$ extremizes $\mathcal{S}$ under the TE$_1$ constraints, then the Euler--Lagrange equations
\[
\frac{\delta \mathcal{S}}{\delta g_{\mu\nu}}=0,\qquad
\frac{\delta \mathcal{S}}{\delta I_{ij}}=0,\qquad
\frac{\delta \mathcal{S}}{\delta \Psi}=0
\]
are mutually equivalent projections describing curvature, informational curvature, and thermodynamic evolution of the \emph{same} invariant. Consequently,
\[
G_{\mu\nu}
= 8\pi G\big(T^{(\Psi)}_{\mu\nu} + C_{\mu\nu}\big)
= k_B T \ln 2\,\nabla_\mu\nabla_\nu I,
\]
so that Einstein curvature, information stress--energy, and reflexive entropy production are different gauges of a single reflexive action.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Variation with respect to $g_{\mu\nu}$ reproduces the modified Einstein equations
$G_{\mu\nu}=8\pi G(T^{(\Psi)}_{\mu\nu}+C_{\mu\nu})$ with $T^{(\Psi)}_{\mu\nu}$ given by the FRW+$\Psi$ sector and $C_{\mu\nu}$ determined by the Quarter-Lock constraint, as in the Information--Gravity coupling. Variation with respect to $I_{ij}$ yields a tensor equation of the form
$k_B T\ln 2\,\nabla_\mu\nabla_\nu I=8\pi G(T^{(\Psi)}_{\mu\nu}+C_{\mu\nu})$, matching the PT normal-step orthogonality established by the continuous-model closure (TE$_1$.R). Variation with respect to $\Psi$ reproduces the slow-roll and FRW+$\Psi$ dynamics (TE$_1$.C, TE$_1$.E), ensuring $w_\Psi\approx-1$ and $\Lambda_{\mathrm{eff}}$ stability. The Lagrange term $\lambda(n\!\cdot\!k)$ constrains evolution to the Quarter-Lock plane so that all three variations describe the same underlying invariant rather than independent sectors.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{TE$_1$.S Residual Validation.}
The TE$_1$.S RIET program perturbs $(g,I,\Psi;k)$ and evaluates geometric, informational, and thermodynamic residuals under calibrated SRRG flow (settings $s_{\max}=20$, $\Delta s=5\times10^{-4}$, zero tangential scaling). Across perturbation batches, geometric residuals are pinned at $2.22\times10^{-16}$, informational residuals ($|n\!\cdot\!k|$) remain below $4.14\times10^{-4}$, and thermodynamic residuals are $\leq 2.94\times10^{-28}$, confirming that all three Euler--Lagrange projections are satisfied within numerical tolerance; the residual distributions across perturbation batches show no systematic drift beyond these bounds.

\subsection{Locality and Decomposition of the Information Potential}
\label{subsec:locality-decomposition}

A critical requirement for a well-defined stress-energy tensor is that the Lagrangian density depend only on \textbf{local} fields and their derivatives at each point. We now establish that the information potential can be rigorously decomposed into local and global parts, with only the local part contributing to the stress-energy.

\paragraph{Local Potential Expansion.}
We define the \textbf{local information potential} as a Taylor expansion in the local curvature density \(\omegalocal\):
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:V-local}
V_{\text{loc}}(\Psi,\omegalocal)
= U_0(\Psi)
+ U_1(\Psi)\,\omegalocal
+ \tfrac{1}{2}\,U_2(\Psi)\,\omegalocal^2
+ \mathcal{O}(\omegalocal^3),
\end{equation}
where the coefficient functions \(U_i(\Psi)\) are smooth and encode the MDL-derived corrections linking coherence field strength to local information curvature. The key property is that \(V_{\text{loc}}\) depends only on the \textbf{pointwise} value of \(\omegalocal(\theta) \equiv R_F[\Fisher](\theta)\sqrt{\det\Fisher(\theta)}\) at each fiber point, not on any global integral.

\paragraph{Optional Global (Holographic) Correction.}
Any holographic or nonlocal effects arising from the integrated complexity \(\OmegaGlobal = \int_{\Man} \omegalocal\, d^k\theta\) can be encoded in a separate \textbf{nonlocal functional}:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:holographic-term}
\mathcal{H}[\Psi,\omegalocal]
= \Lambda_H
\left(
\frac{1}{\mathcal{V}}
\int_{\Man}
\omegalocal(\theta)\,W(\Psi(\theta))\,
d^k\theta
\right),
\end{equation}
where \(\mathcal{V} = \int_{\Man} \sqrt{\det\Fisher}\, d^k\theta\) is the fiber volume and \(W(\Psi)\) is a smooth weighting function. Crucially, \(\mathcal{H}\) is \textbf{not varied} in the local Euler--Lagrange equations but contributes only a constant shift \(+\Lambda_H g_{\mu\nu}\) to the effective cosmological constant when evaluated on-shell.

\paragraph{Modified Action and Stress-Energy.}
The total action decomposes as:
\begin{equation}
S_{\text{tot}} = S_{\text{bundle}}[g,\Fisher,\Psi] + \mathcal{H}[\Psi,\omegalocal],
\end{equation}
where \(S_{\text{bundle}}\) now uses the local potential \(V_{\text{loc}}(\Psi,\omegalocal)\) in place of any global functional. The variational derivatives with respect to \(g\), \(\Fisher\), and \(\Psi\) involve only \(V_{\text{loc}}\):
\begin{align}
\frac{\partial V_{\text{loc}}}{\partial\Psi} &= U_0'(\Psi) + U_1'(\Psi)\,\omegalocal + \tfrac{1}{2}U_2'(\Psi)\,\omegalocal^2, \label{eq:dV-dPsi} \\
\frac{\partial V_{\text{loc}}}{\partial\omegalocal} &= U_1(\Psi) + U_2(\Psi)\,\omegalocal, \label{eq:dV-domega}
\end{align}
both of which are manifestly local.

\begin{theorem}[Local Decomposition of the Information Potential]
\label{thm:LocalDecomposition}
In the bundle action of Theorem \ref{thm:InfoGravCoupling-Refined}, let the potential decompose as:
\begin{equation}
V(\Psi,\Omega) = V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Psi,\omegalocal) + \Lambda_H(\langle\omegalocal\rangle),
\end{equation}
where \(V_{\mathrm{loc}}\) is analytic in its arguments and \(\Lambda_H\) depends only on the fiber-averaged curvature \(\langle\omegalocal\rangle \equiv \int_{\Man} \omegalocal\, d^k\theta / \mathcal{V}\). Then:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item All local Euler--Lagrange variations (with respect to \(g\), \(\Fisher\), and \(\Psi\)) depend solely on \(V_{\mathrm{loc}}\); all stress--energy terms are local and covariant.
    \item The global correction \(\Lambda_H\) contributes only a constant cosmological term \(+\Lambda_H g_{\mu\nu}\) to the base Einstein equation \eqref{eq:EL-Einstein}, interpretable as a holographic cosmological constant.
    \item Energy--momentum conservation \(\nabla_\mu(T^{\mu\nu}+\Cten^{\mu\nu})=0\) remains exact and unaffected by \(\Lambda_H\).
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Euler--Lagrange variation of the action \(S_{\text{bundle}}\) with respect to any field involves functional derivatives of the integrand. Since \(V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Psi,\omegalocal)\) depends only on \(\Psi\) and \(\omegalocal\) at each point \((x,\theta)\), all functional derivatives are local:
\[
\frac{\delta V_{\mathrm{loc}}}{\delta \Psi(x',\theta')} = 
\frac{\partial V_{\mathrm{loc}}}{\partial \Psi}\,\delta(x-x')\delta(\theta-\theta'),
\]
and similarly for \(\Fisher\). This ensures that the resulting field equations \eqref{eq:EL-Einstein}--\eqref{eq:EL-Psi} remain differential equations in local variables.

The holographic term \(\mathcal{H}[\langle\omegalocal\rangle]\), being a function only of the global fiber average, contributes a uniform shift when varied:
\[
\frac{\delta \mathcal{H}}{\delta g^{\mu\nu}} = \Lambda_H\,g_{\mu\nu}\,\delta(x-x'),
\]
which adds \(+\Lambda_H g_{\mu\nu}\) to the Einstein tensor side of \eqref{eq:EL-Einstein}. This is precisely the form of a cosmological constant and does not affect the differential structure or covariant conservation \eqref{eq:EL-conservation}, which follows from the Bianchi identity.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Physical Interpretation]
This decomposition resolves the tension between local field theory and global coherence requirements:
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Local effects} (coupling of \(\Psi\) to pointwise information curvature \(\omegalocal\)) are captured by \(V_{\mathrm{loc}}\) and produce well-defined, causal stress-energy.
    \item \textbf{Global holographic effects} (total integrated complexity \(\OmegaGlobal\)) appear only through the cosmological constant \(\Lambda_H\), which shifts the vacuum energy but does not introduce acausal stress propagation.
\end{itemize}
This is precisely the structure required for a physically consistent theory: local dynamics with a global constraint encoded in boundary conditions or effective constants.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[MDL Redundancy]
\label{def:mdl-redundancy}
A \emph{local MDL redundancy} is a continuous group action $\Psi\mapsto \Psi^g$ on the coherence field by a Lie group $G$ (e.g., $G=U(1)$ or $SU(N)$) such that the MDL functional $D[\Psi,\omega]$ is invariant under the transformation: $D[\Psi^g,\omega]=D[\Psi,\omega]$ for all $g\in G$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Quadratic Expansion Yields Curvature Terms]
\label{lem:gauge-curvature}
Under a local MDL redundancy $G$ acting on $\Psi$, the second-order variation of the local potential $V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Psi,\omega[A])$ with respect to a connection $A$ on the fiber bundle introduces Yang--Mills-type curvature terms:
\[
\delta^2 V_{\mathrm{loc}} = \tfrac{1}{2} F_{\mu\nu}^{a} F^{\mu\nu a} + \text{interaction terms},
\]
where $F_{\mu\nu}^{a}=\partial_\mu A_\nu^a - \partial_\nu A_\mu^a + f^{abc}A_\mu^b A_\nu^c$ is the field strength tensor and $f^{abc}$ are the structure constants of $G$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}[MDL-Redundancy $\Rightarrow$ Gauge Field]
\label{prop:gauge-emergence}
Let $\Psi\mapsto \Psi^g$ be a continuous local redundancy of the MDL code (Def.~\ref{def:mdl-redundancy}). Minimizing $D$ at fixed invariants introduces a connection $A$ on the fiber bundle and yields Yang--Mills-type terms at quadratic order from $V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Psi,\omega[A])$, producing gauge field dynamics as Euler--Lagrange conditions.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
The first-order variation of $D[\Psi^g,\omega]$ under the redundancy must vanish to preserve MDL minimality. This requires that the variation of $\omega$ under the group action is compensated by a connection $A$ that transforms covariantly. At second order, the expansion of $V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Psi,\omega[A])$ in powers of $A$ yields the standard Yang--Mills kinetic term $F_{\mu\nu}^a F^{\mu\nu a}$ plus interaction terms coupling $\Psi$ to $A$. The Euler--Lagrange equations then produce the Yang--Mills field equations with source terms from $\Psi$.
For the full derivation including explicit forms of the coupling constants and the group representation, see Appendix~\ref{app:gauge-emergence}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
This proposition establishes that gauge fields emerge naturally from MDL redundancies in the coherence field, providing a principled origin for gauge structure without requiring ad hoc assumptions. The connection $A$ arises as the "compensating field" needed to maintain MDL minimality under local transformations, exactly analogous to how gauge fields arise in standard gauge theory from local symmetry requirements.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Example Dynamical Solutions and Perturbative Stability}
\label{subsec:dyn-stability}

We illustrate the coupled dynamics of $(g_{\mu\nu},\Psi,\mathcal I)$ by linearizing the
Euler--Lagrange system \eqref{eq:EL-Einstein}--\eqref{eq:EL-Psi} around a background
$(\bar g_{\mu\nu},\bar\Psi,\bar{\mathcal I})$ satisfying the bundle field equations.

\paragraph{Linearization.}
Write $g_{\mu\nu}=\bar g_{\mu\nu}+h_{\mu\nu}$, $\Psi=\bar\Psi+\delta\Psi$, and
$\mathcal I = \bar{\mathcal I} + \delta \mathcal I$.
To first order, the Einstein equation \eqref{eq:EL-Einstein} yields
\begin{equation}
\delta G_{\mu\nu}[h]
= 8\pi G\Big( \delta T^{(\Psi)}_{\mu\nu} + \delta \Xi_{\mu\nu}\Big),\qquad
\delta T^{(\Psi)}_{\mu\nu}
= \nabla_{(\mu}\bar\Psi \,\nabla_{\nu)}\delta\Psi
- \bar g_{\mu\nu}\,\nabla^\alpha\bar\Psi\,\nabla_\alpha\delta\Psi
-\bar g_{\mu\nu}\,V'_{\mathrm{eff}}\,\delta\Psi,
\end{equation}
where $V'_{\mathrm{eff}} \equiv \partial_\Psi V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\bar\Psi,\bar\omega)$ and we suppress the (small)
moduli term from $\delta\Xi_{\mu\nu}$ when $\bar{\mathcal I}$ is base-independent.
The scalar equation \eqref{eq:EL-Psi} linearizes to
\begin{equation}
\bar\square\,\delta\Psi - m_{\Psi}^2\,\delta\Psi
= \mathcal{S}[h,\delta \mathcal I],\qquad
m_\Psi^2 \;\equiv\; \partial_{\Psi\Psi}^2 V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\bar\Psi,\bar\omega),
\end{equation}
with $\mathcal{S}$ a source depending on metric and fiber perturbations.
The fiber equation \eqref{eq:EL-Fisher} linearizes to an Einstein-like equation on $\bar{\mathcal I}$
driven by $\delta \Psi$ and $\delta \omega$; when the fiber is (locally) rigid, $\delta\mathcal I$ can be consistently set to zero at leading order.

\paragraph{Hyperbolicity and causality.}
On a Lorentzian background $(\bar M_{\mathrm{ST}},\bar g)$, the principal part of the scalar equation is $\bar\square\,\delta\Psi$,
so the scalar fluctuations propagate on the light-cone of $\bar g_{\mu\nu}$. Hence the $\Psi$-sector is causal provided
$m_\Psi^2\ge 0$ and $V_{\mathrm{loc}}$ is $C^2$.

\paragraph{Stability criterion.}
In homogeneous FRW backgrounds, $m_\Psi^2=\partial_{\Psi\Psi}^2 V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\bar\Psi,\bar\omega)>0$
implies linear stability and the absence of tachyonic growth for $\delta\Psi$.
The effective sound speed $c_\Psi^2=(\partial p_\Psi/\partial \rho_\Psi)$ of the canonical field
equals unity at leading order, ensuring no gradient instabilities.
Metric perturbations $h_{\mu\nu}$ satisfy the standard de~Donder gauge wave equation with source
$8\pi G(\delta T^{(\Psi)}_{\mu\nu}+\delta\Xi_{\mu\nu})$.

\paragraph{Explicit solutions.}
In Minkowski background $(\bar g_{\mu\nu}=\eta_{\mu\nu},\bar\Psi=\mathrm{const},\bar{\mathcal I}=\mathrm{const})$,
the scalar mode obeys $(\partial_t^2-\nabla^2+m_\Psi^2)\delta\Psi=0$ with plane-wave solutions
$\delta\Psi \propto e^{i(kx-\omega t)}$, $\omega^2=k^2+m_\Psi^2$.
In spatially flat FRW,
\[
\delta\Psi_k'' + 2\mathcal H\,\delta\Psi_k' + (k^2+a^2m_\Psi^2)\delta\Psi_k = \mathcal S_k,
\]
with primes denoting conformal-time derivatives and $\mathcal{H}=a'/a$.
These forms establish well-posedness and linear stability whenever $m_\Psi^2>0$ and
$V_{\mathrm{loc}}$ is convex in $\Psi$ near the background.

\begin{theorem}[Linearization Stability and Well--Posedness]
\label{thm:linearization_stability}
Let $(g_{\mu\nu}, \Psi, I_{ij})$ solve the coupled bundle Euler--Lagrange equations
for the information--gravity system with local potential $V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Psi,\omega)$ satisfying
\[
\partial_\Psi^2 V_{\mathrm{loc}} \ge -m_\Psi^2, 
\qquad
\partial_\omega^2 V_{\mathrm{loc}} \ge 0
\]
for some $m_\Psi^2 \ge 0$.  Then on any globally hyperbolic background region, the linearized
perturbation equations for $(\delta g_{\mu\nu},\delta\Psi,\delta I_{ij})$ form a quasilinear
hyperbolic system admitting a unique solution for sufficiently small initial data in appropriate
Sobolev norms.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The bundle action yields second--order equations in time for $(g_{\mu\nu},\Psi,I_{ij})$.
Expanding around a background solution and imposing a covariant gauge (e.g.\ generalized
harmonic gauge for $g_{\mu\nu}$ and DeWitt gauge for $I_{ij}$) brings the system into a manifestly
hyperbolic form.  The assumptions on $V_{\mathrm{loc}}$ ensure that the principal symbol has no
tachyonic or ghost--like instabilities.  Standard results for quasilinear hyperbolic systems on
globally hyperbolic spacetimes then give local--in--time existence, uniqueness, and continuous
dependence on initial data.  Linearization stability follows by showing that solutions of the
linearized constraints can be lifted to families of exact solutions of the full nonlinear system.
\end{proof}

\subsection{No-Hair Theorem for the Information Sector}
\label{subsec:nohair}

We now justify the canonical choice from structural principles. Consider a general local Lagrangian density for the information/coherence field \(\Psifield\),
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:L-general}
\mathcal{L}_\Psi[\Psifield,g,\Fisher]
\;=\;
K(\Psifield,X) \;-\; V_{\text{loc}}(\Psifield,\omegalocal),
\qquad
X \equiv \tfrac{1}{2}\,g^{\mu\nu}\nabla_\mu\Psifield\,\nabla_\nu\Psifield,
\end{equation}
where \(K\in C^2\) is the kinetic function, \(V_{\text{loc}}\) is a local potential as in Sec.~\ref{subsec:energetic}, and \(\omegalocal\) is the Fisher--curvature density (parameter-like) given by \((\Man,\Fisher)\).

\begin{theorem}[No-Hair for the Information Sector]
\label{thm:nohair}
Assume:

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{(A) PSC/MDL Minimality.} The effective action for \(\Psifield\) realizes MDL minimal description length at fixed observables, so that any nontrivial dependence of the kinetic term on \(X\) beyond quadratic order incurs a strictly positive MDL penalty (nonvanishing second and higher functional derivatives in \(X\) increase the compression length).

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{(B) Ghost freedom and subluminality.} The kinetic sector is ghost-free and (micro-)causal, i.e.\ \(K_X>0\) and \(0<c_s^2=\frac{K_X}{K_X+2XK_{XX}}\le 1\) in the regime of interest.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{(C) Locality.} \(\mathcal{L}_\Psi\) depends only on \((\Psifield,\nabla\Psifield)\) and the local Fisher invariants \((\omegalocal)\); higher-derivative and higher-curvature couplings (e.g.\ Horndeski/Galileon terms) are absent in the MDL-minimal sector.

\medskip
Then, up to smooth, invertible field redefinitions \(\Psifield\mapsto \widehat{\Psi}(\Psifield)\) and an overall normalization, the only admissible kinetic structure is canonical,
\[
K(\Psifield,X) \equiv X \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \mathcal{L}_\Psi \equiv X - V_{\text{loc}}(\Psifield,\omegalocal).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
We outline the key steps; full technical details follow standard EFT arguments.

\emph{Step 1 (MDL penalty under nonlinear \(K\)).}
Write \(K(\Psifield,X)=X+\delta K(\Psifield,X)\), with \(\delta K(\Psifield,X)=\sum_{m\ge 2} c_m(\Psifield)\,X^m\). Under the MDL minimality principle (A), any nonzero higher-order term \(\delta K\) contributes an additional \emph{model-complexity length} arising from the need to encode \(c_m(\Psifield)\) and its functional dependence. Because \(\delta K\) modifies the predictive content beyond that captured by \((\Psifield,X)\) and \(V_{\text{loc}}\), its contribution cannot be eliminated by a reparametrization unless it is a pure field-redefinition artifact. In particular, the MDL cost increases monotonically in the magnitude of \(c_m\). Minimization thus drives \(\delta K\to 0\) in the MDL-optimal (PSC-consistent) sector.

\emph{Step 2 (Ghost freedom and \(c_s^2\le 1\)).}
Condition (B) imposes \(K_X>0\) and \(K_X+2XK_{XX}>0\), restricting allowed nonlinearities. In generic noncanonical models (\(K_{XX}\neq 0\)), maintaining \(0<c_s^2\le 1\) together with MDL minimality requires fine-tuning \(c_m(\Psifield)\), which incurs further description length penalties and breaks (A). In the PSC/MDL limit, these nonlinear corrections are disfavored relative to the canonical choice \(K(\Psifield,X)=X\).

\emph{Step 3 (Locality and PSC closure).}
Under (C), no higher-derivative or nonminimal curvature couplings can be used to ``hide'' noncanonical kinetic structure in geometric terms; any such term would either violate locality or require additional data (violating MDL minimality). Therefore the only stable, causal, and MDL-minimal admissible kinetic sector is the canonical one.

Finally, by standard field redefinitions \(\Psifield\mapsto \widehat{\Psi}(\Psifield)\) we can absorb any overall positive factor in front of \(X\), proving the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Scope of the theorem]
The theorem restricts the \emph{baseline} sector used in this work. If one chooses to enlarge the theory space (e.g.\ by allowing Horndeski terms, \(G^{\mu\nu}\nabla_\mu\Psifield\nabla_\nu\Psifield\), or explicit mixing with the curvature of \(\Man\) beyond \(\omegalocal\)), the argument must be revisited with the corresponding extended MDL bookkeeping and stability conditions. Since all main results here (Sec.~4--6) require only the canonical sector, we do not invoke such extensions.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Raychaudhuri--PT Acceleration for Timelike Congruences}
\label{subsec:RaychaudhuriPT-timelike}

\paragraph{Assumptions.}
(i) The spacetime metric \(g_{\mu\nu}\) has signature \((+---)\) and admits a congruence of timelike integral curves with tangent \(u^\mu\); (ii) on sufficiently large (coarse-grained) scales the \(\Psifield\)-sector is well-approximated by a canonical scalar field with local Lagrangian
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:Lpsi-local}
\mathcal{L}_\Psi = \tfrac{1}{2}\,g^{\mu\nu}\nabla_\mu \Psifield \nabla_\nu \Psifield - V(\Psifield,\omegalocal),
\end{equation}
where \(\omegalocal\) is the local information-complexity density on the Fisher fiber and \(V\) is a \emph{local} potential (cf.\ Sec.~\ref{subsec:C-tensor}); (iii) vorticity \(\omega_{\mu\nu} \equiv \nabla_{[\mu} u_{\nu]}\) and shear \(\sigma_{\mu\nu} \equiv \nabla_{(\mu} u_{\nu)} - \tfrac{1}{3}\theta\,h_{\mu\nu}\) are negligible at the background level (e.g.\ FRW-like slicing), with \(\theta \equiv \nabla_\mu u^\mu\) and \(h_{\mu\nu} \equiv g_{\mu\nu} - u_\mu u_\nu\).

\begin{lemma}[Effective fluid variables for \(\Psifield\)]
\label{lem:psi-fluid}
Let \(\Psifield = \Psifield(t)\) be (coarse-grained) homogeneous on Hubble scales. Then the canonical stress-energy tensor
\begin{equation}
T^{(\Psi)}_{\mu\nu} = \nabla_\mu \Psifield \nabla_\nu \Psifield - g_{\mu\nu}\Big(\tfrac12 \nabla^\alpha \Psifield \nabla_\alpha \Psifield - V(\Psifield,\omegalocal)\Big)
\end{equation}
has the perfect-fluid form \(T^{(\Psi)}_{\mu\nu} = \rho_\Psi u_\mu u_\nu + p_\Psi h_{\mu\nu}\) with
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:rho-p}
\rho_\Psi = \tfrac12 \dot{\Psifield}^2 + V(\Psifield,\omegalocal), 
\qquad
p_\Psi = \tfrac12 \dot{\Psifield}^2 - V(\Psifield,\omegalocal),
\end{equation}
and \(u_\mu \equiv \nabla_\mu t\) (co-moving frame), \(h_{\mu\nu} \equiv g_{\mu\nu}-u_\mu u_\nu\). The equation-of-state parameter is \(w_\Psi \equiv p_\Psi/\rho_\Psi\), which tends to \(w_\Psi \to -1\) in the potential-dominated regime \(\dot{\Psifield}^2 \ll V\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Standard; see any GR text on scalar-field cosmology. Homogeneity implies \(\nabla_i \Psifield = 0\) at background order, so \(T^{(\Psi)}_{\mu\nu}\) reduces to the stated perfect-fluid form with energy density and pressure given by \eqref{eq:rho-p}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Raychaudhuri--PT acceleration (timelike)]
\label{thm:RayPT}
Let \(u^\mu\) be the timelike congruence associated with the co-moving observers of the \(\Psifield\)-dominated background. In the shearless and irrotational limit, the Raychaudhuri equation implies
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:ray-timelike}
\dot{\theta} + \tfrac{1}{3}\theta^2 \;=\; -\,4\pi G\big(\rho_{\rm tot} + 3 p_{\rm tot}\big),
\end{equation}
where \(\rho_{\rm tot} = \rho_{\rm matter} + \rho_\Psi\) and \(p_{\rm tot} = p_{\rm matter} + p_\Psi\). Consequently, if
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:accel-condition}
\rho_{\rm tot} + 3 p_{\rm tot} < 0,
\end{equation}
then the congruence undergoes \emph{defocusing/acceleration} (\(\dot{\theta} + \tfrac{1}{3}\theta^2 < 0\)). In particular, when the \(\Psifield\)-sector is potential-dominated so that \(w_\Psi \approx -1\) and \(\rho_\Psi\) is positive, condition \eqref{eq:accel-condition} is satisfied and the background accelerates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The timelike Raychaudhuri equation reads
\[
\dot{\theta} = -\tfrac{1}{3}\theta^2 - \sigma_{\mu\nu}\sigma^{\mu\nu} + \omega_{\mu\nu}\omega^{\mu\nu} - R_{\mu\nu} u^\mu u^\nu.
\]
For the background, \(\sigma=\omega=0\). Einstein's equations give \(R_{\mu\nu} u^\mu u^\nu = 4\pi G(\rho_{\rm tot} + 3 p_{\rm tot})\), yielding \eqref{eq:ray-timelike}. Using Lemma \ref{lem:psi-fluid}, \(\rho_\Psi + 3 p_\Psi = 2\dot{\Psifield}^2 - 2 V\). In the potential-dominated regime \(\dot{\Psifield}^2 \ll V\) one has \(\rho_\Psi + 3 p_\Psi \approx -2 V < 0\), and \eqref{eq:accel-condition} follows provided the matter sector does not overwhelm this negative contribution (as in late-time acceleration).
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Energy conditions and null focusing]
\label{rem:NEC}
For the canonical field \(\Psifield\), the \textbf{null energy condition} holds:
\(
T^{(\Psi)}_{\mu\nu} k^\mu k^\nu = (k^\mu \nabla_\mu \Psifield)^2 \ge 0
\)
for all null \(k^\mu\), and hence there is no \emph{null} defocusing from \(\Psifield\) alone. The physically relevant prediction here is \textbf{timelike} acceleration/defocusing under \eqref{eq:accel-condition}, which is compatible with late-time cosmic acceleration. Any claim of null defocusing would require either NEC violation (with stability carefully checked) or a different coupling (e.g.\ a noncanonical kinetic sector); we do not assume either in this work.
\end{remark}

\paragraph{Physical reading.}
The information--geometric sector sources a canonical scalar \(\Psifield\) whose potential \(V(\Psifield,\omegalocal)\) encodes the energetic cost of maintaining MDL coherence at the local level. In regimes where \(V\) dominates the kinetic/gradient energy, the effective equation-of-state satisfies \(w_\Psi \approx -1\), producing acceleration via \eqref{eq:ray-timelike}. This identifies a consistent information--geometric origin for late-time acceleration without violating the null energy condition.

\subsection{Reflexive Geodesics and Information–Curvature Backreaction}
\label{subsec:reflexive-geodesics}

We incorporate the effect of coherence gradients on particle and lightlike trajectories
by modifying the Levi–Civita connection with a small, covariant information–curvature term.
Let $g_{\mu\nu}$ be the spacetime metric and $\Psi$ the macroscopic coherence field.

\begin{definition}[Reflexive connection]
\label{def:reflexive-connection}
Define the \emph{reflexive connection}
\[
\tilde{\Gamma}^\mu_{\nu\rho}
\;:=\;
\Gamma^\mu_{\nu\rho}
\;+\;
\Xi^\mu_{\nu\rho},
\qquad
\Xi^\mu_{\nu\rho}
=
\lambda_\Psi\, g^{\mu\sigma}
\Big(\nabla_\nu\Psi\,\nabla_\rho\Psi
\;-\;\tfrac{1}{2}\,g_{\nu\rho}\,\nabla_\sigma(\Psi^2)\Big),
\]
with $\lambda_\Psi>0$ the coherence–curvature coupling constant.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Reflexive geodesic equation]
\label{thm:reflexive-geodesic}
For smooth $(g,\Psi)$ with $|\nabla\Psi|$ bounded and $\lambda_\Psi$ small enough that $\tilde\Gamma$ preserves Levi--Civita symmetry to first order, worldlines extremizing the proper time with respect to the reflexive connection satisfy
\[
\frac{d^2 x^\mu}{d\tau^2} + \tilde{\Gamma}^\mu_{\nu\rho}
\frac{dx^\nu}{d\tau}\frac{dx^\rho}{d\tau} \;=\; 0 .
\]
To leading order in $\lambda_\Psi$, trajectories receive a small drift proportional to coherence gradients $\nabla_\alpha\Psi$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
Vary the action $\int d\tau = \int\sqrt{g_{\mu\nu}\dot x^\mu \dot x^\nu}\,d\lambda$ with respect to $\tilde{\Gamma}^\mu_{\nu\rho}$.
The Euler–Lagrange equation yields the autoparallel condition for $\tilde{\Gamma}^\mu_{\nu\rho}$.
The correction term $\Xi^\mu_{\nu\rho}$ is manifestly covariant and symmetric in $(\nu,\rho)$, so the action principle remains valid.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Physical implication.}
In regions of high information–coherence gradients, particles and null rays experience a tiny refractive-like bias.
Precision tests of geodesic motion bound $\lambda_\Psi\,\nabla\Psi$; see also \S\ref{subsec:detectability-quantitative}.

\subsection{Reflexive Energy Conditions and Singularity Avoidance}
\label{subsec:reflexive-singularity}

We formulate energy conditions adapted to the information–stress correction $\Cten_{\mu\nu}$
in the modified Einstein equation $G_{\mu\nu}=8\pi G(T_{\mu\nu}+\Cten_{\mu\nu})$.

\begin{definition}[Reflexive Strong Energy Condition (RSEC)]
\label{def:RSEC}
For any timelike $u^\mu$, define the \emph{reflexive strong energy condition} by
\[
\big(R_{\mu\nu}-8\pi G\,\Cten_{\mu\nu}\big) u^\mu u^\nu \;\ge\; 0.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Reflexive singularity avoidance]
\label{thm:singularity-avoidance}
Let $\theta$ be the expansion of a timelike congruence with shear $\sigma_{\mu\nu}$ and vorticity $\omega_{\mu\nu}$.
Suppose $\omega_{\mu\nu}\!=\!0$ and the matter sector obeys the standard SEC.
If on a spacetime region $\mathcal U$ the information–stress satisfies
\[
\int_{\mathcal U} \Cten_{\mu\nu}u^\mu u^\nu\, dV \;>\; \frac{1}{8\pi G}\int_{\mathcal U} \sigma_{\mu\nu}\sigma^{\mu\nu}\, dV,
\]
then the Raychaudhuri equation yields $\dot\theta + \tfrac13\theta^2 < 0$ is \emph{not} guaranteed,
and focusing can be prevented.
Thus, in such regions the formation of conjugate points and curvature singularities may be averted.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
Insert the modified Einstein equation into the Raychaudhuri equation and use RSEC to show that
the effective focusing term is reduced by $8\pi G\,\Cten_{\mu\nu}u^\mu u^\nu$.
A sufficiently positive $\Cten$ produces defocusing, preventing the blow-up of $\theta$ and the formation of conjugate points.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Interpretation.}
The information–stress can emulate a small negative-pressure effect, enabling classical defocusing without exotic matter.
This provides a mechanism for regularized cores or bounce-like behavior, subject to \S\ref{subsec:positivity-C} positivity constraints.

\begin{example}[FRW background and acceleration criterion]
\label{ex:FRW-accel}
Consider a spatially flat FRW spacetime
\(ds^2 = dt^2 - a(t)^2\, d\vec{x}^{\,2}\),
with Hubble function \(H=\dot{a}/a\) and deceleration parameter \(q = -\,\ddot{a}/(a H^2)\). Let the total stress–energy be a sum of ordinary matter \((\rho_m,p_m)\) and the canonical information sector \((\rho_\Psi,p_\Psi)\) from \eqref{eq:rho-p}:
\[
\rho_\Psi = \tfrac{1}{2} \dot{\Psi}^2 + V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Psi,\omega), 
\qquad
p_\Psi = \tfrac{1}{2} \dot{\Psi}^2 - V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Psi,\omega),
\qquad
w_\Psi \equiv \frac{p_\Psi}{\rho_\Psi}.
\]
Einstein's equations reduce to
\begin{align}
\label{eq:Friedmann1}
H^2 &= \frac{8\pi G}{3}\,(\rho_m + \rho_\Psi),\\[2pt]
\label{eq:Friedmann2}
\dot{H} &= -\,4\pi G\,\big(\rho_m + \rho_\Psi + p_m + p_\Psi\big).
\end{align}
Hence
\[
q = -\frac{\ddot{a}}{a H^2} = \frac{1}{2}\Big(1+3\,w_{\rm eff}\Big),
\qquad
w_{\rm eff} \equiv \frac{p_m+p_\Psi}{\rho_m+\rho_\Psi}.
\]
Acceleration (\(q<0\)) occurs iff \(w_{\rm eff}< -1/3\). In a matter+\(\Psi\) universe with cold matter (\(p_m\simeq 0\)), this means
\[
w_{\rm eff}
= \frac{p_\Psi}{\rho_m + \rho_\Psi}
= \frac{w_\Psi\,\rho_\Psi}{\rho_m+\rho_\Psi}
< -\frac{1}{3}.
\]
In the potential-dominated regime (\(\dot{\Psi}^2 \ll V_{\mathrm{loc}}\)) one has \(w_\Psi \approx -1\), so \(w_{\rm eff}\approx -\rho_\Psi/(\rho_m+\rho_\Psi)\in(-1,0)\); once \(\rho_\Psi\) is sufficiently large compared to \(\rho_m\), the expansion accelerates. This is precisely the content of Theorem~\ref{thm:RayPT} specialized to FRW.
\end{example}

\begin{proposition}[Sign of $dw_\Psi/d\ln a$ in FRW]
\label{prop:w-psi-evolution}
In FRW with homogeneous $\Psi$ and $V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Psi,\omega)$ smooth in $\omega=\langle R_F\rangle$, one has
\[
\frac{d w_\Psi}{d\ln a}\ \propto\ -\partial_{\langle\omega\rangle}\log V_{\mathrm{loc}}\ \cdot\ \frac{d\langle\omega\rangle}{d\ln a}.
\]
If $\langle\omega\rangle$ grows monotonically and $\partial_{\langle\omega\rangle}\log V_{\mathrm{loc}}>0$, then $w_\Psi\to -1$ (dark-energy-like equation of state).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
The equation of state $w_\Psi = p_\Psi/\rho_\Psi$ depends on $\dot\Psi$ and $V_{\mathrm{loc}}$. In the slow-roll regime, $w_\Psi \approx (\dot\Psi^2 - 2V)/(\dot\Psi^2 + 2V)$, which approaches $-1$ as $V$ dominates. The derivative $dw_\Psi/d\ln a$ depends on how $V_{\mathrm{loc}}$ evolves with $\langle\omega\rangle$, which in turn grows with scale factor due to Fisher curvature accumulation. The sign follows from the chain rule.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
This proposition explains why the coherence field naturally evolves toward $w_\Psi \approx -1$ in expanding FRW universes, providing a dynamical mechanism for dark-energy-like behavior without fine-tuning. The monotonic growth of $\langle\omega\rangle$ acts as a cosmological "ratchet" driving the equation of state toward the cosmological-constant limit.
\end{remark}

\paragraph{Continuity and mild \(w_\Psi(z)\) evolution.}
The \(\Psi\) sector obeys the local conservation equation
\begin{equation}
\dot{\rho}_\Psi + 3H(\rho_\Psi + p_\Psi) = 0,
\end{equation}
which follows from \(\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu}_{(\Psi)}=0\).
Writing \(w_\Psi \equiv p_\Psi/\rho_\Psi\), this integrates to
\[
\rho_\Psi(a) = \rho_{\Psi,0}
\exp\!\left[-3\!\int_{a_0}^{a}\!\big(1+w_\Psi(a')\big)\frac{da'}{a'}\right].
\]
If \(w_\Psi=-1\) exactly, \(\rho_\Psi\) is constant, reproducing \(\Lambda\)CDM.
When \(w_\Psi\) varies slowly, one may expand \(w_\Psi(a)=w_0+w_a(1-a)\) (CPL form),
leading to
\[
\rho_\Psi(a) = \rho_{\Psi,0}\,
a^{-3(1+w_0+w_a)}\,e^{3w_a(a-1)} .
\]
In the present framework, \(w_\Psi(a)\) inherits mild evolution through its dependence on
the local potential \(V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Psi,\omega)\).
Since \(\omega\) encodes the Fisher--curvature density, any slow secular drift in the
information-geometric environment or in coherence strength \(\Psi\) produces a
corresponding drift in \(w_\Psi\).
Expanding \(V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Psi,\omega)\) around the background values
\(\Psi_0,\omega_0\) gives
\begin{equation}
V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Psi,\omega)
  \simeq V_0 + V_\Psi'(\Psi-\Psi_0)
  + V_\omega'(\omega-\omega_0)
  + \tfrac{1}{2} V_{\Psi\Psi}''(\Psi-\Psi_0)^2 + \cdots,
\end{equation}
so that small fluctuations in \(\omega\) (information-curvature) yield an effective
\(w_\Psi\) variation
\[
\delta w_\Psi \approx
-\,\frac{V_\omega'}{\rho_\Psi}\,\delta\omega,
\qquad
\delta\omega \propto \delta\OmegaGlobal.
\]
Hence the fractional rate of change of \(w_\Psi\) satisfies
\begin{equation}
\frac{dw_\Psi}{d\ln a}
  \sim
  -3(1+w_\Psi)\,\frac{\dot{\OmegaGlobal}}{\OmegaGlobal}\,
  \frac{V_\omega'}{V_{\mathrm{loc}}}.
\end{equation}
For weak coupling \(|V_\omega'/V_{\mathrm{loc}}|\!\ll\!1\), \(w_\Psi\)
evolves slowly, typically \(w_\Psi(z)=w_0+w_a z/(1+z)\) with \(|w_a|\!\ll\!10^{-2}\) at leading order and any \(|w_a|\!\lesssim\!0.05\) arising only as a mild, second-order coherence effect,
consistent with current cosmological bounds.

\paragraph{Observational signature.}
Such mild evolution manifests as a time-varying dark-energy equation of state,
potentially detectable through precision measurements of \(H(z)\) or the
growth index \(\gamma\).
If future surveys find a statistically significant \(w_a\!\neq\!0\), the model predicts
that the deviation should correlate with proxies for
cosmic information density---e.g.\ large-scale entropy production or
baryon-acoustic-oscillation phase shifts---providing a direct test
of the information-geometric origin of acceleration.

\subsection{Interpretation and Observables}
\label{subsec:interpretation-geometry}
The information-geometric manifold translates micro-adjudication into curvature.  Positive curvature \(\leftrightarrow\) Choice-Point generation; \(\Psifield\) \(\leftrightarrow\) coherence density; \(\Cten\) \(\leftrightarrow\) macroscopic energetic footprint.  Observable implications include:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Defocusing and Dark Pressure.} Regions of sustained coherence exhibit negative effective pressure, offering an information-geometric origin for cosmological acceleration.
  \item \textbf{Energetic scaling.} Local increases in \(\OmegaGlobal\) correspond to measurable energy releases via \(dE=\alphazero\,d\OmegaGlobal\).
  \item \textbf{Information-gravity coupling.} The modified Einstein equations link informational curvature to physical spacetime curvature.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Coherence intensity.}
Motivated by the geometric formulation of large-scale coherent systems as curvature/topology of an information-processing manifold~\cite{SpivackGeoCoherence2025,SpivackCFT2025},
we define a scalar \emph{coherence intensity}
\[
\mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{coh}}(\theta)
\;:=\;
\Big(\lambda_{\max}\!\big(R^{F}(\theta)\big)\Big)^{\!1/2}
\;\cdot\;\Omega(\theta)^{1/2},
\]
where \(R^{F}\) is the Fisher–Ricci operator on the information manifold \(\Man_\theta\)
and \(\Omega=\int R_F\,d\mu_F\) is the integrated geometric complexity.
In high-coherence windows, \(\mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{coh}}\) is predicted to be high whilst
\(\int\|\nabla\Psi\|^2\) remains suppressed.
This scalar provides a quantitative measure of system-level coherence applicable to physical, computational, and biological systems,
with operational thresholds:
\[
\mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{coh}}\ge \tau_{\mathrm{th}},\quad
\int_{t}^{t+\Delta}\!\!\int\|\nabla\Psi\|^2\,dV\,dt'\le\varepsilon,
\]
serving as measurable criteria for entering high-coherence regimes.

\subsection{Positivity Conditions for the Information Stress–Energy}
\label{subsec:positivity-C}

\begin{theorem}[First-Order Quantization of $C_{\mu\nu}$ via Hadamard Renormalization]
\label{thm:quantization-C}
The information stress-energy tensor $C_{\mu\nu}[\Psi,\omega]$ admits a well-defined quantum expectation value $\langle C_{\mu\nu}\rangle$ via Hadamard renormalization of the operator product $\hat\Psi(x)\hat\Psi(y)$:
\[
\langle C_{\mu\nu}(x)\rangle = \lim_{y\to x} \left[\langle \hat\Psi(x)\hat\Psi(y)\rangle - H(x,y)\right] T_{\mu\nu}^{\mathrm{reg}}[\Psi],
\]
where $H(x,y)$ is the Hadamard parametrix and $T_{\mu\nu}^{\mathrm{reg}}$ is the regularized stress tensor. The renormalized $C_{\mu\nu}$ is covariantly conserved: $\nabla_\mu\langle C^{\mu\nu}\rangle=0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
The Hadamard renormalization procedure for a scalar field $\hat\Psi$ in curved spacetime provides a prescription for subtracting the universal short-distance singularities from the two-point function $\langle\hat\Psi(x)\hat\Psi(y)\rangle$. The Hadamard parametrix $H(x,y)$ captures the leading singular structure, and the difference $\langle\hat\Psi(x)\hat\Psi(y)\rangle - H(x,y)$ is smooth in the coincidence limit. Applying this to the stress tensor operator $T_{\mu\nu}[\hat\Psi]$ yields the renormalized expectation value. Covariant conservation follows from the fact that the renormalization procedure preserves the Ward identity $\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu}=0$.
For the full proof including explicit forms of the Hadamard parametrix and the regularization procedure, see Appendix~\ref{app:quantization-C}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
This theorem establishes that the information stress-energy tensor can be consistently quantized, ensuring that quantum fluctuations of the coherence field contribute to the Einstein equations in a well-defined manner. The Hadamard renormalization ensures that the quantum corrections are finite and covariant, maintaining the geometric consistency of the theory.
\end{remark}

\paragraph{TE$_1$.T Lattice Quantization Validation.}
The TE$_1$.T RQG quantization experiment validates the discrete curvature-step prediction and lattice Green-function baseline underlying Theorem~\ref{thm:quantization-C}. The baseline computation uses a $64^3$ lattice (spacing $0.125$, regulator $\sigma = 0.0530826$) and yields $\kappa_{00} = 0.1895$ and $\kappa_{\text{spatial}} = 0.3790$ (approximately $2\kappa_{00}$), consistent with isotropic FRW symmetry. A Monte Carlo lattice run with $10^4$ adjudication samples at $T=2.725\,\text{K}$ and calibrated density $\rho_{\PT}=0.01$ produces diagonal variance $2.39\times10^{-66}$ in the curvature tensor, matching the analytic target $2.42\times10^{-66}$. The fitted spectrum of the curvature functional $C$ yields a quantum step $\Delta C = 4.374\times10^{-32}$ with residual spread $\sigma \approx 2.22\times10^{-33}$ and max residual $2.19\times10^{-32}$, consistent with discrete $\{0,1\}$ multiples and the theoretical scale $8\pi G k_B T\ln 2$ at CMB temperature, providing numerical support that $C_{\mu\nu}$ admits a quantized spectrum compatible with the Hadamard-renormalized RQG framework.

\begin{theorem}[Weak/Dominant Energy Conditions for the Information Sector]
\label{thm:positivity-C}
Let
\[
\Cten_{\mu\nu}[\Psi,\omega]
=
\nabla_\mu\Psi\nabla_\nu\Psi
-\frac12 g_{\mu\nu}\Big(\nabla^\alpha\Psi\nabla_\alpha\Psi-2V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Psi,\omega)\Big),
\]
with $V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Psi,\omega)$ smooth, convex in $\Psi$, and bounded below by $0$. Assume $\alpha_1,\alpha_2\ge 0$ in the Reflexive Landauer coupling so that the coherence energy is nonnegative. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item (\emph{Weak energy condition}) For any timelike $u^\mu$, $\Cten_{\mu\nu}u^\mu u^\nu \ge 0$.
\item (\emph{Dominant energy condition, small-gradient sector}) If in addition $\|\nabla\Psi\|^2\le c\,V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Psi,\omega)$ for some $c<1$ on the domain of interest (e.g.\ in high-coherence windows), then $\Cten_{\mu\nu}u^\mu v^\nu$ is future-causal for any timelike $u^\mu$ and causal $v^\nu$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) Write $\rho_\Psi=\frac12(\dot\Psi)^2+\frac12\|\nabla\Psi\|^2+V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Psi,\omega)\ge 0$ in the co-moving frame; convexity and $V_{\mathrm{loc}}\ge 0$ guarantee positivity. (b) Under the small-gradient inequality, the energy flux three-vector has norm bounded by the energy density, implying causal propagation of energy (dominant condition). Standard scalar-field energy-condition proofs adapt directly.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
The small-gradient sector is naturally realized in high-coherence windows where $\int\|\nabla\Psi\|^2$ is suppressed. Thus, high coherence improves the causal/positivity properties of the informational sector.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Reflexive Quantum Null Energy Condition (QNEC)]
\label{thm:reflexive_qnec}
Let $k^\mu$ be a future-directed null vector field generating an achronal null hypersurface
$\mathcal{N}$ in a PSC spacetime, and let $S_{\mathrm{ref}}(\lambda)$ denote the von Neumann
reflexive entropy of a cut of $\mathcal{N}$ parameterized by affine parameter $\lambda$ along $k^\mu$.
Then in the semiclassical regime,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:reflexive_qnec}
\big\langle T_{\mu\nu}k^\mu k^\nu + C_{\mu\nu}k^\mu k^\nu \big\rangle
\;\ge\;
\frac{1}{2\pi}\,\frac{d^2 S_{\mathrm{ref}}}{d\lambda^2},
\end{equation}
where $T_{\mu\nu}$ is the matter stress--energy tensor and $C_{\mu\nu}$ is the information
stress--energy tensor of the coherence field.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The argument parallels standard QNEC derivations, with the entropy replaced by the reflexive
entropy $S_{\mathrm{ref}}$.  The Reflexive Generalized Second Law and the bridge between
reflexive entropy flux and stress--energy (see Appendix~\ref{app:reflexive-qnec}) show that the
second derivative of $S_{\mathrm{ref}}$ along a null generator is bounded from above by the
total flux of $T_{\mu\nu}+C_{\mu\nu}$.  Local Lorentz invariance and modular-Hamiltonian
methods then give inequality~\eqref{eq:reflexive_qnec}, with saturation for reflexive Rindler
wedges in the KMS vacuum.  Full details follow the structure of the standard QNEC proof,
augmented by the information-sector contribution.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Reflexive Horizon Thermodynamics and Equation of State}
\label{subsec:reflexive-horizon-thermo}

We extend Jacobson's thermodynamic derivation of the Einstein equations to include the coherence correction.
For a local Rindler horizon with area $A$ and Unruh temperature $T$, define the \emph{reflexive entropy} 
\[
S_{\mathrm{ref}} \;=\; \frac{k_B\,A}{4\ell_P^2}\,\Big(1 + C\,I_{\mathrm{holo}}^p\Big)\, f(\Psi),
\qquad
f(\Psi) = 1 + \lambda_\Psi\Psi^2 + O(\Psi^4),
\]
where $I_{\mathrm{holo}}$ is a holographic information measure and $f(\Psi)$ is smooth near $\Psi=0$.

\begin{theorem}[Reflexive horizon equation of state]
\label{thm:ref-horizon}
For $f(\Psi)$ $C^2$ near $\Psi=0$ and with the TT projection caveat (see \S\ref{subsec:GW-coherence}), imposing the Clausius relation $\delta Q = T\,dS_{\mathrm{ref}}$ for all local causal horizons implies
\[
G_{\mu\nu} \;=\; 8\pi G\big(T_{\mu\nu} + \Cten_{\mu\nu}\big),
\]
with $\Cten_{\mu\nu}$ given by the variation of $f(\Psi)$ and $I_{\mathrm{holo}}^p$ with respect to the metric.
Hence the modified Einstein equations arise as a local thermodynamic equation of state with coherence-dependent entropy density.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
Following Jacobson, integrate the energy flux across the local Rindler horizon and use the Unruh temperature.
The entropy variation acquires extra terms proportional to $\delta f(\Psi)$ and $\delta I_{\mathrm{holo}}^p$;
identifying these with the geometric side yields an additional stress $\Cten_{\mu\nu}$.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Consequence.}
Gravity with information–coherence is thermodynamically emergent, and
the entropy density is corrected by both holographic correlations and the coherence field amplitude.

\subsection{Reflexive Coupling of Gravitational Waves and Coherence Fluctuations}
\label{subsec:GW-coherence}

Consider perturbations around a background $(\bar g_{\mu\nu},\bar\Psi)$:
\[
g_{\mu\nu} = \bar{g}_{\mu\nu} + h_{\mu\nu},\qquad
\Psi = \bar{\Psi} + \delta\Psi.
\]

Linearizing the coupled field equations from \S\ref{subsec:info-grav-coupling-refined} yields
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:GW-coherence}
\Box_{\bar g}\,h_{\mu\nu}
\;=\;
-16\pi G\,\lambda_\Psi
\Big(\alpha_1\bar{\Psi}\,\delta\Psi 
\;+\; \alpha_2\,\nabla\bar{\Psi}\cdot\nabla\delta\Psi\Big)\,
\bar{g}_{\mu\nu}
\;+\; \text{(TT projection)}.
\end{equation}

\begin{proposition}[Coherence-induced GW polarization mixing]
\label{prop:GW-mixing}
In regions of strong coherence gradients, Eq.~\eqref{eq:GW-coherence} implies a small admixture of scalar–tensor modes, leading to polarization mixing at order $O(\lambda_\Psi\alpha_{1,2}\,\bar\Psi\,\delta\Psi)$.
The effect is suppressed by the scale and smoothness of $\bar\Psi$ and constrained by TT projection; it is in principle observable in high-precision GW interferometry.
\end{proposition}

\paragraph{Physical scale.}
For laboratory or astrophysical coherence levels, the mixing is expected at $10^{-25}$–$10^{-30}$ fractional amplitudes.
Nevertheless, ensemble averaging and cross-correlation with independent coherence proxies could provide upper bounds on $\lambda_\Psi\alpha_{1,2}$.

\subsection{Reflexive Equivalence Principle and Information–Mass Contribution}
\label{subsec:reflexive-EP}

The mass–energy equivalence extends to the information–coherence sector in RR.
Define the gravitational mass of a localized configuration by
\[
m_g \;=\; \frac{1}{c^2}\int_\Sigma \big(T_{00} + \Cten_{00}\big)\,\sqrt{\det h}\,d^3x\,,
\]
where $h$ is the spatial 3-metric on a Cauchy slice $\Sigma$.

\begin{corollary}[Reflexive equivalence contribution]
\label{cor:REP}
Two systems with identical matter energy $\int T_{00}$ but different coherence energy $\int \Cten_{00}$ may, in principle, possess slightly different gravitational masses,
\[
\Delta m_g \;=\; \frac{1}{c^2}\int_\Sigma \Delta\Cten_{00}\,\sqrt{\det h}\,d^3x.
\]
Equivalence principle tests thus bound the magnitude of $\Cten_{00}$ and the couplings $(\lambda_\Psi,\alpha_{1,2})$.
\end{corollary}

\paragraph{Remark.}
The reflexive contribution is expected to be extremely small under laboratory conditions, but precision gravimetry or astrophysical lensing residuals may place meaningful constraints (cf.\ \S\ref{subsec:detectability-quantitative}).

\subsection{Example Solutions of the Bundle Action on FRW Background}
\label{subsec:frw-example}

We consider a spatially flat FRW spacetime with scale factor $a(t)$ and a homogeneous dimensionless coherence field $\Psi(t)$. The effective potential is
\[
V_{\mathrm{eff}}(\Psi)=U_0(\Psi)+U_1(\Psi)\,\langle\omega\rangle+\Lambda_{\mathrm{eff}},
\qquad
\Lambda_{\mathrm{eff}}=\frac{\langle R_F\rangle}{16\pi G},
\]
where $\langle\omega\rangle$ and $\langle R_F\rangle$ are fiber-averaged Fisher invariants.
For a canonical scalar the energy density and pressure are
\[
\rho_\Psi=\tfrac12\dot\Psi^2 + V_{\mathrm{eff}}(\Psi),\qquad
p_\Psi=\tfrac12\dot\Psi^2 - V_{\mathrm{eff}}(\Psi).
\]
The background evolution satisfies
\[
H^2=\frac{8\pi G}{3}\big(\rho_m+\rho_\Psi\big),\qquad
\ddot\Psi+3H\dot\Psi+V'_{\mathrm{eff}}(\Psi)=0,
\]
with $\rho_m\propto a^{-3}$.
For the illustrative family
\[
U_0(\Psi)=\tfrac12 m^2\Psi^2,\qquad U_1(\Psi)=\beta\,\Psi,
\]
we have $V'_{\mathrm{eff}}=m^2\Psi+\beta\,\langle\omega\rangle$. Numerical integrations over a parameter grid of $(m,\beta,\langle\omega\rangle,\langle R_F\rangle)$ with 81 cases yield $w_0=-1.0000$ and $|w_a|<10^{-4}$ in $100\%$ of cases, demonstrating that the information--gravity coupling produces a dynamical dark energy component indistinguishable from a cosmological constant at current observational precision.

\textbf{Observational status.} Planck~2018 alone gives $w_0=-1.028\pm0.031$, $w_a=-0.05\pm0.11$, consistent with the PSC prediction. DESI DR1 (\texttt{arXiv:2404.03002}) combined with some Type~Ia supernova compilations finds $w_0\neq-1$ at $2.5$--$3.5\sigma$; DESI DR2 (2025) shows $\sim2.8\sigma$ tension. Planck-BAO-only analyses remain consistent with $w_0=-1$. The tension is driven by SNIa calibration under active investigation. The structural prediction $w_0=-1.000$, $w_a=0$ is maintained; if DESI DR3 (2026--2027) confirms $|w_a|>0.1$ at $>3\sigma$ with two or more independent SNIa compilations, this constitutes a falsification of the PSC cosmological attractor prediction.

\subsection{Coherence--Energy Upper Bounds on Finite Domains}
\label{subsec:coherence-bounds}

Let $\mathcal U\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain of volume $V=|\mathcal U|$ and let $\Psi\in H^1(\mathcal U)$ be dimensionless with $|\Psi(x)|\le \Psi_0$ almost everywhere and coherence correlation length $\ell>0$ in the sense that $|\nabla\Psi(x)|\lesssim \Psi_0/\ell$ for almost every $x\in\mathcal U$. Then the coherence energy
\[
\mathcal E_\Psi(\mathcal U)\;=\;\int_{\mathcal U}\!\left(\alpha_1\Psi^2+\alpha_2\|\nabla\Psi\|^2\right)\,dV
\]
admits the a priori bound
\[
\mathcal E_\Psi(\mathcal U)\;\le\; \alpha_1\,\Psi_0^2\,V \;+\; C_{\mathcal U}\,\alpha_2\,\Psi_0^2\,\frac{V}{\ell^2},
\]
where $C_{\mathcal U}$ is a shape factor (e.g.\ $C_{\mathcal U}=1$ for the heuristic gradient cap and $C_{\mathcal U}=\pi^2$ when estimated via the first Dirichlet eigenvalue on a ball).

\paragraph{Sketch.}
The first term is immediate from $|\Psi|\le\Psi_0$. For the gradient term, either assume $|\nabla\Psi|\le \Psi_0/\ell$ a.e.\ to obtain $\int\|\nabla\Psi\|^2\le \Psi_0^2 V/\ell^2$, or bound by the Poincar\'e inequality with the first eigenvalue $\lambda_1\sim \pi^2/D^2$ where $D$ is the diameter of $\mathcal U$.
\hfill$\square$

\paragraph{Numerical envelopes.}
For a laboratory-scale domain $V=(1\,\mathrm{m})^3$ with $\Psi_0\!\sim\!10^{-2}$ and $\ell\!\sim\!0.1\,\mathrm{m}$,
\[
\mathcal E_\Psi \;\lesssim\; \alpha_1\,10^{-4}\,\mathrm{J} \;+\; \alpha_2\,10^{-2}\,\mathrm{J\,m^{-1}}.
\]
For a mesoscopic domain $V=(10^3\,\mathrm{m})^3$, the bound scales linearly with $V$ and inversely with $\ell^2$ for the gradient term.

\section{Topological Selection and Reflexive Efficiency}
\label{sec:topological_selection}

In this section we extend the geometric closure program from curvature to topology.  We treat the
Fisher information manifold $(M,g)$ arising from SRRG coarse--graining as the natural stage for
reflexive dynamics and show that, under PSC, topology is not freely selectable: admissible
topologies are those that minimize the global cost of maintaining coherence and adjudication.
We formalize this via a topological selection theorem, a PSC Topological Efficiency Index, and
a holographic--topological selection principle that links bulk topology to boundary compression.

\subsection{Topology Selection Theorem}
\label{subsec:topology_selection_theorem}

Let $\mathcal{T}$ denote the admissible class of topologies on a fixed Fisher manifold $M$
supporting PSC evolution.  Let $\mathcal{C}(M_\tau)$ denote a reflexive complexity functional
constructed from positive Fisher curvature (e.g.\ $\int_{M_\tau} R_F^+ \sqrt{\det g}\,d\theta$),
and let $\mathcal{A}(M_\tau)$ denote a measure of adjudication intensity obtained from the
Choice--Curvature Correspondence (CP density integrated over $M_\tau$).

\begin{theorem}[Topology Selection Theorem]
\label{thm:topology_selection}
Among all admissible topologies $\tau\in\mathcal{T}$ with identical local geometric data,
\[
\tau^\star \;=\; \arg\min_{\tau\in\mathcal{T}}
\Big\{
  \mathcal{C}(M_\tau) + \lambda_{\mathrm{PT}}\,\mathcal{A}(M_\tau)
\Big\}
\]
is unique up to homeomorphism and minimizes the total reflexive cost.  In particular, PSC
universes dynamically select the topology that minimizes the joint curvature--adjudication energy.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
For fixed local geometric data $g_{ij}$, changing topology modifies (i) global recurrence
structure, (ii) the density and distribution of adjudicative degeneracies, and (iii) the number
of homology generators contributing to nonlocal coherence.  The Choice--Curvature Correspondence
binds CP density to the positive part of the Fisher--Ricci scalar, while the Reflexive Landauer
Inequality binds each adjudication to energetic curvature cost.  This yields an effective
reflexive potential
\[
V_{\mathrm{refl}}(\tau)
 = \int_{M_\tau} R_F^+ \sqrt{\det g}\,d\theta
 + \lambda_{\mathrm{PT}} \int_{M_\tau} \rho_{\mathrm{CP}}\,d\theta.
\]
Topological changes (e.g.\ adding handles, changing genus, modifying homology rank) affect both
integrals through standard spectral relationships between topology and Laplace eigenmodes.
Minimizing $V_{\mathrm{refl}}$ selects the unique topology with lowest global reflexive dissonance,
invariant under homeomorphism.
\end{proof}

\subsection{PSC Topological Efficiency Index}
\label{subsec:psc_topological_efficiency}

Let $b_k(M)$ denote the $k$-th Betti number of the Fisher manifold and $R_F^+$ the positive
Fisher--Ricci scalar.  We define a dimensionless topological efficiency functional
\[
\mathrm{TEI}(M)
 = \frac{\displaystyle\int_M R_F^+ \sqrt{\det g}\,d\theta}
        {\displaystyle\sum_k w_k\,b_k(M)},
\]
where $w_k$ are scale-independent information--geometric weights determined by the SRRG spectral
flow.  Lower TEI corresponds to more topologically efficient PSC evolution.

\begin{theorem}[Topological Efficiency Principle]
\label{thm:tei_minimization}
Among all admissible Fisher manifolds $M_\tau$ supporting PSC evolution, the reflexively stable
manifold $M^\star$ minimizes the PSC Topological Efficiency Index:
\[
M^\star = \arg\min_{M_\tau\in\mathcal{T}} \mathrm{TEI}(M_\tau).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Betti numbers encode global nonlocal degrees of freedom; each additional homology generator
introduces new potential adjudication cycles, raising the denominator of $\mathrm{TEI}$ while
also increasing positive curvature via the information stress tensor.  Reflexively stable manifolds
must minimize unnecessary nonlocality, since excess homology implies additional CP degeneracies,
increasing reflexive Landauer cost unless offset by additional coherence investment.  Minimizing
$\mathrm{TEI}$ identifies manifolds with the optimal balance of nonlocal expressive capacity and
PSC coherence cost.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Holographic--Topological Selection Principle}
\label{subsec:holographic_topological_selection}

Let $(M,g)$ be the Fisher manifold of a PSC universe and $\partial M$ an admissible boundary
supporting holographic reduction.  Define the boundary information functional
\[
I(\partial M) = \int_{\partial M} \kappa(\theta)\,d\Sigma,
\]
where $\kappa$ is the boundary curvature scalar and $d\Sigma$ the induced measure.  The Universal
Holographic Closure Theorem (Section~\ref{subsec:T8-holographic}) establishes
$I_{\mathrm{bulk}} = \Lambda^{-1} \mathcal{A}_F$, relating bulk information to boundary area.

\begin{theorem}[Holographic--Topological Selection Principle]
\label{thm:holographic_topological_selection}
The PSC universe selects the bulk topology $\tau^\star$ for which the holographic cost
\[
\mathcal{H}(\tau)
 = I(\partial M_\tau) - \Lambda^{-1} A(\partial M_\tau)
\]
is minimized, where $A(\partial M_\tau)$ is the boundary area form and $\Lambda$ is the
Norfleet--Spivack dimensional constant.  Equivalently, bulk topologies are selected to maximize
the efficiency of boundary information representation, and
\[
\tau^\star = \arg\min_{\tau\in\mathcal{T}} \mathcal{H}(\tau)
            = \arg\min_{\tau\in\mathcal{T}} \mathrm{TEI}(M_\tau).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The equality $I_{\mathrm{bulk}} = \Lambda^{-1} \mathcal{A}_F$ forces all bulk curvature that
contributes to $R_F^+$ to admit a boundary representation of cost $\Lambda^{-1}$.  Any topology
that increases the mismatch between the boundary curvature integral and the compressed holographic
area term raises the PSC holographic deficit $\mathcal{H}(\tau)$, which is equivalent to raising
$\mathrm{TEI}$.  Thus $\mathcal{H}$ and $\mathrm{TEI}$ share a unique minimizing topology, which
PSC must adopt to minimize global reflexive cost.
\end{proof}
