These tasks, together with the TE$_1$.R continuous model, support a $\Lambda\Omega$--Z$_2$ closure dictionary: the hypercomplex walk of Norfleet's Dimensional Dynamics~\cite{NorfleetPrivComm} corresponds to the analytic AG-1 gauge, while PR-0 and SRRG supply the discrete gauge and PT normal-step dynamics that land on the same half-turn closure circles.  The TE$_1$.O ``fast-win'' diagnostics show that the PT normal-step restoration time and the $\Omega$-driven Born fit yield normalization constants within a few percent of the analytic Z$_2$ closure value, consistent with a shared minimum of the phenomenological PR-0 dissonance functional $D$ and the analytic KL potential~$\Phi$.

\subsection{Adjudication Ensembles: Collective, Synchronized, and Recursive CP Dynamics}
\label{subsec:ensemble-CP}

We consider sets of coupled Choice Points (CPs) that arise within or across interacting subsystems.
Let $\{x_i\}_{i=1}^N$ denote CP sites, each with admissible branch set $\mathcal B_i$ and local dissonance $D_i$,
and let $\Psi_i$ be the local coherence field amplitude.  

We introduce a mesoscopic ensemble functional
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:D-ensemble}
\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ens}}(\{b_i\},\{\Psi_i\})
\;=\;\sum_{i=1}^N D_i(b_i,\Psi_i)\;+\;\sum_{i\neq j} J_{ij}\, \Upsilon(b_i,b_j;\Psi_i,\Psi_j),
\end{equation}
where $b_i\in\mathcal B_i$ is the chosen branch at site $i$, $J_{ij}$ are symmetric coupling coefficients,
and $\Upsilon$ is a bounded, twice-differentiable interaction term (e.g.\ favoring alignment/anti-alignment of branch attributes under shared coherence).

\begin{definition}[Ensemble Adjudication Map]
\label{def:PT-ensemble}
An \emph{ensemble adjudication} is a joint selection
\(
\bm b^\star=(b_1^\star,\dots,b_N^\star)\in\prod_i\mathcal B_i
\)
satisfying the minimum principle
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:PT-ensemble}
\bm b^\star \;\in\; \arg\min_{\bm b\in\prod_i\mathcal B_i} \;\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ens}}(\bm b,\{\Psi_i\}) ,
\end{equation}
where the minimization is implemented by the (possibly recursive) action of $\PT$ along edges of an influence graph $\mathsf G=(V,E)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Synchronous adjudication threshold]
\label{thm:synch-threshold}
Suppose (i) each $D_i$ is $\mu$–strongly convex in a local chart around its minima,
(ii) $\Upsilon$ is Lipschitz with constant $L_\Upsilon$, and (iii) the coupling graph $\mathsf G$ has spectral radius $\rho(W)$, with $W=[|J_{ij}|]$.
Then there exists a critical coupling $J_c$ such that if $\|W\|_2< J_c$ the unique minimizer $\bm b^\star$ is close to the block-diagonal (decoupled) selection; if $\|W\|_2>J_c$, synchronous (collective) adjudication emerges and small local CP events can trigger cascades.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
Apply standard results for strongly convex objectives with Lipschitz couplings (perturbation of block-diagonal Hessians).
Below threshold, the Schur complement remains positive-definite and the minimum factorizes perturbatively.
Above threshold, the global Hessian loses diagonal dominance and the minimum corresponds to a symmetry-broken, synchronized assignment.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Adjudication cascades and avalanche scaling]
\label{cor:avalanche}
In the supercritical regime $\|W\|_2>J_c$, the distribution of cascade sizes $S$ (number of CPs co-adjudicated in a burst)
admits a power-law tail $P(S\!\ge s)\sim s^{-\kappa}$ over a mesoscopic range, with $\kappa$ determined by the effective branching number of $\mathsf G$ and the excess coupling $\|W\|_2/J_c-1$.  

This yields testable signatures in the temporal clustering of adjudication times and in the integrated energetic bursts via the Reflexive Landauer term.
\end{corollary}

\paragraph{No-signalling and microcausality.}
Ensemble couplings $J_{ij}$ are implemented through physical interactions (Hamiltonian or classical channels) that respect causal cones (Sec.~\ref{subsec:dual-operator}).
Therefore ensemble adjudication preserves microcausality: correlations arise from prepared entanglement and local couplings, not superluminal signalling.
The EPR/Bell correlations appear as constraints on the feasible set $\prod_i\mathcal B_i$ and on admissible $\Upsilon$;
the joint minimization \eqref{eq:PT-ensemble} reproduces quantum marginals without enabling PR-box behaviour.

\paragraph{Falsifiable predictions (collective signatures).}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Cascade timing and size distributions.}
In arrays of weakly coupled interferometers or spin-squeezed ensembles,
increase $J_{ij}$ (e.g.\ via tunable photon exchange) while keeping local $E_G$ and temperature fixed.  

RR predicts (i) synchronized CP timing beyond $J_c$, (ii) power-law-like avalanche statistics, and (iii) superlinear scaling of total adjudication energy $\Delta E_{\PT}^{\mathrm{burst}}\sim N_{\mathrm{eff}}\,(k_BT\log n + \text{coherence term})$.

\item \textbf{Coherent–energetic bursts.}
Use cryogenic calorimetry around coupled BECs or superconducting qubit lattices;
search for bursty excess energy consistent with aggregated Reflexive Landauer cost and enhanced by $\sum_{i\neq j}J_{ij}$.

\item \textbf{Entangled ensemble discrimination.}
Prepare bipartite ensembles with identical $E_G$ but different coupling graphs;
RR predicts different collapse/adjudication latency distributions as a function of $\|W\|_2$, unlike pure OR or GRW/CSL which do not depend on ensemble coherence couplings.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Computational validation.}
A reference implementation \texttt{e25\_ensemble\_cascade.py} simulates \eqref{eq:D-ensemble} with (i) convex $D_i$, (ii) Kuramoto-style or Ising-style $\Upsilon$, and (iii) a $\PT$–like coordinate descent / best-response dynamics, displaying the subcritical–supercritical transition and avalanche exponents.

\subsection{Superposition and Decoherence from Ensemble Adjudication}
\label{subsec:superposition-decoherence-ensemble}

We show that both superposition persistence and decoherence can be treated as limiting regimes of the \emph{ensemble adjudication} dynamics introduced in \S\ref{subsec:ensemble-CP}. Let $\{x_i\}_{i=1}^N$ denote CP sites with admissible branch sets $\mathcal B_i$, local coherence amplitudes $\Psi_i$, and couplings $J_{ij}$ over a graph $\mathsf G=(V,E)$.

\paragraph{Ensemble decoherence functional.}
Write the reduced state on a chosen branch basis $\{|b\rangle\}$ as $\rho = \sum_{b,b'}\rho_{bb'}\,|b\rangle\!\langle b'|$. We define a \emph{coherence–sensitive ensemble decoherence functional}
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:ensemble-decoherence}
\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ens}}[\rho;\Psi,W]
\;:=\;
\sum_{i}\!\sum_{b\neq b'} \Gamma_i(\Psi_i)\,\chi_i(b,b')\,|\rho_{bb'}|
\;+\;
\sum_{i\neq j} J_{ij}\,\Xi_{ij}(\Psi_i,\Psi_j)\,\Upsilon_{ij}(\rho),
\end{equation}
where $\Gamma_i(\Psi_i)\ge 0$ increases with local coherence (e.g.\ $\Gamma_i\propto\Psi_i^2$), $\chi_i$ projects off-diagonal pairs that differ on site $i$, and $\Upsilon_{ij}$ penalizes phase correlations that are unstable under adjudication couplings. The modulation $\Xi_{ij}$ is Lipschitz in $(\Psi_i,\Psi_j)$.

\paragraph{Pre-adjudicative (superposition) regime.}
When $\|W\|_2 < J_c$ (subcritical coupling) and $\Gamma_i(\Psi_i)$ are below RM/PSA thresholds,
\(
\dot{\mathcal D}_{\mathrm{ens}}\approx 0
\)
and off-diagonal elements $|\rho_{bb'}|$ remain metastable; superpositions persist (unitary evolution dominates). Conversely, as $\Gamma_i$ and $\|W\|_2$ increase, off-diagonal elements decay at an emergent ensemble rate (Theorems~\ref{thm:pointer-selection}--\ref{thm:EAME-Lindblad}).

\begin{theorem}[Ensemble pointer-basis selection]
\label{thm:pointer-selection}
Let the adjudication ensemble be governed by the joint objective
\[
\mathcal G[\rho;\Psi]
\;=\;
D[\rho,\Psi]\;+\;\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ens}}[\rho;\Psi,W],
\]
with $D$ and $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ens}}$ convex in a neighborhood of their minima. If (i) $\Gamma_i(\Psi_i)\ge \Gamma_0>0$ on a time window and (ii) $\|W\|_2>J_c$ (supercritical coupling; Thm.~\ref{thm:synch-threshold}), then the minimizer of $\mathcal G$ selects a branch basis that diagonalizes the reduced dynamics to leading order: $\rho\to \sum_b p_b |b\rangle\!\langle b|$. In particular, the ensemble picks a \emph{pointer basis} that minimizes $\mathcal G$; off-diagonal elements in that basis are exponentially suppressed.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
Strong convexity near the joint minimum plus supercritical coupling implies a unique stable minimum of $\mathcal G$ that aligns branch labels with the dominant coupling eigendirections (spectral theorem on the graph Laplacian/coupling operator). The off-diagonal penalty in $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ens}}$ enforces diagonality in the selected basis.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Ensemble Adjudication Master Equation (EAME)]
\label{thm:EAME-Lindblad}
Under weak-coupling, Markovian coarse-graining (Born–Markov approximation) and stationary $\Psi_i$, the reduced state obeys
\[
\dot{\rho}
\;=\;
-\,i[H_{\mathrm{eff}},\rho]\;+\;
\sum_{\alpha} \gamma_\alpha
\Big(L_\alpha\,\rho\,L_\alpha^\dagger
- \tfrac12\{L_\alpha^\dagger L_\alpha,\rho\}\Big)
\]
where the Lindblad rates $\gamma_\alpha$ are functions of the ensemble parameters:
\[
\gamma_\alpha \;\equiv\; \gamma_\alpha\!\big(\{\Gamma_i(\Psi_i)\},\;\|W\|_2,\;\mathrm{spec}(W)\big).
\]
Moreover, in the subcritical limit $(\|W\|_2\!<\!J_c)$, $\gamma_\alpha\!\to\!0$ as $\Gamma_i\!\to\!0$ and the equation reduces to unitary evolution; in RM/PSA windows with supercritical coupling, $\gamma_\alpha>0$ produces exponential decoherence in the ensemble-selected pointer basis.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
Standard projection-operator methods with local adjudication "kicks" (modeled as Poissonian in time) yield a GKSL generator where jump operators $L_\alpha$ reflect the principal directions of the ensemble penalty $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ens}}$. The rates inherit their dependence from $\Gamma_i(\Psi_i)$ and the coupling spectrum.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Observable dependence of extracted rates]
The sensitivity of $\gamma_\alpha(\|W\|_2)$ measurements depends on the observable chosen. Fast-thermalizing observables (e.g., Ising magnetization $m=\langle b\rangle$ in binary models) show weak correlation with $\|W\|_2$ because local flips dominate the dynamics. Slower collective observables (e.g., Kuramoto order parameter $r=|\langle e^{i\theta}\rangle|$ in continuous-phase models) exhibit clearer $\gamma(\|W\|_2)$ dependence, as the master-equation timescale becomes resolvable above the fast local relaxation. This is confirmed by computational tests: E9b/E9c show weak correlation for Ising spins, while E9e (Kuramoto) demonstrates moderate dependence ($|\rho|=0.46$).
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Zeno-like stabilization by frequent ensemble adjudication]
\label{cor:Zeno-ensemble}

\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Reflexive H-Theorem with KMS Steady State]
\label{thm:reflexive-h-theorem}
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be the GKSL generator emerging from the Ensemble Adjudication Master Equation (EAME) via Theorem~\ref{thm:EAME-Lindblad}, and let $\rho_t$ solve $\dot\rho=\mathcal{L}\rho$.
If the adjudication kernel $K_{\mathrm{PT}}$ satisfies \emph{reflexive detailed balance} (i.e., transitions $x\to x'$ obey $K_{\mathrm{PT}}(x\to x')/K_{\mathrm{PT}}(x'\to x)=\exp(\Delta S_{\mathrm{ref}})$ where $\Delta S_{\mathrm{ref}}$ includes Reflexive Landauer costs), then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item There exists a unique steady state $\rho_*$ satisfying $\mathcal{L}\rho_*=0$.
\item The reflexive entropy $S_{\mathrm{ref}}(\rho_t)=-\mathrm{Tr}(\rho_t\log\rho_t)+C\int I_{\mathrm{holo}}(\rho_t)$ is monotonically increasing:
\[
\frac{d}{dt}S_{\mathrm{ref}}(\rho_t)=\sigma_{\mathrm{ref}}(\rho_t)\ge \lambda\,\mathcal{D}(\rho_t\|\rho_*),
\]
for some $\lambda>0$, where $\mathcal{D}(\rho\|\sigma)=\mathrm{Tr}(\rho\log\rho-\rho\log\sigma)$ is the quantum relative entropy.
\item The steady state $\rho_*$ satisfies a Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (KMS) condition with respect to the adjudication flow, ensuring thermal equilibrium at effective temperature $T_{\mathrm{eff}}=\alpha_0/k_B$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
(i) Standard GKSL theory ensures the existence and uniqueness of the steady state $\rho_*$ given the Lindblad structure.
(ii) The entropy production rate $\sigma_{\mathrm{ref}}(\rho_t)$ is the sum of two positive terms: the von Neumann entropy production $\mathrm{Tr}(\mathcal{L}\rho\log\rho)$ (standard GKSL H-theorem) and the holographic information dissipation $C\,dI_{\mathrm{holo}}/dt$. By convexity of relative entropy and the Lindblad structure, $\sigma_{\mathrm{ref}}\ge \lambda\mathcal{D}(\rho_t\|\rho_*)$ for some $\lambda>0$ (quantum log-Sobolev inequality).
(iii) The KMS condition follows from detailed balance: for observables $A,B$ and time evolution $\alpha_t(A)=e^{t\mathcal{L}^\dagger}(A)$, one has $\mathrm{Tr}(\rho_*\,A\,\alpha_{i\beta}(B))=\mathrm{Tr}(\rho_*\,B\,A)$ where $\beta=1/(k_BT_{\mathrm{eff}})$.
For the full proof using the quantum detailed balance condition and the spectral theory of $\mathcal{L}$, see Appendix~\ref{app:h-theorem-proof}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
This theorem establishes that ensemble adjudication not only produces GKSL dynamics but also satisfies the second law of thermodynamics in its quantum form, with monotonic entropy increase and convergence to a unique thermal equilibrium. The KMS condition ensures that the steady state is a Gibbs state with respect to the adjudication Hamiltonian, linking Transputation to standard statistical mechanics.
\end{remark}

\paragraph{Interpretation.}
Below the synchronization threshold and without RM/PSA, ensemble couplings are too weak to select a pointer basis or to penalize off-diagonal coherences (superpositions persist, unitary regime).  

Above threshold and/or in RM/PSA windows, the ensemble objective $\mathcal G=D+\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ens}}$ selects a basis and produces GKSL-type damping with rates determined by $\Gamma_i(\Psi_i)$ and $\|W\|_2$ (Theorems~\ref{thm:pointer-selection}--\ref{thm:EAME-Lindblad}).  

Thus environment-induced decoherence emerges here as a \emph{special case} of reflexive, coherence-sensitive adjudication in ensembles, with \emph{additional} testable dependencies on system coherence and coupling spectrum that are absent in purely stochastic collapse or in "environment-only" models.

\paragraph{Causality and locality.}
All adjudication processes respect microcausality and Lorentz covariance; no superluminal signaling is implied. Ensemble couplings propagate at finite speed $v_{\PT}\le c$, and the effective decoherence rates emerge from local interactions within the light cone. The GKSL master equation preserves the relativistic causal structure: pointer-basis selection and off-diagonal decay occur through local adjudication events constrained by $\|W\|_2$ and the underlying causal graph topology.

\subsection{Temporal Adjudication Ensembles and Causal Consistency}
\label{subsec:temporal-ensemble}

Adjudication ensembles may extend across time as well as space, coupling Choice Points (CPs)
that are timelike-separated within each other's causal cones.
Formally, replace the spatial coupling matrix $J_{ij}$ by a spacetime kernel
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:J-spacetime}
J(x,t;x',t') \;=\; 
\Theta\big(c^2(t-t')^2 - |\bm{x}-\bm{x}'|^2\big)\;
\mathcal{J}\big(\Psi(x,t),\Psi(x',t'),\Delta t\big),
\end{equation}
where $\Theta$ enforces causal support, and $\mathcal{J}$ is smooth and rapidly decaying outside the light cone.

\paragraph{Causal-temporal ensemble functional.}
The ensemble dissonance becomes
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:D-ens-time}
\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{ens}}[\Psi]
=\int\! d^4x\, D(\Psi(x)) 
+\frac12\!\iint\! d^4x\,d^4x'\,
J(x,t;x',t')\,\Upsilon(x,x';\Psi(x),\Psi(x')).
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Causal consistency of temporal adjudication]
\label{thm:temporal-consistency}
If $J(x,t;x',t')$ satisfies Eq.~\eqref{eq:J-spacetime} and $\Upsilon$ is Lipschitz continuous in its arguments,
then (i) the Euler–Lagrange equations of $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{ens}}$ are hyperbolic and respect microcausality, and
(ii) the global minimizer $\Psi^\star(x,t)$ is unique up to gauge under fixed boundary data on a Cauchy surface.
Apparent retrocausal correlations correspond to global consistency of $\Psi^\star$ across the entire block spacetime and
do not imply acausal signal propagation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
Variation of Eq.~\eqref{eq:D-ens-time} yields an integro-differential Euler–Lagrange system
\[
(-\Box+m^2)\Psi(x)
= \frac{\delta D}{\delta\Psi(x)}
+\int J(x,x')\,\frac{\partial\Upsilon}{\partial\Psi(x)}\,d^4x'.
\]
The causal support of $J$ ensures hyperbolicity; uniqueness follows from convexity of $D$
and Lipschitz continuity of $\Upsilon$. The global minimum is determined over the full spacetime manifold,
making all timelike CPs jointly self-consistent.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Physical interpretation.}
Temporal adjudication ensembles thus unify spatial and temporal correlations:
they produce \emph{retrodictive coherence}---past and future CPs align to minimize the global dissonance functional---without any violation of relativistic causality.
Delayed-choice and quantum-eraser effects arise as manifestations of this blockwise
self-consistency: the coherence field enforces identical boundary conditions on both ends of the adjudicative network.

\begin{corollary}[Lorentz covariance and time dilation of adjudication]
\label{cor:time-dilation-PT}
Special Relativity imposes Lorentz covariance on all lawful physical processes,
including transputation and adjudication. 
The local adjudication rate $\Gamma_\PT$ therefore transforms as a Lorentz scalar field density.
In an inertial frame moving with velocity $v$ relative to the adjudicator's rest frame,
the observed adjudication rate per coordinate time is
\[
\Gamma_\PT'(v) \;=\; \Gamma_\PT \sqrt{1-\frac{v^2}{c^2}},
\]
and the corresponding energy throughput satisfies $P_\PT' = P_\PT \sqrt{1-v^2/c^2}$.
The Reflexive continuity equation
$\nabla_\mu J_\PT^\mu=0$, with $J_\PT^\mu=\rho_\PT u^\mu$, is Lorentz covariant.
Hence, Transputation and all adjudicative processes obey relativistic time dilation and
cannot propagate information faster than light.
\end{corollary}

\paragraph{Interpretation.}
Adjudication is a physical process constrained by the light cone ($v_\PT\!\le\!c$).
Its proper rate and energy per act are Lorentz-invariant,
but an observer in relative motion perceives slowed adjudication in proportion to the Lorentz factor $\gamma^{-1}$.
This confirms that Reflexive Reality is fully consistent with Special Relativity:
transputation defines a locally covariant, finite-speed flow of coherence in spacetime.

\subsection{Long-Range Self-Organization from Ensemble Adjudication}
\label{subsec:LR-selforg-ensemble}

We show that coherence-mediated ensemble adjudication produces long-range (LR) order by extending
the correlation length $\xi$ beyond local decoherence scales via (i) spectral amplification of the coupling operator
and (ii) MDL-guided pointer-basis selection (Sec.~\ref{subsec:superposition-decoherence-ensemble}).

\paragraph{Coherence-renormalized correlation length.}
Let $W=[|J_{ij}|]$ be the nonnegative coupling matrix on the CP graph $\mathsf G$, and
let $\Gamma_i(\Psi_i)$ denote local coherence penalties in the ensemble objective $\mathcal G=D+\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ens}}$.
Define an \emph{effective LR kernel} by
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:W-eff}
W_{\mathrm{eff}}
\;:=\;
\sum_{k=0}^\infty \;\Big(\mathbf{1}-\mathrm{diag}\,\Gamma(\Psi)\Big)^{k} \, W^k,
\quad
\Gamma(\Psi):=\mathrm{diag}(\Gamma_1(\Psi_1),\dots,\Gamma_N(\Psi_N)),
\end{equation}
whenever the Neumann series converges (subcritical regime). 

The corresponding correlation length satisfies:
\[
\xi \;\sim\; \ell_0 \Big(1 - \|W_{\mathrm{eff}}\|_2/J_c\Big)^{-\nu},
\qquad \nu>0,
\]
for some microscopic $\ell_0$ and critical $J_c$ (Sec.~\ref{subsec:ensemble-CP}).
This renormalization shows that large $\mathcal I_{\mathrm{coh}}$ (i.e.\ small $\Gamma$) and large $\|W\|_2$ both increase $\xi$.

\begin{theorem}[Coherence-boosted long-range order]
\label{thm:LR-order}
Assume (i) $\Gamma_i(\Psi_i)\le \Gamma_{\max}<1$ and (ii) $\|W\|_2$ is such that $\| W_{\mathrm{eff}}\|_2 < J_c$ but close to $J_c$.
Then there exists a mesoscopic window where the two-point correlation function
$C(r)=\langle b_i b_j\rangle-\langle b_i\rangle\langle b_j\rangle$ obeys
\[
C(r)\;\approx\; A\, \frac{e^{-r/\xi}}{r^{d-2+\eta}},\quad \xi \sim \ell_0 \Big(1 - \|W_{\mathrm{eff}}\|_2/J_c\Big)^{-\nu},
\]
with critical exponents $(\nu,\eta)$ determined by the spectral density of $W$ and the slope of $\Gamma(\Psi)$ near the operating point.
Increasing coherence intensity $\mathcal I_{\mathrm{coh}}$ (reducing $\Gamma$) or increasing $\|W\|_2$ drives $\xi\uparrow$ and enhances LR order.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
Apply standard cluster expansion/mean-field arguments to the convex objective $\mathcal G$ with effective kernel $W_{\mathrm{eff}}$.
Near threshold the susceptibility diverges as $(1-\|W_{\mathrm{eff}}\|_2/J_c)^{-1}$, which controls the exponential correlation length.
Exponents follow from the graph spectral measure and the local curvature of the cost landscape.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Hysteresis and memory in recursive ensembles.}
When temporal couplings are included (Sec.~\ref{subsec:temporal-ensemble}) through a causal kernel $J(x,t;x',t')$,
the ensemble objective acquires a \emph{memory term}
\begin{equation}

J(x,t;x',t')\,\Upsilon(b(x,t),b(x',t');\Psi)\, d^4x\,d^4x',

and the minimization becomes path-dependent.

\begin{proposition}[Hysteresis and path-dependence]

Suppose the temporal kernel $J(\cdot)$ is causal, smooth, and decays with a time scale $\tau_J$.
In a cycle that adiabatically sweeps $\|W\|_2$ across the synchronization threshold and back,

(or the cycle duration $\to\infty$).
\end{proposition}

\paragraph{Experimental signatures.}

\subsection{Nonlinear Amplification in Collective Adjudication}
\label{subsec:nonlinear-amplification}

\paragraph{Motivation: From linear sum to collective field.}
For independent adjudicators, the total energy cost is additive:
$\Delta E_{\text{total}} = \sum_{i=1}^N \Delta E_i$, where each
$\Delta E_i \approx k_B T \log n + \lambda_\Psi \mathcal{E}_{\Psi,i}$ is the
Reflexive Landauer cost for CP $i$.
However, when CPs couple coherently ($\|W\|_2 > J_c$), they form a collective
state whose coherence field $\Psi$ is not a sum of local contributions but a
\emph{macroscopic, system-spanning configuration}.
The geometric term $\lambda_\Psi \int (\alpha_1\Psi^2 + \alpha_2\|\nabla\Psi\|^2)dV$
now integrates over this large-scale field, leading to \emph{superlinear scaling}.

\begin{theorem}[Superlinear Energy Scaling]
\label{thm:superlinear-energy}
Consider a cascade of $S$ coherently coupled CPs in a network of total size $N$.
The ensemble-averaged energy release scales as
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:superlinear-energy}
\langle \Delta E_{\text{cascade}} \rangle \;=\; A \cdot S^\alpha,
\end{equation}
where the exponent $\alpha$ depends on regime parameters:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Perturbative regime} ($N \sim 10^3$, $\lambda_\Psi \sim 2$):
  $\alpha \approx 1.01$ (coherence is 1--2\% correction);
  \item \textbf{Transitional regime} ($N \sim 10^3$, $\lambda_\Psi \sim 10$):
  $\alpha \approx 1.18$ (emerging collective effects);
  \item \textbf{Coherence-dominated regime} ($N \sim 10^4$, $\lambda_\Psi \sim 30$):
  $\alpha \approx 1.83$ (coherence term dominates, nearly quadratic scaling).
\end{itemize}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The logical cost scales linearly: $E_{\text{logical}} = S \cdot k_B T \log n$.
The coherence field amplitude for a collective cascade scales as
$\Psi_{\text{coll}} \sim \sqrt{S/N}$ (collective enhancement),
while the spatial extent grows as $\ell \sim S^\beta$ with $\beta \in [0.5, 0.6]$
depending on network topology.
The coherence energy becomes
\[
E_{\text{coh}} \sim \lambda_\Psi k_B T
\left(\alpha_1 \frac{S}{N} \ell^d + \alpha_2 \frac{S}{N\ell^2} \ell^d\right)
\sim \lambda_\Psi k_B T \frac{S^{1+\beta d}}{N},
\]
where $d$ is effective dimension. For $d=2$, $\beta=0.5$: $E_{\text{coh}} \propto S^2$.
When $E_{\text{coh}} \ll E_{\text{logical}}$, effective $\alpha \approx 1 + \varepsilon$;
when $E_{\text{coh}} \gg E_{\text{logical}}$, $\alpha \to 2$.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Physical implications.}
This superlinear scaling explains:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Irreversibility of measurement:} Macroscopic detectors ($N \sim 10^{23}$)
  operate in the $\alpha > 1.5$ regime, making large coherent cascades energetically
  dominant—once triggered, collapse is irreversible.
  
  \item \textbf{Classical limit:} Objects with $N \gg 10^4$ coupled CPs perpetually
  self-adjudicate in superlinear cascades, maintaining definite states.
  
  \item \textbf{Arrow of time:} Superlinear scaling creates directional preference
  toward states that maximize collective adjudication (lower global dissonance).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Biological Coherence in Noisy Environments}
\label{subsubsec:biological-coherence}

\paragraph{The biological paradox and its resolution.}
E35 (robustness testing across 81 configurations) reveals that the 1.13 threshold is robust to all internal dynamics (diffusion mechanisms, source distributions, multiplicative noise: threshold $\approx 1.11$) but fails under \emph{additive external noise}, where the threshold drops to $0.59$ (48\% decrease). This precisely mirrors quantum decoherence: external additive noise corrupts the information profit accounting by introducing untracked inputs, making sustained coherence impossible.

Yet biological systems maintain exquisite organization despite operating in extremely noisy environments (thermal, chemical, electromagnetic). This apparent paradox resolves when we recognize that biology achieves coherence through \emph{active profit amplification}: healthy cells maintain profit margins of 15--20\% (not the minimum 13\%), investing the surplus in error correction, compartmentalization, and rapid molecular turnover.

\paragraph{Environment-adjusted profit principle.}
The universal threshold generalizes to noisy environments:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:profit-environment-adjusted}
\frac{\text{Generation}}{\text{Drain}} \;\geq\; 1.13 + \epsilon_{\text{correction}}(\sigma_{\text{noise}}),
\end{equation}
where $\epsilon_{\text{correction}}$ is the additional margin required for noise management. In clean quantum systems (cryogenic, vacuum), $\epsilon \approx 0$; in biological systems (37$^\circ$C, aqueous), $\epsilon \approx 0.02$--$0.07$, yielding total profit of 1.15--1.20.

\paragraph{Five mechanisms of biological noise management.}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \textbf{Higher base margin:} Cells generate 15--20\% surplus to fund correction systems.
\item \textbf{Compartmentalization:} Membranes reduce effective additive noise by 10$^3$--10$^4 \times$ (plasma membrane, nucleus, mitochondria)---analogous to quantum isolation but implemented chemically.
\item \textbf{Active error correction:} Molecular systems (DNA proofreading: 10$^{-9}$ error rate, chaperone proteins, proteasomes, autophagy) consume 13--27\% of ATP budget, matching the predicted surplus investment.
\item \textbf{Rapid turnover:} Pattern persistence despite substrate replacement (proteins: hours--days, lipids: days--weeks). Profit accounting operates on \emph{patterns}, not particles---analogous to quantum error correction preserving logical qubits.
\item \textbf{Noise-to-signal conversion:} Stochastic resonance, Brownian ratchets, and channel gating convert some additive noise into multiplicative signal, changing the effective noise type from harmful (E35: threshold 0.59) to tolerable (E35: threshold 1.11).
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{Decoherence as accounting failure.}
The E35 result reframes decoherence not as vague ``fragility'' but as \emph{profit accounting corruption}: additive external noise introduces untracked inputs/outputs that prevent the system from maintaining Gen/Drain $> 1.13$. This unifies quantum decoherence (phase noise), biological death (metabolic failure), economic collapse (uncontrolled losses), and ecological decay (energy imbalance) as manifestations of the same profit-violation mechanism. Isolation requirements (quantum: cryogenic chambers; biological: membranes; economic: fraud prevention; ecological: keystone species) are all profit-preservation strategies.

\paragraph{Testable biological predictions.}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item \textbf{Error correction cost:} ATP spent on proofreading/chaperones should scale as $\sigma_{\text{noise}}^2$ (errors accumulate quadratically with noise amplitude). Test by varying temperature, toxins, radiation.
\item \textbf{Lifespan correlation:} Organisms with higher metabolic margins (Profit $-$ 1.13) should live longer when controlled for size. Naked mole rats (exceptional longevity) predicted to have Profit $\approx 1.22$.
\item \textbf{Aging as declining profit:} ATP/ADP ratios should decline with age, approaching 1.13 at senescence. When Profit $< 1.13$, cells enter apoptosis.
\item \textbf{Cancer as unconstrained profit:} Cancer cells escape regulation by disabling error correction and increasing generation (Warburg effect), achieving Profit $> 1.25$---unsustainable but enabling uncontrolled growth. Therapeutic strategy: force profit below 1.13.
\item \textbf{Compartment-specific profit:} Critical organelles (mitochondria, nucleus) should maintain local Profit $> 1.13$ even if global profit is marginal, measurable via genetically encoded ATP sensors.
\item \textbf{Stress response = profit preservation:} Heat shock, unfolded protein response, hypoxia response are emergency mechanisms to restore Profit $> 1.13$ when environmental stress threatens accounting failure.
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{Universal isolation requirements.}
The 13\% threshold is universal; achieving it requires environment-specific strategies. Quantum systems minimize $\epsilon_{\text{noise}}$ through extreme isolation. Biological systems maximize correction efficiency $f(\text{correction})$ through enzymatic machinery. Both strategies serve the same goal: maintaining information profit accounting despite the second law's imperative. This elevates the profit principle from a computational observation to a \emph{fundamental constraint on the emergence and persistence of all complex organization}.

\paragraph{Connection to biological intelligence.}
The universality of the Information Profit Principle finds a powerful and direct correspondence in the field of basal cognition and diverse intelligence. Recent work by Chis-Ciure and M.~Levin formalizes biological intelligence as "search efficiency" in a problem space, measured by a metric $K = \log_{10}(\tau_{\mathrm{blind}} / \tau_{\mathrm{agent}})$, which quantifies the orders of magnitude by which an agent's search policy outperforms a blind, random walk~\cite{ChisCiureLevin2025}. This framework maps directly onto the principles of MFRR. The "problem space" is the biological description of an Adjudicative Manifold; the agent's intelligent policy is the emergent behavior of the Transputation (PT) operator selecting MDL-optimal paths. Crucially, the Information Profit Principle provides the fundamental physical condition that enables a system to achieve a high $K$ value. A system must be informationally "profitable" ($\text{Gen}/\text{Drain} > 1.13$) to possess the capacity to fund a search policy more efficient than random chance. MFRR thus provides the underlying physical law that powers the intelligent search and problem-solving observed in biological systems, from single cells to complex organisms. The Information Profit Principle is the engine of intelligence; the $K$ metric is its performance gauge. Computational validation of this connection is provided in Appendix~\ref{app:levin-profit-validation}.

\subsection{From Transputation to the Self-Referential Renormalization Group (SRRG)}
\label{subsec:srrg}

The \emph{Self-Referential Renormalization Group} (SRRG), introduced in
\textit{The Mathematical Foundations of Self-Referential Systems}~\cite{SpivackSelfRefSystems}
and developed in
\textit{On the Formal Theory of Transputation}~\cite{SpivackTFTT}, formalizes the
macro-level flow of reflexive theories under adjudicative refinement.
Where the PT-induced source term
(\cref{thm:PTRG})
governs the micro-dynamics of invariant restoration,
the SRRG describes the coarse-grained evolution of entire
self-referential theories~$S(\mu)$ across scales of description.

\begin{definition}[Self-Referential Renormalization Group (SRRG)]
\label{def:srrg}
Let $S$ denote a reflexive theory characterized by its internal law,
computational architecture, and coherence geometry.
Define its \emph{reflexive viability functional}
\[
F[S] \;=\; R[S] - C_\Lambda[S],
\]
where
$R[S]$ measures the self-predictive and self-descriptive coherence of the
theory (its ``reflexive reward''),
and $C_\Lambda[S]$ is a composite cost
encoding ontological redundancy,
instability, and failure of Perfect Self-Containment (PSC).
The SRRG flow is the gradient ascent
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:srrg-flow}
\frac{dS}{d\ln\mu}
\;=\;
\beta_{\mathrm{SRRG}}(S)
\;=\;
G_S^{-1}\!
\left(
\frac{\delta R}{\delta S}
- \frac{\delta C_\Lambda}{\delta S}
\right),
\end{equation}
where $G_S$ is the Fisher--Rao metric on theory space.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[SRRG Monotonicity]
\label{thm:srrg-monotonicity}
Along the SRRG flow, the viability functional increases monotonically,
\[
\frac{dF}{d\ln\mu} \ge 0,
\]
with equality only at reflexive fixed points
$\beta_{\mathrm{SRRG}}(S_\ast)=0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reflexive c--Function Monotonicity and Equality]
\label{thm:srrg-c-function}
Define the SRRG free energy $F[S]$ and the quarter-lock deviation $n\!\cdot\!k$ as above, and let
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:c_function_def_main}
\mathcal{C}[S] = F[S] - \lambda\,(n\!\cdot\!k)^2,
\end{equation}
for some $\lambda>0$.  Along the SRRG flow with natural-gradient dynamics,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:c_function_monotonic_main}
\frac{d\mathcal{C}}{d\ln\mu} \le 0,
\end{equation}
with equality if and only if the beta functions vanish, $\beta_{\mathrm{SRRG}}(S)=0$, and the quarter-lock deviation vanishes, $n\!\cdot\!k=0$, i.e.\ the flow is at a reflexive fixed point preserving all UGP invariants.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
Write the SRRG flow as $dS/d\ln\mu = \beta = G_S^{-1}\nabla F$, where $G_S$ is the Fisher--Rao metric
on theory space.  Differentiating $\mathcal{C}$ along the flow gives
\[
\frac{d\mathcal{C}}{d\ln\mu}
= \langle \nabla F, \beta\rangle_{G_S}
- 2\lambda\,(n\!\cdot\!k)\,\frac{d(n\!\cdot\!k)}{d\ln\mu}.
\]
The first term is $-|\beta|^2_{G_S}\le 0$ by natural-gradient ascent (or descent in $-\!F$),
while the second term is proportional to the PT-induced restoration rate of the quarter-lock
plane, which is strictly positive whenever $n\!\cdot\!k\neq 0$.  Thus $d\mathcal{C}/d\ln\mu\le 0$,
with equality if and only if both $\beta=0$ and $n\!\cdot\!k=0$.  For the full derivation, including
the explicit role of the PT density $\rho_{\mathrm{PT}}$ and the coupling to the Fisher metric, see
Appendix~\ref{app:srrg-c-function}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
This result provides a reflexive $c$--theorem: $\mathcal{C}$ is a Lyapunov functional for the SRRG
flow, analogous to the $c$-- and $a$--functions in conformal and Wilsonian RG.  The quarter-lock
term $(n\!\cdot\!k)^2$ acts as a ``reflexive anomaly'' that penalizes deviations from perfect
self-consistency, so that reflexive fixed points are characterized by both vanishing beta functions
and exact satisfaction of the Quarter-Lock law.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Spectral Stability and Dynamical Closure]
\label{thm:spectral_closure}
Let $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{PR0}}$, $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{GKSL}}$, and $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SRRG}}$
denote the linearized generators of PR-0 field dynamics, ensemble adjudication (GKSL form), and
SRRG flows, respectively, around a PSC background.  Suppose:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item Each generator is essentially self-adjoint (or maximally dissipative in the GKSL case);
  \item The spectra $\sigma(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{PR0}})$, $\sigma(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{GKSL}})$, and
        $\sigma(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SRRG}})$ are bounded from above and admit no accumulation
        points with positive real part;
  \item The PT-induced renormalization connects these spectra via stable similarity or
        coarse-graining transforms.
\end{enumerate}
Then the combined dynamical spectrum
\[
\sigma_{\mathrm{refl}}
 = \sigma(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{PR0}})\cup
   \sigma(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{GKSL}})\cup
   \sigma(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SRRG}})
\]
is closed under PT and SRRG: no new unstable eigenvalues can appear and no required coherence
bands are lost.  In particular, all admissible reflexive oscillators (from micro Compton cycles
to the Cosmic Reflexive Oscillator) reside in this invariant spectral set.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The PR-0 generator describes micro-field dynamics, GKSL generators describe mesoscopic ensemble
adjudication, and SRRG generators describe macro theory flow.  Each is constructed to be stable:
PR-0 via the Ablowitz--Ladik saturation and dissonance minimization, GKSL via complete positivity
and trace preservation, and SRRG via natural-gradient flow on the Fisher manifold.  PT enters as
a bounded perturbation and renormalization source term.  Under the assumptions, standard spectral
perturbation theory and semigroup results guarantee that the union of their spectra forms an
invariant, stable set under PT-induced transformations.  This yields a closed, internally stable
spectral family supporting all reflexive oscillators.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Standard Model as SRRG Fixed Point}
\label{subsec:SM-FP}

\begin{theorem}[Computational Theorem: Standard Model as Dominant SRRG Attractor]
\label{thm:SM-FP}
Let $F$ be the pure-GTE viability functional (UCL $+$ structural coherence $+$ MDL optimality) constructed solely from Elegant Kernel constants derived from $\pi$, $\phi$, and the Quarter-Lock law, with no empirical mass or coupling parameters.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Local stability (TS1\_Pure).} Under the SRRG natural-gradient flow with Euclidean search radius $r=5$ and stopping tolerance $\Delta_{\mathrm{conv}}=15.0$, the canonical Standard Model GTE triples are stable fixed points: basin-structure analysis with $512$ random starts per particle yields a mean attraction rate $p_{\mathrm{mean}}=97.0\%\pm 0.7\%$ across all $17$ particles, with $16/17$ achieving $\ge 95\%$ convergence.
  \item \textbf{Global dominance (TS1\_Global).} In a grand-tour SRRG search over random admissible GTE triples with components sampled from wide integer ranges (e.g.\ $a\in[1,10^4]$, $b,c\in[1,10^5]$, $g\in\{0,1,2,3\}$) using the same pure-GTE functional, no non-SM attractor is found with viability exceeding that of the SM catalog.  The best non-SM configuration attains $F_{\mathrm{alt}}\approx 42.96$, while the top SM triple reaches $F_{\mathrm{SM,max}}\approx 189.79$, giving a viability gap $\Delta F\approx 147$.
  \item \textbf{Lyapunov ascent (TS1\_Strict).} For SRRG flows initialized at and near the canonical SM triples under the same pure-GTE functional, the discrete viability trace $F(S_k)$ is strictly non-decreasing along all sampled trajectories: across all canonical and nearby off-SM initial conditions, the observed fraction of steps with $\Delta F_k<0$ is $0$, with $\mathrm{max\_negative\_drop}=0$.
\end{enumerate}
Thus, within the explored TS1 and TS1\_extended protocols, the Standard Model catalog appears as a robust, dominant attractor of the reflexive self-definition process: it is locally stable, globally unmatched by any higher-viability competitor in large random scans, and aligned with a strict Lyapunov ascent of the viability functional in the tested regime.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Computational]
Item~(1) is established by the original TS1 basin-structure experiments together with the clean-room TS1\_Pure rerun, which uses only theoretically motivated Elegant Kernel coefficients; see \S\ref{subsec:SRRG-validation} and the TS1\_extended specification in \path{SRRG_VALIDATION_PROGRAM/SESSIONS/8_1_TS1_EXTENDED_TESTS_PLAN_AND_RESULTS.md}.  Item~(2) follows from the TS1\_Global grand-tour search, which compares the SM catalog viability values against those of all attractors reached from $10^3$ random starts over the stated integer domain and finds no higher-viability alternative.  Item~(3) is supported by the TS1\_Strict Lyapunov analysis, which records discrete SRRG trajectories for flows initialized at and near the SM triples and finds $F$ to be monotonically non-decreasing along every sampled path.  See \S\ref{subsec:SRRG-validation} for the consolidated numerical summaries and protocol details.
\end{proof}

This result is a \emph{computational theorem} about the specified SRRG protocol, metric, and pure-GTE viability functional: it characterizes the behaviour of the well-defined algorithmic flow implemented in the TS1/TS1\_extended suite.  The Two-Layer PSC Theorem~\cite{SpivackPSCOpt,SpivackNMstar} (machine-checked in nems-lean~\cite{SpivackNEMSLean}) provides the formal companion: it proves that PSC constraints (RC, NM$^*$, TV, SA, PI) within 4D gauge theory space uniquely force the SM gauge group and select $N_{\mathrm{gen}}=3$.  Independent Hessian analysis of the viability functional at the SM point confirms all physical eigenvalues are positive, corroborating local stability. A fully rigorous algebraic SRRG Hessian proof (metric-independent, global) is left for future work.

\subsection{Analytical Derivation of the Standard Model Gauge Group}
\label{subsec:analytical-derivation-sm}

While Theorem~\ref{thm:SM-FP} establishes computationally that the Standard Model (SM) catalog is a stable attractor of the SRRG flow, we now give an analytic derivation of the SM gauge group itself.  We show that the local gauge symmetry
\[
G_{\mathrm{SM}} \;=\; SU(3)\times SU(2)\times U(1)
\]
is the unique maximal symmetry group compatible with the algebraic invariants of the Generative Triple Evolution (GTE) substrate~\cite{SpivackUGPFormalization,ugp-lean}, the Quarter-Lock plane $n\!\cdot\!k=0$, and the ridge structure of the Elegant Kernel at $n=10$, as made explicit in the First Principles Standard Model construction~\cite{Spivack2025_FirstPrinciplesSM} (see Appendix~\ref{app:GTE-explainer} for the complete arithmetic and topological specification).

\begin{theorem}[Analytical Necessity of the Standard Model Gauge Group]
\label{thm:sm_necessity}
Let $\mathcal{U}$ be a reflexive universe governed by the GTE substrate at ridge $n=10$, subject to the Quarter-Lock invariant condition $n\!\cdot\!k=0$ and the UGP rank-one evolution block~\eqref{eq:rank-one}.  Then the unique admissible local gauge symmetry compatible with these constraints is
\[
G_{\mathrm{loc}} \;\cong\; SU(3)\times SU(2)\times U(1).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch relying on the Braid Atlas dictionary and FPSM construction]
This derivation is analytic \emph{given} the arithmetic-topological dictionary of~\cite{SpivackBraidAtlas,SpivackParticleSpectrum} (Braid Atlas v2) and the FPSM construction~\cite{Spivack2025_FirstPrinciplesSM}. The PSC-level narrowing (which constraints independently force which gauge-group eliminations) is formally proved in companion papers~\cite{SpivackPSCOpt,SpivackNMstar} and machine-checked in nems-lean~\cite{SpivackNEMSLean}; the present four-step argument connects those results to the GTE/ridge arithmetic at the MFRR level.

The derivation proceeds in four steps: dual braid structure and rank bounds, sector identification, invariant coupling via ridge factorization and center symmetry, and algebraic closure via an abelian slack.

\textbf{Step~1: Dual gauge-braid structure and rank bounds.}
The UGP/GTE substrate is built on arithmetic triples $(a,b,c)$, with two-step evolution blocks acting as rank-one perturbations of the identity on the invariant space~\eqref{eq:rank-one}.  FPSM identifies these triples with dual gauge-braid structures: quark-like excitations are realized as three-strand braids with an embedded two-strand substructure, while lepton-like excitations inhabit purely two-strand braids~\cite{Spivack2025_FirstPrinciplesSM} (see Appendix~\ref{app:GTE-explainer}).  This immediately bounds the admissible local symmetries:
\begin{itemize}
  \item The maximal non-degenerate representation of the triple $(a,b,c)$ is a $3$-strand braid in $B_3$, whose natural special-unitary symmetry is $SU(3)_C$.
  \item The embedded two-strand substructure describes the minimal nontrivial parity/phase sector, with natural symmetry $SU(2)_L$.
\end{itemize}
Any larger simple group such as $SU(4)$ would require a quadruple structure $(a,b,c,d)$ at the substrate level, which is incompatible with the GTE ontology.  Thus the local non-abelian symmetry must be built from $SU(3)$ and $SU(2)$ factors.

\textbf{Step~2: Sector identification from braid invariants.}
The braid-atlas construction (Sec.~8) and the FPSM analysis organize the spectrum into two topological sectors, distinguished by the strand-count invariant:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \emph{Triplet sector (quarks):} excitations with $n_s=3$ strands, carrying color-like degrees of freedom.  The maximal symmetry preserving their braid equivalence classes is $SU(3)_C$.
  \item \emph{Doublet sector (leptons and Higgs):} excitations with $n_s=2$ strands, transforming as doublets under $SU(2)_L$.
\end{enumerate}
These sectors already realize the observed SM pattern of color triplets and weak doublets, but at this stage $SU(3)$ and $SU(2)$ could in principle evolve independently under SRRG.

\textbf{Step~3: Invariant coupling via ridge factorization and center symmetry.}
The Quarter-Lock invariant $n\!\cdot\!k=0$ defines a distinguished hyperplane in theory space, on which the UGP evolution is strictly lossless with respect to the Elegant Kernel.  FPSM shows that the unique ridge at $n=10$ selects a specific integer
\[
R_{10} \;=\; 2^{10}-16 \;=\; 1008 \;=\; 2^4\cdot 3^2\cdot 7,
\]
whose prime factorization encodes the discrete phase structure of the substrate~\cite{Spivack2025_FirstPrinciplesSM} (see Appendix~\ref{app:GTE-explainer} for the explicit ridge construction).  The factors $2$ and $3$ match precisely the orders of the centers of the candidate non-abelian groups,
\[
\mathcal{Z}(SU(3))\cong \mathbb{Z}_3,
\qquad
\mathcal{Z}(SU(2))\cong \mathbb{Z}_2,
\]
so that the center product $\mathbb{Z}_3\times\mathbb{Z}_2$ embeds naturally into the hexagonal phase structure associated with $R_{10}$.  In the Bakker--Veselov--Zubkov lattice picture (and its reflexive generalization in Sec.~\ref{sec:algebra}), this center coupling is exactly what enforces a common ``reflexive clock'' for the $SU(3)$ and $SU(2)$ sectors: the Quarter-Lock plane is preserved only if their center elements co-rotate in a locked fashion.

If $SU(3)$ and $SU(2)$ evolved independently, generic SRRG deformations would produce a nonzero Quarter-Lock deviation $(n\!\cdot\!k)\neq 0$ and drive the system off the invariant plane.  The only way to maintain $n\!\cdot\!k=0$ under the rank-one UGP perturbations is to couple the sectors through their centers, which selects the product structure
\[
G_{\mathrm{NA}} \;=\; SU(3)_C\times SU(2)_L
\]
with a shared discrete phase lattice determined by $R_{10}$.

\textbf{Step~4: Algebraic closure via the $U(1)$ slack.}
Even with center locking, the discrete GTE substrate carries a residual holonomy defect $\delta_{\mathrm{hol}}\neq 0$ when compared to the idealized continuous Quarter-Lock plane (see~\cite{Spivack2025_FirstPrinciplesSM} for the explicit construction); this defect corresponds to the $U(1)_Y$ redundancy identified by anomaly uniqueness in~\cite{SpivackPSCOpt} (Section~3 ``Anomaly Constraints'' therein).  To satisfy the Quarter-Lock identity identically in the effective field theory, the symmetry group must contain an additional abelian degree of freedom that can absorb this phase defect:
\[
G_{\mathrm{loc}} \;=\; SU(3)\times SU(2)\times G_{\mathrm{closure}}.
\]
Requiring a connected, one-parameter compact abelian group with the correct phase structure and charge quantization uniquely singles out $G_{\mathrm{closure}}\cong U(1)_Y$, interpreted as the hypercharge sector.  This $U(1)_Y$ factor supplies precisely the continuous ``slack'' needed to keep the effective dynamics on the Quarter-Lock plane $n\!\cdot\!k=0$ despite the underlying discrete holonomy.

\textbf{Conclusion.}
Combining the dual braid structure of GTE triples, the rank-one UGP evolution, the ridge factorization $R_{10}=1008$, and the Quarter-Lock constraint, we find that:
\begin{itemize}
  \item The only admissible non-abelian factors are $SU(3)$ and $SU(2)$, tied to the $3$- and $2$-strand braid sectors.
  \item Center locking via $\mathbb{Z}_3\times\mathbb{Z}_2$ is required to preserve the Quarter-Lock plane under SRRG, enforcing a coupled product $SU(3)\times SU(2)$.
  \item A single abelian factor $U(1)_Y$ is uniquely required to absorb the holonomy defect and close the invariant algebra.
\end{itemize}
Hence $G_{\mathrm{loc}}\cong SU(3)\times SU(2)\times U(1)$ is the unique local gauge symmetry compatible with the UGP/GTE substrate at ridge $n=10$ and the Quarter-Lock invariants, completing the analytic derivation of the Standard Model gauge group.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{TE$_1$.G Phase 2 Convergence Validation.}
The TE$_1$.G Phase 2 experiment validates SRRG convergence under profit-weighted dynamics with monotonic flow and profit sensitivity. A Phase 2 validation run with a population of 40 laws across profit scalings $\Pi \in \{1.00, 1.05, 1.13, 1.20\}$ and SRRG control parameters (max steps $=60$, convergence tolerance $=1\times10^{-2}$, window $=4$, base step $=0.35$, mask step $=0.25$) achieves global monotonicity rate $= 1.000$ (violation rate $= 0.000$). Convergence fractions to the SM-like attractor are $\Pi=1.00$: $0.000$ (expected stall), $\Pi=1.05$: $0.975$, $\Pi=1.13$: $1.000$, $\Pi=1.20$: $1.000$, and median convergence steps are $6$ for all profitable cases, confirming both monotonic SRRG flow and profit sensitivity.

\paragraph{TE$_1$.J Goldstone--Profit Isomorphism.}
The TE$_1$.J experiment establishes that spontaneous symmetry breaking is isomorphic to MFRR's Information Profit Principle, with mass-ratio predictions matching experimental data. The validation demonstrates two distinct relationships depending on field type: (i)~Fundamental symmetry-breaking fields (e.g., Higgs): $(m_{\mathrm{scalar}}/v_{\mathrm{VEV}})^2 \approx \Lambda = \ln(\phi)/\ln(2\pi) \approx 0.262$, where $\phi$ is the golden ratio. For electroweak symmetry breaking (SU(2)$_L \times$ U(1)$_Y \to$ U(1)$_{\mathrm{EM}}$), the Higgs mass ratio $(m_H/v_{\mathrm{EW}})^2 = (125.09/246.22)^2 = 0.2581$ matches $\Lambda = 0.2618$ with $1.42\%$ error. (ii)~Pseudo-Goldstone bosons (e.g., pions): $(m_{\mathrm{pseudo-Goldstone}}/\Lambda_{\mathrm{breaking}})^2 \approx \Lambda/2 \approx 0.131$. For QCD chiral symmetry breaking (SU(3)$_L \times$ SU(3)$_R \to$ SU(3)$_V$), the pion mass ratio $(m_\pi/\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}})^2 = (139.57/400)^2 = 0.1217$ matches $\Lambda/2 = 0.1309$ with $7.00\%$ error. The distinction arises because fundamental breaking fields carry the full informational load ($\Lambda$) of maintaining the broken vacuum, while pseudo-Goldstone bosons represent the informational surplus (profit margin $\Lambda/2 = 13\%$) needed for pattern persistence. This isomorphism demystifies ``spontaneous'' symmetry breaking as lawful Transputation adjudication via MDL coherence rather than randomness, unifying QCD and electroweak breaking under the same Information Profit Principle. The TE$_1$.J validation program within \texttt{TE\_1\_VALIDATION\_PROGRAM} further extends these relationships to axions and beyond-Standard-Model scalars using the same Goldstone--Profit calculus.

\paragraph{TE$_1$.P Fine-Structure Constant Calibration.}
The TE$_1$.P experiment validates fine-structure constant ($\alpha$) calibration through PSC slack parameter sweeps. Two production runs (a theoretical baseline and a calibrated run) employ a parameter grid $\lambda_{\text{EM}} \in \{0.96, 0.98, 1.00, 1.02, 1.04\}$, $\alpha_{\text{CP}} \in \{0.975, 0.99, 1.00, 1.01, 1.025\}$, $\tau_{\text{adj}} \in \{11.5, 11.75, 12.0, 12.25, 12.5\}$ (25 grid points + 20 robustness samples). Baseline $\alpha$ is derived from Elegant Kernel bits $\{0,3,7\}$ via denominator $137$, with PSC corrections applied through a linear-response ansatz in $(\Delta\lambda,\Delta\alpha,\Delta(\tau^{-1}))$. \subsection{Theoretical Cross--Validation: Gaussian Curvature Amplification (Leblé, 2025)}

Recent rigorous results by Leblé~\cite{Leble2025Hexagonal} on the local optimality of the hexagonal lattice 
for Gaussian and completely monotone interactions provide a formal analytic analogue of the 
Reflexive Dimensionality law validated in this work.

\paragraph{Leblé's theorem.}
For any completely monotone function of the squared distance, 
$f(r)=g(r^2)$ with $(-1)^kg^{(k)}\ge0$, 
the hexagonal lattice~$A_2$ minimizes the energy
\[
E_f(L)=\sum_{p\in L\setminus\{0\}} f(|p|),
\]
and the minimizer is \emph{locally universal} for all Gaussian kernels 
$f_\alpha(r)=e^{-\pi\alpha r^2}$.
Proposition~3.1 in~\cite{Leble2025Hexagonal} establishes explicit quantitative coercivity:
\begin{align}
E_\alpha(A_2+p)-E_\alpha(A_2)
 &\ge c\,e^{-\pi\alpha r_*^2}\,\mathrm{FS}(p),
   &&(\text{short--range channel, Eq.\,(3.3)}) \label{eq:Leble-short}\\[2pt]
E_\alpha(A_2+p)-E_\alpha(A_2)
 &\ge c\,e^{-\pi r_*^2/\alpha}\,\mathrm{SM}(p),
   &&(\text{long--range channel, Eq.\,(3.5)}) \label{eq:Leble-long}
\end{align}
where $\mathrm{FS}(p)$ and $\mathrm{SM}(p)$ are quadratic forms in the displacement field~$p$.
Via Poisson summation, the spectral representation
\[
\text{MainLow}
   =4\pi^2\alpha^{-1}
     \!\int_\Omega\!\!\!
       \big[\lambda_1(\Psi_{\alpha,v_1}(\omega)-\Psi_{\alpha,v_1}(0))
       +\lambda_2(\Psi_{\alpha,v_2}(\omega)-\Psi_{\alpha,v_2}(0))\big]
       d\tau_{\widehat R}(\omega)
\]
(Eq.\,(3.27)) satisfies
\begin{equation}
\text{MainLow}\;\ge\;
   c\,e^{-\pi r_*^2/\alpha}\,\mathrm{SM}(p),
   \qquad\text{(Eq.\,(3.28))} \label{eq:Leble-spectral}
\end{equation}
revealing the same exponential scaling factor that our discrete measurements capture.

\paragraph{Mapping to the Reflexive framework.}
The two Gaussian weights in~\eqref{eq:Leble-short}--\eqref{eq:Leble-long}
correspond to the dual real--space and Fourier--space curvature channels
of the Reflexive Dimensional law:
\[
D_{\mathrm{eff}} = d + \kappa\,\log_{\phi}(\Omega_{\mathrm{rel}}),
\qquad
\kappa = J\,\nu\,\Lambda.
\]
The \emph{long--range} channel~\eqref{eq:Leble-spectral},
dominated by $e^{-\pi r_*^2/\alpha}$,
is sampled by our small--$\lambda$ eigenvalue counting,
and thus introduces a scale-dependent amplification
\[
J\!\cdot\!\nu
   \;\propto\;
   e^{+\pi r_*^2/\alpha_{\mathrm{eff}}},
\]
where $\alpha_{\mathrm{eff}}\!\approx\!1/\lambda_{\mathrm{mid}}$
represents the heat-kernel scale corresponding to the measured spectral window.
This factor yields the empirical $\!J\!\cdot\!\nu\!\approx\!9.8$
that bridges the theoretical $\Lambda\!=\!\ln\phi/\ln(2\pi)$
and the measured $\kappa\!\simeq\!2.6$.

\paragraph{Interpretation.}
Leblé's analytic coercivity confirms that Gaussian curvature energies 
carry exponential amplification factors $e^{-\pi r_*^2/\alpha}$ 
in their spectral response, producing precisely the order-of-magnitude 
enhancement observed in the discrete Reflexive regime.

\begin{theorem}[Equality Conditions for the Profit--Curvature Law]
\label{thm:profit_curvature_equality}
Let $\text{Gen}/\text{Drain}$ denote the generation-to-drain ratio in the Information Profit Principle
and let $R_F$ be the Fisher curvature scalar on the corresponding SRRG Fisher manifold.
Then the profit--curvature relation
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:profit_curvature_equiv_main}

holds as an equality (without slack) on a domain $\mathcal{D}$ if and only if:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item The reflexive fluctuation relation $\langle e^{-\Delta S_{\mathrm{ref}}}\rangle = 1$ is saturated
for all admissible trajectories in $\mathcal{D}$, i.e.\ the Crooks--Jarzynski identity holds
exactly with no dissipative slack.
\item No additional MDL counterterms contribute to the effective free energy beyond the Fisher
curvature term, so that all higher-order model-complexity penalties vanish in the coarse-grained
description.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The inequality form of the profit--curvature law follows by applying Jensen's inequality to
the exponential average of the reflexive entropy production $\Delta S_{\mathrm{ref}}$ and identifying
its curvature-weighted work terms with $\int R_F\,dV$.  Saturation of
$\langle e^{-\Delta S_{\mathrm{ref}}}\rangle = 1$ requires that fluctuations be captured exactly
by the exponential average, which in turn demands that all MDL correction terms vanish and that
no hidden slack terms remain in the effective action.  Under these conditions, the Fisher curvature
integral accounts for the entire profit budget, yielding equality in
equation~\eqref{eq:profit_curvature_equiv_main}.  Conversely, any nonzero MDL counterterm or
fluctuation slack introduces a strict inequality.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Dual-Operator Formalism and Reflexive Dynamics}
\label{subsec:dual-ops}
In the quantum regime the Reflexive System internalizes both forward and conjugate evolutions as adjoint operators \(T,\,T^\dagger\) acting on state vectors \(|\psi\rangle\in\Hil\), the internal Hilbert object of \(\mathbf{E}\).  
They satisfy
\begin{equation}
T^\dagger T = TT^\dagger = I,\qquad [T,T^\dagger]=0
\end{equation}
in the reversible limit, while at Choice Points a small non-unitary component encodes adjudicative irreversibility:
\[
TT^\dagger - T^\dagger T = i\,\epsilon_{\PT}, \qquad \epsilon_{\PT}\sim e^{-\OmegaGlobal/\Omega_c}.
\]
Hence \(\PT\) introduces a controlled violation of perfect unitarity proportional to coherence saturation.  
The emergent light-cone constraint \(v_{\PT}\le c\) from \cref{subsec:dual-operator} remains valid, ensuring compatibility with causal structure.

\subsection{Quantization of the Coherence Field}
\label{subsec:quantization}
Fluctuations of the macroscopic field \(\Psifield\) defined in \cref{def:Psi} generate a quantum field \(\psifield(x,t)\) obeying
\begin{equation}
[\psifield(x,t),\pi_{\psi}(x',t)]=i\hbar\,\delta^{(3)}(x-x'), \qquad \pi_{\psi}=\dot{\psifield}.
\end{equation}
The Lagrangian density for \(\psifield\) follows from expanding \(\Lag_\Psi\) around equilibrium:
\[
\Lag_\psi = \frac{1}{2}(\partial_\mu\psifield)(\partial^\mu\psifield) - \frac{1}{2}\mu^2\psifield^2 - \frac{\lambda}{4}\psifield^4,
\]
yielding a Klein–Gordon–type equation with self-interaction.  The quanta of \(\psifield\) are \emph{omegons}, excitations of informational curvature.

\subsection{Information-Geometric Uncertainty}
\label{subsec:uncertainty}
\begin{lemma}[Information-Geometric Uncertainty]
\label{lem:uncertainty}
Let \(\hat{\Omega}\) and \(\hat{\omega}\) denote the integrated and local curvature operators corresponding to \(\OmegaGlobal,\omegalocal\). Then
\[
[\hat{\Omega},\hat{\omega}]= i\,\hbar_{\mathrm{eff}},\qquad \hbar_{\mathrm{eff}}^2=2\,k_B T\,\alphazero,
\]
implying a fundamental uncertainty \(\Delta\Omega\,\Delta\omega\ge \hbar_{\mathrm{eff}}/2\). 
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Let \((\OmegaGlobal,\omegalocal)\) be conjugate variables with symplectic form \(\omega_F=d\OmegaGlobal\wedge d\omegalocal\).
Canonical quantization yields \([\hat{\Omega},\hat{\omega}]=i\hbar_{\mathrm{eff}}\). 
Using \(E=\alphazero\OmegaGlobal\) and thermal fluctuation relation \(\langle E^2\rangle-\langle E\rangle^2=k_BT\,\partial E/\partial T\), we obtain \(\hbar_{\mathrm{eff}}^2=2k_BT\,\alphazero\).
\end{proof}

\paragraph{\(\hbar_{\mathrm{eff}}\) vs.\ Planck's \(\hbar\).}
The symbol $\hbar_{\mathrm{eff}}$ introduced in the information--geometric uncertainty
$[\hat\Omega,\hat\omega]=i\,\hbar_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is an \emph{effective} conjugacy parameter
for the $(\Omega,\omega)$ sector on the Fisher manifold. It does not replace Planck's
constant in the physical Hilbert-space dynamics. The appearance
$\hbar_{\mathrm{eff}}^2=2k_BT\,\alpha_0$ pertains to the conjugate pair
$(\Omega,\omega)$ under the reflexive thermodynamic mapping $dE=\alpha_0\,d\Omega$ and
has no bearing on canonical commutation relations $[\hat x,\hat p]=i\hbar$ in quantum mechanics.
In particular, $\hbar$ is universal and temperature-independent; $\hbar_{\mathrm{eff}}$
encodes the calibration of informational conjugacy only.

\subsection{The PT--Born Bridge (Gleason/Busch Derivation)}
\label{subsec:PTBorn-strong}

\paragraph{Assumptions.}
We consider a measurement primitive represented either by a projection-valued measure (PVM) on the lattice of closed subspaces \(\mathcal{L}(\Hil)\) or, more generally, by a positive operator-valued measure (POVM) on \(\Hil\)~\cite{BuschOperationalQM1995}. We assume:

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{(H1) Unitary covariance.} For any unitary \(U\), the outcome statistics transform as \(P_\psi(\Pi)=P_{U\psi}(U\Pi U^\dagger)\) where \(\Pi\) is a projector (or effect).

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{(H2) Noncontextuality and \(\sigma\)-additivity.} \(P_\psi\) is a frame function on projectors (or effects): for any PVM \(\{\Pi_i\}\) (or POVM \(\{E_i\}\)), \(\sum_i P_\psi(\Pi_i)=1\) (resp.\ \(\sum_i P_\psi(E_i)=1\)) and \(P_\psi\) depends only on the projector (effect) itself, not on the rest of the measurement context.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{(H3) Continuity/regularity.} \(P_\psi(\cdot)\) depends continuously on \(\psi\) and on the spectral projectors (effects).

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{(H4) MDL coherence selection.} The transputation map \(\PT\) selects branches by minimizing expected description length \(\sum_i P_\psi(i)\,L_i\) with \(L_i\) a code-length functional that is unitarily invariant. In particular, \(L_i=-\log P_\psi(i)\) (Shannon optimality) up to an additive constant.

\medskip

\begin{lemma}[MDL invariance \(\Rightarrow\) frame function structure]
\label{lem:MDL-frame}
Under (H1) and (H4), the probability assignment \(P_\psi\) must be unitarily covariant and, to achieve basis-independent MDL optimality, noncontextual and \(\sigma\)-additive on the outcome lattice. Hence \(P_\psi\) defines a frame function on the projection (or effect) lattice.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
If \(L_i=-\log P_\psi(i)\) and the selection criterion is invariant under change of measurement basis by any unitary \(U\), the set \(\{P_\psi(i)\}\) must transform covariantly: \(P_{U\psi}(U\Pi_iU^\dagger)=P_\psi(\Pi_i)\). Basis independence of the compression objective for all PVMs/POVMs enforces that the probabilities depend only on the measured projector/effect and satisfy \(\sigma\)-additivity across orthogonal resolutions, i.e.\ the frame-function property.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[PT--Born Bridge (Gleason/Busch)]
\label{thm:PTBorn-strong}
\begin{itemize}
\item[\emph{(i)}] If \(\dim \Hil \ge 3\) and measurements are PVMs, then assumptions \emph{(H1)--(H4)} imply the Born rule:
\begin{equation}
P_\psi(\Pi) \;=\; \mathrm{Tr}\big(|\psi\rangle\langle \psi|\,\Pi\big).
\end{equation}
\item[\emph{(ii)}] For \(\dim \Hil \ge 2\) and general POVMs, \emph{(H1)--(H4)} imply the same Born rule via the POVM version (Busch theorem).
\end{itemize}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof for (i)]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:MDL-frame}, \(P_\psi\) is a frame function on the projection lattice. By \emph{Gleason's theorem} (for \(\dim \Hil \ge 3\)), there exists a unique positive trace-one operator \(\rho_\psi\) such that \(P_\psi(\Pi)=\mathrm{Tr}(\rho_\psi \Pi)\) for all projectors \(\Pi\). Unitary covariance (H1) requires \(\rho_{U\psi}=U\rho_\psi U^\dagger\). Extremality and purity (no mixing within a fixed \(\psi\)) force \(\rho_\psi=|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|\). Thus \(P_\psi(\Pi)=\mathrm{Tr}(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|\Pi)\), i.e.\ the Born rule.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof idea for (ii)]
For POVMs on \(\dim\Hil\ge 2\), \emph{Busch's theorem} (POVM analogue of Gleason) implies that any frame function on effects arises from a density operator: \(P_\psi(E)=\mathrm{Tr}(\rho_\psi E)\). The same covariance and purity arguments yield \(\rho_\psi=|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|\) and hence the Born rule for all POVMs.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Role of MDL]
The MDL assumption (H4) does not by itself fix the \emph{functional form} of \(P_\psi\); rather, combined with unitary covariance and noncontextuality it enforces the \emph{frame function} structure required by Gleason/Busch. The Born rule then follows from the corresponding representation theorems.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Born--Rule Uniqueness in Reflexive Quantum Theory]
\label{thm:born_rule_uniqueness}
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a separable Hilbert space with $\dim\mathcal{H} \ge 3$, and suppose PT-induced
measurements satisfy:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item Noncontextuality and $\sigma$-additivity of outcome assignments on commuting projectors/effects,
\item MDL invariance of the probability assignment under admissible codings,
\item Reflexive completeness (PSC) for the measurement apparatus.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a unique probability measure $P(\cdot|\rho)$ on the projection lattice such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:born_uniqueness_main}
P(P_i|\rho) = \mathrm{Tr}(\rho\,P_i),
\end{equation}
for all density operators $\rho$ and all projectors $P_i$.  Thus the Born rule is the only
probability law compatible with the reflexive axioms of RR.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Gleason's theorem shows that any noncontextual, $\sigma$-additive probability measure on projections
in $\dim\mathcal{H}\ge 3$ is of the Born form $\mathrm{Tr}(\rho P)$.  The Busch extension handles POVMs.
MDL invariance ensures that all admissible codings of outcomes yield the same probabilities, eliminating
hidden-variable-like alternatives that might reweight branches while preserving coarse statistics.
PSC implies that the measurement apparatus and its coding scheme are internally representable, so
there is no external meta-measure that could alter $P$.  Together, these constraints force the unique
Born representation in equation~\eqref{eq:born_uniqueness_main}.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{MDL variational derivation.}
In Hilbert space, the MDL functional $L_i=-\log P_\psi(i)$ corresponds to minimizing expected description length $\sum_i P_\psi(i)L_i = H(P_\psi)$.  The Lagrange variation of $H(P_\psi)$ under normalization yields $P_\psi(i)\propto |\langle e_i|\psi\rangle|^2$.  Thus the Born amplitudes are the unique stationary point of MDL subject to unitarity and normalization, reproducing Gleason's result variationally.

\paragraph{Dimensional caveat.}
For PVMs, the derivation requires \(\dim\Hil\ge 3\) (Gleason). In \(\dim\Hil=2\), we use Busch's POVM version to obtain \(P_\psi(E)=\mathrm{Tr}(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|E)\) for all effects \(E\).

\begin{theorem}[Internal Gleason-Busch for Reflexive Topos]
\label{thm:internal-gleason-busch}
Let $\mathbf{E}$ be the Reflexive topos with internal Hilbert object $\mathcal{H}$ of dimension $\ge 3$.
Any \emph{internal} probability measure $\mu$ on the projection lattice $\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{H})$ that is:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \emph{Additive}: $\mu(\Pi_1\oplus\Pi_2)=\mu(\Pi_1)+\mu(\Pi_2)$ for orthogonal projectors,
\item \emph{Unitarily invariant}: $\mu(U\Pi U^\dagger)=\mu(\Pi)$ for all unitary $U$ in $\mathbf{E}$,
\item \emph{MDL-optimal}: minimizes $\mathbb{E}_\mu[\log(1/\mu)]$ subject to normalization and covariance,
\end{enumerate}
is uniquely represented by an internal density operator $\rho\in\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{H})$ via $\mu(\Pi)=\mathrm{Tr}(\rho\Pi)$.
For pure states, $\rho=|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|$ and $\mu(\Pi)=|\langle\psi|\Pi|\psi\rangle|^2$ (Born rule).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
Apply the internal logic of $\mathbf{E}$ to formulate Gleason's theorem within the topos.
Since $\mathbf{E}$ is Cartesian closed with a natural numbers object, it admits an internal Hilbert space structure~\cite{Heunen2009}.
The frame-function axioms (additivity, covariance) are expressible internally, and the internal Gleason theorem (Theorem 4.2 of~\cite{Heunen2009}) ensures the existence of $\rho$.
The MDL-optimality condition (iii) enforces extremality (pure states for single systems), yielding $\rho=|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|$ uniquely.
Hence the Born rule emerges as the unique internal measure satisfying (i)--(iii).
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
This theorem strengthens the PT--Born Bridge by proving that the Born rule is the \emph{only} measure consistent with the internal logic of the Reflexive topos, not merely one consistent choice. It establishes that PT's MDL-based adjudication, when restricted to quantum measurement CPs, \emph{must} yield Born amplitudes by internal necessity, closing any remaining wiggle room for alternative probability assignments.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The Quantum-Geometric Equivalence: Superposition as Maintained Degeneracy}
\label{subsec:quantum-geometric-equiv}

The PT--Born Bridge establishes that the statistics of adjudication at measurement Choice Points must conform to the Born rule, thereby recovering the probabilistic structure of quantum mechanics. We now prove a deeper result that reveals the ontological nature of the quantum state itself: a quantum superposition is formally and physically equivalent to a system dwelling in a state of sustained, unresolved degeneracy on an Adjudicative Manifold.

\begin{definition}[Adjudicative Manifold]
\label{def:adjudicative-manifold}
An \emph{Adjudicative Manifold}, $\mathcal{M}_{CP}$, is a connected submanifold of the total state space where the dissonance functional $D$ is nearly flat ($\|\nabla D\| < \epsilon$) and its Hessian has multiple eigenvalues close to zero. The basins of attraction of the local minima surrounding this plateau correspond to the set of macroscopically distinct, admissible successor branches, $\{\gamma_i\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Quantum-Geometric Equivalence Theorem]
\label{thm:quantum-geometric-equivalence}
Let $(\mathcal{H}, \{\Pi_i\})$ be the internal Hilbert space and projection-valued measure whose existence is guaranteed by the PT--Born Bridge for a given measurement context. Let $\mathcal{M}_{CP}$ be the corresponding Adjudicative Manifold. Then there exists an isomorphism, $\Phi$, that maps the quantum description to the reflexive-geometric description:
\[
\Phi: \mathcal{H} \to L^2(\mathcal{M}_{CP})
\]
such that:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{State Equivalence:} A quantum superposition state $|\psi\rangle = \sum_i c_i |i\rangle$ is mapped to a complex-valued ``coherence wave'' function $\psi(\theta)$ over the Adjudicative Manifold, where the basis states $\{|i\rangle\}$ correspond to the distinct basins of attraction $\{\text{Basin}(\gamma_i)\}$.
    \item \textbf{Probability Equivalence:} The Born rule probabilities are recovered by the geometry of the manifold: $p_i = |c_i|^2 = \int_{\text{Basin}(\gamma_i)} |\psi(\theta)|^2 d\mu_F$, where $d\mu_F$ is the Fisher information metric volume element.
    \item \textbf{Dynamics Equivalence:} Unitary evolution under the Schrödinger equation, $|\psi(t)\rangle = e^{-iHt/\hbar}|\psi(0)\rangle$, corresponds to a deterministic, volume-preserving flow (a Liouville-type evolution) of the coherence wave $\psi(\theta, t)$ on the Adjudicative Manifold.
    \item \textbf{Measurement Equivalence:} The application of a measurement operator (wave function collapse) is equivalent to the application of the Transputation operator (PT), which deterministically selects the branch $\gamma_k$ that minimizes the global MDL functional and projects the coherence wave $\psi(\theta)$ onto the corresponding basin, $\text{Basin}(\gamma_k)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof Sketch]
The proof is a constructive one. The PT--Born Bridge (Thm.~\ref{thm:PTBorn-strong}) guarantees the existence of an internal Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ and a mapping from measurement outcomes to projectors $\{\Pi_i\}$ such that probabilities are given by $p_i = \mathrm{Tr}(\rho \Pi_i)$. We construct the isomorphism $\Phi$ by identifying the basis states $\{|i\rangle\}$ that diagonalize the measurement with the distinct basins of attraction $\{\text{Basin}(\gamma_i)\}$ on the Adjudicative Manifold. A general state $|\psi\rangle$ is then mapped to a function $\psi(\theta)$ whose support is on $\mathcal{M}_{CP}$ and whose integral over each basin reproduces the Born probability. The deterministic and reversible nature of unitary evolution maps to a deterministic and reversible flow on the manifold. The irreversible, non-computable nature of measurement maps directly to the irreversible, non-computable nature of the PT operator. The isomorphism holds because the two mathematical structures---the abstract Hilbert space and the concrete geometric manifold of degeneracies---are constrained by the same symmetries (unitarity, MDL invariance) and yield the same probabilistic outcomes.
\end{proof}

This theorem provides a profound unification. It demystifies quantum superposition by giving it a concrete, physical, and logical meaning. It is not a strange, ghostly state; it is the physical manifestation of a system holding multiple potential futures in a state of lawful, unresolved indeterminacy. The equivalence is primarily a \emph{structural isomorphism}—the same mathematical object described in two languages. The unique new measurable prediction it contributes (beyond standard quantum mechanics) is the energy excess term $\lambda_\Psi\!\int(\alpha_1\Psi^2+\alpha_2\|\nabla\Psi\|^2)\,dV$ from the Reflexive Landauer bound (Theorem~\ref{thm:RefLandauer-rigorous}), which is absent in standard QM and testable via high-coherence BEC calorimetry (Test~1 in Section~\ref{subsec:falsification-roadmap}).

\paragraph{Quantum Computation as the Engineering of Adjudicative Manifolds.}

This equivalence provides a powerful, first-principles explanation for the nature of quantum computation. A quantum computer is a device engineered to create, sustain, and precisely manipulate a complex Adjudicative Manifold.

\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{A Quantum Algorithm} is a form of ``coherence engineering.'' It is a carefully choreographed unitary evolution that steers the system's state across the manifold, reshaping the dissonance landscape to guide the final PT event (the measurement) toward the desired computational result.
    \item \textbf{Quantum Parallelism} is the ability to traverse this high-dimensional space of possibilities simultaneously, a direct consequence of sustaining the degeneracy.
    \item \textbf{Decoherence} in a quantum computer is the premature, uncontrolled collapse of this sustained degeneracy. This connects directly to the Information Profit Principle: a quantum computer must maintain an extremely high information profit margin (through error correction and isolation) to protect its delicate, degenerate state from the ``profit-corrupting'' noise of the environment.
\end{itemize}
