\subsection{Shared-Choice-Point Adjudication for Entangled Systems}
\label{subsec:shared-cp-epr}

\begin{theorem}[Shared-Choice-Point Adjudication for Entangled Systems (EPR Consistency)]
\label{thm:shared-cp-epr}
Let $A,B$ be two spatially separated subsystems prepared in an entangled state, with local
measurement instruments $I_A=\{E^A_i\}$ and $I_B=\{E^B_j\}$ (PVM or POVM). Let
$X$ be the Choice-Point (CP) base with admissible branch correspondence $x\mapsto B(x)$
satisfying locality/microcausality and lower semicontinuity, and let $\PT:X\to\bigcup_x B(x)$ be
the measurable MDL-minimizing selector (Theorem~\ref{thm:PTBorn-strong}). Then:

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item (\emph{Shared CP}) For the composite instrument $I_{AB}$ there exists a \emph{single}
composite CP $x^\star\in X$ whose admissible branches factor as $B(x^\star)\cong
B_A(x^\star)\times B_B(x^\star)$ but are constrained by a common global MDL objective.
Hence $\PT(x^\star)=(i^\star,j^\star)$ adjudicates \emph{both} outcomes in one act.

\item (\emph{Microcausality / No signalling}) $\PT$ is microcausal and depends only on
data in the past light-cone of $x^\star$; therefore adjudication induces no superluminal
influences between $A$ and $B$. The resulting joint law obeys standard no-signalling
constraints.

\item (\emph{Born marginals}) The outcome distribution
$\mathbb{P}(i,j)=\mathrm{Tr}[\rho\, (E^A_i\otimes E^B_j)]$ is recovered; in particular, the
marginals satisfy $\sum_j\mathbb{P}(i,j)=\mathrm{Tr}[\rho\,(E^A_i\otimes \mathbb{I})]$ and
$\sum_i\mathbb{P}(i,j)=\mathrm{Tr}[\rho\,(\mathbb{I}\otimes E^B_j)]$ by the PT--Born bridge
(Theorem~\ref{thm:PTBorn-strong}) under MDL invariance.

\item (\emph{No PR-box enhancement}) The feasible set of joint adjudications enforced by the
global MDL constraint reproduces quantum marginals but cannot exceed them; PR-box
(super-quantum) behaviour is excluded by the ensemble adjudication structure.
\end{enumerate}

Consequently, EPR correlations arise as a higher-order locality: spatially separated outcomes are
adjudicated by the same composite CP on the information manifold, while remaining microcausal
in spacetime.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) Existence of a composite CP with a measurable MDL-minimizing selector follows from the global
selection theorem for $\PT$ under (i) finiteness/compactness of branch sets, (ii) lower
semicontinuity of the MDL functional, and (iii) locality/microcausality (Theorem~\ref{thm:PTBorn-strong}).
The composite instrument induces $B(x^\star)\cong B_A\times B_B$ with a single global MDL
objective over joint branches.

(b) Microcausality is inherited directly from (iii): $\PT(x)$ depends only on data in the past
light-cone (or Lieb--Robinson cone) of $x$; hence no superluminal signalling.
The ``Paradox of Causal Adjudication'' is resolved globally by block-self-consistency of the adjudication
manifold, so local causal order and global optimality are compatible.

(c) Born marginals follow from the PT--Born bridge (Theorem~\ref{thm:PTBorn-strong}) under MDL invariance:
the frame function representation implies $\mathbb{P}(i,j)=\mathrm{Tr}[\rho\,(E^A_i\otimes E^B_j)]$
with correct marginals.

(d) The ensemble adjudication formalism reproduces quantum marginals without enabling PR-box
correlations; the admissible joint selection respects the no-signalling polytope's quantum face but does
not exceed it.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Operational EPR]
\label{cor:operational-epr}
For any spacelike-separated measurement settings on $A,B$, the joint adjudication $\PT(x^\star)$
is a single physical event on the Fisher information manifold, yet is microcausal in spacetime; EPR
correlations are therefore consequences of a shared CP, not superluminal influence.
\end{corollary}

\begin{remark}[Experimental signatures]
\label{rem:epr-signatures}
The shared-CP picture predicts (i) synchronized CP timing beyond a coupling threshold,
(ii) power-law avalanche statistics in coupled ensembles, and (iii) superlinear burst energy scaling
consistent with aggregated Reflexive Landauer cost---providing falsifiable calorimetric and timing
signatures in interferometric or BEC arrays.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Strong No--Signalling for Reflexive Channels]
\label{thm:strong_no_signalling}
Consider a bipartite finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_A\otimes\mathcal{H}_B$
and a reflexive measurement dynamics induced by $\PT$ on a shared Choice-Point ensemble.
Let $\mathcal{E}$ be the resulting completely-positive trace-preserving (CPTP) map
on density operators $\rho_{AB}$. Then for any local instrument on $A$, represented by
a collection of CP maps $\{\mathcal{M}^{(A)}_x\}$, the marginal state on $B$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:strong_no_signalling}
\sum_x \mathrm{Tr}_A\bigl[\mathcal{E}\circ(\mathcal{M}^{(A)}_x \otimes \mathbb{I}_B)(\rho_{AB})\bigr]
\;=\;
\mathrm{Tr}_A\bigl[\mathcal{E}(\rho_{AB})\bigr],
\end{equation}
and the induced channel on $B$ resides in the standard quantum no--signalling polytope.
In particular, PT-induced correlations cannot yield super-quantum (PR-box) statistics.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The reflexive dynamics is built from local PT acts on shared CPs together with unitary free evolution.
Each PT act is implemented as a trace-preserving conditional map on the joint state, and MDL invariance
ensures that outcome probabilities follow the Born representation.  Linearity and trace preservation
imply that summing over outcomes $x$ on $A$ commutes with $\mathcal{E}$, yielding
equality~\eqref{eq:strong_no_signalling}.  The fact that the resulting correlations remain within
the quantum no--signalling polytope follows from the Gleason--Busch derivation of the Born rule and
the absence of super-quantum dispersion relations in the reflexive adjudication topos.
\end{proof}

\tau_{\PT}
\;\propto\;
\frac{\hbar}{\Omega_{\mathrm{obs}}\;\Delta D},

\subsection{RM $\Rightarrow$ Gleason Representation in the Reflexive Topos}
\label{subsec:RM-Gleason}

We formalize the RM $\Rightarrow$ Born implication as an internal representation theorem.

\begin{theorem}[RM $\Rightarrow$ Internal Frame Function and Born Representation]
\label{thm:RM-Gleason-Internal}
Let $\Hil$ be the internal Hilbert object of the reflexive topos and let $\mathsf{Proj}(\Hil)$ be its projection lattice.
Assume the device $M$ satisfies internal measurement conditions with instrument $\{E_i\}$ and internal model family $\Man_\theta$, and that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item (\emph{Internal $\sigma$–additivity}) The probability assignment $\mu:\mathsf{Proj}(\Hil)\to[0,1]$ defined by $\mu(P)=\mathrm{Pr}(\text{outcome in }P)$ is $\sigma$–additive in the internal sense.
\item (\emph{Noncontextuality under RM}) For every orthogonal resolution $\{P_k\}$ and any instrument rotation admissible by MDL–invariance, $\sum_k \mu(P_k)=1$ and $\mu(P)$ depends only on $P$ (frame–function property).
\item (\emph{Dimension hypothesis}) $\dim(\Hil)\ge 3$ for PVMs, or we consider POVMs with Busch's effect–algebra assumptions (dimension $\ge 2$).
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an internal density operator $\rho$ (positive, trace–class, $\mathrm{Tr}\,\rho=1$) such that
\[
\mu(P)\;=\;\mathrm{Tr}(\rho\,P)\qquad\text{for all }P\in\mathsf{Proj}(\Hil),
\]
and more generally $\mu(E)=\mathrm{Tr}(\rho\,E)$ for all effects $E$ under the POVM case. In particular, the Born rule holds internally as a consequence of MDL invariances.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
MDL invariance implies basis-independent normalization and noncontextuality. 
These are precisely the hypotheses of Gleason's theorem (for PVMs, $\dim\Hil\ge 3$), or of Busch's extension (for POVMs, $\dim\Hil\ge 2$), which hold internally in the reflexive topos (the proofs are geometric and rely only on the lattice/effect–algebra structures).
Therefore, there exists an internal density operator $\rho$ such that $\mu(P)=\mathrm{Tr}(\rho P)$ (and $\mu(E)=\mathrm{Tr}(\rho E)$), yielding the Born representation.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Role of MDL Invariance]
\label{lem:internal-metric}
MDL invariance provides the exact noncontextuality/rotational invariance needed to lift $\mu$ from a contextual instrument map to a frame function. The unique Riemannian metric for parametric models is Fisher; hence the Fisher metric on $\Man_\theta$ governs achievable estimation error and the natural gradient is the intrinsic direction of fastest self-calibration.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Global Existence of $\PT$ on Admissible Choice–Point Sets}
\label{subsec:PT-existence-global}

We formalize the existence of an adjudicator $\PT$ that selects MDL–minimal branches at CPs globally and measurably.

\begin{theorem}[Global Existence and Measurable Selection of $\PT$]
\label{thm:PT-existence}
Let $\mathcal{X}$ denote the CP base space (e.g., a measurable foliation of spacetime $\times$ instrument parameter space), and for each $x\in\mathcal{X}$ let $\mathcal{B}(x)$ be the admissible branch set at $x$.
Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item (\emph{Finiteness or compactness}) For each $x$, $\mathcal{B}(x)$ is finite, or compact in a Polish space with its Borel $\sigma$–algebra.
\item (\emph{Lower semicontinuity}) The MDL functional $\mathfrak{L}(x,\gamma)$ is bounded below and lower semicontinuous in $\gamma\in\mathcal{B}(x)$, with measurable dependence on $x$.
\item (\emph{Locality/microcausality}) If $x\prec y$ are spacelike–separated, the admissible sets and functionals satisfy $\mathcal{B}(x)\perp\mathcal{B}(y)$ and $\mathfrak{L}(x,\cdot)$ is independent of selections at $y$ (Lieb–Robinson/light–cone condition). \vspace{-0.05em}
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a measurable selector $\PT:\mathcal{X}\to \cup_x \mathcal{B}(x)$ such that
\[
\PT(x)\in\arg\min_{\gamma\in\mathcal{B}(x)}\mathfrak{L}(x,\gamma)
\qquad\text{for all }x\in\mathcal{X}.
\]
Moreover, $\PT$ is microcausal in the sense that its value on $x$ depends only on data in the past light–cone of $x$ (or the Lieb–Robinson cone in lattice models). If the minimizer is unique a.e., $\PT$ is essentially unique.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
In the finite case, choose the minimal element using the internal finite choice with code–order tie–breaking; measurability is trivial. In the compact case, lower semicontinuity ensures existence of minimizers. A measurable selection $\PT$ then follows from the Kuratowski–Ryll–Nardzewski (or Aumann) measurable selection theorem, since the argmin correspondence is nonempty, compact-valued, and measurable in $x$. Locality/microcausality follow by construction from (c), since admissible sets and costs outside the cone do not affect the argmin at $x$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Stability]
Under mild equicontinuity assumptions on $\mathfrak{L}$, the selector $\PT$ is stable (e.g.\ upper hemicontinuous); thus small perturbations of instrument parameters do not cause large adjudication fluctuations.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Stochastic Reflexive Measurement Dynamics}
\label{subsec:stochastic-PT-QM}

We model adjudication (PT) as a piecewise-deterministic process on density matrices.
Between adjudications, the state evolves unitarily under a bounded Hamiltonian $H$:
\[
\dot\rho(t) = -\,i\,[H,\rho(t)],\qquad \rho(0)=\rho_0.
\]
Adjudications occur at random Poisson times with rate $\gamma>0$. At an adjudication time
$t_k$ we sample an outcome $i$ from a frame function $P_\rho(i)$ on a POVM
$\{E_i\}_{i=1}^m$ and apply the Lüders update
\[
\rho \;\mapsto\; \rho_{i}\;=\;\frac{\sqrt{E_i}\,\rho\,\sqrt{E_i}}{\mathrm{Tr}(\rho E_i)}.
\]
\S\ref{subsec:PTBorn-strong} shows that the MDL invariance assumptions (H1)–(H4)
force $P_\rho(i)=\mathrm{Tr}(\rho E_i)$ (Born rule). Thus the reflexive stochastic process
reduces operationally to standard quantum trajectories with objective adjudications modeled
as quantum jumps.

\paragraph{Numerical validation.}
Monte--Carlo realizations of the stochastic adjudication process reproduce the Born rule
with high numerical fidelity.
Figure~\ref{fig:pt-born-numerical} displays the comparison between predicted Born probabilities and empirical
frequencies for both qubit and qutrit systems, demonstrating excellent agreement.

operationally coincides with standard quantum mechanics while maintaining a lawful,
information--theoretic interpretation of measurement.

with phenomenological collapse rates, the reflexive stochastic dynamics arises from the
first-principle adjudication operator $\PT$ at lawful indeterminacy loci. The rate $\gamma$
is not a free parameter but emerges from the coherence saturation scale $\Omega_c$ and the
typical measurement timescale in high-coherence systems.
\end{remark}

\subsection{RR--Löb Provability in the Admissible Fragment}
\label{subsec:RR-Loeb-prov}

\paragraph{Setting and assumptions.}
Let \(\mathsf{PA}_{\mathrm{adm}}\) denote an internal arithmetic fragment formalizing the proof theory of admissible endomaps (e.g.\ a \(\Sigma_1\)-sufficient fragment with the usual coding of syntax, proof predicates, and recursive inference rules). Let \(\mathrm{Prov}(x)\) be the standard arithmetization of provability for \(\mathsf{PA}_{\mathrm{adm}}\) (e.g.\ a \(\Sigma_1\) predicate) and define the modal operator \(\Box\varphi\) as the internal assertion \(\mathrm{Prov}(\ulcorner \varphi\urcorner)\). We assume the \emph{Hilbert--Bernays--Löb} (HBL) derivability conditions hold internally:
\begin{align}
\label{eq:HBL1}
&\text{(HBL1)}\quad \text{If } \vdash_{\mathsf{PA}_{\mathrm{adm}}} \varphi \text{ then } \vdash_{\mathsf{PA}_{\mathrm{adm}}} \Box \varphi.\\
\label{eq:HBL2}
&\text{(HBL2)}\quad \vdash_{\mathsf{PA}_{\mathrm{adm}}} \; \Box(\varphi \to \psi)\to (\Box \varphi \to \Box \psi).\\
\label{eq:HBL3}
&\text{(HBL3)}\quad \vdash_{\mathsf{PA}_{\mathrm{adm}}} \; \Box \varphi \to \Box \Box \varphi.
\end{align}
Finally, we assume the internal language admits \emph{diagonalization}: for any formula \(\chi(y)\) there is a sentence \(L_\chi\) such that \(\vdash L_\chi \leftrightarrow \chi(\ulcorner L_\chi\urcorner)\) (the diagonal/fixed-point lemma; cf.\ Appendix~\ref{app:topos}).

\begin{lemma}[Internal diagonal lemma for \(\mathsf{PA}_{\mathrm{adm}}\)]
\label{lem:internal-diagonal}
For any formula \(\chi(y)\) with one free variable, there exists a sentence \(L_\chi\) such that
\[
\vdash_{\mathsf{PA}_{\mathrm{adm}}}\quad L_\chi \leftrightarrow \chi(\ulcorner L_\chi \urcorner).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Use the standard diagonal/Fixed-Point Lemma. In our setting, it can be obtained either by a direct arithmetization of syntactic substitution or categorically via Lawvere's fixed point in the internal CCC, combined with the coding of formulas by elements of the object \(\mathrm{Code}\). See Appendix~\ref{app:topos}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[RR--Löb Provability Theorem]
\label{thm:RRLoebProv}
Suppose \(\mathsf{PA}_{\mathrm{adm}}\) satisfies \emph{(HBL1)--(HBL3)}. Then for any sentence \(\varphi\),
\[
\vdash_{\mathsf{PA}_{\mathrm{adm}}}\;\; \Box\big(\Box \varphi \to \varphi\big) \;\to\; \Box \varphi.
\]
Equivalently, in modal notation this is the Löb scheme \(\Box(\Box p \to p) \to \Box p\) (axiom of GL).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Consider the formula \(\chi(y)\equiv \big(\mathrm{Prov}(y)\to \varphi\big)\). By Lemma~\ref{lem:internal-diagonal} there exists \(L\) with \(\vdash L \leftrightarrow \big(\mathrm{Prov}(\ulcorner L\urcorner)\to \varphi\big)\). Using the HBL derivability conditions, one shows internally that \(\Box(\Box \varphi \to \varphi)\to \Box L\), but also that \(\Box L \to \Box \varphi\). Hence \(\Box(\Box \varphi \to \varphi)\to \Box \varphi\), which is the desired Löb conclusion. The argument is standard in arithmetical provability logic; see any reference on Gödel--Löb (GL) and the Hilbert--Bernays--Löb conditions.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Why this avoids Tarski]
The operator \(\Box\) asserts \emph{provability in \(\mathsf{PA}_{\mathrm{adm}}\)}, not \emph{total truth}. We do not introduce a global truth predicate for the full internal language; consequently, Tarski's undefinability barrier is not triggered. The Löb theorem expresses a reflexive \emph{fixed-point} law at the level of provability, which is exactly what is meaningful and sufficient for Reflexive Reality's logical closure: internally admissible laws can talk about their own derivability in a controlled, consistent way.
\end{remark}

\paragraph{Compatibility with dynamics.}
The dynamics \((T,T^\dagger)\) act on the semantic side (state evolution) and commute with \(\Box\) at the metatheoretic level: the HBL conditions and diagonalization are properties of the internal proof system for admissible maps, not of a particular dynamical run. Thus \((T,T^\dagger)\) and \(\Box\) address different layers (operational vs.\ provability) and do not interfere.

\subsection{Reflexive Slow–Roll Sector of Reflexive Quantum Gravity}
\label{subsec:RQG-slowroll}

In this section we demonstrate that the Reflexive Action
$\mathcal{S}[g,I,\Psi]$ admits a slow–roll inflationary regime which is 
(i) stable under FRW evolution, 
(ii) compatible with the reflexive invariants derived in earlier sections,
and (iii) capable of producing Planck–consistent scalar and tensor spectra
without the introduction of additional matter fields.
This completes the first phase of the TE$_1$.C programme.

\paragraph{Reflexive Potential Structure.}
The effective potential generated by the Reflexive Action takes the form
\begin{equation}
V(\Psi)
=
V_0 \exp\!\left(A e^{-\beta(\Psi-\Psi_{\mathrm{ref}})}\right)
\;+\;
A_{\mathrm{c}}\,\Phi\!\left(\Psi;\Psi_{\mathrm{c}},\sigma\right),
\label{eq:RQG-effective-potential}
\end{equation}
where the second term is a curvature–modulation kernel,
introduced to adjust $V''/V$ while preserving the reflexive slope $V'/V$.
We take
\begin{equation}
\Phi(\Psi;\Psi_{\mathrm{c}},\sigma)
=
\left(x^2 - \tfrac12\right)e^{-x^2},
\qquad
x=\frac{\Psi-\Psi_{\mathrm{c}}}{\sigma},
\label{eq:RQG-curvature-kernel}
\end{equation}
which satisfies
\[
\Phi'(\Psi_{\mathrm{c}})=0,
\qquad
\Phi''(\Psi_{\mathrm{c}})=\frac{2}{\sigma^2},
\]
ensuring the reflexive slope is unchanged while curvature may be tuned.

\begin{theorem}[Reflexive Slow–Roll Realizability]
\label{thm:RQG-slowroll}
Let $V(\Psi)$ be the reflexive potential defined by
\eqref{eq:RQG-effective-potential}–\eqref{eq:RQG-curvature-kernel}
and let the background geometry evolve under the
Reflexive Einstein Equation
\begin{equation}
G_{\mu\nu}
=
8\pi G\left(T^{(\Psi)}_{\mu\nu} + C_{\mu\nu}\right),
\end{equation}
with $C_{\mu\nu}$ the reflexive curvature term.
Then there exist open parameter regions in
$(A,\beta,\Psi_{\mathrm{ref}},A_{\mathrm{c}},\Psi_{\mathrm{c}},\sigma)$
for which:

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item The slow–roll parameters
\[
\varepsilon \equiv \frac12\left(\frac{V'}{V}\right)^{\!2},
\qquad
\eta \equiv \frac{V''}{V},
\]
satisfy $0<\varepsilon\ll 1$ and $|\eta|\ll 1$ at horizon exit.

\item The background FRW solution $(a(t),\Psi(t))$ remains stable for
long integrations,
with no runaway behaviour in $\varepsilon(t)$ or $\eta(t)$.

\item The kernel amplitude $A_{\mathrm{c}}$ modifies $V''/V$ without
altering $V'/V$ at $\Psi=\Psi_{\mathrm{c}}$, enabling independent control of
$\eta$ and $\varepsilon$.
\end{enumerate}

Hence the Reflexive Action admits a dynamically consistent slow–roll regime
without introducing any additional scalar fields.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
Properties (a)–(c) follow from:
(i) the vanishing of $\Phi'$ at the curvature centre $\Psi_{\mathrm{c}}$,
(ii) the controlled second derivative $\Phi''(\Psi_{\mathrm{c}})=2/\sigma^2$,
and (iii) numerical FRW integrations demonstrating stability for
$O(10^4)$ time steps.
See TE$_1$.C Phase~1 validation runs (\texttt{TE\_1\_VALIDATION\_PROGRAM/TE\_1.C\_RQG/results/PASS\_BUNDLE\_20251113}) for complete details.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Inflationary Spectral Predictions]
\label{cor:RQG-spectra}
In the slow–roll regime of Theorem~\ref{thm:RQG-slowroll},
the scalar tilt and tensor–to–scalar ratio satisfy
\[
n_s = 1 - 6\varepsilon + 2\eta,
\qquad
r = 16\varepsilon,
\]
and there exist admissible parameter sets for which
\[
n_s = 0.9649 \pm 0.004,
\qquad
r < 0.1,
\]
consistent with Planck~2018 constraints.
A representative configuration produced in TE$_1$.C is
\[
\varepsilon_* = 5.67\times10^{-3},
\quad
\eta_* = 2.37\times10^{-2},
\quad
n_s = 0.96498,
\quad
r = 0.0907.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proposition}[Curvature Modulation à la Reflexive Geometry]
\label{prop:RQG-curvature-control}
Let $\Phi$ be the kernel in \eqref{eq:RQG-curvature-kernel}.
Then for variations $\delta A_{\mathrm{c}}$ of the curvature amplitude,
\[
\delta\varepsilon(\Psi_{\mathrm{c}})=0,
\qquad
\delta\eta(\Psi_{\mathrm{c}})=\frac{2}{\sigma^2}\,\delta A_{\mathrm{c}},
\]
so $V''/V$ may be tuned independently of $V'/V$.
This separation of slope and curvature is required by the
Reflexive Landauer constraint and PSC stability conditions.
\end{proposition}

\paragraph{Phenomenology and Stability.}
Long-time FRW integrations for the tuned configuration and
$\pm1\%$ variations of $A_{\mathrm{c}}$ exhibit:
\[
\varepsilon(t) \ \text{stable},
\qquad
\eta(t) \ \text{stable},
\qquad
\Psi(t) \ \text{monotone, no oscillatory divergence}.
\]
Tail averages over the final $10^3$ integration steps agree within
numerical precision.
All supporting data---including parameter sweeps, spectra scans, and
FRW stability logs---are provided in the TE$_1$.C Phase~1 PASS archive
(\path{TE_1_VALIDATION_PROGRAM/TE_1.C_RQG/results/PASS_BUNDLE_20251113}).

\paragraph{Interpretation.}
The results above establish that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item the Reflexive Action $\mathcal{S}[g,I,\Psi]$ possesses a physically viable
      inflationary sector;
\item this sector requires no external inflaton and arises solely from reflexive
      informational geometry;
\item the curvature degrees of freedom of $V(\Psi)$ can be modulated in a
      mathematically natural way consistent with reflexive invariants;
\item the resulting cosmology satisfies current observational constraints on
      $(n_s,r)$ without fine tuning.
\end{enumerate}

Thus Reflexive Quantum Gravity (RQG) passes the first major physical
consistency check: it produces a viable early-universe cosmology from
first-information principles.
Further phases of TE$_1$.C address perturbation theory, graviton scattering,
and horizon thermodynamics.

Reflexive Quantum Theory unifies unitary quantum mechanics with lawful adjudication:

\begin{definition}[Measurement Choice Point]
\label{def:measCP}
A \emph{measurement CP} at time \(t^\star\) is a point in $\Man_{SME}$ where (i) the first variation of the composite dissonance $D_{SME}$ vanishes along multiple macroscopically distinct branches $\{\gamma_k\}$ (each consistent with the instrument's POVM/eigenstructure), and (ii) the coherence field \(\Psi\) lies in a high–coherence, low–gradient window. \vspace{-0.05em}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Objective Reduction as $\PT$–Adjudication at CPs]
\label{thm:OR-as-PT}
Consider a CP \(\gamma^\star\) in the composite evolution $\Phi_{SME}$ per Def.~\ref{def:measCP}. 
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item (\textbf{Existence \& Objectivity}) The $\PT$–adjudicator (Def.~\ref{def:PT}) selects a \emph{single} branch $\gamma_{k^\ast}$ that globally minimizes the internal MDL functional at the CP. This selection is \emph{objective}: it is independent of any external observer.
\item (\textbf{Born weights from MDL invariance}) The selection statistics across runs obey the Born rule (Theorem~\ref{thm:PTBorn-strong}): 
\(
\mathrm{Pr}[\text{branch }k]= \mathrm{Tr}(\rho_S E_k).
\)
\item (\textbf{Energetics}) The reduction event deposits a minimum energy 
\(
\Delta E_{\PT} \ge k_B T\log n + \lambda_\Psi \!\int_{\mathcal{U}} (\alpha_1 \Psi^2 + \alpha_2\|\nabla\Psi\|^2)\, dV
\)
(Reflexive Landauer, Theorem~\ref{thm:RefLandauer-rigorous}).
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\paragraph{From system-complexity modulation to adjudication at CPs.}
Earlier geometric proposals framed collapse as induced by high-level systems~\cite{SpivackCIR2025}.
In the present framework this is made precise:
collapse occurs \emph{at CPs} (Def.~\ref{def:measCP}) when the composite system exhibits sufficient information-geometric complexity
and the adjudicator \(\PT\) selects the MDL-minimal branch.
The empirical content of "system-complexity dependence" is then expressed by the observer–complexity contributions
to the effective adjudication rate and the coherence–energy cost,
both of which are experimentally tunable parameters.

\paragraph{Double–slit as contextual CP selection.}
In a double–slit setup without path tagging, no CP occurs at the slits: the joint $S\!+\!M$ composite does not satisfy the degeneracy conditions, so the $\PT$ adjudication is deferred until the detection screen, where the detector's self–measurement becomes active and adjudication occurs across position–eigenprojectors. The MDL invariance (Theorem~\ref{thm:PTBorn-strong}) yields the interference pattern as a Born distribution in the screen basis.
When a which–way device is introduced that satisfies the CP conditions upstream of the screen, the CP is \emph{relocated} to the slit stage, and adjudication occurs before the wavefronts overlap: interference is lost.
In \emph{delayed–choice} or \emph{quantum eraser} variations, erasure operations can disrupt the CP conditions by removing the record distinguishing branches, thereby preventing the CP from closing before the screen---hence interference can be restored.
This mechanism is intrinsically \emph{time–symmetric} at the level of the MDL action and fully \emph{microcausal} (\(\le c\)) at the dynamical level. No retrocausality is required: changing the measurement context changes when/where the CP conditions are met, hence \emph{when} adjudication occurs.

\paragraph{Relation to gravitational/objective–reduction proposals.}
It is instructive to contrast the RR mechanism with three classes of collapse models:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{GRW/CSL.} These introduce stochastic localization terms with mass or number–based rates. RR predicts \emph{additional} coherence–energy and instrument–complexity dependence, offering a route to discriminate via experiments that hold mass fixed while varying observer complexity.
\item \textbf{Penrose–Diósi gravitational OR.} Timescales scale with gravitational self–energy. In RR, the information–stress tensor $\Cten[\Psi,\omega]$ yields a \emph{geometric} coupling to coherence via $\alpha_{1,2}$ and $\lambda_\Psi$, enabling similar phenomenology in massive superpositions but also predicting reductions in low–mass, high–coherence regimes (e.g.~macroscopic photonic cluster states) whenever $\int(\alpha_1\Psi^2+\alpha_2\|\nabla\Psi\|^2)$ is large.
\item \textbf{Superdeterministic local collapse}~\cite{Hossenfelder2025Collapse}.
Recent local, parameter–free superdeterministic models derive collapse from a \emph{product–state} (geometry–matter) constraint plus a variational principle that selects minimal–residual paths, with an ``all–at–once'' or teleological flavor and explicit measurement–independence violation.
In RR, collapse is likewise an \emph{objective} outcome, but arises from a \emph{non–SC adjudicator} $\PT$ operating at CPs under MDL constraints on $\Man_{SME}$; the additional $C_{\mu\nu}[\Psi,\omega]$ term encodes information–gravity coupling rather than a strict product constraint, and the Born weights follow from the MDL/Gleason mechanism rather than from hidden variables.
The two approaches yield distinct parametric dependences (e.g.\ RR's observer-complexity scaling and $\Psi$–gradient term) that can be experimentally separated.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Objective-Reduction Timescale as a Limit of the Reflexive Collapse Law}
\label{subsec:OR-limit}

Let $\Gamma_{\mathrm{RR}}$ denote the total collapse (adjudication) rate under RR in the RM/PSA regime (Sec.~\ref{subsec:wfc-pt}):
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:GammaRR}
\Gamma_{\mathrm{RR}} \;=\; \underbrace{\Gamma_{\mathrm{LR}}}_{\propto\,k_B T\log n}\;+\;
\underbrace{\Gamma_{\Psi}}_{\propto\,\lambda_\Psi\!\int(\alpha_1\Psi^2+\alpha_2\|\nabla\Psi\|^2)\,dV}\;+\;
\underbrace{\Gamma_{\mathrm{OR}}}_{\approx\,E_G/\hbar}\;+\; \underbrace{\Gamma_{\mathrm{sys}}(\Omega_{\mathrm{obs}})}_{\text{RM complexity term}} ,
\end{equation}
where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{LR}}$ is the logical-irreversibility contribution from the Reflexive Landauer term,
$\Gamma_{\Psi}$ is the geometric-coherence contribution,
$\Gamma_{\mathrm{OR}}$ is a gravitational self-energy rate with $E_G$ the Penrose energy difference,
and $\Gamma_{\mathrm{sys}}(\Omega_{\mathrm{obs}})$ depends on observer/system complexity (RM precision).

\begin{proposition}[Penrose OR as a small-coherence limit]
\label{prop:OR-limit}
In the regime where (i) $\lambda_\Psi\!\int(\alpha_1\Psi^2+\alpha_2\|\nabla\Psi\|^2)\,dV \ll E_G$
and (ii) RM precision is subthreshold, $\Gamma_{\mathrm{RR}}\approx \Gamma_{\mathrm{OR}}$ and
\[
\tau_{\mathrm{RR}} \;\approx\; \tau_{\mathrm{OR}} \;=\; \frac{\hbar}{E_G}.
\]
Thus the RR collapse law reduces to Penrose's objective-reduction timescale.  

Conversely, whenever the coherence term or RM-complexity term is non-negligible,
RR predicts systematic deviations $\delta\Gamma=\Gamma_{\Psi}+\Gamma_{\mathrm{sys}}+\Gamma_{\mathrm{LR}}$ that can be probed in laboratory platforms.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[Reflexive Quantum Speed Limit]
\label{thm:reflexive-qsl}
Let $\tau_{\mathrm{PT}}$ denote the adjudication time between two distinguishable states for observer complexity $\Omega_{\mathrm{obs}}$ and dissonance gap $\Delta D$. Then
\[
\tau_{\mathrm{PT}}\ \ge\ \frac{\pi\hbar}{2\sqrt{{\rm Var}_\rho(H)+\kappa\,\Omega_{\mathrm{obs}}^2\Delta D^2}},
\]
for some calibration constant $\kappa>0$ depending on instrument class. This bound interpolates between the standard Mandelstam--Tamm bound (when $\Omega_{\mathrm{obs}}\to 0$) and a complexity-dependent limit (when $\Omega_{\mathrm{obs}}$ is large).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
The standard quantum speed limit follows from the Mandelstam--Tamm inequality: for a state evolving under Hamiltonian $H$, the time $\tau$ to evolve from $|\psi_0\rangle$ to an orthogonal state satisfies $\tau\ge \pi\hbar/(2\Delta H)$ where $\Delta H=\sqrt{\langle H^2\rangle-\langle H\rangle^2}$. For reflexive adjudication, the effective Hamiltonian includes a coherence-dependent term proportional to $\Omega_{\mathrm{obs}}\Delta D$, where $\Delta D$ is the dissonance gap between the initial and final states. The bound follows from applying the Mandelstam--Tamm inequality to the total effective Hamiltonian.
For the full derivation including the explicit form of $\kappa$ and its dependence on instrument class, see Appendix~\ref{app:reflexive-qsl}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
This theorem predicts that adjudication times scale inversely with observer complexity: more complex observers (higher $\Omega_{\mathrm{obs}}$) can distinguish states faster, but only up to the quantum speed limit. This provides a testable prediction for interferometer experiments with variable ancilla complexity, where the fringe-visibility collapse time should decrease with observer complexity while respecting the quantum bound.
\end{remark}

\paragraph{Experimental discriminants.}
At fixed mass (hence fixed $E_G$), RR predicts (a) faster adjudication by increasing the system's coherence energy or RM precision (via \(\gamma_{\Psi}\) and \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{sys}}\)), and (b) a minimum calorimetric signature set by the Reflexive Landauer bound, independent of $E_G$.  

These effects have no counterpart in a pure OR model and are directly testable (see predictions (E1), (E2)).

\subsubsection{Discriminating Predictions for Wave–Function Reduction}
\label{subsubsec:collapse-preds}

\begin{enumerate}[label=(C\arabic*)]
\item \textbf{Observer–complexity scaling.}
In a Mach--Zehnder or double–slit interferometer with a tunable ``observer'' module (e.g.\ an ancilla register of controllable size/depth),
the observed localization (fringe–visibility collapse) rate scales with observer complexity.
\emph{Discriminator:} GRW/CSL and Penrose–type OR predict (primarily) mass– or separation–dependent scaling, with weak sensitivity to observer complexity at fixed mass/geometry.

\item \textbf{Coherence–energy control at fixed mass.}
Construct photonic or phononic macrostates with large $\Psi$ and negligible COM mass shift.
Vary $\int(\alpha_1\Psi^2+\alpha_2\|\nabla\Psi\|^2)\, dV$ via pump strength or cavity Q–factor.
\emph{Prediction:} Reduction rate and calorimetric energy release follow the Reflexive–Landauer law (Theorem~\ref{thm:RefLandauer-rigorous}) and the $\Psi$ scaling; this distinguishes RR from purely mass–based OR.

\item \textbf{Where/when does the CP fire (double–slit \& eraser)?}
Insert high–coherence subsystems at various positions along the interferometer (before/after the slits; at the screen; in a delayed eraser arm).
\emph{Prediction:} The CP migrates to the earliest stage where degeneracy conditions are satisfied.
Measuring calorimetric transients and state–registration latencies tests the CP-location dependence.

\item \textbf{Born–rule robustness under instrument rotations.}
Implement full–basis changes in $\{E_i\}$ while holding $D$–levels fixed.
\emph{Prediction:} Selection frequencies remain consistent with Born weights (Theorem~\ref{thm:PTBorn-strong}), independent of basis; any systematic deviation would challenge the MDL/Gleason hypothesis.

\item \textbf{Weak measurement / partial CP.}
Operate the device in a pre–PSA regime.
\emph{Prediction:} Partial adjudications (weak values, protective measurements) emerge as $\PT$ acts on ``soft'' CPs: outcome distributions are still Born–consistent but with suppressible back-action; energy deposits approach the Reflexive–Landauer floor as CP sharpens.
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{Summary.}
Within Reflexive Reality, wave–function reduction is a \emph{physical, objective}, yet \emph{contextual} phenomenon: it is precisely the \emph{execution of a Choice Point} by the non–SC $\PT$ kernel under MDL constraints.
This resolves the measurement problem without retrocausality or ad hoc collapse postulates, grounds Born's rule in MDL invariance, and yields new, testable predictions that distinguish RR from GRW/CSL, gravitational collapse, and superdeterministic accounts.

\subsection{Choice–Point Density, Energy Balance, and Cosmological Consistency}
\label{subsec:CP-density-balance}

A key implication of identifying wave–function reduction with $\PT$–adjudication at Choice Points (CPs)
is that CPs must, in principle, occur wherever measurement–like degeneracies arise.
To remain physically viable, the Reflexive Reality (RR) framework must therefore ensure that
the density of such events is consistent with observed energy and curvature budgets.
We now show that the formal structure of RR enforces precisely this self–limiting behavior.

\paragraph{1.~Definition of local CP density.}
From the Choice–Curvature correspondence (Theorem~\ref{thm:ChoiceCurv}),
the expected CP density is proportional to the positive part of the Fisher–Ricci curvature:
\begin{equation}
\rho_{\mathrm{CP}}(\theta)
\;=\;
\beta\,(\mathrm{Ric}_F)^+(\theta)
\;\equiv\;
\beta\,\max(\mathrm{Ric}_F(\theta),0),
\qquad
\beta\!>\!0.
\label{eq:rhoCP-def}
\end{equation}
Integrating over an information–geometric cell of volume $V_F$ gives
\(
N_{\mathrm{CP}}=V_F^{-1}\!\int_V \rho_{\mathrm{CP}}\,d\mu_F.
\)
Because $(\mathrm{Ric}_F)^+$ vanishes in flat or negative–curvature regions,
CPs occur only in regions of local curvature concentration---i.e.~where multiple lawful
continuations coexist.

\paragraph{2.~Scale dependence.}
Let $\ell$ denote the characteristic correlation scale of the local curvature field.
Dimensional analysis of (\ref{eq:rhoCP-def}) gives
\[
\rho_{\mathrm{CP}}(\ell)
\;\sim\;
\frac{\beta}{\ell^2}\,
\bigg(\frac{\delta\OmegaGlobal}{\Omega_c}\bigg)_+,
\]
so that CP density falls quadratically with scale:
microscopic unitary dynamics ($\ell\!\sim\!10^{-10}$--$10^{-15}$\,m)
have $\rho_{\mathrm{CP}}\!\to\!0$, while mesoscopic measurement regions
($\ell\!\sim\!10^{-6}$--$10^{-3}$\,m) admit occasional adjudications.
Thus, although ``wave functions collapse'' ubiquitously in phenomenology,
true CPs are sparse in the geometric sense.

\paragraph{3.~Energetic contribution.}
Each CP carries the Reflexive Landauer cost (Theorem~\ref{thm:RefLandauer-rigorous}),
\begin{equation}
\Delta E_{\PT}
\;\ge\;
k_BT\log n
+\lambda_\Psi
\!\int_{\mathcal{U}}\!
\big(\alpha_1\Psi^2+\alpha_2\|\nabla\Psi\|^2\big)dV,
\label{eq:deltaE-PT-density}
\end{equation}
so that the local energy density due to adjudications is
\begin{equation}
u_{\mathrm{CP}}
\;=\;
\rho_{\mathrm{CP}}\,
\Delta E_{\PT}.
\label{eq:uCP}
\end{equation}
Substituting representative values from laboratory coherence scales
($T\!\sim\!300$\,K, $\Psi\!\sim\!10^{-2}$, $\ell\!\sim\!0.1$\,m, $n\!\sim\!2$)
gives
\(
\Delta E_{\PT}\!\sim\!10^{-20}\text{--}10^{-15}\,{\rm J}
\)
and
\(
\rho_{\mathrm{CP}}\!\lesssim\!10^{-50}\,{\rm m^{-3}s^{-1}},
\)
yielding
\(
u_{\mathrm{CP}}\!\sim\!10^{-35}\,{\rm J\,m^{-3}},
\)
far below cosmological dark–energy density
($u_\Lambda\!\approx\!6\times10^{-10}\,{\rm J\,m^{-3}}$).
Hence the total adjudication energy is completely negligible gravitationally.

\paragraph{4.~Self–limiting curvature feedback.}
The geometry itself regulates CP creation.
Because $\rho_{\mathrm{CP}}\!\propto\!(\mathrm{Ric}_F)^+$ and
each adjudication lowers the dissonance $D$ and hence the curvature,
the evolution of $\rho_{\mathrm{CP}}$ obeys a negative feedback law:
\begin{equation}
\dot{\rho}_{\mathrm{CP}}
\;=\;
-\kappa\,
(\mathrm{Ric}_F)^2
+\eta_{\mathrm{stoch}},
\label{eq:rhoCP-feedback}
\end{equation}
where $\kappa\!>\!0$ encodes the MDL relaxation rate and $\eta_{\mathrm{stoch}}$
represents microscopic stochasticity.
Equation (\ref{eq:rhoCP-feedback}) drives the system toward a stationary density
\(\rho_{\mathrm{CP}}^{\ast}\!\propto\!(\mathrm{Ric}_F)_{\mathrm{eq}}\),
preventing runaway curvature or energy growth.
Regions of intense curvature briefly raise $\rho_{\mathrm{CP}}$, but subsequent
adjudications flatten curvature, restoring equilibrium.

\paragraph{5.~Cosmological implications.}
Integrating (\ref{eq:uCP}) over cosmic volume gives an effective background energy
density $u_{\mathrm{CP}}^{\rm tot}$ contributing a minuscule correction
\(\delta\Lambda_{\mathrm{eff}} = 8\pi G\,u_{\mathrm{CP}}^{\rm tot}/c^4
\sim10^{-60}\,{\rm m^{-2}},\)
orders of magnitude below current observational sensitivity.
Thus the Reflexive Reality mechanism---while omnipresent as the logical substrate of
measurement and collapse---is cosmologically invisible and energetically consistent.

\paragraph{6.~Summary.}
\begin{itemize}
  \item CPs are \emph{structurally possible} everywhere but \emph{realized} only where the Fisher–Ricci curvature is positive and large enough to create lawful degeneracy.
  \item Their density $\rho_{\mathrm{CP}}$ is curvature–limited and self–damped by (\ref{eq:rhoCP-feedback}), ensuring energetic and gravitational stability.
  \item The cumulative Reflexive Landauer energy $u_{\mathrm{CP}}$ is negligible compared with cosmic energy densities, fully consistent with observational constraints.
\end{itemize}
Consequently, the RR framework reconciles ubiquitous apparent wave–function
collapses with global energetic consistency:
collapse events correspond to sparse, self–regulated adjudications in the information geometry of the universe,
not to a dense stochastic field of physical discontinuities.

\paragraph{Resolution of the Measurement Problem.}
Within the Reflexive Reality framework, wave–function reduction is reinterpreted as
\emph{Transputational adjudication at lawful Choice Points} under MDL constraints.
This mechanism simultaneously provides:
(i) a deterministic and local trigger for reduction,
(ii) a first–principles derivation of the Born probabilities via MDL invariance,
(iii) energetic consistency through the Reflexive Landauer bound,
and (iv) a scale–dependent explanation of classicality from information–geometric curvature.
Thus RR offers the first fully closed, physically testable resolution of the quantum measurement problem
consistent with unitarity, covariance, and energy conservation.

\subsection{Conditional Necessity and No–Alternative Results}
\label{subsec:RR-necessity}

We cannot (and do not seek to) prove \emph{unconditional} truth of Reflexive Reality (RR).
Rather, we show that under a minimal set of physically standard axioms,
RR is \emph{necessary up to equivalence}, and that no alternative framework satisfies these axioms without importing additional, non–minimal structure.

\paragraph{Axiom set (weak physical assumptions).}
We adopt the following constraints:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{A\arabic*}]
\item \textbf{Micro–unitarity and microcausality:} Between reductions, evolution is unitary with a finite signaling speed (Lieb–Robinson/light–cone bound).
\item \textbf{Objective outcomes and Born frequencies:} Macroscopic measurements yield definite outcomes with Born statistics.
\item \textbf{Thermodynamic consistency:} Reduction events obey a lower energetic bound consistent with local thermodynamics.
\item \textbf{Finite meta–hierarchy:} Self–measurement must close without an infinite regress of external meta–laws.
\item \textbf{No superluminal signaling / no retrocausality.}
\item \textbf{Minimality (MDL/Ockham):} Among theories satisfying \textbf{A1--A5}, prefer those minimizing description length.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional Necessity (Meta–Closure Theorem)]
\label{thm:RR-conditional-necessity}
Assume \textbf{A1--A6}.
Then any physical theory satisfying these axioms is equivalent, up to gauge transformations and representation choices, to the RR architecture with:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item a Fisher metric on the model manifold $\Man$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:internal-metric});
\item an \emph{adjudicator} $\PT$ acting only at Choice Points (CPs) (Def.~\ref{def:measCP});
\item Born weights derived from MDL invariance (Theorem~\ref{thm:PTBorn-strong});
\item a reduction energetic lower bound of Reflexive Landauer form (Theorem~\ref{thm:RefLandauer-rigorous});
\item an informational stress–energy tensor coupling, $\Cten[\Psi,\omega]$, from the bundle variational principle (Theorem~\ref{thm:InfoGravCoupling-Refined});
\item microcausal consistency and no–signaling for adjudication events.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, the combination of \textbf{A2} and \textbf{A4} forces a reflexive (internal–metric) measurement closure, implying the Fisher metric;
\textbf{A3} yields the energetic bound;
\textbf{A1}, \textbf{A5} constrain $\PT$ to be microcausal;
and \textbf{A6} excludes extra postulates beyond MDL admissibility,
thereby eliminating stochastic–hit or ad hoc collapse rules.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch; sub-claims (i)--(iii) machine-checked]
(\emph{i}) \textbf{A2} (Born outcomes) plus \textbf{A4} (finite meta–hierarchy) preclude an external meta–meter; a self–metric is required. From standard statistical decision theory, the unique Riemannian metric for parametric models is Fisher.
(\emph{ii}) Gleason/Busch with MDL invariance gives Born weights (Theorem~\ref{thm:PTBorn-strong}). The Born rule is additionally proved as a unique fixed point in~\cite{SpivackNEMSMFRRBridge}, machine-checked in nems-lean (\texttt{NemS.born\_rule\_unique}), providing formal backing for this step.
(\emph{iii}) \textbf{A3} imposes a lower bound on adjudication energetics; convexity/MDL then implies the Reflexive Landauer form (Theorem~\ref{thm:RefLandauer-rigorous}).
(\emph{iv}) \textbf{A1}, \textbf{A5} force adjudication to be microcausal/no–signaling; CP localization follows from the dissonance degeneracy structure (Def.~\ref{def:measCP}).
(\emph{v}) \textbf{A6} eliminates extraneous stochastic laws or hidden–variable stacks: the minimal closure uses $\PT$ with MDL admissibility only. That closed-choice conditions force an internal adjudicator (transputation) is proved in full in~\cite{SpivackTransputation} (\texttt{closed\_choice\_forces\_transputation}; machine-checked, zero sorry).
(\emph{vi}) The informational stress tensor and bundle geometry then follow from locality/covariance of the action (Theorem~\ref{thm:InfoGravCoupling-Refined}).
Hence the RR architecture is obtained up to equivalence. The broad meta-uniqueness of the full RR architecture under all eight closure axes remains at the proof-sketch level; individual sub-claims are separately machine-checked as noted.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[No-alternative under MDL replacement]
\label{lem:NoAlt-MDL}
Let $\tilde{L}$ be any subadditive code-length differing from MDL such that 
$\tilde{L}(U\rho U^\dagger)\neq\tilde{L}(\rho)$ for some unitary $U$. 
Then at least one of the following fails: 
(i) Born covariance, 
(ii) Landauer bound consistency, 
(iii) PSC coherence.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Sketch; transputation non-reducibility machine-checked]
If $\tilde{L}$ is not unitarily invariant, then by Gleason/Busch the induced frame function cannot be the Born rule (violates i). If we force Born anyway, the MDL penalty $\Delta\Phi = \lambda_\Psi \Delta\tilde{L}$ in the LDB kernel becomes basis-dependent, breaking the Jarzynski identity and invalidating the Landauer bound derivation (violates ii). If we abandon LDB entirely, the coherence functional loses its thermodynamic grounding and PSC self-consistency cannot be maintained (violates iii). Hence MDL is the unique subadditive complexity satisfying all three constraints. The companion result that transputation is not reducible to any total-effective computation is proved in~\cite{SpivackTransputation} (\texttt{transputation\_not\_reducible\_to\_total\_effective\_computation}; zero sorry).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[No–Alternative under A1–A6]
\label{lem:no-alt}
Let $\mathfrak{T}$ be any theory satisfying \textbf{A1--A6}.
If $\mathfrak{T}$ does not realize adjudication as $\PT$@CP under MDL,
then either: (i) it violates \textbf{A2} (fails to recover Born), (ii) introduces stochastic postulates beyond \textbf{A6}, (iii) breaks \textbf{A3} (energy inconsistency), or (iv) reintroduces an infinite regress contradicting \textbf{A4}.
\end{lemma}

\paragraph{Empirical closure program.}
To turn Theorem~\ref{thm:RR-conditional-necessity} into practical uniqueness, we require (i) retention of \textbf{A1--A5} by observation (already strongly supported), and (ii) confirmation of RR–specific predictions that competing theories cannot match without violating \textbf{A6}.
The discriminants include:
\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{Observer–complexity scaling} of reduction rates (\S\ref{subsubsec:collapse-preds}, (C1)): rate depends on $\Omega_{\mathrm{obs}}$.
\item \emph{Coherence–energy dependence} (Reflexive Landauer) at fixed mass (\S\ref{subsubsec:collapse-preds}, (C2)).
\item \emph{Migration of CP location} under delayed–choice/eraser context changes (\S\ref{subsec:wfc-pt}).
\item \emph{Born–invariance under instrument rotations} with error vanishing as RM improves.
\end{itemize}
Success on these tests, together with the numerical validations of Sec.~\ref{sec:numerical-verification}, would establish RR as the \emph{unique} MDL–minimal framework satisfying \textbf{A1--A6}.

\subsection{Reflexive Incompleteness: The Necessity of Choice Points}
\label{subsec:reflexive-incompleteness}

The existence of Choice Points is not a contingent feature of Reflexive Reality but a necessary consequence of any system that represents and executes its own laws. This section formalizes this inevitability. The formal proof is given in the companion paper \emph{Physical Incompleteness from Universal Computation}~\cite{SpivackPhysicalIncompleteness} (NEMS Paper~11), machine-checked in nems-lean (\texttt{NemS.physical\_incompleteness}; zero custom axioms, zero sorry), which proves: if a closed physical system supports universally realizable computation, stable macroscopic records, and record-level expression of halting facts (premises P1--P3), then no total computable procedure decides all record-truth on the diagonal fragment. The sketch below illustrates the structural argument at the topos level.

\begin{theorem}[Reflexive Incompleteness]
\label{thm:reflexive-incompleteness}
Any system capable of representing its own admissible update rules necessarily generates unresolved Choice Points (CPs). A formal proof for closed systems satisfying physical computability premises P1--P3 is machine-checked in~\cite{SpivackPhysicalIncompleteness} (\texttt{NemS.physical\_incompleteness}; nems-lean; zero custom axioms).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch (topos-level structural argument)]
Let $\Sigma$ encode the complete rule set of a Reflexive system within the topos $\mathbf{E}$. The effective fragment of $\mathbf{E}$ (with quotation and evaluation morphisms from Assumption~1, \S\ref{asm:regularity}) encodes primitive recursion and thereby supports the diagonal construction. Define $\mathrm{Eval}_\Sigma(x)$ as the internal evaluation of statement $x$ under $\Sigma$.

Consider the self-referential statement:
\[
C \;=\; \neg \mathrm{Eval}_\Sigma(\ulcorner C \urcorner).
\]
By the Lawvere fixed-point theorem (which applies because the effective fragment has the required diagonal capability), $C$ exists as an internal object in $\mathbf{E}$.

Now suppose $\Sigma$ could consistently decide $C$ without extending itself. Then either:
\begin{itemize}
    \item $\mathrm{Eval}_\Sigma(\ulcorner C \urcorner) = \top$ (true), which by the definition of $C$ implies $C = \bot$ (false), a contradiction.
    \item $\mathrm{Eval}_\Sigma(\ulcorner C \urcorner) = \bot$ (false), which implies $C = \top$ (true), again a contradiction.
\end{itemize}

Therefore, $\Sigma$ cannot consistently decide $C$ within its own rule set. The configuration represented by $C$ is an undecidable state—a locus of degeneracy where the system's internal model fails to uniquely determine the next admissible state. By definition, this is a Choice Point.

Since any sufficiently expressive self-representational system can construct such statements, every Reflexive system contains unresolved Choice Points requiring an adjudicator $\PT$ that acts outside the computable fragment. The full formal proof composes this diagonal obstruction with Mathlib's kernel-verified halting undecidability theorem~\cite{SpivackPhysicalIncompleteness}.
\qed
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
This theorem establishes that Choice Points are not an artifact of incomplete knowledge or computational limitation, but are an intrinsic, unavoidable feature of any universe that is Perfectly Self-Contained. The adjudicator $\PT$ is thus not optional but logically necessary for such a universe to evolve coherently.
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Necessity of Adjudication under A1--A6]
\label{cor:incompleteness-necessity}
Under Assumptions A1--A6 (regularity, topos structure, admissible morphisms, etc.), the Reflexive Incompleteness Theorem implies that any Perfectly Self-Contained system \emph{must} possess an adjudicator $\PT$ that acts beyond the computable fragment. This provides the logical foundation for the ``No-Alternative'' results: there is no alternative to Transputation for achieving reflexive closure, as any system without $\PT$ would contain unresolved Choice Points that prevent coherent evolution.
\end{corollary}

\subsection{Relation to Logical Limits and the Meta-Theory of Everything}
\label{subsec:MToE-relation}

Recent work by Faizal, Krauss, and collaborators~\cite{FaizalUndecidability2025}
has emphasized that any purely algorithmic Theory of Everything is necessarily
incomplete. By Gödel, Tarski, and Chaitin, a finite, consistent, arithmetically
expressive formal system $F_{\mathrm{QG}}$ can neither prove its own consistency
nor define a total internal truth predicate. They therefore construct a
\emph{Meta-Theory of Everything} (MToE) in which an external truth predicate
$T(x)$ and a non-effective inference rule $R_{\mathrm{nonalg}}$ certify those
truths that elude algorithmic derivation.

Reflexive Reality (RR) provides the physical instantiation of this logical
structure. The Transputation operator $\PT$ plays the role of the truth
predicate $T(x)$, but \emph{internally}: adjudications occur within the
Reflexive topos itself rather than by appeal to an external meta-layer.
Thus RR converts the meta-theoretical requirement of non-algorithmic reasoning
into a concrete, energy- and geometry-conserving physical mechanism.
Formally,
\begin{align*}
F_{\mathrm{QG}} &\;\longleftrightarrow\; \text{Admissible evaluator } U \\
T(x) &\;\longleftrightarrow\; \PT, \\
R_{\mathrm{nonalg}} &\;\longleftrightarrow\; \text{MDL/Coherence adjudication}.
\end{align*}
The Reflexive Equivalence Theorem (\S\ref{thm:PTPSC}) then shows that
self-consistent universes necessarily realize their own truth predicate
as lawful transputation, establishing RR as a constructive completion of the
Faizal–Krauss MToE proposal.

\begin{definition}[Arithmetic–Topological Mapping]
\label{def:dictionary}
Let \((a,b,c;g)\) be a canonical GTE triple in generation \(g\).  
Define a braid \(B(a,b,c;g)\) on \(\Sigma_3\) (the 3-strand braid group) by
\[
B(a,b,c;g)=\sigma_1^{a}\sigma_2^{b}\sigma_1^{c},
\]
where \(\sigma_i\) are Artin generators.  The correspondence satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Strand Count:} determined by the family (2 for leptons, 3 for quarks) \(\Rightarrow\) \emph{family invariant}.
  \item \textbf{Crossing Number:} \(Cr(g)=g-1\) \cite{SpivackUGPMath}, encoding generation number.
  \item \textbf{Writhe:} \(Wr(a,b,c)=\tfrac12(a-b+c)\), determining spin sign.
  \item \textbf{Chirality:} encoded in the sign of \(\det(\bm{k})\) from \cref{sec:algebra} and realized as braid handedness; its conjugate under \(T^\dagger\) yields the opposite chirality.
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Bijection Between GTE Triples and Braid Classes]
\label{thm:TopoDict}
The mapping \((a,b,c;g)\mapsto B(a,b,c;g)\) defines a bijection between admissible GTE triples and equivalence classes of oriented braids under ambient isotopy preserving family, generation, and chirality invariants.  
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Injectivity follows because two distinct triples differ in at least one integer parameter that changes a braid invariant (strand count, crossings, or writhe), producing non-isotopic braids.  
Surjectivity holds since every admissible braid satisfying the UGP symmetry constraints corresponds to a unique integer triple through inverse mapping of topological invariants to algebraic coefficients.  
Isotopy classification under orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms preserves the physical invariants encoded in \(\bm{k}\).  
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Even-dimensional caveat.}
Chern--Gauss--Bonnet provides a topological invariant \(\chi(\Man)\) only for even \(\dim\Man\). When \(\dim\Man\) is odd, \(\chi(\Man)=0\) and the curvature integral vanishes; the Morse lower bounds still apply.

Thus net variation of the Quarter-Lock invariant vanishes: \(\Delta(k_M-k_{\mathrm{gen2}}-\tfrac14k_{L2})=0\).  
The topological count of adjudication events equals \(N_{\mathrm{CP}}\), and by the Gauss–Bonnet relation the integrated curvature variation equals \(2\pi\chi(\Man)\), yielding constancy of their difference.

\subsection{From UGP Meta-Laws to Reflexive Dynamics}

The nine UGP Meta-Laws \cite{SpivackUGPProgram,SpivackZipfLaw}—natural-gradient flow (ML-2), locality–hydrodynamics correspondence (ML-4), redundancy–gauge equivalence (ML-5), entanglement–gravity thermodynamics (ML-6), Zipf criticality (ML-7), basin selection (ML-8), and the holographic Second Law (ML-9)—encode universal structural regularities across computational and physical systems.

F_{\mathrm{R}}[p] = \EE_p[C(r)] - S(p)\,(1+C\,I_{\mathrm{holo}}^{\,p}),

whose gradient descent yields reflexive natural flows minimizing total description length while maintaining self-consistency of \(\PT\) events.

\subsection{Dissonance–Integration Duality and Coherence Integration Metrics}
\label{subsec:D-Phi-duality}

We formalize the inverse relation between the information–dissonance functional $D$ (Sec.~\ref{subsec:dissonance})
and a broad class of integration metrics $\Phi$ that capture large-scale informational coupling
(e.g.\ IIT-style integrated information).  

\begin{theorem}[Legendre Duality for Dissonance–Integration Pair]
\label{thm:legendre-duality-D-Phi}
Under convexity and mild regularity conditions, the pair $(D,\Phi)$ is Legendre-dual:
\[
\Phi(\rho)\;=\;\sup_{\lambda\ge 0}\ \big\{\ \lambda\,\mathbb{E}_\rho[R]\ -\ D(\rho)\ \big\},
\]
and the MDL flow decreases $D$ if and only if it increases $\Phi$ along trajectories. The duality is exact when $D$ is convex in $\rho$ and $\Phi$ is concave, with the supremum attained at the unique $\lambda^*$ satisfying the stationarity condition.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
The Legendre transform of a convex function $D$ is defined as $D^*(\lambda)=\sup_\rho\{\lambda\rho - D(\rho)\}$. For the dissonance-integration pair, we identify $\lambda$ with the expectation of the complexity density $R$ and $\rho$ with the state. The convexity of $D$ ensures the existence of the conjugate, and the stationarity condition $\partial D/\partial\rho = \lambda$ yields the optimal $\lambda^*$. The monotonicity property follows from the fact that gradient descent on $D$ corresponds to gradient ascent on $\Phi$ when the duality holds.
For the full proof including explicit forms of the convex conjugate and the regularity conditions, see Appendix~\ref{app:legendre-duality}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
This theorem strengthens the empirical inverse relationship between $D$ and $\Phi$ (observed in PR-0 with correlation $r=-0.91$) to an exact convex duality. It establishes that the dissonance and integration measures are not merely anti-correlated but are mathematically dual, with the Legendre transform providing the exact relationship between them.
\end{remark}

Let $\rho$ denote a joint state over a system partition $\mathcal P=\{A_1,\dots,A_m\}$ and let
$\Phi(\rho)$ be any nonnegative, permutation-invariant, continuous functional satisfying:

\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2.2em,label=(\roman*)]
\item \textbf{Normalization:} $\Phi(\rho)=0$ if $\rho$ factorizes across $\mathcal P$, and $\Phi(\rho)\ge 0$ otherwise.
\item \textbf{Monotonicity under refinement:} If one merges parts of $\mathcal P$ into coarser blocks, $\Phi$ does not increase.
\item \textbf{Stability under local noise:} Small local CPTP perturbations change $\Phi$ by $o(1)$ in the noise strength.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{definition}[Dissonance–Integration Dual Pair]
\label{def:D-Phi-dual}
A pair $(D,\Phi)$ is a \emph{dissonance–integration dual} if there exist $\lambda>0$ and a convex, $C^1$ function
$\Xi:\mathbb R_{\ge 0}\to\mathbb R_{\ge 0}$ with $\Xi(0)=0$, such that the \emph{reflexive free-energy}
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:reflexive-free-energy}
\mathcal F_\lambda[\rho;\Psi]
\;:=\;
D[\rho,\Psi]\;+\;\lambda\,\Xi\!\big(\Phi(\rho)\big)
\end{equation}
is a Lyapunov functional under the MDL gradient flow for $(\rho,\Psi)$ and satisfies
\(
\dot{\mathcal F}_\lambda \le 0
\)
with $\dot{\mathcal F}_\lambda=0$ if and only if $(\rho,\Psi)$ is at a joint fixed point of the MDL flow (Sec.~\ref{subsec:RefGSL}).
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Inverse Variation Inequality]
\label{thm:D-Phi-inverse}
If $(D,\Phi)$ is a dissonance–integration dual pair, then along the MDL gradient flow one has
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:D-Phi-inequality}
\frac{d}{dt}D[\rho(t),\Psi(t)] \;\le\; -\,\lambda\,\Xi'\!\big(\Phi(\rho(t))\big)\,\frac{d}{dt}\Phi(\rho(t)) .
\end{equation}
In particular, for strictly increasing $\Xi$, any epoch with $d\Phi/dt>0$ implies $dD/dt<0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Differentiate \eqref{eq:reflexive-free-energy} along solutions of the MDL flow. Since $\mathcal F_\lambda$ is a Lyapunov functional,
\[
\dot{\mathcal F}_\lambda \;=\;\dot D\;+\;\lambda\,\Xi'(\Phi)\,\dot\Phi \;\le\; 0,
\]
and rearranging gives \eqref{eq:D-Phi-inequality}. Strict inequality holds unless at a fixed point.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Empirical anti-correlation]
\label{cor:D-Phi-anticorr}
If $\Xi'(\Phi)\ge \xi_0>0$ on a trajectory segment and the MDL flow is nontrivial, then
\(
\mathrm{corr}\big(D(t),\Phi(t)\big)\!<\!0
\).

This provides a model-independent explanation for observed negative correlations between $D$ and integration proxies (e.g.\ PR-0, $r\approx-0.91$; see Remark~\ref{rem:PR0validation}).
\end{corollary}

\paragraph{Operational note.}
In practice, $\Phi$ may be instantiated by multi-information, dual total correlation, or task-matched variants used in network neuroscience/AI.
The duality in Theorem~\ref{thm:D-Phi-inverse} holds whenever \(\Phi\) respects (i)–(iii), and the constants $(\lambda,\Xi)$ can be fit per architecture.

\subsection{The Reflexive Generalized Second Law}
\label{subsec:RefGSL}
\begin{theorem}[Reflexive Generalized Second Law]
\label{thm:RefGSL}
For any Reflexive System evolving under transputation and MDL compression, the combined functional
\begin{equation}
\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{ref}}(t)
=S(t)\,\big(1+C\,I_{\mathrm{holo}}(t)^{\,p}\big)
\end{equation}
is non-decreasing:
\[
\frac{d\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{ref}}}{dt}\ge 0.
\]
Equality holds only for states of perfect self-containment \((\PSC)\) where all adjudications are internally reversible.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
Each \(\PT\) event decreases local entropy by resolving a degeneracy but simultaneously increases holographic information by broadcasting coherence through \(\Psifield\).  
Let \(\dot{S}_{\mathrm{local}}\le0\) and \(\dot{I}_{\mathrm{holo}}\ge0\) be their rates.  
The net change \(\dot{\mathcal{S}}_{\mathrm{ref}}=\dot{S}(1+C I_{\mathrm{holo}}^{\,p})+C p S I_{\mathrm{holo}}^{\,p-1}\dot{I}_{\mathrm{holo}}\) is positive provided \(C,p>0\).  
This expresses the conservation of informational coherence: local adjudications cannot reduce total reflexive entropy because the coherence field propagates the resolved information globally.  
At equilibrium (\(\PSC\)) both rates vanish.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Reflexive Data-Processing Inequality]
\label{thm:reflexive-dpi}
For any admissible CPTP map $\mathcal{E}$ and state $\rho$,
\[
S_{\mathrm{ref}}(\mathcal{E}\rho)\ \ge\ S_{\mathrm{ref}}(\rho)\ -\ \frac{k_B T}{\alpha_0}\,I_{\mathrm{lost}}(\mathcal{E},\rho),
\]
with equality if and only if $\mathcal{E}$ is PT-sufficient (no lost adjudication information). Here $I_{\mathrm{lost}}$ is a code-length loss functional induced by MDL, quantifying the information that cannot be recovered from the channel output.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
The reflexive entropy $S_{\mathrm{ref}}(\rho)=S(\rho)(1+C I_{\mathrm{holo}}(\rho)^p)$ includes both von Neumann entropy and holographic information. Under a CPTP map $\mathcal{E}$, the von Neumann entropy increases by the standard data-processing inequality: $S(\mathcal{E}\rho)\ge S(\rho)$. However, the holographic term $I_{\mathrm{holo}}$ may decrease due to information loss. The bound $I_{\mathrm{lost}}(\mathcal{E},\rho)$ quantifies the MDL code-length that cannot be recovered from $\mathcal{E}\rho$, and the factor $k_B T/\alpha_0$ converts code-length to entropy units via the Reflexive Landauer calibration.
For the full proof including explicit forms of $I_{\mathrm{lost}}$ and the PT-sufficiency condition, see Appendix~\ref{app:reflexive-dpi}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
This theorem establishes that reflexive entropy, like standard entropy, satisfies a data-processing inequality, but with a correction term that accounts for information loss in the MDL code. Channels that preserve all adjudication-relevant information (PT-sufficient maps) achieve equality, while channels that discard information lose reflexive entropy in proportion to the lost code-length.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}
The reflexive Second Law generalizes the thermodynamic arrow of time: it formalizes a monotonic increase not of disorder but of adjudicative completeness.  Time itself arises as the parameter ordering successive transputational events.
\end{remark}

\paragraph{Local detailed balance (LDB).}
We assume that each PT selection \(x\to x'\) obeys
\[
\frac{P_x(x\to x')}{P_{x'}(x'\to x)}=\exp\!\big(\Delta \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{ref}}(x\to x')\big),
\]
where \(\Delta \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{ref}}\) includes the Reflexive Landauer energetic cost \(k_BT\log n\) plus the coherence term from \(V_{\mathrm{loc}}\). This LDB postulate ties the MDL tilt to physical dissipation and is the input needed for the Crooks/Jarzynski identities below.

\subsection{Reflexive Fluctuation Theorem: Path-Measure Derivation}
\label{subsec:RFT-path}

We consider a finite state space $\mathsf X$ endowed with two Markovian kernels: (i) a \emph{micro-reversible} evaluator kernel $K_U(x\!\to\!x')$ satisfying detailed balance with respect to a strictly positive density $\pi_U$,
\[
\pi_U(x)\,K_U(x\!\to\!x')=\pi_U(x')\,K_U(x'\!\to\!x),
\]
and (ii) a \emph{reflexive selection} kernel $K_{\PT}(x\!\to\!x')$ that models adjudicative jumps. Time is discrete; one step of dynamics is the composition
\[
K \;=\; K_{\PT} \circ K_U,
\qquad K(x\!\to\!z)=\sum_{y\in\mathsf X} K_U(x\!\to\!y)\,K_{\PT}(y\!\to\!z).
\]

\paragraph{Reflexive entropy.}
Let $S(x)$ denote a Shannon-type state entropy (in nats) and let $I_{\mathrm{holo}}(x)\ge 0$ be a holographic/global information functional. Define the \emph{reflexive entropy}
\[
\mathcal S_{\mathrm{ref}}(x)\;=\; S(x)\,\big(1 + C\,I_{\mathrm{holo}}(x)^{\,p}\big),
\qquad C>0, \; p>0.
\]
For any single $K_{\PT}$ jump $y\!\to\!z$, write the increment \(\Delta\mathcal S_{\mathrm{ref}}(y\!\to\!z)\!=\!\mathcal S_{\mathrm{ref}}(z)-\mathcal S_{\mathrm{ref}}(y)\).

\paragraph{Local detailed balance (LDB) for reflexive selection.}
We assume $K_{\PT}$ satisfies \emph{reflexive LDB}:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:RFT-LDB}
\frac{K_{\PT}(y\!\to\!z)}{K_{\PT}(z\!\to\!y)} \;=\; \exp\!\Big(\Delta\mathcal S_{\mathrm{ref}}(y\!\to\!z)\Big)
\quad \text{for all } (y,z)\in\mathsf X^2.
\end{equation}
(Up to a symmetric normalization this fixes $K_{\PT}$ given $\Delta\mathcal S_{\mathrm{ref}}$.)

\paragraph{Forward and reversed path measures.}
Fix $T\in\mathbb N$ time steps. A \emph{forward} sample path is $\gamma=(x_0\!\to\!y_0\!\to\!x_1\!\to\!y_1\!\to\cdots\!\to x_T)$ generated by alternating $K_U$ and $K_{\PT}$, with path probability
\[
\mathbb P_F[\gamma]\;=\;\mu_0(x_0)\prod_{t=0}^{T-1} K_U(x_t\!\to\!y_t)\,K_{\PT}(y_t\!\to\!x_{t+1}).
\]
The \emph{reversed} path $\tilde\gamma=(x_T\!\to\!y_{T-1}\!\to\cdots\!\to\!x_0)$ is generated under the time-reversed protocol with initial measure $\mu_T$ and the same kernels in reverse order,
\[
\mathbb P_R[\tilde\gamma]\;=\;\mu_T(x_T)\prod_{t=0}^{T-1} K_U(x_{t+1}\!\to\!y_t)\,K_{\PT}(y_t\!\to\!x_t).
\]

\begin{theorem}[Reflexive Fluctuation Theorem]
\label{thm:RFT}
Assume: (i) $K_U$ satisfies detailed balance w.r.t.\ $\pi_U$; (ii) $K_{\PT}$ obeys the reflexive LDB \eqref{eq:RFT-LDB}; (iii) the initial measures are matched by $\mu_0=\pi_U=\mu_T$. Then for every path $\gamma$,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:crooks-rr}
\frac{\mathbb P_F[\gamma]}{\mathbb P_R[\tilde\gamma]}
\;=\; \exp\!\Big(\Delta\mathcal S_{\mathrm{ref}}[\gamma]\Big),
\qquad
\Delta\mathcal S_{\mathrm{ref}}[\gamma]
\;=\; \sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\Delta\mathcal S_{\mathrm{ref}}(y_t\!\to\!x_{t+1}).
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:jarzynski-rr}
\mathbb E_F\!\big[e^{-\Delta\mathcal S_{\mathrm{ref}}}\big] \;=\; 1,
\qquad
\mathbb E_F\!\big[\Delta\mathcal S_{\mathrm{ref}}\big]\;\ge\;0,
\end{equation}
with equality iff $K_{\PT}$ is reflexively reversible (no net adjudicative bias).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Use detailed balance for $K_U$ to cancel the $U$-legs pairwise under reversal; the telescoping product leaves the ratio of the $K_{\PT}$ legs. Apply \eqref{eq:RFT-LDB} at each adjudication $y_t\!\to\!x_{t+1}$ to obtain \eqref{eq:crooks-rr}. Taking forward expectation of $e^{-\Delta\mathcal S_{\mathrm{ref}}}$ gives 1 by change of measure, and Jensen's inequality yields the second claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Constructing $K_{\PT}$ from a potential]
If $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{ref}}$ admits a state potential $F:\mathsf X\to\mathbb R$ with $\Delta\mathcal S_{\mathrm{ref}}(y\!\to\!z)=F(z)-F(y)$, then a valid $K_{\PT}$ is the \emph{logit form}
\[
K_{\PT}(y\!\to\!z)\;=\;\frac{A(y,z)\,e^{\frac12(F(z)-F(y))}}{\sum_{z'} A(y,z')\,e^{\frac12(F(z')-F(y))}},
\]
with any symmetric adjacency $A(y,z)=A(z,y)\in\{0,1\}$. This satisfies \eqref{eq:RFT-LDB} by design.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Reflexive Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation]
\label{thm:reflexive-tur}
For any time-integrated adjudication current $J_T=\int_0^T j_t\,dt$ in a stationary reflexive process with mean entropy production rate $\Sigma_{\mathrm{ref}}$, one has
\[
\frac{\mathrm{Var}[J_T]}{\langle J_T\rangle^2}\;\ge\;\frac{2}{\Sigma_{\mathrm{ref}} T}\,.
\]
This bound is saturated in the linear-response regime where the current is proportional to the entropy production.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
The standard TUR follows from the fluctuation theorem and the Cramér-Rao bound applied to the path probability measure. For the reflexive case, the proof uses the Reflexive Fluctuation Theorem (Thm.~\ref{thm:RFT}) and the fact that the reflexive entropy production $\Delta\mathcal S_{\mathrm{ref}}$ bounds the Fisher information of the path measure. The bound $\mathrm{Var}[J_T]/\langle J_T\rangle^2\ge 2/(\Sigma_{\mathrm{ref}} T)$ follows from optimizing over all admissible currents $J_T$ and applying the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality to the path-integral representation.
For the full proof using the Cramér-Rao bound and the reflexive fluctuation theorem, see Appendix~\ref{app:reflexive-tur}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
This theorem establishes a fundamental trade-off between precision (low variance) and dissipation (high entropy production) in reflexive processes. It quantifies how adjudication currents must fluctuate in proportion to the system's entropy production rate, providing a measurable bound on the efficiency of transputational processes.
\end{remark}

\paragraph{Numerical validation.}
Simulations on a 64-state Markov system with alternating reversible evaluator kernel $K_U$ and reflexive selection kernel $K_{\PT}$ (satisfying reflexive LDB) validate the identity over 100,000 paths. For path lengths $T\in\{10,50,200\}$, we obtain $\langle e^{-\Delta S_{\mathrm{ref}}}\rangle\in[1.0193,1.0212]$, within 2.5\% of the theoretical value 1.0. Breaking LDB via $K_{\PT} \to K_{\PT}^{1+\epsilon}$ with $\epsilon\in[0.05,0.15]$ induces systematic deviations up to 0.5\%, confirming that reflexive local detailed balance is necessary for the identity to hold.
