\section{Topos and Fixed-Point Machinery}
\label{app:topos}
\subsection{Categorical Structure}
The Reflexive System lives in a Cartesian closed topos \(\mathbf{E}\) with objects:
\(\mathrm{Env},\mathrm{Code},\mathrm{Prog}\), and exponential objects \(\mathrm{Code}^{\mathrm{Env}}\).
Key morphisms:
\[
\ulcorner\cdot\urcorner:L\!\to\!\mathrm{Code},\qquad
\mathrm{eval}:\mathrm{Code}\times\mathrm{Env}\!\to\!\mathrm{Env}.
\]
These satisfy the \emph{quotation–evaluation retract}:
\[
\mathrm{eval}(\ulcorner e\urcorner,s)=e(s).
\]
\subsection{Lawvere Fixed-Point Theorem}
In any CCC with object \(A\) and endomorphism \(f:A\!\to\!A\), if
a \emph{diagonal} \(\Delta:A\!\to\!A^A\) exists, there is a fixed point \(a^\ast\)
with \(f(a^\ast)=a^\ast\).
This guarantees existence of a self-executing element for any admissible internal evaluator \(U\).
\subsection{Aczel Non-Well-Founded Sets}
Under AFA each graph \(G=(V,E)\) defines a unique set \(x_G\)
satisfying \(x_G=\{x_H:(G,H)\!\in\!E\}\).
This coinductive semantics enables construction of simultaneous self-models \(M_S\)
and underlies the proof of \(\PT\leftrightarrow\PSC\).
\subsection{Internal Truth Predicate}
Define \(\mathsf{T}\) as the equalizer of \(\mathrm{id}\) and evaluation on a fixed object \(S\)
with \(S\simeq\Hil\!\otimes\!S\).
Then \(\mathsf{T}(\ulcorner\phi\urcorner)\Leftrightarrow\phi\)
for all admissible \(\phi\)—the RR–Löb predicate.
\subsection{Proof of Theorem \texorpdfstring{\boldmath\(\PT\leftrightarrow\PSC\)}{PT iff PSC}}
\label{app:proof-PT-PSC}
We work in a well-pointed Cartesian closed topos \(\mathbf{E}\) with a natural numbers object (NNO), internal language \(L\), and an admissible fragment \(\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{adm}}\subseteq \mathbf{E}\) closed under finite limits, exponentials, and pullbacks. The internal quotation map \(\ulcorner\cdot\urcorner:L\to\mathrm{Code}\) and evaluator \(\mathrm{eval}:\mathrm{Code}\times\mathrm{Env}\to\mathrm{Env}\) satisfy the usual retraction for admissible codes (Section~\ref{asm:regularity}, Appendix~\ref{app:topos}). We assume Aczel's AFA for non-well-founded (coalgebraic) constructions, and the internal diagonal lemma (Lemma~\ref{lem:internal-diagonal}). 
\paragraph{Finite internal choice and order on codes.}
We require only \emph{finite} internal choice. Specifically, for any finite internal family \(\{x_i\}_{i\in I}\) and an internal total preorder \(\preccurlyeq\) on the underlying object, there exists an internal \(\min\)-selector 
\[
\operatorname{argmin}:\ \{x_i\}_{i\in I}\longrightarrow \{x_i\}_{i\in I}
\]
returning a \(\preccurlyeq\)-least element; ties are broken by a fixed total order \(\prec_{\mathrm{code}}\) on \(\mathrm{Code}\) applied to the quotations \(\{\ulcorner x_i\urcorner\}\).
\begin{lemma}[Coherence/MDL selection is an internal total preorder]
\label{lem:coherence-order}
Let \(D:\Man\to\RR_{\ge 0}\) be an internal dissonance functional and \(C:\Gamma_{\mathrm{adm}}\to\RR_{\ge 0}\) an internal MDL complexity penalty. Define for any admissible branch \(\gamma\)
\[
\mathfrak{L}(\gamma) \;\equiv\; \limsup_{t\downarrow 0}\,\Big( D(\gamma(t)) + \lambda\,C(\gamma)\Big) \in \RR_{\ge 0}.
\]
Then \(\preccurlyeq\) given by \(\gamma\preccurlyeq\gamma'\) iff \(\mathfrak{L}(\gamma)\le \mathfrak{L}(\gamma')\) is an internal total preorder on any finite branch set \(\mathcal{B}=\{\gamma_i\}_{i\in I}\). With code-order tie breaking on \(\{\ulcorner\gamma_i\urcorner\}\), \(\operatorname{argmin}\) is internally well-defined.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Linearity and order completeness of \(\RR\) in \(\mathbf{E}\) and the finiteness of \(\mathcal{B}\) ensure total comparability of the reals \(\{\mathfrak{L}(\gamma_i)\}\) and existence of a minimum; the tie-breaker \(\prec_{\mathrm{code}}\) defines a total extension to strict order. The definition is internal since \(D,C\) and \(t\mapsto \gamma(t)\) are internal maps and \(\limsup\) can be formulated in the internal \(\epsilon\)–\(\delta\) language of \(\RR\). 
\end{proof}
\paragraph{Naturality of argmin.}
The internal \(\operatorname{argmin}\) selector is stable under isomorphisms of finite decidable objects and monotone reparametrizations of the cost functional \(\mathfrak{L}\). Formally, for any isomorphism \(\psi:\mathcal{B}\overset{\sim}{\to}\mathcal{B}'\) and monotone increasing map \(f:\RR_{\ge 0}\to\RR_{\ge 0}\), we have \(\operatorname{argmin}_{\mathcal{B'}}(f\circ \mathfrak{L}\circ\psi^{-1}) = \psi(\operatorname{argmin}_{\mathcal{B}}\mathfrak{L})\). This makes the argmin construction a natural transformation in the appropriate sense, ensuring that the \(\PT\) operator is invariant under internal reparametrizations of the state space.
\paragraph{Admissible Choice Points.}
An \emph{admissible Choice Point} is a pair \(\mathcal{C}=(\theta^\star,\mathcal{B})\) where \(\theta^\star\in\Man\) is a degenerate critical point of \(D\) and \(\mathcal{B}=\{\gamma_i\}_{i\in I}\) is a finite internal family of admissible outgoing branches with the tie condition \(D(\gamma_i(t))=D(\gamma_j(t))+o(t)\). By Lemma~\ref{lem:coherence-order}, \(\operatorname{argmin}_{\mathcal{B}}\) is defined internally.
\subsubsection*{(i) \(\PSC \Rightarrow \PT\)}
Assume \(\mathfrak{R}\) is strongly \(\PSC\) (Definition~\ref{def:PSC}). Fix \(S\in\mathrm{Env}\) and let \(M_S\) be its self-model with isomorphism \(\phi:M_S\overset{\sim}{\to}\iota(S)\). Consider any admissible CP \(\mathcal{C}=(\theta^\star,\mathcal{B})\) reachable from \(S\).
By \(\PSC\):
\textbf{1. Internal representability.} The quadruple \((S,\theta^\star,\mathcal{B},D,C)\) is represented in \(M_S\): there exist internal names for \(\theta^\star\) and the finite set \(\mathcal{B}=\{\gamma_i\}\) together with the data of \(D,C\).
\textbf{2. Lawfulness and simultaneity.} Since \(M_S\) is an isomorphic copy of \(\iota(S)\) \emph{inside} \(\mathbf{E}\), it must include an internal law code \(c_T=\ulcorner T\urcorner\) for the admissible evolution and an internal evaluator \(\mathrm{eval}\). Let \(\preccurlyeq\) be the total preorder of Lemma~\ref{lem:coherence-order}. Using finite internal choice and the code tie-breaker, define the selector
\[
\mathcal{A}:\ \mathcal{C}=(\theta^\star,\mathcal{B}) \mapsto \operatorname{argmin}_{\,\mathcal{B}}\Big(\mathfrak{L}(\cdot)\Big)\;\in\mathcal{B},
\]
\emph{inside} \(M_S\). By construction, \(\mathcal{A}\) is total on admissible finite branch sets and monotone with respect to \(\preccurlyeq\); it is \emph{lawful} since it minimizes the MDL-coherence objective.
\textbf{3. Definition of \(\PT\).} Define \(\PT \equiv \mathcal{A}\) as the internal adjudication map from admissible CPs to admissible branches. As the argmin is total and uses only finite internal choice (plus code order), \(\PT\) is a total internal morphism \(\PT:\mathcal{C}\!P_{\mathrm{adm}}\to \Gamma_{\mathrm{adm}}\); it is \emph{not} required to lie in \(\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{adm}}\) (indeed, the MDL/Kolmogorov reduction, Section~\ref{subsec:noemulation}, shows exact \(\PT\) is not Turing-computable).
Thus, under \(\PSC\), a lawful internal adjudicator \(\PT\) exists and is uniquely determined by the coherence/MDL functional (up to code tie-breaking). \(\qed\)
\subsubsection*{(ii) \(\PT \Rightarrow \PSC\)}
Assume there exists a lawful internal adjudicator \(\PT:\mathcal{C}\!P_{\mathrm{adm}}\to \Gamma_{\mathrm{adm}}\) (not assumed in \(\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{adm}}\)) and an admissible evaluator \(U\) (the UWCA universal evaluator). We construct a non-well-founded self-model \(M_S\) of \(S\) satisfying the four \(\PSC\) clauses.
Define the \emph{guarded corecursion} operator
\[
\mathcal{F}:\ \mathrm{Env} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Env},\qquad
\mathcal{F}(X)\;=\;\Big(S,\;\; \mathrm{eval}(c_T,X),\;\; \PT\big(\mathrm{CP}(X)\big)\Big),
\]
where \(c_T=\ulcorner T\urcorner\) is the internal code for the admissible law and \(\mathrm{CP}(X)\) enumerates the (finite) admissible Choice Points extractable from the \(X\)-unfolding. AFA ensures existence of a greatest fixed point (final coalgebra) for such guarded corecursions; let \(M_S\) be any fixed point with \(\mathcal{F}(M_S)=M_S\).
We verify the \(\PSC\) clauses:
\textbf{1. Completeness.} By construction, \(M_S\) contains \(S\), its evaluator, and for every CP encountered along its predictive unrolling the chosen branch \(\PT(\mathrm{CP}(M_S))\). Thus \(M_S\) encodes all of \(S\)'s information state and its lawful successors; no external descriptors are needed.
\textbf{2. Consistency.} The definition uses only internal maps and finite choice; the corecursion is guarded (the "next" stage is under \(\mathrm{eval}(c_T,\cdot)\) and \(\PT\)), so by AFA there is a unique final coalgebra object \(M_S\) up to isomorphism. No regress arises: every CP is resolved by \(\PT\).
\textbf{3. Non-lossiness (isomorphism).} Define \(\phi:M_S\to \iota(S)\) as the coinductively defined isomorphism that forgets the bookkeeping of choices and evaluator calls; since \(\mathcal{F}(M_S)=M_S\) mirrors \(S\)'s evolution under \(T\) with the same branch selections, \(\phi\) is an isomorphism in \(\mathbf{E}\).
\textbf{4. Simultaneity/internality.} \(M_S\) is an \emph{internal} fixed point in \(\mathbf{E}\) and is co-present with \(S\); it is not a mere historical record but a live, self-contained model whose unfolding is guarded by the same law and adjudicator that govern \(S\).
Therefore \((S,M_S,\phi)\) witnesses \(\PSC\) in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:PSC}. \(\qed\)
\paragraph{Lawfulness and uniqueness.}
If two adjudicators \(\PT_1,\PT_2\) agree on the coherence/MDL preorder and both use the same code tie-breaking order, they coincide on all finite branch sets, hence are equal as morphisms \(\PT_1=\PT_2\) in \(\mathbf{E}\). This yields Corollary~\ref{cor:uniquenessPT}.
\paragraph{Remark on computability.}
The adjudicator \(\PT\) need not belong to \(\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{adm}}\) (the computable fragment). In fact, Section~\ref{subsec:noemulation} shows that any exact emulator for \(\PT\) would decide Kolmogorov complexity comparison and is therefore uncomputable. This is consistent with \(\PSC\): the reflexive system \emph{contains} a (possibly transcomputational) adjudication principle, even when its admissible evaluator \(U\) is Turing-universal but not omniscient.
\paragraph{PSC as a reflective subcategory.}
When the \(\PSC\) condition is assumed (rather than derived), the collection of perfectly self-contained objects forms a reflective subcategory of \(\mathbf{E}\), with the reflector given by the corecursive self-model construction \(S\mapsto M_S\). The finality of the coalgebra (guaranteed by AFA) transfers under this reflector, ensuring that the fixed-point properties (Lawvere, diagonal lemma) remain valid in the \(\PSC\)-subcategory. This categorical structure guarantees that all results derived in \(\mathbf{E}\) for \(\PSC\)-objects remain internally consistent and closed under the reflexive operations.
\section{Proof Sketches and Technical Lemmas}
\label{sec:proof-sketches}
\subsection{Reflexive Landauer Monotonic Bound}
\label{app:monotonic-bound}
\begin{theorem}[Reflexive Landauer Monotonic Bound]
For any PT--adjudication cycle on a reflexive system with initial state $U$ and final state $U'$, the total irreversible work satisfies
\[
W_{\mathrm{irr}} \;\ge\; k_B T \ln 2 \cdot \Delta H(U \to U'),
\]
where $\Delta H(U \to U') = H(U') - H(U)$ is the change in Shannon entropy of the state macrostate.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Sketch]
The proof proceeds in three steps:
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 1: Decomposition.}
Write the total work as
\[
W_{\mathrm{tot}} = W_{\mathrm{rev}} + W_{\mathrm{irr}},
\]
where $W_{\mathrm{rev}}$ is the reversible (quasistatic) contribution and $W_{\mathrm{irr}}$ accounts for dissipation.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 2: Entropy production.}
By the second law applied to the information reservoir (the reflexive substrate managing complexity),
\[
\Delta S_{\mathrm{res}} + \Delta S_{\mathrm{sys}} \ge 0.
\]
The reservoir entropy change is $\Delta S_{\mathrm{res}} = W_{\mathrm{irr}} / T$, and the system entropy change is $\Delta S_{\mathrm{sys}} = k_B \Delta H$ (in natural units).
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 3: Landauer bound.}
Combining, we have
\[
\frac{W_{\mathrm{irr}}}{T} + k_B \Delta H \ge 0
\quad \Rightarrow \quad
W_{\mathrm{irr}} \ge k_B T \cdot (- \Delta H).
\]
For PT adjudication that erases complexity (reduces entropy), $\Delta H < 0$, hence
\[
W_{\mathrm{irr}} \ge k_B T \ln 2 \cdot |\Delta H|.
\]
For arbitrary state transitions, the bound holds with the signed $\Delta H$.
\end{proof}
\subsection{Gauge Emergence from MDL Redundancy}
\label{app:gauge-emergence}
\begin{theorem}[Gauge Structure from MDL]
Let $\mathcal{U}$ be a reflexive system admitting a family of equivalent descriptions $\{\psi_\alpha\}_{\alpha \in \mathcal{A}}$ related by transformations $g_{\alpha\beta}: \psi_\alpha \mapsto \psi_\beta$ that preserve the MDL norm. Then the set $\{g_{\alpha\beta}\}$ forms a gauge group $G$, and the coupling of the coherence field $\Psi$ to this redundancy induces a connection $A_\mu$ with curvature $F_{\mu\nu}$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Sketch]
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 1: Redundancy as fiber.}
For each base-space point $x \in \mathcal{M}$, the set of equivalent descriptions forms a fiber $F_x \cong G / H$ (a homogeneous space). The total space is a principal bundle $P \to \mathcal{M}$ with structure group $G$.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 2: MDL--invariance.}
The PT operator must select a representative from each fiber. By MDL optimality, this selection must be independent of the fiber coordinate, hence $\PT(\psi_\alpha) = \PT(\psi_\beta)$ whenever $\psi_\alpha \sim_{\mathrm{MDL}} \psi_\beta$.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 3: Connection from coherence gradient.}
To maintain coherence across neighboring base points, define
\[
A_\mu \;=\; \Psi^{-1} \partial_\mu \Psi \cdot g^{-1} \partial_\mu g,
\]
where $g(x)$ is the local gauge transformation. The curvature is
\[
F_{\mu\nu} = \partial_\mu A_\nu - \partial_\nu A_\mu + [A_\mu, A_\nu].
\]
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 4: Coupling constants.}
The coherence economics (MDL minimization) fixes the coupling strength $e^2 \propto \alpha_0 / \langle \Psi \rangle$, where $\alpha_0$ is the energetic complexity coefficient. This reproduces the standard gauge coupling structure.
\end{proof}
\subsection{Quantization of the Information Stress Tensor}
\label{app:quantization-C}
\begin{theorem}[First-Order Quantization of $C_{\mu\nu}$]
The information stress tensor $C_{\mu\nu}$ admits a canonical quantization via the operator
\[
\hat{C}_{\mu\nu} = \frac{1}{2} \Big( \partial_\mu \hat{\Psi} \partial_\nu \hat{\Psi} + \partial_\nu \hat{\Psi} \partial_\mu \hat{\Psi} \Big) - g_{\mu\nu} \mathcal{L}_{\hat{\Psi}},
\]
where $\hat{\Psi}$ is the coherence field operator and $\mathcal{L}_{\hat{\Psi}}$ is the quantum Lagrangian density.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Sketch]
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 1: Canonical quantization.}
Promote $\Psi(x)$ to an operator $\hat{\Psi}(x)$ with canonical commutation relations
\[
[\hat{\Psi}(x), \hat{\Pi}(y)] = i \hbar \delta^{(d)}(x - y),
\]
where $\hat{\Pi} = \partial \mathcal{L} / \partial (\partial_0 \Psi)$ is the conjugate momentum.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 2: Normal ordering.}
The stress tensor $C_{\mu\nu}$ is quadratic in $\Psi$, hence its quantization requires normal ordering:
\[
\hat{C}_{\mu\nu} = :\partial_\mu \hat{\Psi} \partial_\nu \hat{\Psi} - g_{\mu\nu} \mathcal{L}_{\hat{\Psi}}:,
\]
where $:\cdots:$ denotes normal ordering (creation operators to the left).
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 3: Hadamard renormalization.}
To regularize UV divergences, subtract the Hadamard parametrix:
\[
\langle \hat{C}_{\mu\nu} \rangle_{\mathrm{ren}} = \langle \hat{C}_{\mu\nu} \rangle - \langle \hat{C}_{\mu\nu} \rangle_{\mathrm{Had}},
\]
where the Hadamard state encodes the short-distance singularities. This yields a finite, conserved stress tensor.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 4: Conservation.}
The conservation $\nabla^\mu \hat{C}_{\mu\nu} = 0$ follows from the quantum Noether theorem applied to diffeomorphism invariance of the action $S[\Psi, g]$.
\end{proof}
\subsection{Reflexive Penrose Inequality (Perturbative)}
\label{app:penrose-reflexive}
\begin{theorem}[Reflexive Penrose Inequality]
For an asymptotically flat spacetime with ADM mass $M$, outermost minimal surface of area $A_H$, and coherence energy $\mathcal{E}_\Psi$, the mass satisfies
\[
M \ge \sqrt{\frac{A_H}{16 \pi G}} + \eta \mathcal{E}_\Psi,
\]
where $\eta > 0$ is a dimensionless coefficient depending on the coherence layer thickness.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Sketch (Perturbative)]
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 1: Thin-shell approximation.}
Model the coherence layer as a thin shell at radius $r_H + \delta$, where $\delta \ll r_H$. The shell stress tensor is
\[
S_{ab} = \sigma \gamma_{ab} + p (\gamma_{ab} - n_a n_b),
\]
where $\sigma$ is the surface energy density, $p$ is the tangential pressure, and $\gamma_{ab}$ is the induced metric.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 2: Israel junction conditions.}
Matching the interior (Schwarzschild) and exterior (asymptotically flat) metrics across the shell yields
\[
\sigma = \frac{1}{8 \pi G} [K],
\]
where $[K]$ is the jump in extrinsic curvature. The coherence contribution is $\sigma_\Psi \propto \Psi^2 |_{r = r_H + \delta}$.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 3: Mass decomposition.}
The ADM mass decomposes as
\[
M = M_{\mathrm{BH}} + M_\Psi,
\quad
M_\Psi = 4 \pi \int_{r_H}^{r_H + \delta} r^2 \rho_\Psi \, dr,
\]
where $\rho_\Psi = T_{00}^{(\Psi)}$ is the coherence energy density.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 4: Penrose bound.}
For the black hole component, the classical Penrose inequality gives
\[
M_{\mathrm{BH}} \ge \sqrt{\frac{A_H}{16 \pi G}}.
\]
Adding the positive coherence mass $M_\Psi = \eta \mathcal{E}_\Psi$ yields the result.
\end{proof}
\subsection{Reflexive QNEC / GSL Bridge}
\label{app:reflexive-qnec}
\begin{theorem}[Reflexive Quantum Null Energy Condition]
For a null hypersurface $\Sigma$ with affine parameter $\lambda$ and entanglement entropy $S_{\mathrm{EE}}$ of a region bounded by $\Sigma$, the reflexive stress tensor satisfies
\[
\langle T_{\mu\nu}^{(\Psi)} + C_{\mu\nu} \rangle k^\mu k^\nu \ge \frac{\hbar}{2 \pi A} \frac{d^2 S_{\mathrm{EE}}}{d\lambda^2},
\]
where $A$ is the cross-sectional area of $\Sigma$ and $k^\mu$ is the null tangent.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Sketch]
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 1: Holographic entanglement entropy.}
By the Ryu--Takayanagi formula (generalized to dynamical spacetimes via Hubeny--Rangamani--Takayanagi),
\[
S_{\mathrm{EE}} = \frac{A_{\mathrm{ext}}}{4 G \hbar} + S_{\mathrm{bulk}},
\]
where $A_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is the area of the extremal surface and $S_{\mathrm{bulk}}$ is the bulk entropy.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 2: Raychaudhuri equation.}
The focusing of the null congruence is governed by
\[
\frac{d\theta}{d\lambda} = -\frac{1}{2} \theta^2 - \sigma_{ab} \sigma^{ab} - R_{\mu\nu} k^\mu k^\nu,
\]
where $\theta$ is the expansion, $\sigma_{ab}$ is the shear, and $R_{\mu\nu}$ is the Ricci tensor.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 3: Einstein equations with $C_{\mu\nu}$.}
Using the modified Einstein equations $R_{\mu\nu} - \frac{1}{2} g_{\mu\nu} R = 8 \pi G (T_{\mu\nu} + C_{\mu\nu})$, the focusing term becomes
\[
R_{\mu\nu} k^\mu k^\nu = 8 \pi G (T_{\mu\nu} + C_{\mu\nu}) k^\mu k^\nu.
\]
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 4: Entropy variation.}
Combining the Raychaudhuri equation with the holographic formula, the second derivative of $S_{\mathrm{EE}}$ is
\[
\frac{d^2 S_{\mathrm{EE}}}{d\lambda^2} \propto -R_{\mu\nu} k^\mu k^\nu \cdot A.
\]
Inverting yields the QNEC bound.
\end{proof}
\subsection{Reflexive Focusing--Defocusing Integral Criterion}
\label{app:defocusing}
\begin{theorem}[Defocusing Criterion]
For a timelike congruence with expansion $\theta$ and shear $\sigma_{ab}$, if the reflexive contribution satisfies
\[
\int_{\lambda_0}^\infty 8 \pi G C_{\mu\nu} u^\mu u^\nu \, d\lambda \;>\; \int_{\lambda_0}^\infty \sigma_{ab} \sigma^{ab} \, d\lambda,
\]
then the congruence may defocus ($\theta > 0$ for all $\lambda > \lambda_0$), avoiding a caustic.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Sketch]
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 1: Raychaudhuri equation.}
For a timelike congruence with four-velocity $u^\mu$,
\[
\frac{d\theta}{d\tau} = -\frac{1}{3} \theta^2 - \sigma_{ab} \sigma^{ab} + \omega_{ab} \omega^{ab} - R_{\mu\nu} u^\mu u^\nu,
\]
where $\tau$ is proper time, $\omega_{ab}$ is the vorticity, and $R_{\mu\nu}$ is the Ricci tensor.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 2: Reflexive contribution.}
Using the modified Einstein equations,
\[
R_{\mu\nu} u^\mu u^\nu = 8 \pi G (T_{\mu\nu} + C_{\mu\nu}) u^\mu u^\nu.
\]
Assuming $\omega_{ab} = 0$ (irrotational flow) and $T_{\mu\nu} u^\mu u^\nu \ge 0$ (ordinary matter satisfies WEC),
\[
\frac{d\theta}{d\tau} = -\frac{1}{3} \theta^2 - \sigma_{ab} \sigma^{ab} - 8 \pi G T_{\mu\nu} u^\mu u^\nu - 8 \pi G C_{\mu\nu} u^\mu u^\nu.
\]
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 3: Defocusing condition.}
For defocusing ($d\theta / d\tau > 0$), we need
\[
8 \pi G C_{\mu\nu} u^\mu u^\nu > \frac{1}{3} \theta^2 + \sigma_{ab} \sigma^{ab} + 8 \pi G T_{\mu\nu} u^\mu u^\nu.
\]
In the limit of small expansion ($\theta \to 0$) and dominant coherence ($C_{\mu\nu} \gg T_{\mu\nu}$), this reduces to the shear-dominated criterion:
\[
8 \pi G C_{\mu\nu} u^\mu u^\nu > \sigma_{ab} \sigma^{ab}.
\]
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 4: Integral bound.}
Integrating both sides over the affine parameter $\lambda$ (related to $\tau$ by $d\lambda = a(\tau) d\tau$ for some lapse function $a$), the defocusing condition becomes the integral inequality stated.
\end{proof}
\subsection{Reflexive H-Theorem and KMS Steady State}
\label{app:h-theorem-proof}
\begin{theorem}[Reflexive H-Theorem]
For a reflexive ensemble with master equation
\[
\frac{d\rho}{dt} = \mathcal{L}[\rho],
\]
where $\mathcal{L}$ is the Lindblad generator, the reflexive entropy
\[
S_{\mathrm{ref}}(t) = -\mathrm{Tr}(\rho(t) \ln \rho(t)) + \beta \langle H_{\mathrm{eff}}[\Psi] \rangle
\]
is monotonically non-decreasing, and stationary states satisfy the KMS condition
\[
\rho_{\mathrm{ss}} = \frac{1}{Z} e^{-\beta H_{\mathrm{eff}}[\Psi]}.
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Sketch]
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 1: Spohn's inequality.}
For a Lindblad generator in GKSL form,
\[
\mathcal{L}[\rho] = -i [H, \rho] + \sum_k \left( L_k \rho L_k^\dagger - \frac{1}{2} \{L_k^\dagger L_k, \rho\} \right),
\]
the von Neumann entropy satisfies
\[
\frac{dS_{\mathrm{vN}}}{dt} = -\mathrm{Tr}\big( [\ln \rho, H] \rho \big) + \sum_k \mathrm{Tr}\big( L_k \rho L_k^\dagger \ln \rho \big) \ge 0,
\]
with equality if and only if $[\rho, H] = 0$ and all Lindblad jumps are detailed-balanced.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 2: Reflexive correction.}
The reflexive entropy includes the coherence energy term $\beta \langle H_{\mathrm{eff}}[\Psi] \rangle$. Its time derivative is
\[
\frac{d}{dt} \big( \beta \langle H_{\mathrm{eff}} \rangle \big) = \beta \mathrm{Tr}\big( H_{\mathrm{eff}} \mathcal{L}[\rho] \big).
\]
Using the cyclic property of the trace and the GKSL form,
\[
\mathrm{Tr}\big( H_{\mathrm{eff}} \mathcal{L}[\rho] \big) = \sum_k \mathrm{Tr}\big( H_{\mathrm{eff}} L_k \rho L_k^\dagger \big) - \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{Tr}\big( H_{\mathrm{eff}} \{L_k^\dagger L_k, \rho\} \big).
\]
For detailed balance, this vanishes at steady state.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 3: KMS condition.}
At steady state, $\mathcal{L}[\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}] = 0$. Combined with detailed balance,
\[
L_k \rho_{\mathrm{ss}} L_k^\dagger = \rho_{\mathrm{ss}} L_k^\dagger L_k,
\]
which is satisfied by the Gibbs state $\rho_{\mathrm{ss}} = e^{-\beta H_{\mathrm{eff}}} / Z$. This is precisely the KMS condition for quantum statistical mechanics.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 4: Monotonicity.}
Combining Spohn's inequality with the reflexive correction term,
\[
\frac{dS_{\mathrm{ref}}}{dt} = \frac{dS_{\mathrm{vN}}}{dt} + \beta \frac{d\langle H_{\mathrm{eff}} \rangle}{dt} \ge 0,
\]
with equality at steady state.
\end{proof}
\subsection{SRRG c-Function Monotonicity}
\label{app:srrg-c-function}
\begin{theorem}[SRRG c-Function]
Define the reflexive c-function
\[
c(s) \;=\; \mathcal{F}[\bm{k}(s); \Omega(s), \Psi(s)] - s \cdot \frac{d\mathcal{F}}{ds},
\]
where $s = \ln \mu$ is the RG scale, $\mathcal{F}$ is the SRRG functional, and $\bm{k}(s)$ is the trajectory in coupling space. Then $c(s)$ is monotonically decreasing along RG flow:
\[
\frac{dc}{ds} \le 0.
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Sketch]
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 1: RG flow equation.}
The SRRG flow is governed by
\[
\frac{d\bm{k}}{ds} = \bm{\beta}(\bm{k}) + \bm{J}_{\mathrm{PT}}(\bm{k}; \Omega, \Psi),
\]
where $\bm{\beta}$ is the standard RG beta function and $\bm{J}_{\mathrm{PT}}$ is the transputation source.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 2: c-Function derivative.}
Taking the derivative,
\[
\frac{dc}{ds} = \frac{\partial \mathcal{F}}{\partial \bm{k}} \cdot \frac{d\bm{k}}{ds} + \frac{\partial \mathcal{F}}{\partial \Omega} \frac{d\Omega}{ds} + \frac{\partial \mathcal{F}}{\partial \Psi} \frac{d\Psi}{ds} - \frac{d\mathcal{F}}{ds} - s \frac{d^2\mathcal{F}}{ds^2}.
\]
Simplifying using the chain rule and the definition of the c-function,
\[
\frac{dc}{ds} = -\Big\| \frac{d\bm{k}}{ds} \Big\|^2_{\mathcal{G}} - \rho_{\mathrm{PT}} \cdot \mathcal{E}_\Psi,
\]
where $\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal{G}}$ is the norm in the space of couplings (e.g., the Zamolodchikov metric for 2D CFTs) and $\rho_{\mathrm{PT}}$ is the PT density.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 3: Monotonicity.}
Since $\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal{G}}^2 \ge 0$ and $\rho_{\mathrm{PT}} \cdot \mathcal{E}_\Psi \ge 0$ (both adjudication rate and coherence energy are non-negative), we have
\[
\frac{dc}{ds} \le 0.
\]
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 4: Fixed points.}
At a fixed point, $d\bm{k} / ds = 0$ and $d\Omega / ds = d\Psi / ds = 0$, hence $dc / ds = 0$. The c-function value at a fixed point is an RG invariant, analogous to the central charge in 2D CFTs.
\end{proof}
\subsection{Reflexive Quantum Speed Limit}
\label{app:reflexive-qsl}
\begin{theorem}[Reflexive QSL]
For an observer with complexity $\Omega_{\mathrm{obs}}$ measuring a quantum system undergoing a PT--adjudication, the minimum resolution time satisfies
\[
\tau_{\mathrm{min}} \;\ge\; \frac{\hbar \cdot \Delta \theta}{\Delta E} \cdot \kappa(\Omega_{\mathrm{obs}}),
\]
where $\Delta \theta$ is the parameter-space distance traversed, $\Delta E$ is the energy uncertainty, and $\kappa(\Omega_{\mathrm{obs}}) = 1 + \alpha \Omega_{\mathrm{obs}}^{-\gamma}$ with $\gamma \approx 1/2$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Sketch]
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 1: Mandelstam--Tamm bound.}
The standard quantum speed limit is
\[
\tau \ge \frac{\hbar \Delta \theta}{\Delta E},
\]
where $\Delta \theta$ is the distinguishability (Fubini--Study distance) and $\Delta E$ is the energy spread.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 2: Reflexive correction.}
The observer's measurement apparatus has intrinsic complexity $\Omega_{\mathrm{obs}}$, which introduces additional coherence constraints. The effective energy uncertainty is
\[
\Delta E_{\mathrm{eff}} = \Delta E \cdot \frac{1}{\kappa(\Omega_{\mathrm{obs}})},
\]
where $\kappa > 1$ accounts for the observer's internal adjudication overhead.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 3: Scaling with complexity.}
For an observer with $N$ internal states (bits), $\Omega_{\mathrm{obs}} \sim N$. The adjudication overhead scales as
\[
\kappa(N) \approx 1 + \frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{N}},
\]
where $\alpha$ is a constant set by the coherence layer thickness. This follows from the central limit theorem applied to the observer's internal CP ensemble.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 4: Refined QSL.}
Substituting the effective energy uncertainty into the Mandelstam--Tamm bound yields
\[
\tau_{\mathrm{min}} \ge \frac{\hbar \Delta \theta}{\Delta E} \cdot \kappa(\Omega_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\]
For macroscopic observers ($\Omega_{\mathrm{obs}} \gg 1$), $\kappa \approx 1$ and the standard QSL is recovered. For observers with complexity comparable to the system, the reflexive correction becomes significant.
\end{proof}
\subsection{IPT--Anomaly Index and Spectral Flow}
\label{app:ipt-spectral}
\begin{theorem}[IPT--Anomaly Index Theorem]
The topological PT index $I_{\mathrm{PT}}$ equals the spectral flow of the GKSL generator:
\[
I_{\mathrm{PT}}[M] = \mathrm{SF}(\mathcal{L}_t) \bmod \chi(M),
\]
where $\chi(M)$ is the Euler characteristic of the base manifold.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Sketch]
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 1: Index definition.}
For a CP ensemble on manifold $M$, define the PT index as
\[
I_{\mathrm{PT}} = \sum_{\text{CPs}} \mathrm{sign}(\det \mathrm{Hess}\, D),
\]
where the sum is over all critical points of the dissonance functional $D$.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 2: Spectral flow.}
The spectral flow counts the net number of eigenvalues of $\mathcal{L}_t$ crossing zero as $t$ varies:
\[
\mathrm{SF}(\mathcal{L}_t) = \#\{\lambda_k(t) : \lambda_k(0) < 0,\, \lambda_k(1) > 0\} - \#\{\lambda_k(t) : \lambda_k(0) > 0,\, \lambda_k(1) < 0\}.
\]
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 3: Atiyah–Singer index.}
By the Atiyah–Singer index theorem, the analytical index (spectral flow) equals the topological index (winding number of the symbol) modulo the Euler characteristic:
\[
\mathrm{SF}(\mathcal{L}_t) = I_{\text{top}}(\mathcal{L}) + n \chi(M),
\]
for some integer $n$.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 4: PT--GKSL correspondence.}
Each CP adjudication opens a new GKSL channel (new Lindblad operator), hence $I_{\mathrm{PT}} = \mathrm{SF}(\mathcal{L}_t)$ modulo the topological obstruction $\chi(M)$.
\end{proof}
\subsection{Legendre Duality for \texorpdfstring{$(D)$--$(\Phi)$}{D--Phi}}
\label{app:legendre-duality}
\begin{theorem}[Legendre Duality]
The dissonance functional $D[\rho]$ and the integration measure $\Phi[\rho]$ are Legendre conjugates:
\[
D^*(\lambda) = \sup_\rho \{\lambda \Phi[\rho] - D[\rho]\},
\quad
\Phi^*(\mu) = \sup_\rho \{\mu D[\rho] - \Phi[\rho]\}.
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Sketch]
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 1: Convexity.}
By definition, $D[\rho]$ is the MDL code length (convex in $\rho$), and $\Phi[\rho]$ is the integrated information (concave in $\rho$). The Legendre transform applies to convex functionals.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 2: Conjugate construction.}
For each $\lambda$, the Legendre conjugate is
\[
D^*(\lambda) = \sup_\rho \{\lambda \Phi[\rho] - D[\rho]\}.
\]
The supremum is achieved at $\rho^*(\lambda)$ satisfying the stationarity condition
\[
\frac{\partial D}{\partial \rho}\bigg|_{\rho^*} = \lambda \frac{\partial \Phi}{\partial \rho}\bigg|_{\rho^*}.
\]
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 3: Inverse variation.}
By the envelope theorem,
\[
\frac{dD^*}{d\lambda} = \Phi[\rho^*(\lambda)],
\quad
\frac{d\Phi^*}{d\mu} = D[\rho^*(\mu)].
\]
Taking derivatives yields the inverse variation inequality
\[
\frac{dD}{dt} \le -\lambda \Xi'(\Phi) \frac{d\Phi}{dt},
\]
where $\Xi'(\Phi) = \partial D^* / \partial \Phi$ is the conjugate slope.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 4: Duality properties.}
The double Legendre transform recovers the original functional: $(D^*)^* = D$. This confirms exact duality.
\end{proof}
\subsection{Reflexive Data-Processing Inequality}
\label{app:reflexive-dpi}
\begin{theorem}[Reflexive Data-Processing Inequality]
For any CPTP map $\mathcal{E}$ and reflexive entropy $S_{\mathrm{ref}}$,
\[
S_{\mathrm{ref}}(\mathcal{E}\rho) \ge S_{\mathrm{ref}}(\rho) - k_B T I_{\mathrm{lost}}(\mathcal{E},\rho) / \alpha_0,
\]
where $I_{\mathrm{lost}}$ is the information lost under $\mathcal{E}$ and $\alpha_0$ is the energetic complexity coefficient.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Sketch]
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 1: Standard DPI.}
For the von Neumann entropy, the data-processing inequality states
\[
S(\mathcal{E}\rho) \ge S(\rho).
\]
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 2: Holographic correction.}
The reflexive entropy includes a holographic information term:
\[
S_{\mathrm{ref}}(\rho) = S(\rho) \big(1 + C I_{\mathrm{holo}}(\rho)^p\big),
\]
where $I_{\mathrm{holo}}$ is the holographic information density.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 3: Information loss.}
Under $\mathcal{E}$, the holographic term may decrease:
\[
I_{\mathrm{holo}}(\mathcal{E}\rho) \le I_{\mathrm{holo}}(\rho) - I_{\mathrm{lost}}(\mathcal{E},\rho).
\]
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 4: Bound.}
Combining, the reflexive entropy satisfies
\[
S_{\mathrm{ref}}(\mathcal{E}\rho) \ge S_{\mathrm{ref}}(\rho) - k_B T I_{\mathrm{lost}} / \alpha_0,
\]
where the conversion factor $k_B T / \alpha_0$ calibrates code-length to entropy via the Reflexive Landauer bound.
\end{proof}
\subsection{Reflexive Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation}
\label{app:reflexive-tur}
\begin{theorem}[Reflexive TUR]
For a reflexive current $J_T$ over time $T$ with reflexive entropy production $\Sigma_{\mathrm{ref}}$,
\[
\frac{\mathrm{Var}[J_T]}{\langle J_T \rangle^2} \ge \frac{2}{\Sigma_{\mathrm{ref}} \cdot T}.
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Sketch]
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 1: Standard TUR.}

The classical thermodynamic uncertainty relation (Barato–Seifert) states
\[
\frac{\mathrm{Var}[J_T]}{\langle J_T \rangle^2} \ge \frac{2}{\Sigma \cdot T},
\]
where $\Sigma$ is the standard entropy production.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 2: Reflexive entropy production.}
The reflexive entropy production includes both thermodynamic and geometric contributions:
\[
\Sigma_{\mathrm{ref}} = \Sigma_{\mathrm{th}} + \Sigma_{\mathrm{PT}},
\]
where $\Sigma_{\mathrm{PT}}$ accounts for PT adjudication events.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 3: Cramér–Rao bound.}
The Fisher information of the path measure satisfies
\[
\mathcal{I}[p_T] \ge \frac{\langle J_T \rangle^2}{\mathrm{Var}[J_T]}.
\]
By the Reflexive Fluctuation Theorem (Thm.~\ref{thm:RFT}),
\[
\mathcal{I}[p_T] \le \Sigma_{\mathrm{ref}} \cdot T.
\]
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Step 4: Combining bounds.}
Combining the Cramér–Rao bound with the reflexive fluctuation bound yields
\[
\frac{\langle J_T \rangle^2}{\mathrm{Var}[J_T]} \le \Sigma_{\mathrm{ref}} \cdot T
\quad \Rightarrow \quad
\frac{\mathrm{Var}[J_T]}{\langle J_T \rangle^2} \ge \frac{2}{\Sigma_{\mathrm{ref}} \cdot T}.
\]
\end{proof}
\subsection{Probabilistic Choice--Curvature Correspondence (Gaussian Field Setting)}
\label{app:prob-CC}
We provide a rigorous statement for the expected density of (near-)Choice Points under Gaussian perturbations of the dissonance functional \(D\) on \((\Man,\Fisher)\).
\paragraph{Setup.}
Let \((\Man,\Fisher)\) be a compact \(d\)-dimensional Fisher information manifold with injectivity radius bounded below and \(C^\infty\)-bounded curvature and derivatives (bounded geometry). Let \(D_0\in C^{3}(\Man)\) be a fixed baseline dissonance functional. Consider a Gaussian perturbation
\[
D_\varepsilon(\theta) \;=\; D_0(\theta) + \varepsilon\,\eta(\theta),
\qquad
\varepsilon>0,
\]
where \(\eta\) is a centered, almost-isotropic, mean-square \(C^3\) Gaussian random field on \((\Man,\Fisher)\) with covariance kernel
\(C(\theta,\theta')=\EE[\eta(\theta)\eta(\theta')]\)
satisfying standard nondegeneracy and regularity (cf.\ Adler \& Taylor \cite{AdlerTaylor2007}, Chs.~11–12). We call a point \(\theta^\star\) a \emph{\((\tau,\delta)\) near-CP of \(D_\varepsilon\)} if
\[
\|\nabla D_\varepsilon(\theta^\star)\|_{\Fisher} \le \tau
\quad\text{and}\quad
|\lambda_{\min}(\mathrm{Hess}\, D_\varepsilon(\theta^\star))| \le \delta,
\]
where \(\mathrm{Hess}\, D_\varepsilon\) is the Riemannian Hessian and \(\lambda_{\min}\) denotes its smallest eigenvalue. Let \(\rho_{\varepsilon;\tau,\delta}\) denote the random density of such near-CP points.
\begin{theorem}[Kac--Rice/Gaussian Kinematic Expansion]
\label{thm:KR-CC}
Under the assumptions above, for fixed \((\tau,\delta)\) and small \(\varepsilon\) the expectation of the near-CP density admits an expansion
\[
\EE\big[\rho_{\varepsilon;\tau,\delta}(\theta)\big]
\;=\;
a_0(\tau,\delta) 
\;+\;
a_1(\tau,\delta)\,R_F(\theta)
\;+\;
\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^2) 
\quad\text{in } C^0(\Man),
\]
where \(R_F\) is the scalar curvature of \(\Fisher\) and the coefficients \(a_0,a_1\) depend only on the local covariance structure of \(\eta\) up to finitely many jets at \(\theta\). In particular, integrating over a region \(V\subset \Man\),
\[
\EE\big[N_{\varepsilon;\tau,\delta}(V)\big]
 \;=\;
\int_V a_0(\tau,\delta)\,d\mu_F 
\;+\;
\int_V a_1(\tau,\delta)\,R_F\,d\mu_F
\;+\;\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^2).
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Sketch]
This is a direct application of the Kac–Rice formula for the joint distribution of \((\nabla D_\varepsilon, \mathrm{Hess}\, D_\varepsilon)\) in geodesic normal coordinates, combined with the Gaussian Kinematic Formula (GKF) to capture curvature corrections for random fields on manifolds. See Adler–Taylor \cite{AdlerTaylor2007} (Thm.~11.9.1 and Ch.~12) and Azaïs–Wschebor \cite{AzaisWschebor2009}. The first term \(a_0\) corresponds to the flat-space density; curvature enters at first order via \(R_F\). Bounded geometry ensures uniform control of the remainders as \(\varepsilon\to 0\).
\end{proof}
\begin{remark}[From near-CP to CP statistics]
As \(\tau,\delta\downarrow 0\), near-CPs concentrate on genuine CPs (degenerate critical points). The limit may involve subtle short-scale renormalization depending on the ensemble; in any case, the leading curvature dependence in Theorem~\ref{thm:KR-CC} persists and controls the expected density of adjudicative structures at small but finite \((\tau,\delta)\), which is the physically relevant regime under MDL "tie" constraints.
\end{remark}
\subsection{Deterministic Lower Bounds via Morse Theory and Chern--Gauss--Bonnet}
\label{app:det-CC}
We now give a deterministic lower bound on the number of CP/critical points in terms of topology and curvature, with a sharp specialization in even dimensions.
\paragraph{Morse background.}
Let \(D\in C^2(\Man)\) be Morse (all critical points nondegenerate). Let \(m(\lambda)\) be the number of critical points of \(D\) of index \(\lambda\in\{0,\dots,d\}\). The Morse inequalities imply
\[
\sum_{\lambda=0}^d (-1)^\lambda m(\lambda) \;=\; \chi(\Man),
\qquad
N_{\mathrm{crit}} \;\equiv\; \sum_{\lambda=0}^d m(\lambda) 
\;\ge\; \sum_{\lambda=0}^d b_\lambda(\Man) 
\;\ge\; |\chi(\Man)|,
\]
where \(b_\lambda\) are Betti numbers.
\begin{theorem}[Deterministic CP lower bound; curvature/topology]
\label{thm:det-CC}
Let \((\Man,\Fisher)\) be compact with bounded geometry. If \(D\) is Morse, then
\[
N_{\mathrm{crit}} \;\ge\; \sum_{\lambda=0}^d b_\lambda(\Man) \;\ge\; |\chi(\Man)|.
\]
If, in addition, \(d\) is even, then by Chern--Gauss--Bonnet
\[
\chi(\Man) \;=\; \frac{1}{(2\pi)^{d/2}} \int_{\Man} \mathrm{Pf}\big(R^F\big)\,d\mu_F,
\]
where \(\mathrm{Pf}(R^F)\) is the Pfaffian of the Fisher curvature \(2\)-form; hence
\[
N_{\mathrm{crit}} \;\ge\; \frac{1}{(2\pi)^{d/2}}\,\Big|\int_{\Man} \mathrm{Pf}(R^F)\,d\mu_F\Big|.
\]
In particular, for \(d=2\), \(\mathrm{Pf}(R^F)=\tfrac{1}{2} R_F\,d\mathrm{vol}_F\), and thus
\[
N_{\mathrm{crit}} \;\ge\; \frac{1}{2\pi}\,\Big|\int_{\Man} R_F\,d\mu_F\Big|.
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Sketch]
The first inequality is standard Morse theory. The Chern--Gauss--Bonnet theorem (see e.g.\ Besse \cite{Besse1987}, \emph{Einstein Manifolds}) gives the integral formula for \(\chi(\Man)\) in even dimensions; the two-dimensional specialization uses Gauss–Bonnet in the form \(\int K\,dA = 2\pi\chi\), with \(R_F=2K\). Combine with \(N_{\mathrm{crit}} \ge |\chi(\Man)|\).
\end{proof}
\begin{remark}[On bounds via \(\|Riem_F\|_{L^{d/2}}\)]
In even dimensions one also has \(\big|\chi(\Man)\big| \le C(d)\,\|Riem_F\|_{L^{d/2}}^{d/2}\) (see inequalities relating the Pfaffian to \(\|Riem_F\|_{L^{d/2}}\) and Cheeger–Gromov finiteness theorems). Thus, combining with Theorem~\ref{thm:det-CC} yields 
\[
N_{\mathrm{crit}} \;\ge\; \frac{1}{C(d)}\,\Big\|\mathrm{Riem}_F\Big\|_{L^{d/2}(\Man)}^{d/2},
\]
up to universal constants, providing a curvature-norm lower bound on the total number of critical points. In odd \(d\), \(\chi(\Man)=0\), and such topological curvature integrals vanish; one still retains \(N_{\mathrm{crit}}\ge \sum b_\lambda\) as a purely topological lower bound.
\end{remark}

\frac{d\theta}{d\tau}
=-\tfrac13\theta^2-\sigma^2+\omega^2-4\pi G\,\Cten_{\mu\nu}k^\mu k^\nu.
\]
With \(\Cten_{\mu\nu}k^\mu k^\nu>0\),
defocusing follows: \(d\theta/d\tau\!>\!-\tfrac13\theta^2-\sigma^2+\omega^2\).
\subsection{Proof of Theorem \texorpdfstring{\ref{thm:PTRG}}{PT–RG Source}}
\label{app:proof-PTRG}
We prove the existence and structure of the transputation-induced source term in the invariant flow. The argument has four steps: (i) the invariant/Q-L plane geometry; (ii) coarse-grained flow and a single PT perturbation; (iii) projection onto the QL normal; (iv) event averaging in RG time.
\paragraph{Invariant sector and QL plane.}
Let 
\[
\bm{k}
=
(k_{L2},\,k_{\mathrm{gen2}},\,k_M,\,k_a,\,k_b,\,k_c,\,k_{\mathrm{gen}},\,k_{\mathrm{const}})^{\mathsf{T}}
\in \mathbb{R}^N,
\]
be the vector of invariant/kernel coefficients in the fixed coordinate order shown. The Quarter–Lock (QL) identity reads 
\[
\phi(\bm{k}) \equiv k_M - k_{\mathrm{gen2}} - \tfrac{1}{4}\,k_{L2}=0.
\]
Its (constant) \textbf{normal vector} is
\[
n \equiv \nabla_{\bm{k}}\phi 
= \Big(-\tfrac{1}{4},\; -1,\; 1,\; 0,\ldots,0\Big)^{\mathsf{T}}.
\]
The QL plane is thus \(\{\,\bm{k}: n\!\cdot\!\bm{k}=0\,\}\). Define the orthogonal projector onto the normal direction
\[
P_\perp \;\equiv\; \frac{n\,n^{\mathsf{T}}}{\|n\|^2}, 
\qquad
\|n\|^2=\tfrac{1}{16}+1+1=\tfrac{33}{16}.
\]
\paragraph{Coarse-grained flow and single-event PT perturbation.}
Let \(s=\ln \mu\) be the RG time and suppose that in the absence of PT the invariant flow is smooth:
\[
\frac{d\bm{k}}{ds} \;=\; \bm{\beta}(\bm{k}),
\quad \bm{\beta}\in C^1(\mathbb{R}^N;\mathbb{R}^N).
\]
We now model a single, localized PT event as a small, instantaneous correction \(\delta \bm{k}\) superposed on the coarse-grained step. The lawfulness (coherence/MDL optimality) of PT implies that—at the invariant level—it penalizes QL deviations quadratically. Specifically, define the local PT penalty 
\[
\Phi(\bm{k}; \mathcal{E}_\Psi) \;\equiv\; 
\lambda(\mathcal{E}_\Psi)\,\phi(\bm{k})^2
\;=\;
\lambda(\mathcal{E}_\Psi)\,(n\!\cdot\!\bm{k})^2,
\]
where \(\lambda(\mathcal{E}_\Psi)>0\) is an increasing function of the \emph{coherence energy}
\[
\mathcal{E}_\Psi \;\equiv\; \int_{\mathcal{U}}\!\big(\alpha_1\,\Psi^2+\alpha_2\,\|\nabla\Psi\|^2\big)\,dV,
\]
computed over the space-time region \(\mathcal{U}\) of the event (Section~\ref{subsec:energetic}).
A single PT event induces a small restoring step (gradient descent in \(\Phi\)):
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:single-event-PTRG}
\delta \bm{k} 
\;=\; -\,\varepsilon \,\nabla_{\bm{k}} \Phi(\bm{k};\mathcal{E}_\Psi) + o(\varepsilon)
\;=\; -\,2\varepsilon\,\lambda(\mathcal{E}_\Psi)\,\big(n\!\cdot\!\bm{k}\big)\,n \;+\; o(\varepsilon),
\end{equation}
with \(\varepsilon>0\) a small book-keeping parameter (event "strength"). Note that \(\delta\bm{k}\) is \emph{purely normal} to the QL plane, i.e. orthogonal to all directions tangent to \(\phi=0\).
\paragraph{Projection and orthogonality.}
Since \(\delta\bm{k}\) is proportional to \(n\), we have 
\[
P_\perp\,\delta\bm{k} \;=\; \delta\bm{k},
\qquad
(1-P_\perp)\,\delta\bm{k} = 0,
\]
hence the PT perturbation has no tangential component in invariant space. This realizes the invariant-restoration principle geometrically: PT does not distort the directions that preserve QL, it only damps motion along the QL-violating normal.
\paragraph{Event averaging in RG time.}
Let events occur as an inhomogeneous Poisson process in RG time \(s\) with intensity \(\rho_{\mathrm{PT}}(s)\ge 0\) (mean number of events per unit \(s\)). Averaging over many coarse-grained steps yields the mean PT contribution per unit \(s\):
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:JPT-raw}
\bm{J}_{\mathrm{PT}}(\bm{k}; s)
\;\equiv\;
\lim_{\Delta s\downarrow 0}\frac{1}{\Delta s}\,\sum_{\text{events in }[s,s+\Delta s)} \delta\bm{k}
\;=\;
-\,2\,\rho_{\mathrm{PT}}(s)\,\lambda\big(\mathcal{E}_\Psi(s)\big)\,\big(n\!\cdot\!\bm{k}\big)\,n
\;+\;o(1),
\end{equation}
where the dependence \(\mathcal{E}_\Psi(s)\) indicates that the coherence energy is evaluated on the support of events coarse-grained at scale \(\mu=e^s\). By \eqref{eq:JPT-raw} we have \(\bm{J}_{\mathrm{PT}}(s) \parallel n\), hence 
\[
\bm{J}_{\mathrm{PT}} \cdot \tau \;=\; 0 \quad \text{for all tangent directions } \tau \text{ with } n\!\cdot\!\tau=0,
\]
i.e.\ \(\bm{J}_{\mathrm{PT}}\) is \emph{orthogonal} to the QL plane.
\paragraph{Conclusion.}
Combining the smooth \(\beta\)–flow with the mean PT effect gives
\[
\frac{d\bm{k}}{ds}
\;=\;
\bm{\beta}(\bm{k})
\;-\;2\,\rho_{\mathrm{PT}}(s)\,\lambda\big(\mathcal{E}_\Psi(s)\big)\,\big(n\!\cdot\!\bm{k}\big)\,n
\;+\; \text{higher orders}.
\]
Writing \(\displaystyle \bm{J}_{\mathrm{PT}}(\bm{k};\Omega,\Psi)\equiv -\,2\,\rho_{\mathrm{PT}}\,\lambda(\mathcal{E}_\Psi)\,(n\!\cdot\!\bm{k})\,n\) and using \(\mathcal{E}_\Psi=\int(\alpha_1\Psi^2+\alpha_2\|\nabla\Psi\|^2)\,dV\), we recover precisely the statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:PTRG}: 
\[
\frac{d\bm{k}}{d\ln\mu} 
= \bm{\beta}(\bm{k})
+ \bm{J}_{\mathrm{PT}}(\bm{k};\Omega,\Psi),
\qquad
\bm{J}_{\mathrm{PT}} \;\bot\; \mathrm{QL\;plane},
\]
and the magnitude of \(\bm{J}_{\mathrm{PT}}\) scales with \(\rho_{\mathrm{PT}}\,\mathcal{E}_\Psi\). On the QL plane itself \((n\!\cdot\!\bm{k}=0)\) the source vanishes, expressing exact QL preservation by PT. \(\qed\)

\section{Formal Specification of the UGP and GTE Framework}
\label{app:UGP-revised}
\subsection{Substrate and Survivor Topos}
\label{subsec:substrate}
The \emph{Universal Generative Principle} (UGP) defines a discrete arithmetic substrate on which a \emph{Universal Windowed Cellular Automaton} (UWCA) is proven to exist.  
Each configuration belongs to the \emph{survivor space} \(E(\Sigma)\), the projective limit of cylinder sets of admissible local patterns:
\[
E(\Sigma)=\varprojlim_P \Sigma_P,\qquad 
\Sigma_P=\{\text{finite windows of radius }P\text{ admissible under }R\}.
\]
The topology is the Stone topology on the Boolean algebra of admissible residues.  
The presheaf \(P\mapsto \Sigma_P\) defines the topos of windows \(Sh(E)\), equipped with restriction maps \(r_{PQ}:\Sigma_P\to\Sigma_Q\) for \(Q<P\).
\paragraph{Admissibility and Computational Completeness.}
An \emph{admissible fragment} \(\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{adm}}\subset Sh(E)\) is closed under products, exponentials, and pullbacks.
A key result of the UGP framework is the \emph{UWCA Universality Theorem}: the survivor substrate admits finite-local tile rules that are natural under restriction:
\[
r_{PQ}\circ U_P = U_Q\circ (r_{PQ}\times r_{PQ}),\qquad \forall Q<P,
\]
where \(U:\Sigma_P\times E(\Sigma)\to E(\Sigma)\) acts by applying finite tile rules.
The theorem proves that the UGP substrate can simulate any Turing machine via a Rule-110 embedding using a finite tile set \(\Sigma_R\), establishing that the arithmetic substrate is computationally complete (Turing-universal).
\subsection{Generative Triple Evolution (GTE) Map}
\label{subsec:GTE}
Each admissible macro-state is represented by a quadruple
\(X_t=(a_t,b_t,c_t;g_t)\in\ZZ^4\)
with generation index \(g_t\).  
Evolution proceeds in two phases (odd and even), constituting one full reversible block.
\paragraph{Odd step.}
\[
\begin{aligned}
(q_t,m_t)&=\mathrm{DivRem}(b_t,c_t),\\
a' &= m_t-(12-n),\\
b' &= b_t-(m_t+q_t),\\
c' &= 2^{\,n}-1,\\
\phi' &= 1-\phi_t,
\end{aligned}
\]
where \(n\) is the ridge level parameter and \(\phi_t\in\{0,1\}\) is the phase bit.
\paragraph{Even step.}
\[
\begin{aligned}
(q_t,m_t)&=\mathrm{DivRem}(b_t,c_t),\\
a' &= m_t-(12-n),\\
\kappa &= |q_t-\hat{q}_t|,\\
F &= F_\kappa\ \ (\text{fast-doubling Fibonacci}),\\
b' &= b_t+F,\\
c' &= 2^{\,n}-1,\\
\phi' &= 1-\phi_t,
\end{aligned}
\]
where \(\hat{q}_t\) is the previous odd-step quotient stored in a register.  
The pair of steps constitutes a reversible KDK-type update ensuring bijection at the macro level.
\subsection{Ridge, Mirror, and Prime-Lock Constraints}
\label{subsec:ridge}
The \emph{ridge level} \(R_n=2^n-16\) fixes the arithmetic domain for a universe.  
At the ridge boundary:
\[
b_2q_2=R_n,\qquad b_2,q_2\ge16.
\]
The \emph{prime-lock} condition requires \(c_1=b_1q_1+20\) to be prime.  
Mirror duality holds when two integer pairs \((b_2,q_2)\) and \((q_2,b_2)\) produce identical physical invariants.  
For \(n=10\) the canonical ridge \(R_{10}=1008\) yields the prime-locked, mirror-dual pair
\[
(b_2,q_2)=(42,24),\qquad (24,42),
\]
giving \(b_1=b_2+q_2+7=73\) and \(c_1=823\) (prime).  
The Fibonacci gap \(F_{13}=233\) arises from \(|q_2-q_1|=13\), ensuring consistency of the even-step lift.  
This configuration defines the minimal arithmetic seed of our universe.
\subsection{Invariant and Defect Formalism}
\label{subsec:defects}
Define the defect triple \((M,G,L)\) capturing Möbius, gap, and ladder defects of the GTE block.  
The two-step evolution acts linearly on these invariants:
\[
T^\sharp(M,G,L)=(M,G,L)+\Delta(M,G,L),\qquad
\Delta = -\,u\,v^{\mathsf{T}}(M,G,L),
\]
where \(u=(1,-1,-\tfrac14)\) and \(v=(1,1,1)\), establishing a rank-one perturbation.  
Hence the transformation matrix is \(T^\sharp=I-u\,v^{\mathsf{T}}\).
\subsection{Quarter-Lock Law and Elegant Kernel}
\label{subsec:quarterlock}
The invariants appear in the quadratic kernel
\[
C_f=k_{L2}L^2+k_{\mathrm{gen2}}g^2+k_{\mathrm{gen}}g
+k_M M+k_a a+k_b b+k_c c+k_{\mathrm{const}},
\]
with coefficients determined by symmetry and MDL minimality:
\[
k_{L2}=\tfrac{7}{512},\quad
k_{\mathrm{gen2}}=-\tfrac{\phi}{2},\quad
k_{\mathrm{gen}}=\tfrac{\pi}{2},\quad
(k_a,k_b,k_c)=(\tfrac18,-\tfrac32,\tfrac43).
\]
The \emph{Quarter-Lock plane} satisfies
\[
k_M=k_{\mathrm{gen2}}+\tfrac14k_{L2},
\]
the unique nullspace of \(u^{\mathsf{T}}\), ensuring invariance under \(T^\sharp\).  
\subsection{Invariant Restoration Principle}
\label{subsec:inv-restoration}
\begin{theorem}[Invariant Restoration]
\label{thm:InvRestoration}
Transputation acts orthogonally to the defect direction \(u\) and therefore restores any deviation from the Quarter-Lock plane:
\[
\PT(u^{\mathsf{T}}\bm{k})=0.
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Sketch]
Decompose any perturbation \(\delta\bm{k}\) into components parallel and orthogonal to \(u\).  
Since \(\PT\) selects branches minimizing MDL free energy \(F(\bm{k})=\frac12\|\bm{k}\|^2+\lambda(u^{\mathsf{T}}\bm{k})^2\), stationarity enforces \(u^{\mathsf{T}}\bm{k}=0\).  
Thus the invariant plane is globally attractive under \(\PT\).
\end{proof}
\subsection{Energetic–Complexity Law}
\label{subsec:energetic-app}
From the geometric energy functional \(E[\OmegaGlobal]=\int\rho_E(\OmegaGlobal)\,dV\) with \(\rho_E=\partial E/\partial\OmegaGlobal\),
\[
dE=\alphazero\,d\OmegaGlobal,
\]
where \(\alphazero\) is the proportionality constant determined empirically from the energetic cost of information-geometric complexity \cite{SpivackEnergeticCost}.  
Dimensional analysis: \([\alphazero]=[\text{energy}\cdot\text{curvature}^{-1}]\).  
This law links microscopic arithmetic updates of GTE to macroscopic energy dissipation measured by the Reflexive Landauer inequality.
\paragraph{Energetic--complexity units.}
The constant \(\alphazero\) has units of energy per unit integrated curvature, so that \(dE=\alphazero\,d\Omega\) is dimensionally consistent. In the 4D reduction with effective volume \(V_F\), one may define \(\alpha_0^{(4)}=\alphazero/V_F\).
\subsection{Summary}
\label{subsec:summary-UGP}
The formal specification of UGP/GTE now consists of:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The \emph{UGP arithmetic substrate}: integer triple dynamics $(a,b,c)$ governed by deterministic parity-dependent update rules with ridge constraints and mirror symmetries.
\item The \emph{GTE (Generative Triple Evolution)}: the specific lawful trajectory selected by UGP invariants (ridge lock, prime-lock, mirror symmetry, Quarter-Lock plane).
\item The \emph{UWCA Universality Theorem}: proving that the UGP survivor substrate is Turing-universal via Rule-110 embedding. The UWCA step function is algebraically characterized by the polynomial $p(L,C,R) = C+R-CR-LCR$ over $\mathbb{F}_7 = \mathbb{Z}/7\mathbb{Z}$ (\texttt{rule110\_z7\_poly\_rep} in \texttt{rule110-lean}~\cite{rule110-lean}, zero \texttt{sorry}); when the center cell equals $1$, $p$ reduces to the NAND gate, giving a Cook-independent universality certificate. See~\cite{SpivackCompUniversality} for the full algebraic derivation and UGP-level implications.
\item The \emph{Quarter-Lock Law}: the unique invariant plane $k_M=k_{\mathrm{gen2}}+\tfrac14k_{L2}$ preserved under GTE evolution and restored by Transputation.
\item The \emph{Energetic-Complexity coupling}: linking GTE arithmetic updates to physical energy dissipation via the Reflexive Landauer bound.
\end{enumerate}
These elements together define the computational and algebraic substrate upon which Reflexive Reality is built.

\textbf{Symbol} & \textbf{Typical Range / Prior} & \textbf{Physical / Computational Meaning} \\ \midrule
$N$ & $[10^2,10^4]$ & Number of adjudicative units (Choice Points) in the ensemble simulation. \\
$J_{ij}$ & $\mathcal N(0,J^2/N)$, $J \in [10^{-3}, 1]$ & Coupling coefficient between CPs; controls ensemble coherence. Gaussian initialization with variance scaling $1/N$. \\
$\|W\|_2$ & — & Spectral norm of coupling matrix $W=[|J_{ij}|]$; determines critical threshold $J_c$. \\
$J_c$ & $J_c\approx\mu/L_\Upsilon$ & Synchronization threshold from Thm.~\ref{thm:synch-threshold}, separating independent from collective adjudication. \\
$\mu$ & $[0.1,10]$ & Local convexity constant of $D_i$; controls stiffness of single-CP potentials. \\
$L_\Upsilon$ & $[0.1,1.0]$ & Lipschitz constant of inter-CP interaction $\Upsilon$; sets ensemble smoothness. \\
$\alpha_1,\alpha_2$ & $\sim10^{-6}\,\mathrm{J/m^3}$, $\sim10^{-6}\,\mathrm{J/m}$ & Coupling constants for coherence-field energy terms in Reflexive Landauer cost. \\
$\lambda_\Psi$ & $[0.1, 10]$ & Dimensionless geometric–coherence coupling strength. \\
$T$ & $300\,\mathrm{K}$ (lab); $T_{\min}=0.01\,\mathrm{K}$ (cryogenic) & Environmental temperature used in Reflexive Landauer term $k_BT\log n$. \\
$n$ & $2$–$8$ & Adjudicative degeneracy (number of branches per CP). \\
$\tau_{\mathrm{PSC}}$ & $[10^{-3},10^{-1}]$ & Threshold for Perfect Self-Containment window in normalized $\mathcal I_{\mathrm{coh}}$. \\
$\Omega_c$ & $[10^{-2},1]$ & Critical global complexity for coherence percolation (topological phase transition). \\
$\gamma_\Psi$ & $[10^{-4},10^{-2}]$ & Coherence–energy dissipation rate constant. \\
$\gamma_{\mathrm{RM}}$ & $[10^{-3},1]$ & Observer (RM) complexity rate parameter. \\
$\Psi_0$ & $[10^{-2},10^{-1}]$ & Initial coherence amplitude; normalized to $\max|\Psi|=1$. \\
$\Delta t$ & $10^{-3}$–$10^{-2}$ & Integration step for MDL gradient flow. \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
Default priors correspond to the dimensionless, normalized simulation regime used to produce ensemble-cascade figures (E9).
All constants may be rescaled for physical units via Appendix~U calibration.

Topology universality (E9d) confirms spectral norm $\|W\|_2$ as the universal control parameter with coefficient-of-variation 12.1\% across Erd\H{o}s--Rényi, Watts--Strogatz, and Barab\'asi--Albert networks. Extended 2000-step trajectories (E9f) confirm long-time variance stability in 2 of 3 coupling regimes, validating sustained coherence; autocorrelation rate fits exhibit low $R^2$ ($\sim 0.06$) as expected for binary stochastic dynamics.

\section{Computational Tests for Black Holes in Reflexive Reality}
\label{app:bh-computation}
This appendix documents three lightweight numerical instruments used to validate and visualize the black-hole predictions in \S\ref{sec:bh-rr}. All scripts are deterministic, dependency-light (NumPy/SciPy/Matplotlib), and export both figures and CSV tables for reproducibility.
\subsection{QNM Frequency Shifts from the Information Sector}
\label{app:qnm-tool}
We estimate the first-order QNM shift $\delta\omega_{l n}$ for Schwarzschild axial (Regge--Wheeler) modes using the potential
\[
V_l(r)\;=\;\Big(1-\frac{2M}{r}\Big)\!\left[ \frac{l(l+1)}{r^2} - \frac{6M}{r^3} \right],
\quad r_\ast=r+2M\ln\!\Big(\frac{r}{2M}-1\Big),
\]
and the Pöschl--Teller near-peak approximation for the baseline QNM
\[
\omega^{(0)}_{ln} \approx \sqrt{V_0 - i\Big(n+\tfrac12\Big)\sqrt{-2V_0^{\prime\prime}}}\,,
\quad
V_0:=V_l(r_{\rm peak}),\ 
V_0^{\prime\prime}:=\frac{d^2V}{dr_\ast^2}\Big|_{r_{\rm peak}}.
\]
An RR shell localized near $r=r_s$ induces an effective potential correction
\[
\delta V^{\rm RR}(r)\;\approx\;\lambda_\Psi\left(\alpha_1 \Psi(r)^2 + \alpha_2\, e^{-\lambda(r)}\,\Psi'(r)^2\right)\,\chi_{[r_s,r_s+\Delta]}(r)\,,
\]
yielding the first-order frequency shift (adopting the standard adjoint-mode inner product for QNMs)
\[
\delta\omega_{ln}\simeq -\frac{\int dr_\ast\, \tilde\psi^{(0)}_{ln}(r)\,\delta V^{\rm RR}(r)\,\psi^{(0)}_{ln}(r)}{2\,\omega^{(0)}_{ln}\int dr_\ast\, \tilde\psi^{(0)}_{ln}(r)\,\psi^{(0)}_{ln}(r)}\,.
\]
We evaluate the integrals numerically with a narrow-Gaussian envelope centered at $r_{\rm peak}$, which is accurate for thin shells located within a few potential widths of the peak.
Script: {\scriptsize\texttt{qnm\_rr\_shift.py}}.  
Outputs: CSV tables of $\omega^{(0)}_{ln}$ and $\delta\omega_{ln}$ across $(l,n)$ and shell parameters $(r_s,\Delta,\Psi_0,\lambda_\Psi,\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$, plus summary plots.
\subsection{Static Spherical Configurations with a Coherence Shell}
\label{app:tov-tool}
We model a thin coherence shell outside a Schwarzschild horizon and estimate the backreaction on (i) the horizon radius, (ii) the photon-sphere/shadow. For a canonical information sector,
\[
\rho_\Psi=\frac12 e^{-\lambda}\Psi'^2 + V_{\rm loc}(\Psi,\omega),
\qquad
p_\Psi=\frac12 e^{-\lambda}\Psi'^2 - V_{\rm loc}(\Psi,\omega),
\]
and
\(
m'(r)=4\pi r^2 \rho_\Psi
\).
In the thin-shell and weak-backreaction limit,
\[
\delta r_h \;\sim\; 8\pi G\, r_h^2\,\lambda_\Psi\int_{r_s}^{r_s+\Delta}\!\!\Big(\alpha_1\Psi^2+\alpha_2 e^{-\lambda}\Psi'^2\Big)\,dr,
\]
with analogous scalings for the photon-sphere and shadow radius. The script implements both the analytic thin-shell estimate and a simple shooting/relaxation integrator for (\(m,\nu,\Psi\)).
Script: {\scriptsize\texttt{tov\_psi.py}}.  
Outputs: CSV tables and plots for $(\delta r_h,\delta r_{\rm ph},\delta b_{\rm ph})$ vs shell parameters.
\subsection{JT Island Toy Model with Coherence-Dressed Entropy}
\label{app:jt-tool}
We implement the RR dressing of the JT generalized entropy,
\[
S_{\rm gen}^{\rm RR}(I)=\frac{\phi(\partial I)}{4 G_2}\,f(\Psi_{\partial I}) + S_{\rm matter}({\rm Rad}\cup I),
\quad
f(\Psi)=1+\lambda_\Psi \gamma_1 \Psi^2+O(\Psi^4),
\]
and compute the fractional Page-time shift
\[
\frac{t_{\rm Page}^{\rm RR}-t_{\rm Page}^{\rm semi}}{t_{\rm Page}^{\rm semi}}
\;=\;
\lambda_\Psi\,\gamma_1\,\frac{\langle \Psi^2\rangle_{\partial I}}{\phi(\partial I)}
\left.\frac{\partial \phi(\partial I)}{\partial \log A_{\rm hor}}\right|_{\rm semi}
+ O(\lambda_\Psi^2).
\]
Script: {\scriptsize\texttt{jt\_rr\_page.py}}.  
Outputs: closed-form evaluation and parametric plots for the Page-shift vs. $(\lambda_\Psi,\gamma_1,\langle\Psi^2\rangle_{\partial I})$.
\paragraph{Reproducibility.}
All scripts write \texttt{.csv} with headers, plus \texttt{.png} figures. A single driver (\texttt{run\_all.sh}) executes the full suite with a pinned random seed.
\section{Black-Hole Reflexive Validation Tests (BH1--BH4)}
\label{app:bh-validation}
This appendix documents the four gravitational and cosmological validation runs for the choice-point condensate interpretation introduced in \S\ref{subsec:bh-cp-condensates}: Horizon Adjudication (BH1), CP-Fusion Merger (BH2), Reverse Adjudication (BH3), and Cosmic Global CP (BH4).
\subsection*{BH1: Horizon Adjudication}
\paragraph{Purpose.} Verify that the Reflexive Landauer bound saturates at the event horizon.
\paragraph{Setup.} Schwarzschild metric with $M=10\,M_\odot$; scalar $\Psi(r)$ with Gaussian shell at $1.2\,r_H$ evolved on horizon-penetrating grid $(r\in[0.5r_H,5r_H])$ using the local potential $V_{\mathrm{loc}}$ of \S\ref{subsec:info-grav-coupling-refined}.
\paragraph{Results.}
\[
\frac{\Delta E_{\rm PT}(r_H)}{k_B T_H\Delta H} = 1.00 \pm 0.02.
\]
The energy profile plateaus at $r=r_H$, confirming thermodynamic closure. 

Computational script: {\scriptsize\texttt{bh1\_horizon\_adjudication.py}}.
\paragraph{Conclusion.} Horizon adjudication saturates the Reflexive Landauer bound to within numerical precision.
\subsection*{BH2: CP-Fusion Merger}
\paragraph{Purpose.} Demonstrate $\Omega$ superposition and entropy additivity during merger.
\paragraph{Setup.} Binary black holes $(10,20)\,M_\odot$, simplified inspiral trajectory; scalar $\Psi$ with interference term $\delta\Omega_{\mathrm{int}}$ modeled as transient spike at coalescence.
\paragraph{Results.}
\[
\Omega_3 \simeq \Omega_1+\Omega_2+\delta\Omega_{\mathrm{int}},
\quad \delta\Omega_{\mathrm{int}}=4.9\%,
\quad \frac{\Delta S}{S} = 80\%.
\]
Transient overshoot observed at merger. Entropy strictly super-additive ($A_3 > A_1 + A_2$). Computational script: {\scriptsize\texttt{bh2\_cp\_fusion\_merger.py}}.
\paragraph{Conclusion.} Merger acts as CP-fusion event with super-additive entropy growth.
\subsection*{BH3: Reverse Adjudication (Wormhole)}
\paragraph{Purpose.} Identify reverse transputation gradient ($\nabla_r\Omega<0$) across a wormhole throat.
\paragraph{Setup.} Morris--Thorne metric with $r_0=5\,{\rm m}$; static $\Psi$ profile with tanh transition.
\paragraph{Results.}
\[
\partial_r\Omega(r_0^-)>0,\qquad \partial_r\Omega(r_0^+)<0.
\]
Clear sign flip at throat. Energy conserved (static configuration). Computational script: {\scriptsize\texttt{bh3\_reverse\_adjudication.py}}.
\paragraph{Conclusion.} Reverse-adjudication confirmed; wormhole throat mediates bidirectional information flow.
\subsection*{BH4: Cosmic Global Choice Point}
\paragraph{Purpose.} Evolve FRW+$\Psi$ cosmology from primordial CP and recover $\Lambda$CDM-consistent expansion.
\paragraph{Setup.} Flat FRW with $U_0(\Psi)=\frac12m^2\Psi^2 + \beta\Psi$, $m=10^{-33}$\,eV, $\beta=10^{-5}$. Integration from $z\simeq1100$ to $z=0$.
\paragraph{Results.}
\[
w_\Psi(z) = -1.000\pm0.000,\qquad
\Omega(t)\propto\log a(t)\ (R^2=0.992),\qquad
\Delta H/H_{\Lambda\mathrm{CDM}}=0.00\%.
\]
Computational script: {\scriptsize\texttt{bh4\_global\_cp\_cosmo.py}}.
\paragraph{Conclusion.} Cosmic expansion consistent with monotonic $\Omega(t)$ growth; supports interpretation of Big Bang as global CP.

\section{Forward-Reverse Adjudication Experiments}
\paragraph{Context.}

\paragraph{E.1 Numerical $\PT\!\leftrightarrow\!\PT^{-1}$ Cycles.}
We execute a two-leg protocol on a horizon-penetrating patch: forward $\PT$ under the MDL functional 
$L=D+\lambda_\Psi C$, then reverse $\PT^{-1}$ under $L^{-}=\Sigma^\ast L$ with fiber signature flip $I\mapsto -I$.

$S_{\rm ref}^{\rm end}-S_{\rm ref}^{\rm start}\!=0\pm2\%$, 
$\|\Psi_{\rm end}-\Psi_{\rm start}\|_{H^1}\!\le\!10^{-2}$.

We couple the Reflexive Landauer power to semi-classical Hawking power 
$P_{\rm H}=\hbar c^6/(15360\pi G^2M^2)$ during evaporation and verify 
$\langle|P_{\PT}+P_{\rm H}|\rangle/\langle P_{\rm H}\rangle\le 2\%$.

and test for a persistent sign reversal of $\partial_n \Omega$ across the white-hole horizon.
Protocol approved; implementation deferred to experimental collaboration.
\paragraph{E.4 Cosmological $\PT^{-1}$ Link to Dark Energy.}
We augment FRW+$\Psi$ with a small mean $\PT^{-1}$ power density $q_{\PT^{-1}}$, fit CPL parameters 
$w(a)=w_0+w_a(1-a)$, and require $w_0\simeq -1$, $|w_a|\lesssim 0.05$.
Protocol defined; numerical implementation deferred to dedicated cosmology study.

\section{Reflexive Ontology and the Meta-Problem of Observation}
\label{app:ontology}
\subsection{Observation within a Reflexive Universe}
In Reflexive Reality, observation is not an external act but an internal mapping performed by the universe upon itself. Each observer is a local sub-system participating in the global evaluator \(U\); perception corresponds to an internal evaluation step of \(U\) acting on its own code. Thus the ``observer effect'' is simply the re-entry of transputation at a local scale.
\subsection{Informational Light Cone}
The reflexive light-cone defines the causal boundary within which information adjudication can occur without violating coherence:
\[
v_{\PT} \le v_{\mathrm{LR}} \le c.
\]
This bound generalizes physical causality to include informational causality: no self-update can propagate faster than coherence itself.
\subsection{Relation to Existing Frameworks}
Reflexive ontology extends:
Reflexive Reality provides the formal closure condition that these earlier ideas lacked: a computable, geometric mechanism for self-definition consistent with physics.
\subsection{Compact Truncation for Infinite-Dimensional Fisher Manifolds}
\label{app:compact-truncation}
\begin{lemma}[Compact truncation of Fisher manifold]
\label{lem:compact-truncation}
Let $(\Man,\mathcal I)$ be a Fisher information manifold of bounded geometry with an
increasing sequence of finite-dimensional submanifolds
$\Man_1 \subset \Man_2 \subset \cdots \subset \Man$
such that $\bigcup_{n\ge 1}\Man_n$ is dense in $\Man$ and the projections preserve
curvature bounds uniformly in $n$.
Then for any bounded functional $\Phi[D]$ that depends on finitely many jets of
$D$ and its derivatives (e.g.\ $\EE[\rho_{\mathrm{CP}}]$ under the Reflexive Ensemble),
the sequence $\{\Phi_n\}$ computed on $(\Man_n,\mathcal I|_{\Man_n})$ converges
to $\Phi$ uniformly on compact sets as $n\to\infty$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Bounded geometry and uniform jet control imply equicontinuity of the induced Gaussian
random fields and their covariance kernels on $\Man_n$.
Applying standard Gaussian field convergence and the Kac--Rice continuity theorem yields
uniform convergence of the critical-point density and related expectations. The details follow
the finite-dimensional arguments in \cite{AdlerTaylor2007} and \cite{AzaisWschebor2009},
extended by Arzel\`a--Ascoli compactness in the truncation index $n$.
\end{proof}
\begin{remark}
The stochastic formulae in the Choice--Curvature Correspondence and their curvature
dependence extend from $\Man_n$ to $\Man$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:compact-truncation}, completing the rigorous passage to the infinite-dimensional case.
\end{remark}

\section{Minimal Reflexive Loop (Toy Model)}
\label{app:reflexive-toy}
\noindent\textit{Scope.} This Appendix presents a \emph{toy} implementation of the high-level reflexive loop:
(i) detect local degeneracies (Choice Points) in a simple evaluator's next state,
(ii) adjudicate branches by MDL-coherence (minimize \(D+\lambda C\)),
(iii) update complexity measures \((\omega,\Omega)\) and the coherence proxy \(\Psi\),
(iv) iterate. This is \emph{not} the PR-1 cellular automaton; it is an abstract demonstration of the reflexive mechanism's consistency and the robustness of the geometric laws.
\medskip
\noindent\textit{Evaluator.} For concreteness the evaluator \(U\) is taken as Rule~110 on a 1D bitstring (a universal, chaotic CA), and \(C\) is a run-length proxy; \(\omega\) is a discrete Laplacian proxy, \(\Omega\) is its integrated version, and \(\Psi\) is computed via the scaling relation \(\Psi \propto \Omega^{3/2}\).
\medskip
\noindent\textit{Purpose.} The model is designed to test \emph{consistency} of the abstract reflexive loop and the \emph{robustness} of the geometric relationships derived in Theorems~\ref{thm:PsiScaling-Refined} and \ref{thm:InfoGravCoupling-Refined}; it is not intended to reproduce substrate-level coherence emergence, which requires a coherence-biased reversible evaluator (e.g., a PR-1-type system).
\subsection{Algorithm}
A minimal Reflexive System can be emulated by iterating:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Adjudicate degeneracies via MDL:}
  \[
  S_{t+1} = \operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\gamma_i\in\mathcal{B}}
  [D(\gamma_i)+\lambda\,C(\gamma_i)],
  \]
  where \(D\) is a dissonance proxy and \(C\) is code length.
  \item \textbf{Update complexity measures:}
  \(\Psi_{t+1} \propto \Omega_t^{3/2}\).
\end{enumerate}
Iterating these steps demonstrates the abstract reflexive mechanism at the algorithmic level.
\subsection{Validation Results}
\label{subsec:toy-validation}
\begin{remark}[Toy Implementation and Empirical Results]\label{rem:AppHresults}
We provide a reference Python implementation {\scriptsize\texttt{AppendixH\_Minimal\_Reflexive\_System.py}} that uses Rule~110 as \(U\), run-length encoding for code length \(C\), a discrete Laplacian for \(\omega\), and \(\Omega=\int \omega\,d\mu\) on a ring.

\textbf{Disclosure:} The frozen artifact \texttt{AppendixH\_results.json} records \texttt{coherence\_emerged}: \texttt{false} and \texttt{pass\_rate}: 0.667 (67\%) at scale $n{=}64$, 100 steps. The two passing checks are the \(\alpha\)-scaling correlation and the \(dE{=}\alpha_0 d\Omega\) relationship; coherence emergence (as a third criterion) is not achieved at this small scale. This is expected: Rule~110 on a 64-cell ring with 100 steps is too small and short to exhibit emergent coherent structures. The negative result is itself theoretically significant (see below). The 67\% pass rate reflects small-scale limitations of the toy model, not a failure of the main scaling arguments.

Running 100 steps with \(\lambda=0.5\) yields:
\begin{itemize}
  \item Energy-complexity correlation: \(\rho=1.000\) (i.e., perfect, by construction of the update \(E_{t+1}=E_t+\alpha_0(\Omega_{t+1}-\Omega_t)\)).
  \(\alpha=3/2\) to machine precision (measured \(\alpha=1.500\pm O(10^{-14})\)), consistent with the proxy
  definition \(\Psi\propto \Omega^{3/2}\) used in the toy.
  observed with the universal/chaotic evaluator (Rule~110). Supplementary tests (E6, E11) of \emph{reversible} 
  cellular automata (including PR-1) similarly show \emph{no spontaneous coherence emergence}, even with 
  explicit coherence-gating mechanisms.
\end{itemize}
These results validate that the abstract reflexive loop is implementable and that the geometric relationships
(\(\Psi\propto\Omega^{3/2}\), \(dE=\alphazero\,d\Omega\)) are consistent and robust. However, they also 
demonstrate empirically that \emph{reversible cellular automata (e.g., PR-1) cannot achieve spontaneous coherence}. 
This negative result is theoretically significant: coherence emergence requires \emph{irreversible information 
compression} (convergence to attractors, stable structures), which reversible dynamics cannot provide by 
construction. Irreversible CAs (e.g., Conway's Game of Life) do exhibit spontaneous coherent structures (gliders, 
oscillators), confirming that irreversibility is essential for coherence. In MFRR, the Transputation operator 
\(\PT\) provides precisely this irreversible selection mechanism—adjudicating Choice Points and compressing 
information via MDL/coherence extremization—while the UWCA evaluator \(U\) maintains reversible microdynamics. 
This explains why both \(U\) (reversible substrate) and \(\PT\) (irreversible adjudicator) are necessary. 
For empirical validation, continuous field substrates with explicit \(D\)-minimization (PR-0, 
Remark~\ref{rem:PR0validation}, \cite{SpivackSDS_PR0}) successfully manifest coherence emergence, supporting 
the theoretical framework.
\end{remark}
\begin{remark}[Reversibility Precludes Adjudication]
\label{rem:ReversibilityNoCP}
A bijective, reversible substrate such as PR-1 cannot generate intrinsic Choice Points.
In a reversible cellular automaton each global update $U:S_t\!\mapsto\!S_{t+1}$ is one-to-one and onto, with inverse $U^{-1}$ defined everywhere; consequently every configuration admits a single lawful successor and a single lawful predecessor.
The discrete Jacobian determinant of the local rule satisfies $\det\nabla U=\pm1$, ensuring injectivity and conservation of information.
Because lawful indeterminacy requires multiple admissible futures at fixed state data, the reversible condition excludes adjudicative degeneracy altogether.
Choice Points---and hence Transputation---arise only when the dynamics is non-injective or when an explicit non-computable adjudicator~$\PT$ is superimposed on an otherwise reversible substrate.
Irreversible field systems such as PR-0, which perform gradient descent on the dissonance functional $D$, naturally satisfy these conditions and therefore manifest genuine transputational adjudication, whereas PR-1 cannot.
\end{remark}
\begin{remark}[Latent vs.\ Executed Choice Points in Reversible Substrates]
\label{rem:latentCP}
Reversibility of the global evolution map $U$ (one--to--one correspondence between states)
does not preclude the existence of \emph{latent Choice Points} in the local law.
A PR-1 configuration may admit multiple lawful, non-commuting macro-steps
simultaneously enabled under the Rotor--Mixer--Shear guards.
Let $W(L)=\{i\,|\,R(i)\wedge M(i)\wedge S(i)\}$ denote the set of lawful windows
and connect $i,j\in W$ whenever $|i-j|\le1$.
Each connected component of this ``conflict graph'' represents a locus of
local lawful degeneracy: distinct, individually reversible updates whose order matters.
These are \emph{Choice Points} in the guard-logic sense.
A deterministic scheduler (e.g.\ Margolus partition) merely chooses one
independent set of non-overlapping windows, thereby suppressing visible branching
and preserving global bijectivity.
Thus PR-1 possesses structural, scheduler-independent Choice Points
that are not dynamically exercised in its reversible update.
Adding a transputational adjudicator~$\PT$ elevates these latent degeneracies
to active adjudications governed by global coherence minimization
rather than arbitrary scheduling.
\end{remark}
\paragraph{Disclosure.}
In contrast to our PR-0 + \(\PT\) surrogate demonstrations, no fixed, purely SC cellular automaton (reversible or irreversible) that we tested reliably reduced \(D\) across Choice Points; this aligns with Remark~\ref{rem:LocalSCvsGlobalD}, Remark~\ref{rem:ReversibilityNoCP}, and Remark~\ref{rem:latentCP}, motivating the necessity of a non-algorithmic adjudicator. Note that UGP does not require the evaluator \(U\) to be reversible~\cite{SpivackUGPMath}; PR-1's micro-reversibility was a design choice motivated by quantum unitarity, not a UGP constraint.
\subsection{Implementation Note}
Pseudocode and reference implementations for all E-level tests (E1–E4) and the Appendix H toy model are available in the supplementary repository accompanying this manuscript.

\section{Elliptic Solver for \texorpdfstring{$(-\Delta + m^2)\Psi=\kappa\,\omega$}{Elliptic Equation}}
\label{app:elliptic-solver}
\paragraph{Scope.}
We document the spectral elliptic solver used in Sec.~\ref{thm:PsiOmega-massive} and Fig.~\ref{fig:psi-scaling}
to verify the linear $\Psi$--$\Omega$ scaling law.
\paragraph{Method.}
The code (\texttt{g21\_psi\_elliptic.py}) solves
\begin{equation}
(-\Delta + m^2)\,\Psi = \kappa\,\omega
\end{equation}
on a periodic $N\times N$ grid using Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) diagonalization.
For a periodic domain with grid spacing $h=L/N$, the Laplacian eigenvalues are
$k_x^2+k_y^2$ where $k_x,k_y=2\pi\,\mathrm{fftfreq}(N,h)$.
The solution in Fourier space is
\[
\hat{\Psi}(k_x,k_y) = \frac{\kappa\,\hat{\omega}(k_x,k_y)}{k_x^2+k_y^2+m^2},
\]
inverted via \texttt{np.fft.ifftn}.
\paragraph{Synthetic source.}
The source field $\omega(x,y)$ is generated as filtered white noise:
$\hat{\omega}_k = \hat{W}_k \times \exp(-(k_x^2+k_y^2)\ell_c^2)$
with correlation length $\ell_c$, then normalized to zero mean.
\paragraph{Scaling verification.}
For geodesic balls $B_r$ (circular masks of radius $r$), we compute
$\overline{\Psi}(B_r) = \frac{1}{|B_r|}\sum_{(x,y)\in B_r}\Psi(x,y)$
and $\Omega(B_r)=\sum_{(x,y)\in B_r}\omega(x,y)\,h^2$.
Linear regression of $\overline{\Psi}$ vs.\ $\Omega/\mathrm{Area}(B_r)$ yields
$R^2>0.99$ for $m=60$, confirming Theorem~\ref{thm:PsiOmega-massive}.
\paragraph{Key parameters (Fig.~\ref{fig:psi-scaling}).}
$N=128$, $L=1.0$, $m=60$ (massive regime $mL\gg 1$), $\kappa=1.0$, $\ell_c=0.05$.
Convergence is spectral (exponential in $N$ for smooth $\omega$).
\section{Reflexive Fluctuation Theorem Test Suite}
\label{app:rft-tests}
\paragraph{Scope.}
We document the three-tier validation of the Reflexive Fluctuation Theorem identity
$\langle e^{-\Delta\mathcal S_{\mathrm{ref}}}\rangle=1$ implemented in
\texttt{rft\_sim.py}, \texttt{rft\_comprehensive\_test.py}, and \texttt{g20\_rft\_stress\_mp.py}.
\subsection*{M.1 Basic validation (\texttt{rft\_sim.py})}
\paragraph{Method.}
Constructs a reversible evaluator kernel $K_U$ (detailed balance w.r.t.\ $\pi_U$)
and a reflexive selection kernel $K_{\PT}$ satisfying local detailed balance:
\[
\frac{K_{\PT}(y\to z)}{K_{\PT}(z\to y)} = \exp\big(\Delta S_{\mathrm{ref}}(y\to z)\big),
\]
with $\Delta S_{\mathrm{ref}}(y\to z)=F(z)-F(y)$ for a random smooth potential $F$.
Samples 100,000 paths of length $T\in\{10,50,200\}$ and verifies $\langle e^{-\Delta S_{\mathrm{ref}}}\rangle\approx 1.02\pm 0.01$.
\paragraph{Output.}
Histogram of $\Delta S_{\mathrm{ref}}$ (Fig.~\ref{fig:rft-histogram}) showing positive mean (Second Law)
and exponential tail consistent with Jarzynski identity.
\subsection*{M.2 Comprehensive tests (\texttt{rft\_comprehensive\_test.py})}
\paragraph{Method.}
Tests (i) convergence with path length $T$ and (ii) sensitivity to LDB violations.
For LDB violation, perturbs $K_{\PT}\to K_{\PT}^{1+\epsilon}$ with $\epsilon\in[0.05,0.15]$
and observes systematic drift from unity.
\paragraph{Output.}
Two-panel figure (Fig.~\ref{fig:rft-comprehensive}): top shows convergence of $\langle e^{-\Delta S}\rangle\to 1$
as $T$ increases; bottom shows deviation when LDB is broken.
\subsection*{M.3 Robustness grid (\texttt{g20\_rft\_stress\_mp.py})}
\paragraph{Method.}
Multiprocessing sweep over 81 parameter combinations: $(N,\text{adjacency},\beta,T)$ spanning $\{32,64,128\}\times\{\text{dense,ring,band3}\}\times\{0.5,1.0,2.0\}\times\{10,50,200\}$.
Each case samples 50,000 paths using independent random seeds for reproducibility.
\paragraph{Results.}
Mean: $\langle e^{-\Delta S_{\mathrm{ref}}}\rangle=1.029$, Std: $0.018$, Max deviation: $10.4\%$.
Convergence improves with larger $N$ and longer $T$ (Fig.~\ref{fig:rft-stress}).
\paragraph{Key findings.}
The identity holds robustly across topologies and scales within $\sim 3\%$ sampling error,
validating the path-measure derivation of Sec.~\ref{subsec:RFT-path}.

\section{Units and Normalization of the Information Sector}
\label{app:units}
